However, we found no information suggesting that Qinghe Valley uses Bone-Rot Flowers or Yin Soul Grass.

At the time, Lee Hyun had wondered whether Qinghe Valley had lost some of its pill recipes over the years.

‘Do they have the pill recipe but no longer use it for alchemy? Or was the investigation back then simply wrong....’

Either way, he would find out once he went there himself.

When Lee Hyun withdrew his divine sense from the jade slip, Fang Jiyun, who had been sorting documents beside him, handed him a sheet of paper.

“These are the ones you'll be responsible for.”

Beside the names of the medicinal ingredients and inheritances were the items he was expected to inspect.

Most were yin-aspected spirit plants and highly toxic medicinal ingredients, and the Spirit-Calming Pill recipe was included near the bottom.

Lee Hyun had specifically asked to inspect the Spirit-Calming Pill recipe himself, if nothing else, and fortunately his request had been accepted.

The fact that he had already learned the Poison-Warding Pill recipe and could compare methods for processing toxic medicinal ingredients seemed to have helped as well.

“If we have to read an inheritance to inspect it, what happens to the contribution points?”

“For inheritances our sect already possesses, the task was assigned to those who had formally accessed them before. As for the ones we're considering purchasing, whoever is designated as the inspector gets to read them.”

Fang Jiyun pointed to the small seal near the bottom of the paper.

“Even if an inheritance you inspect is later registered, you won't have to pay contribution points to access it separately. Consider that one of the rewards for this mission. But you mustn't pass around and read anything assigned to someone else.”

“Understood.”

“And don't overlook flaws just because you like an inheritance. If we end up buying something useless, the person who inspected it will have to answer for it.”

Lee Hyun nodded, folded the paper, and put it in his storage pouch.

He would get to read new pill recipes and receive a mission reward on top of that. This outing was turning out better than expected.

He placed the jade slip against his forehead again.

...

A little over ten days later.

The flying boat entered the mountain range of the southwestern Great Yan Kingdom.

Steep mountains and deep valleys stretched endlessly below. Through clouds clinging to the mountainsides, scattered villages and terraced fields came into view.

Lee Hyun walked to the edge of the deck.

In the distance stood two peaks that seemed to lean toward each other, with a thin stream running between them.

It was terrain he remembered.

As the flying boat passed between the peaks, a broad valley appeared.

Qinghe Valley.

‘It's been a long time...’

The peaks lining the valley did not look very different from what he remembered. Yet many of the spirit fields that had once covered the mountainsides were now overgrown with trees and weeds.

Only the tiered stone walls remained to show that fields had once been there.

Fang Jiyun came up beside him.

“It seems even those outer peaks used to be covered entirely in spirit fields.”

As the flying boat approached Qinghe Valley's main mountain, two streaks of spirit light rose from the Mountain Gate and flew toward them. They carried the spiritual pressure of Foundation Establishment cultivators.

“Are you fellow Daoists from the Danxiao Sect?”

Xu Zhenyue stepped forward.

“I am Xu Zhenyue of the Inner Alchemy Court. We came after receiving the letter sent by the Valley Master of Qinghe Valley.”

He held out his identity token and the sealed letter. After checking the seal, the Qinghe Valley cultivator clasped his hands.

“You've had a long journey. The Valley Master is waiting for you.”

...

The flying boat landed on a stone platform inside the Mountain Gate.

Several people were waiting in front of the platform, including an elderly white-haired cultivator.

The elderly cultivator, whose back was straight and eyes were clear, clasped his hands first.

“I am Wei Qingshan, Valley Master of Qinghe Valley. Thank you for coming such a long way.”

Lee Hyun could sense the aura of Foundation Establishment Great Perfection.

Xu Zhenyue and the other Danxiao Sect cultivators returned the greeting.

As greetings were exchanged, Lee Hyun studied the people standing behind Wei Qingshan.

They appeared to be Qinghe Valley's Elders. Few looked young, and many had white hair and beards.

Wei Qingshan smiled.

“Please, come inside first.”

...

Old fragrant trees lined the path as the group followed Wei Qingshan. When Lee Hyun spotted a lecture hall with a blue-tiled roof beyond them, his steps slowed for a moment.

It was where newly admitted disciples had once gathered to practice Drawing Qi into the Body.

Several children around ten years old were sitting inside the open doors. When the middle-aged cultivator standing before them conjured a small cloud above his fingertips, all the children looked up at once.

A few drops of rain fell from the cloud.

Lee Hyun unconsciously glanced to the right.

That path had once led to the Outer Gate residences, but a stone wall now blocked the way.

While he was looking away, the Qinghe Valley cultivator walking ahead extended a hand to the left.

“This way.”

...

Tea and spirit fruits had already been set out in the Guest Hall.

Qinghe Valley disciples showed them to their seats and poured tea. Once all the visiting cultivators were seated, Wei Qingshan took his place across from them.

The tea carried a faint grassy fragrance.

Lee Hyun took a sip and set down his cup.

He had never entered this hall before. As an outer disciple back then, he would never have had any reason to come to a place like this.

Wei Qingshan spoke.

“Would you like to examine the goods first? Or would you prefer to rest today and begin tomorrow...?”

“We'll hear a brief explanation of the situation first, and if there's time left, we'll inspect the Medicinal Ingredient Storehouse.”

Xu Zhenyue took out the letter.

“This is the list our sect received. Has anything changed since then?”

“A few things have been added.”

Wei Qingshan glanced at an Elder seated beside him, and the Elder handed over a new list.

Xu Zhenyue spread the two lists side by side. At first, his eyes moved rapidly down the writing, but before long, his gaze stopped.

“You intend to part with these mother plants as well?”

“Yes.”

“Even the Seed Storehouse reserves....”

Xu Zhenyue looked up.

“If you put all of these up for sale, won't it be difficult to prepare for the next harvest?”

Wei Qingshan did not answer immediately. One of the Qinghe Valley Elders seated beside him fidgeted with his teacup.

After a moment, Wei Qingshan spoke.

“That is why I have one more request for you fellow Daoists. Our valley does not intend to receive the entire payment in spirit stones.”

Xu Zhenyue removed his hand from the list.

“Then what do you seek?”

Wei Qingshan slowly swept his gaze across the Danxiao Sect cultivators.

“Could you take in the cultivators of our valley as well?”

“......”

The sound of someone setting down a teacup seemed unusually loud.

Wei Qingshan continued.

“Our valley currently has a little over five hundred disciples. Seventeen of us, myself included, are Foundation Establishment cultivators. Many work in spirit-plant cultivation, but we also have people skilled in alchemy and the processing of medicinal ingredients.”

He pointed to the new list.

“We will hand over the medicinal ingredients, mother plants, seeds, and the inheritances that remain in our valley. In return, I hope the Danxiao Sect can provide these people with a place where they can work and continue their cultivation.”

Xu Zhenyue stared at Wei Qingshan for a long moment.

“Valley Master Wei. There was nothing about this in the letter.”

“I know.”

“We came here to appraise and purchase goods. We don't have the authority to accept the cultivators of your valley into our sect...”

Wei Qingshan nodded.

“I am not asking you to agree here and now. First, please see what remains in our valley. Afterward, I ask only that you convey our wishes to the Elders of your sect.”

He paused briefly before adding,

“It was my fault for not making this clear from the beginning.”

Xu Zhenyue's expression turned serious.

“If our sect refuses your request, do you intend to refuse to sell the goods as well? Surely you don't think we came all this way because we have nothing better to do.”

“Please don't worry. The sale of the goods can be discussed separately. Still... I thought it was a request worth making at least once.”

One of the accompanying Danxiao Sect cultivators asked,

“Are things in your valley truly that difficult?”

Wei Qingshan looked out the window for a moment before giving a bitter smile.

“It has already been a long time since our valley produced a Golden Core cultivator. Our younger disciples keep leaving, and now even demon beasts from the distant seas are being driven toward the coast. I sensed that our valley's fortunes were nearing their end. But that does not mean the immortal path of everyone here must end along with it, does it? We have many talented children.”

The Guest Hall fell silent. Lee Hyun stared at the small leaf floating in his teacup.

Xu Zhenyue spoke again.

“I understand your intentions, Valley Master Wei. However, there is no guarantee that every cultivator from your valley will become a formal disciple of our sect.”

Wei Qingshan nodded.

“We do not expect equal treatment from the beginning. We would even accept being assigned to a separate Outer Gate Herb Garden. I only hope that if they accumulate contributions and prove their skills, there will be a path for them to learn inheritances and receive pills.”

Xu Zhenyue considered this for a moment.

“I will relay those conditions exactly as you've stated them. But whatever we may tell the sect after returning, we must inspect the goods first.”

Some of the tension left Wei Qingshan's expression.

“Of course.”

Xu Zhenyue folded the new list.

“Then we'll begin with the Medicinal Ingredient Storehouse. The appraisal and access to the inheritances will proceed as agreed in the letter.”

“Very well.”

Wei Qingshan rose from his seat.

...

The Foundation Establishment cultivator guarding Qinghe Valley's Medicinal Ingredient Storehouse bowed to Wei Qingshan.

Wei Qingshan nodded.

“Elder Lu. Open the storehouse for our fellow Daoists.”

“I am Lu Jingshou. I will guide you through the medicinal ingredients and the living mother plants.”

He appeared to be a little over fifty. Lee Hyun's gaze lingered on his face for a moment.

‘Lu?’

It wasn't merely that they shared the same surname. His face looked remarkably familiar.

‘Genes really are incredible.... I can't believe Senior Brother Lu actually has a distant descendant still living here!’

Lee Hyun studied Lu Jingshou's face once more. It fascinated him that such a similar face could still exist after so many years. He instinctively knew that, one way or another, Lu Jingshou carried Senior Brother Lu's bloodline.

Lu Jingshou inserted his identity token into a groove beside the stone door.

Hummm―

The seal released, and the stone door opened.

Jade caskets and medicine bottles sat on the stone shelves within, each with its own wooden tag hanging in front.

The Danxiao Sect cultivators began comparing the ledgers against the actual stock and examining the quality of the stored spirit plants.

While checking the spirit plants against the list, Lee Hyun discovered that Qinghe Valley no longer cultivated Bone-Rot Flowers or Yin Soul Grass.

...

The next day.

A small stone chamber beside the Medicinal Ingredient Storehouse.

A jade slip and a thin book rested on the table.

They contained the Tier 2 Spirit-Calming Pill recipe and its annotations.

Lee Hyun picked up the jade slip and poured his divine sense into it, and the contents of the pill recipe entered his consciousness.

After the Spirit-Calming Pill's effects and instructions for use came a list of its main ingredient and supplementary medicinal ingredients.

At the very top was Yin Soul Grass with a medicine age exceeding two hundred years.

Lee Hyun read through the pill recipe and annotations in order, committing their contents to memory. Whenever he encountered an ambiguous passage, he asked the Qinghe Valley cultivator beside him for clarification.

About half a shichen (about one hour) had passed when a commotion broke out outside.

Having memorized the entire pill recipe, Lee Hyun went outside with the Qinghe Valley cultivator.

‘What's going on?’

...

A flying boat had landed on the stone platform in front of Qinghe Valley's Guest Hall, its white sail bearing the image of a blue cloud.

‘That's...’

Lee Hyun had seen that emblem back when he lived as a woodcutter in White Wood Village. Much later, he had also seen it inside the torn robe of the cultivator who attacked him.

‘The Azure Cloud Sect?’

The Azure Cloud Sect was a great sect of the Xuan Kingdom, located beyond the northeastern reaches of the Great Yan Kingdom.

From the perspective of the Kun Kingdom, the Xuan Kingdom was a large cultivation nation to the northwest. The Great Yan Kingdom, however, lay along the southern frontier of its sphere of influence.

When Lee Hyun entered the Guest Hall, he found thirteen Azure Cloud Sect cultivators already seated.

The middle-aged cultivator seated deepest inside rose and greeted Xu Zhenyue. He gave off the same aura of Foundation Establishment Great Perfection as Wei Qingshan.

“I am Shi Zhenheng of the Azure Cloud Sect's External Affairs Hall.”

“I am Xu Zhenyue of the Danxiao Sect's Inner Alchemy Court.”

“You've come a long way.”

Shi Zhenheng waited until the Danxiao Sect cultivators had taken their seats.

Lee Hyun sat beside Fang Jiyun as well.

Wei Qingshan lifted the teapot, but Shi Zhenheng raised a hand to decline.

“It seemed something was happening in Qinghe Valley, so I came to see for myself. But I found that the fellow Daoists of the Danxiao Sect had already arrived.”

“We received a letter and came to conduct an appraisal.”

“I hear you're not merely selling medicinal ingredients, but parting with the mother plants and seeds as well? And the spirit-plant cultivators are going to the Kun Kingdom with them.”

Wei Qingshan's hand froze around the teapot.

Xu Zhenyue's expression did not change.

“We have merely received a request from Valley Master Wei regarding that matter. Our sect has not decided anything yet.”

“Then that's fortunate. We can discuss it before anything is decided.”

Shi Zhenheng looked at Wei Qingshan.

“Valley Master Wei. If your Mountain Gate in the Great Yan Kingdom has fallen on hard times, shouldn't you have discussed the matter with the fellow Daoists of the Xuan Kingdom first?”

“It is not as though we never discussed it.”

Wei Qingshan's voice grew slightly harder.

“Under the conditions your sect offered, the cultivators of our valley would find it difficult to continue practicing their skills and cultivation.”

The Guest Hall fell silent.

Wei Qingshan looked directly at Shi Zhenheng.

“Our valley has long devoted itself to spirit-plant cultivation and alchemy. We are looking for a place where our people can continue learning those arts. There is nowhere more suitable than the Danxiao Sect.”

“So to open that path, you intend to hand the Xuan Kingdom's spirit-plant cultivators and mother plants over to the Kun Kingdom?”

Wei Qingshan replied.

“It is true that our valley lies within the Great Yan Kingdom. But the Great Yan Kingdom is merely a division of the mundane world, and this place is a rugged backwater where the cultivation world of the Xuan Kingdom has never extended its reach. In truth, doesn't Qinghe Valley have little connection to the Xuan Kingdom?”

One of the cultivators seated behind Shi Zhenheng set down his teacup.

Clack.

The brief sound echoed through the Guest Hall.

Xu Zhenyue glanced in that direction before speaking.

“Fellow Daoist Shi. Our sect is inspecting these goods at Qinghe Valley's request. The terms of any purchase have not even been decided. If you have something to say on behalf of the Azure Cloud Sect, then say it clearly.”

“Very well. Then I will speak plainly.”

Shi Zhenheng's gaze turned toward the transport crates lined up beneath the eaves.

“If this were merely a few boxes of medicinal ingredients changing hands, we would have no reason to involve ourselves. But if the mother plants, seeds, and the people who cultivated them all leave at once, that is another matter.”

“And who decides where that line is drawn?”

“This is happening in the Great Yan Kingdom. I am saying that the circumstances of the Xuan Kingdom's cultivation world must also be considered. We should find a way to settle this without turning against one another.”

Silence lingered in the Guest Hall for a moment.

One of the Azure Cloud Sect cultivators leaned slightly forward.

“It seems your sect hasn't decided what it intends to take yet either. We should inspect the goods as well. We need to know whether we're interested in the same things, don't we?”

Xu Zhenyue looked at Wei Qingshan.

The goods belonged to Qinghe Valley.

Wei Qingshan thought for a moment before nodding.

“You may inspect them. However, sealed items must be opened in the presence of the person responsible for them.”

Shi Zhenheng called to one of the Azure Cloud Sect cultivators.

“Steward Wen. Take a few people and check the items marked on the list. Look through the scattered records as well.”

“Understood.”

The man, a mid Foundation Establishment cultivator, bowed his head and left the Guest Hall with two other Azure Cloud Sect cultivators.

Fang Jiyun sent Lee Hyun a voice transmission.

[Go back and continue what you were doing. If they try to move any of the goods, tell me.]

Lee Hyun nodded and rose from his seat.

...

When he reached the Medicinal Ingredient Storehouse, Lu Jingshou rose from where he had been crouching in front of a mother plant.

Lee Hyun asked,

“May I continue inspecting them?”

“Of course.”

Lu Jingshou glanced toward the Guest Hall.

“What did the Azure Cloud Sect ask for?”

“They're still discussing it. For now, they said they want to inspect the goods as well.”

“I see...”

Lu Jingshou's expression darkened slightly.

“Do you intend to go to the Danxiao Sect as well, Fellow Daoist Lu?”

“If they'll take me, I'd like to go.”

Having answered so quickly, Lu Jingshou scratched his head with a slightly sheepish look.

...

Some time later.

Raised voices came from outside.

“You were told to inspect the goods, not take them away!”

It was Lu Jingshou's voice. A heavy impact followed.

Boom!

Lee Hyun headed outside while sending a voice-transmission talisman to Fang Jiyun.

One of the Azure Cloud Sect cultivators was using a technique to levitate two wooden cases and move them toward the flying boat.

In front of the Medicinal Ingredient Storehouse, two Danxiao Sect cultivators stood with Lu Jingshou behind them, blocking the way. One used a shield to withstand Steward Wen's palm force, while the other's flying sword knocked aside the silver needles of an Azure Cloud Sect female cultivator.

Clang! Clang-clang!

Ripples spread across the surface of the shield every time Steward Wen's sleeve moved.

“We're only taking them to our flying boat for appraisal. We'll return them when we're done, so move aside.”

“Not even a dog would believe that.”

The Danxiao Sect cultivator holding the shield replied,

“If your sect puts a price on them and then decides to take them, how exactly are we supposed to get them back?”

Steward Wen of the Azure Cloud Sect refused to back down.

“Keep moving them.”

At the Azure Cloud Sect cultivator's gesture, the wooden cases floated over the steps.

At that moment, Lee Hyun reached out and seized a corner of the case in front.

Hummm―

The wooden case slicing through the air stopped dead, as though nailed in place.

The Azure Cloud Sect cultivator radiating the spiritual pressure of Foundation Establishment Stage 3 twitched an eyebrow. He had narrow, sharp eyes and thin lips.

“Let go.”

Instead of answering, Lee Hyun forced the wooden case downward. The instant it settled onto the ground, a blue flying sword shot from the man's sleeve like a flash of light, aiming to sever the wrist gripping the case in one stroke.

“Watch out!”

At his fellow disciple's shout, two streaks of silver curved through the air from Lee Hyun's right. They were the silver needles of the female cultivator, who had been watching for an opening beyond the shield.

Instead of dodging, Lee Hyun punched with his right fist.

Clang!

His fist, wrapped in spirit light, struck the flat of the incoming flying sword at an angle. The flying sword was knocked aside, spinning half a turn before striking the two incoming silver needles out of the air.

Clang! Clatter!

Lee Hyun shot through the scattering sparks like a bolt of lightning.

The man flinched and hurriedly formed a hand seal, but Lee Hyun had already slipped deep inside his guard.

The man hastily thrust his left palm toward Lee Hyun's chest. Spirit light gathered brilliantly in the center of his palm.

Shing―

Lee Hyun drew the Profound Gate Sword while knocking the man's wrist outward with his left hand. At the same time, he slammed the back of the blade into the inside of the man's elbow.

Crack!

The deflected palm force smashed into the stone floor beside their feet.

Lee Hyun immediately folded the man's arm and yanked him forward. At the same time, he kicked out the man's front knee to break his balance and drove the end of the sword hilt into his chest.

Boom!

The body-protecting spirit light shattered with a sharp burst. The man's body flew into the air, and he spat blood as he tumbled five or six paces across the stone floor.

The man struggled, but could not immediately rise. His blue flying sword also lost its luster and hung listlessly in the air.

Clatter!

The dimmed flying sword rolled to Lee Hyun's feet.

At the seamless barrage of attacks, Lu Jingshou involuntarily sucked in a breath.

“How dare you!”

The instant Steward Wen's attention snapped toward his fallen fellow disciple, the Danxiao Sect cultivator drove his shield forward.

Boom!

Steward Wen was forced two or three steps down the stairs.

The fellow disciple holding the shield looked at Lee Hyun.

“Fine work, Junior Brother Li!”

At that moment, more than ten streaks of spirit light surged into the air from the direction of the Guest Hall. Foundation Establishment cultivators from both the Danxiao Sect and the Azure Cloud Sect erupted with spiritual pressure as they flew toward them.

If there is any delay or a day off, I'll make an announcement on Discord, so make sure to join. Thanks!

Chapter 61

The first to land in front of the Medicinal Ingredient Storehouse was Fang Jiyun. He glanced once at the fallen Azure Cloud Sect cultivator and the flying sword lying at Lee Hyun's feet, then immediately approached his junior brother.

"Are you hurt?"

"No."

As Lee Hyun sheathed the Profound Gate Sword in his hand, Fang Jiyun stepped forward. Almost simultaneously, Xu Zhenyue and Shi Zhenheng landed on opposite sides, and the cultivators following them filled the area in front of the Medicinal Ingredient Storehouse.

Shi Zhenheng of the Azure Cloud Sect crouched beside his fallen fellow disciple. After checking his arm and chest in turn, his eyes narrowed slightly.

"Who did this?"

When the fallen man's gaze shifted toward Lee Hyun, Shi Zhenheng looked over and slowly rose to his feet.

"A disciple of the Danxiao Sect certainly has a heavy hand."

"We should find out what happened first."

Xu Zhenyue of the Danxiao Sect pointed toward the wooden crate on the ground. Lu Jingshou stepped forward and explained that the Azure Cloud Sect cultivators had tried to move the goods onto their flying boat without permission, but Steward Wen merely brushed off his sleeves with an expression that suggested he had done nothing wrong.

"We said we would inspect them aboard our flying boat and return them afterward."

"Did our valley give you permission to do that?"

"All that changes is the place where the appraisal is conducted. What is the problem?"

The Danxiao Sect cultivator holding a shield laughed incredulously.

"If we'd believed you and stepped aside, would the goods really have come back? Besides, your side launched a flying sword the moment the crate was put down. If Junior Brother Li hadn’t stopped the attack, his wrist would have been severed. So which side was more heavy-handed?"

Xu Zhenyue looked at Shi Zhenheng.

"You tried to take sealed goods without permission and even launched a flying sword at a disciple of our sect who stopped you. Did the Azure Cloud Sect order you to do that?"

Shi Zhenheng's expression hardened, but after a moment, a faint smile appeared on his lips instead.

"Do we really need to drag our sects into a matter of disciples exchanging a few moves? There's no need to call in the adults over a children's quarrel. Don't make this embarrassing."

"If your sect's disciple had put down the goods and backed away, there would have been no need to exchange moves."

"I'll look into that separately. But one of our fellow disciples was injured as well, so I suppose we should take a closer look at that fellow Daoist's skills."

As he finished speaking, Shi Zhenheng looked at Lee Hyun.

Foundation Establishment Stage 3. The same realm as the fallen disciple. From what the cultivators nearby were saying, it seemed he had fought with a sword in hand and brought his opponent down in an instant.

That was possible for someone skilled at close combat. But if he had recklessly laid hands on a member of the Azure Cloud Sect's party simply because he trusted in such ability, then as the one leading the disciples, Shi Zhenheng could not simply let it pass.

'Those guys are already busy dealing with the overseas cultivators in the south. Would they really want to stir up trouble all the way up here in the north as well?'

Shi Zhenheng knew that the Danxiao Sect was no weak sect. Even so, an appraisal delegation that had come here to purchase Qinghe Valley's medicinal ingredients could hardly do whatever it pleased against the Azure Cloud Sect. If he pressed them down a little, Xu Zhenyue would likely back off at an appropriate point. After that, they could discuss the goods and the future of the spirit-plant cultivators again.

He jerked his chin toward Steward Wen.

"Steward Wen. Ask that fellow Daoist to exchange a few moves with you."

The corner of Steward Wen's mouth twisted. With a shake of his sleeves, two round bronze hammers floated above his hands. One was the size of a small watermelon, while the other was no larger than a plum. The snarling faces of beasts were embossed prominently across the surfaces of both hammers.

Xu Zhenyue's gaze turned cold.

"Fellow Daoist Shi. What exactly are you doing?"

As he stepped forward, a blue flying sword slipped from Shi Zhenheng's sleeve. Its tip still pointed downward, but the aura surrounding it was unmistakably directed at Xu Zhenyue.

At that moment, the large bronze hammer shot into the air.

Vwoooom―

The bronze hammer that had been the size of a small watermelon became larger than a man in the blink of an eye. Steward Wen rose into the air after it and lowered his hand, sending the enormous bronze hammer crashing down toward Lee Hyun's head.

"Those are the Mother-Child Hammers! Watch out for the smaller one!"

The instant his fellow disciple's warning rang out, the plum-sized child hammer silently drove toward Lee Hyun's chest, hidden behind the heavy roar of displaced air created by the enormous mother hammer.

The Profound Iron Buckler tilted diagonally in front of his body.

Clang!

The child hammer grazed the shield's rounded edge and ricocheted harmlessly into empty space. Lee Hyun rode the recoil of the impact and the currents of the wind, shooting through the gap just before the mother hammer could crush him.

BOOM!

The instant the missed mother hammer smashed into the stone ground, Lee Hyun had already surged directly in front of Steward Wen.

Steward Wen's face contorted viciously.

'How is he this fast!?'

He hurriedly raised his body-protecting spirit light and tried to slide backward, but Lee Hyun was already following him like a shadow.

The Profound Gate Sword remained in its sheath.

Swish.

The rounded end of the sheathed Profound Gate Sword flicked lightly upward beneath Steward Wen's chin.

Crack!

With a dull shattering sound, Steward Wen's body-protecting spirit light burst like a bubble.

"Urk!"

Steward Wen's head snapped violently backward as blood and several broken teeth scattered through the air. He was sent flying more than ten zhang (over 33 m) before crashing down and rolling across the ground. The mother hammer embedded in the stone shrank back to its original size, while the smaller child hammer also lost its glow and fell limply.

Thud. Clatter....

The sound of the bronze hammers rolling across the stone filled the silent surroundings.

...

Shi Zhenheng, who had been confronting Xu Zhenyue, saw it as well.

He had assumed the Azure Cloud Sect disciple's earlier defeat had been a fluke. But the moment the Mother-Child Hammers dropped powerlessly and Steward Wen was sent flying in a single move, he realized just how badly he had misjudged the situation.

The skill with which Lee Hyun had redirected the surprise attack with its staggered timing, slipped through the opening, and shut down his opponent in a single strike spoke of deep experience.

'I've been had! Did they sneak a sword cultivator in among the spirit-plant cultivators and alchemists? And they even disguised him as a Foundation Establishment Stage 3 cultivator to make us lower our guard... Danxiao Sect, you crafty bastards!'

Shi Zhenheng recalled his flying sword and raised a hand.

"Enough. Everyone, stand down."

The Azure Cloud Sect cultivators turned toward him.

Shi Zhenheng took a long umbrella from his storage pouch. Its handle was segmented like bamboo, and feathers showed between the blue silk of the folded canopy. A strange sheen, like the luster of a bird's wing, flowed across the umbrella.

Xu Zhenyue's gaze changed.

"The Wind-Thunder Umbrella...."

Shi Zhenheng never took his eyes off Lee Hyun.

"Our sect's disciples are apparently no match for your skills, fellow Daoist. This time, allow me to exchange a few moves with you."

"Fellow Daoist Shi."

Xu Zhenyue started forward, but Lee Hyun spoke first.

"Senior Brother Xu. Please watch for a moment."

Xu Zhenyue looked at his junior brother.

There was only a little dust on his long robe. Even after sending Steward Wen flying in an instant, Li Dongsan's breathing was hardly different from usual.

But his opponent, Shi Zhenheng, was at Foundation Establishment Great Perfection. Even within Foundation Establishment, the gap between the early stage and Great Perfection was far beyond what one might imagine.

Moreover, the Wind-Thunder Umbrella was a treasure ranked among the most lethal magic tools wielded by Foundation Establishment cultivators in the surrounding region. Xu Zhenyue hesitated, but after seeing Lee Hyun's unwavering gaze, he slowly recalled his flying sword.

'Given the Danxiao Sect's standing, Shi Zhenheng won't dare use a killing move. Perhaps it would be better for Junior Brother Li to learn how the world works on this occasion. He may even grow further because of this defeat.'

Xu Zhenyue remained alert, ready to intervene at once if Junior Brother Li fell into danger.

Shi Zhenheng opened the umbrella.

Fwoosh!

Black ribs extended as the canopy spread open in a circle.

At that moment, the sky above the Medicinal Ingredient Storehouse darkened as if by magic.

Whoooooosh―

Dark clouds swirled in from every direction, blotting out the midday sun in an instant. The feathers protruding from the umbrella's surface all stood on end, and thick strands of blue lightning began slithering between them like snakes.

Ruuuumble!

Under the pressure unleashed by a Foundation Establishment Great Perfection cultivator, the towering trees in front of the Medicinal Ingredient Storehouse shook from their roots, while even the light screen formed by the restriction over the roof rippled precariously.

Valley Master Wei Qingshan, who had been watching, raised a hand and fed spiritual power into the restriction, while the Qinghe Valley Elders beside him moved the disciples farther inside the hall.

With cold, sunken eyes, Shi Zhenheng twisted the umbrella handle.

Flash!

A bolt of lightning tore through the air.

More than ten strands of blue lightning filled the sky like a spiderweb before pouring down over Lee Hyun's head. At the same time, violent gusts spiraling in opposite directions sprang up and completely hemmed him in from every side.

At that instant, Lee Hyun's hand moved toward his waist.

Shing―

The Profound Gate Sword slid free, an indescribable light flowing like silk along its blade.

Swoooosh!

Lee Hyun surrendered his body to the currents of the wind and twisted smoothly. Just as the first bolt of lightning grazed past his shoulder, he angled the blade of the Profound Gate Sword and struck obliquely across the middle of the bolt.

Bang!

The fiercely descending lightning lost the direction of its force the instant it touched the flat of the sword, sliding away and scattering through the air.

A massive swirling gale immediately blocked his path, and Lee Hyun's sword traced a simple arc.

Swish.

It was nothing more than a basic Horizontal Sweep.

Yet when the sword tip lightly severed the central axis of the whirlwind, the gale that had roared as though it would swallow a man whole split uselessly to either side like fabric coming apart at the seams.

Lu Jingshou, who had been looking upward, forgot even to breathe.

'The Azure Steel Sword Art...?'

It was unmistakably the ordinary sword art he had seen countless Qinghe Valley Qi Refining disciples practice.

Then why was that sword trajectory cutting through lightning and storms as though slicing through water?

He also had no idea why a man called Li Dongsan of the Danxiao Sect was using this sword art. There were countless sword arts in the world, so perhaps it merely resembled theirs.

Amid exploding lightning and parting clouds, a tranquil path opened wherever Lee Hyun stepped, revealing the blue sky beyond.

Shi Zhenheng's eyes widened.

'What kind of sorcery is this?'

A chill ran down Shi Zhenheng's spine as Lee Hyun casually carved his way through the thunderclouds and approached. He hurriedly drew the umbrella together in front of himself.

Fwoosh!

The canopy folded inward and wrapped around his entire body. Layer upon layer of feathers interlocked like steel, and blue lightning spread across them, forming an impregnable fortress.

Lee Hyun's sword thrust straight toward that citadel of lightning.

This too was merely the most basic thrust of the Azure Steel Sword Art.

Tick.

The sound was astonishingly quiet.

Yet the sword tip drove directly into the central joint of the Wind-Thunder Umbrella, where thirty-six black ribs gathered to support its power. The instant the restriction was severed, the enormous wind-and-lightning energy compressed within the umbrella surged backward.

Cr-cr-crack!

BOOOOM!

The Wind-Thunder Umbrella exploded from within.

The silk and feathers forming its canopy were ripped apart and sent flying. Shi Zhenheng blocked the raining fragments with his body-protecting spirit light, but the backlash made his chest heave violently.

"Urgh...!"

Shi Zhenheng spat blood as he was hurled backward. The moment he reached toward his storage pouch, Lee Hyun lightly curled the fingers of his left hand.

A hand formed from spiritual power wrapped around Shi Zhenheng's right hand. It was the Condensed-Essence Grasping Hand. As his wrist was wrenched outward, Shi Zhenheng's shoulder was dragged sideways and twisted around.

The instant he turned his body and tried to pull his hand free, Lee Hyun's sword blade sliced through the wind after him and came to a quiet stop against his throat.

Shing.

Shi Zhenheng's entire body froze.

The dark clouds that had shaken the heavens dispersed as though they had never existed, and clear sunlight once again fell over Qinghe Valley.

"...."

The cultivators watching from below remained speechless for a long time.

Shi Zhenheng was the first to break the silence.

"That's enough."

Lee Hyun did not withdraw his sword.

"Have you seen enough of my skills?"

Shi Zhenheng's lips trembled. When he shifted his gaze slightly, he saw not only the Danxiao Sect and Qinghe Valley cultivators, but also his own fellow disciples staring up at him.

Shi Zhenheng lowered what remained of the umbrella shaft.

"...I lost."

Only then did the Profound Gate Sword return to its sheath.

Click.

The Condensed-Essence Grasping Hand restraining his wrist also dispersed.

When Lee Hyun backed away a step, Shi Zhenheng descended to the front of the Medicinal Ingredient Storehouse without another word.

Xu Zhenyue landed after him and spoke.

"Since Fellow Daoist Shi said this was merely an exchange of moves, let us end the matter here."

Shi Zhenheng gave no answer.

"Our sect will continue its inspection. If you wish to purchase Qinghe Valley's goods, make an offer to their owners. I would prefer not to see anything loaded onto your flying boat without permission again."

After a brief silence, Shi Zhenheng gave a curt nod and turned to his fellow disciples.

"Take the injured away."

Steward Wen and the cultivator whom Lee Hyun had first subdued were supported by their fellow disciples as they headed toward the flying boat, while the others collected the magic tools and fragments scattered across the ground.

Shi Zhenheng handed Wei Qingshan a pouch containing spirit stones.

"Use this to repair whatever was damaged."

Wei Qingshan accepted the pouch and cupped his hands.

"Safe travels."

A short while later, the flying boat with white sails rose into the air. Once it passed beyond the Mountain Gate, it immediately accelerated and disappeared among the clouds to the northeast.

The gazes of the cultivators remaining in front of the Medicinal Ingredient Storehouse gathered on Lee Hyun.

Lee Hyun was lightly inspecting the surface of the Profound Iron Buckler. There were a few scratches along its edge from deflecting the child hammer, but the restriction itself did not seem to have suffered any damage.

As he put the shield away, Fang Jiyun approached.

"Junior Brother Li."

"Yes."

"Aren't you better suited to fighting than alchemy?"

Lee Hyun thought for a moment, then shook his head.

"Fighting isn't something I get to do only when I feel like it, is it?"

Fang Jiyun stared at him for a moment before bursting into laughter.

Xu Zhenyue also let out a disbelieving chuckle beside them. The tension drained from his shoulders, which had remained rigid while Lee Hyun faced a Great Perfection cultivator.

"In any case, things ended well thanks to you, Junior Brother. I'll make sure today's events are properly reported once we return."

"Thank you."

After showing respect to the two of them, Lee Hyun approached Lu Jingshou. Lu Jingshou had been checking the seals on the transport crates with the other disciples, but when he saw Lee Hyun, he unconsciously bowed slightly at the waist.

"Are the goods all right?"

"Yes. Everything is safe."

"That's a relief. Then I'll finish reading the annotations I was looking at earlier."

Lu Jingshou blinked.

"Right now?"

"I think I'll finish if I read just a little more."

Lu Jingshou looked at Lee Hyun's face for a moment before leading the way. The book he had opened earlier remained on the table in the stone chamber. Lee Hyun sat down, turned several pages, and found the passage where he had left off.

For some time, the sounds of broken stone being cleared away continued outside.

By the time Lee Hyun finished reading all the annotations and raised his head, the noise had nearly died away.

...

After that, the inspection proceeded smoothly.

Xu Zhenyue compiled the list of goods they had already examined, the skills of Qinghe Valley's cultivators, and the circumstances of the clash with the Azure Cloud Sect, then sent the report back to the sect. Wei Qingshan also sent an official letter requesting relocation, and while they waited for a response, they began sorting and packing the contents of the various storehouses.

Lee Hyun examined the medicinal ingredients and inheritances assigned to him one after another.

Whenever they encountered a medicinal ingredient whose meaning was obscure or whose name was archaic, Lu Jingshou found records and samples for him. He remembered not only what was kept in the Medicinal Ingredient Storehouse, but even a considerable amount about when each item had arrived and from which spirit field.

He was skilled at comparing old ledgers with actual stock, and his handling of spirit plants was steady as well. There would likely be plenty of work for him once he joined the Danxiao Sect.

One month later, several large flying boats appeared before Qinghe Valley's Mountain Gate.

It was the escort convoy sent by the Danxiao Sect.

Qinghe Valley's request had been accepted. Its cultivators would be assigned positions suited to their realms and skills, and once they accumulated enough merit, they would receive opportunities to obtain inheritances and pills. Most Qi Refining disciples were scheduled to work in a specially prepared Outer Gate Herb Garden.

In exchange, Qinghe Valley handed over the agreed-upon medicinal ingredients, mother plants, seeds, inheritances, and artifacts. The purchase price also included the cost of closing down the Mountain Gate and spirit stones to be distributed among the small number of disciples who had chosen not to relocate.

The Tier 2 spirit vein remaining in Qinghe Valley was beneath the Danxiao Sect's notice, but if a small number of Foundation Establishment and Qi Refining cultivators had exclusive use of it, it could still provide them with a reasonably good environment.

The medicinal ingredients and jade slips packed into transport crates were loaded onto the flying boats first, followed by the mother plants transplanted into enormous pots and clods of earth containing their roots. Items recorded as Tier 3 spirit plants were stored separately without disturbing their seals. Once they returned, Tan Yunsheng and the other Elders would personally examine them.

Nearly everything that could be taken had been loaded.

On the final day, several hundred disciples boarded the flying boats. Many carried bundles or wooden boxes in addition to their storage pouches. Lee Hyun watched them from one side of the deck until he spotted a middle-aged cultivator bringing a group of young disciples aboard. It was the man who had demonstrated the Spirit Rain Art in the lecture hall on the day they first arrived.

Lu Jingshou came onto the deck after checking the seal on the final transport crate.

"Is everything loaded?"

"Yes. Nothing is missing."

He looked back toward Qinghe Valley for a moment, then cupped his hands toward Lee Hyun.

"I heard from Fellow Daoist Fang. He said you spoke well of me."

"I only told them what I saw."

"Even so, thank you. I owe you a great deal for protecting the goods and for everything you’ve done since."

"Just continue taking good care of the medicinal ingredients after we reach the Danxiao Sect."

Only then did Lu Jingshou nod with a somewhat more relaxed expression.

"That much, I'm confident in."

Lee Hyun studied the somehow familiar expression for a moment.

'Senior Brother Lu. This should count as a small repayment, shouldn't it?'

The flying boat slowly rose.

The stone walls surrounding the spirit fields on the mountainside, the ancient juniper trees, and the lecture hall with its blue-tiled roof receded below them. Lee Hyun watched the scene for a moment before turning toward the inner part of the deck. Fang Jiyun was placing teacups on a table and beckoning him over.

Once, he had racked his brain for every possible way to escape from that place alone. Now he was a member of a great sect with Nascent Soul cultivators, departing with Qinghe Valley's people and possessions aboard the same vessel.

'You really do see all sorts of things if you live long enough.'

...

After returning to the Danxiao Sect, the goods were handed over and the cultivators assigned to their new positions in turn. Qinghe Valley's inheritances were inspected and registered with the Scripture Pavilion and the Inner Alchemy Court's Pill Recipe Pavilion, while the mother plants and seeds were transferred to herb gardens suited to cultivating them.

Lee Hyun also received 160 contribution points, combining the reward for this mission with the additional merit he had earned. He had obtained the Spirit-Calming Pill recipe and its annotations, and the unexpectedly large number of contribution points put him in a good mood.

After completing the accounting, he headed to Yanxia Peak with Fang Jiyun.

...

Around twenty disciples had gathered in the Lecture Hall.

When Lee Hyun took his seat, Yue Wugou, who had arrived earlier, leaned toward him.

"Junior Brother Li. I heard you fought a Great Perfection cultivator from the Azure Cloud Sect?"

"Yes."

"I heard he used the Wind-Thunder Umbrella. Is that true?"

When Lee Hyun nodded, Yue Wugou turned toward Mei Sujun seated beside him.

"See? I told you I hadn't heard wrong."

Mei Sujun first examined Lee Hyun's complexion and aura.

"You weren't hurt?"

"I'm perfectly fine."

Even Chen Xiaoying, who was seated toward the front, turned her head. Liu Zhengyuan did not dare join the conversation and merely looked back and forth between the two of them.

Fang Jiyun sat down on a cushion and spoke.

"You should have seen Shi Zhenheng's face when he backed down. Watching him flee with his tail between his legs was truly satisfying!"

Just as Yue Wugou was about to ask something else, the inner door opened.

When Tan Yunsheng entered, the disciples all rose at once and paid their respects. As usual, he sat in the seat of honor, looked around at his disciples, then turned his gaze toward Lee Hyun.

"Our Dongsan distinguished himself splendidly again."

As the gazes throughout the Lecture Hall gathered on Lee Hyun, he cupped his hands.

"It was thanks to my fellow disciples being there with me."

"Indeed. I read Xu Zhenyue's report, and Jiyun also told me the details. You all did well. But your contribution was especially great."

Tan Yunsheng lightly tapped the letter lying on the table.

"Judging by the Azure Cloud Sect's name, one would think those bastards cultivated the Dao atop the clouds. But from how they actually behave, they're little different from bandits occupying a mountain stronghold."

Several disciples suppressed their laughter.

Tan Yunsheng's expression remained as gentle as usual, but there was an uncommon note of satisfaction in his voice.

"Every now and then, one of my disciples comes back after getting beaten by those bastards outside, and it always frustrates me. This time, Dongsan gave them a thoroughly satisfying beating."

Yue Wugou immediately chimed in, as though he had been waiting for his chance.

"What a shame. If I'd gone with them, I could have beaten even more of them."

"If you had gone, you would have been lucky to return with your pants still on."

Laughter spread through the Lecture Hall. Tan Yunsheng took a sip of tea and looked at Lee Hyun again.

"Dongsan. You didn't kill anyone, did you?"

"No."

"And no one was injured badly enough to be cut off from the immortal path?"

"I didn't go that far."

"You showed good restraint."

The youngest disciple, Liu Zhengyuan, widened his eyes.

'I heard he beat up three of them. And that counts as restraint!?'

Tan Yunsheng continued calmly.

"When fighting, there are times when stopping is harder than killing. Sometimes you don't have the leeway to pull back your strength, and some people win but still cannot contain their anger and continue attacking. Dongsan used only as much force as necessary and then stopped. He did well."

Chen Xiaoying asked cautiously.

"Master. Even so, won't the Azure Cloud Sect make an issue of this? He even defeated a Great Perfection cultivator, so they must have lost a great deal of face."

"They did."

Tan Yunsheng pushed the letter aside.

"But do you think one of their Golden Core Elders will personally come here to beat Dongsan? They were the ones who stepped forward first, claiming it was merely an exchange of moves between disciples. When a mid-stage cultivator wasn't enough, they even sent in a Great Perfection cultivator, and they still lost. If they send an Elder after that, whose face would that possibly save?"

Tan Yunsheng paused and looked around at his disciples.

"Our sect has no intention of creating unnecessary friction while the Nanming Twelve-Sect Alliance is expanding in the south. But that does not mean our disciples should go outside, get beaten, and have their possessions taken from them. If such things happen repeatedly, our sect's reputation will suffer, and that too will lead to losses."

Tan Yunsheng looked at Lee Hyun again.

"The External Affairs Court has already settled this matter with the Azure Cloud Sect. We also received their assurance that they will no longer interfere with Qinghe Valley's relocation, so you need not concern yourself with it."

"Understood, Master."

"And for the next month, Dongsan and Jiyun are exempt from alchemy duties. You've traveled a long way, so rest and take care of yourselves and your magic tools."

Chapter 62

The next day, Danxiao Immortal City.

Lee Hyun opened the wooden boxes containing medicinal ingredients one by one.

They contained the supplementary ingredients for the Spirit-Calming Pill.

Thinking back over the pill recipe and annotations he had read in Qinghe Valley, he realized that every ingredient except the main ingredient, Yin Soul Grass, could be obtained here. None was especially expensive on its own, but buying enough for several practice attempts added up to a considerable sum.

Even so, he did not hesitate to pay. He had already experienced firsthand the effect the Spirit-Nourishing Pill had on strengthening his divine sense. If the Spirit-Calming Pill offered a comparable benefit, it was well worth trying to refine it himself.

‘I'll have to take one to see how much it helps me.’

He put the medicinal ingredients into his storage pouch.

...

After returning to Qingyu Ravine, Lee Hyun picked up a popular novel for the first time in a while.

Two shichen (about four hours) later.

He was half-reclined, turning a page, when the formation plate in his cave abode chimed. Sweeping outside with his divine sense, he found two people standing beyond the Cloud-Barrier Abode-Guarding Formation. One was Fang Jiyun, while the other was a cultivator he had never seen before.

...

The mist at the mouth of the valley parted to either side. When Lee Hyun appeared, Fang Jiyun raised a hand.

"Sorry to disturb you."

"Not at all. What brings you here?"

"Well..."

He gestured toward the cultivator beside him.

"Let me introduce you. This is fellow Daoist Xue Jingxing of the Dharma Protector Court."

Xue Jingxing appeared to be a man around thirty. Beneath his long brows, his features were neat and composed, and an almost undecorated sword sheath hung at his waist. Even from his calmly restrained aura, Lee Hyun could sense that he was at late Foundation Establishment.

"Xue Jingxing."

"Li Dongsan."

The two exchanged brief courtesies.

The Dharma Protector Court was the Danxiao Sect division that specialized in combat. Lee Hyun knew its name, but he had never personally associated with any of its cultivators.

Fang Jiyun said,

"Fellow Daoist Xue wanted to meet you, so I brought him here."

"What might this be about...."

Xue Jingxing immediately stated his purpose.

"I heard you sparred with Shi Zhenheng in Qinghe Valley."

"That's right."

"I was told you cut your way through the Wind-Thunder Umbrella's offensive with your sword. Is that true?"

"It is, but..."

"If you don't mind, would you spar with me as well?"

"You mean a practice match?"

"Indeed."

When Lee Hyun glanced over, Fang Jiyun lifted his shoulders slightly, as if he had expected Lee Hyun to be surprised.

"Fellow Daoist Xue is renowned for his swordsmanship even among our sect's Foundation Establishment cultivators."

Xue Jingxing continued.

"I came without warning to make this request, so naturally I will compensate you. I intend to register it as a skill-exchange request and pay you sixty contribution points. I will arrange the training ground as well."

"Sixty points for a single spar? Regardless of who wins?"

"Indeed."

"I imagine the Dharma Protector Court has many cultivators skilled with the sword. Is there a particular reason you want to spar with me?"

"When people cultivate together for a long time, they inevitably grow accustomed to one another. From what I've heard about you, you seem to use a style of swordsmanship unfamiliar to me."

Lee Hyun considered it for a moment.

He sensed no hostility from the man, nor did it seem as though Xue Jingxing wanted to test him simply to humiliate him. A formal spar on a training ground rented within the same sect should not be particularly dangerous. More than anything, Lee Hyun was curious how a Foundation Establishment sword cultivator who specialized in combat actually fought.

"Very well."

Xue Jingxing cupped his hands.

"Thank you."

...

After Xue Jingxing left, Lee Hyun invited Fang Jiyun into Qingyu Ravine. He set the popular novel aside and brewed some tea, and Fang Jiyun picked up his teacup.

"Are you sure you should have agreed?"

"Senior Brother brought him here, so I assume he's not someone I need to worry about."

"That much is true."

Fang Jiyun took a sip of tea, then continued with a slightly more serious expression.

"But don't think of him the same way you did Shi Zhenheng. Fellow Daoist Xue is at Foundation Establishment Stage 8, but he's probably much stronger than Shi Zhenheng. Frankly, Shi Zhenheng belongs to the Azure Cloud Sect's External Affairs Hall. His realm may be high, but he isn't the strongest Foundation Establishment fighter in the Azure Cloud Sect. Xue Jingxing, on the other hand, is genuinely frightening."

"That much?"

"He's the only Metal-attribute single-spiritual-root cultivator among our sect's Foundation Establishment cultivators. On top of that, they say his innate comprehension for the sword is exceptional, so the Elders have high expectations for him. I hear even the other cultivators of the Dharma Protector Court stay on full alert whenever they cross swords with fellow Daoist Xue."

"How old is fellow Daoist Xue?"

"I'm not certain, but I doubt he's over eighty. That makes him younger than us."

Lee Hyun looked at his reflection in the teacup.

If Xue Jingxing had yet to reach eighty, then the years he had actually spent training with the sword would be shorter still. An exceptional spiritual root could allow someone to advance rapidly through the realms, but skill with a sword did not simply appear on its own.

Just how profound could his attainments have become in such a short span of time for Fang Jiyun to speak of him that way? Lee Hyun had his doubts, but there was no exaggeration in Fang Jiyun's expression.

"I'll be careful."

"Come back without getting hurt. Isn't this supposed to be the rest period Master gave you so you could take care of your body and magic tools?"

"I'll keep that in mind."

...

Three days later, in a valley northeast of the Danxiao Range.

A broad, rocky shallows stretched between towering cliffs on either side. Shallow water flowed over white stone, while deeper in the valley, a waterfall dozens of zhang high (1 zhang is about 3.3 m) plunged into a deep pool. Beyond the mist drifting above it, stone pillars could be seen standing along the cliff edges. Faint curtains of light stretched from pillar to pillar.

When Xue Jingxing inserted a jade token into the formation plate, the entrance closed. The mountain peaks and clouds outside grew hazy, while the outline of the light curtain surrounding the valley became more distinct.

"We have it for two shichen."

Lee Hyun raised his head and examined the light curtain extending high overhead.

There was plenty of space inside. High on the cliffs were scars left by swords and techniques, including some depressions that looked as though a giant beast had taken a bite out of the rock.

Xue Jingxing turned around.

"How about we allow unrestricted use of magic tools and techniques?"

"Fine by me."

"But let's exclude secret arts that consume essence blood and consumable killing moves. If either one's body-protecting spirit light is breached at a vital point such as the neck or chest, we stop immediately."

"Agreed."

Lee Hyun drew the Profound Gate Sword, and Xue Jingxing likewise unsheathed the sword at his waist. Its blade, a little over three chi (about 1 m) long, was white as though coated in frost, and the more spiritual power suffused it, the thinner its edge seemed to become. Simply keeping his eyes on the blade's edge made the space between Lee Hyun's brows tingle.

The mist drifting too close to the chill emanating from the blade turned to frost.

Lee Hyun studied the energy coursing along the sword for a moment, then landed on a boulder over fifty zhang away. Xue Jingxing raised his sword in salute.

"Then allow me."

"Come."

The moment the words left his mouth, the sword rose from Xue Jingxing's hand.

The white sword shot upward without so much as a sound and pierced through the mist. Before Lee Hyun could even raise his head to follow its movement, a long silver-white arc had been drawn across the sky above the valley.

The thin trail of light left in the sword's wake curved, and an entire section of the sky seemed to tilt along with it before pouring down toward Lee Hyun.

Lee Hyun kicked off the boulder and slashed upward with the Profound Gate Sword. The Spirit Aura extending from the blade met the silver-white arc, and his vision flashed white.

Clang!

The rocky shallows beneath his feet split apart in a long line, sending a curtain of water and stone dust surging halfway up the cliffs.

A tiny point of white light pierced straight through the curtain.

Clang!

The flying sword grazed the flat of the Profound Gate Sword with a hair-raising shriek and slid off to the side.

Xue Jingxing was already hovering above the waterfall. At a sweep of his arm, sword light tilted down to block Lee Hyun's retreat, while the flying sword that had circled behind him carved a long white line across the cliff and came flying back.

The black line running through the center of the Profound Gate Sword's blade flared brilliantly.

Flash!

A thick surge of Spirit Aura tore through the mist and stretched forward, opening a gap in the middle of the sword light blocking his way. By the time the pursuing flying sword pierced through that spot, Lee Hyun had already risen to Xue Jingxing's height.

Xue Jingxing was startled.

‘How is he breaking through my sword qi so easily?’

As the white light Xue Jingxing had spread across the sky curved around and closed in on him again, Lee Hyun slashed straight ahead.

But one severed end of the sword qi twisted like a snake, brushing past his shoulder and striking sharply against his body-protecting spirit light.

‘The inheritance he's learned is far too advanced. Trading sword qi from a distance doesn't seem advantageous for me...’

At that instant, Lee Hyun vanished, leaving an afterimage behind.

Driving forward, Lee Hyun unleashed the Boundary-Cleaving Saber Art through his sword.

Clear surprise flashed through Xue Jingxing's eyes. The light of the sword qi floating in the sky immediately descended with perfect precision onto the white sword that had returned to his hand.

The two swords collided before the waterfall.

Boom!

Light exploded between the blades, bathing both men's faces in white, and Xue Jingxing was hurled backward.

‘Where is this tremendous power coming from?!’

The composure vanished from Xue Jingxing's face.

As he was driven downward, Xue Jingxing lashed the surface of the deep pool with the tip of his sword. The water swelled as if exploding, and a spray of white water rose in front of him.

The soaring curtain of water was caught by the sword wind and stopped in midair all at once.

Xue Jingxing forced spiritual power into his blade. The cold imbued within the magic tool burst outward together with keen Metal-attributed energy laden with killing qi, instantly freezing the curtain of water.

Clang–

As tens of thousands of frozen beads of frost reflected silver-white light like mirrors, the white sword appeared like a ghost from beyond the curtain.

Each time the blade cut through the air, its silver-white afterimages split into three streams, then nine, until they became a massive storm of light covering the entire waterfall and surrounding Lee Hyun from every direction.

‘Illusions?’

Sword qi rained down with piercing shrieks through the air, and Lee Hyun's vast spiritual power erupted.

Twenty Spirit Light Shields bloomed in midair.

The shields overlapped at slanted angles, blocking the paths of the sword light.

Boom-boom-boom-boom!

Silver-white sword scars appeared one after another across the rock walls flanking the waterfall and around the edge of the deep pool. Even when spray washed over them, their light did not fade.

The torrent of sword light hammered savagely against the surfaces of the Spirit Light Shields, but the one truly shocked was Xue Jingxing.

‘Spirit Light Shields!? He's blocking my sword qi with those things...?’

Xue Jingxing crooked a finger. Three scattered streams of sword light converged at a single point. Holes punched through two Spirit Light Shields in succession. Lee Hyun hurriedly rotated the remaining shields into place, but the sword light ripped a long tear across their surfaces and shot past his shoulder.

Hovering overhead, Xue Jingxing's sleeves fluttered as two fingers traced a smooth arc like flowing water.

Following that motion, the divided sword lights gathered around the white sword that had once again left his hand. They merged into the shape of a gigantic sword the size of a small building and plunged vertically toward Lee Hyun's head.

The air between the cliffs compressed under its pressure, leaving a deep depression in the surface of the pool below. This was the Sword Control Art of a true Immortal.

Had they continued fighting at range to the very end, Lee Hyun's knowledge would have given him no way to cope with the sharpness of a Metal-attribute spiritual root and the transformations of Sword Control.

Assuming, of course, that their reserves of spiritual power were equal.

Instead of retreating, Lee Hyun twisted at the waist. His left hand swept powerfully upward toward the sky.

The air throughout the valley was violently drawn inward as an enormous hand formed from blue spirit light took shape in midair. It was the Condensed-Essence Grasping Hand.

The giant hand crossed the air and seized the falling greatsword around its middle.

Screeech! Boom!

Sparks erupted where metal and spiritual power collided, burning away the waterfall's mist in a wash of white. The fingers of the Condensed-Essence Grasping Hand were immediately sliced apart, but even that instant of resistance was enough to wrench the greatsword's falling trajectory off to the side.

Boom!

The deflected greatsword buried itself in the opposite cliff face, shaking the entire precipice. Amid the massive cascade of falling rocks, Lee Hyun's figure kicked off empty air.

Thump!

With the Wind-Riding Art combined with the recoil from the Qi Sphere Barrier, Lee Hyun's body shot straight upward through the mist.

Sword qi between the cascading streams of water blocked his path, but the Profound Gate Sword in his right hand swept through a heavy arc.

The Spirit Aura cut horizontally through both the middle of the waterfall and the sword qi. Through the gap where the falling water had been split in two, Lee Hyun shot forward like a ghost.

Xue Jingxing's eyes widened as he hovered above the waterfall.

Lee Hyun was already too close for him to recall the sword embedded in the cliff. Xue Jingxing immediately pulled a spare sword from his storage pouch and gripped it. Razor-sharp sword qi surged from the sword cultivator's fingertips around the hilt.

But Lee Hyun had already torn through the air and reached within arm's reach.

Clang!

The two blades locked head-on.

Xue Jingxing twisted his wrist, trying to deflect Lee Hyun's blade and thrust into his chest.

But.

Lee Hyun's wrist suddenly split into multiple afterimages, and six streams of pure-white sword light fanned out from the tip of the Profound Gate Sword.

Against the spray of the waterfall, a six-petaled sword blossom bloomed and filled Xue Jingxing's entire vision.

"...!"

Xue Jingxing retreated while swinging his sword furiously. Silver-white arcs burst outward, knocking away the first and second petals.

But the instant he deflected the third and fourth sword paths,

Clang–

The tip of the Profound Gate Sword shot forward like lightning and struck the space just above Xue Jingxing's hilt with uncanny precision.

"Ugh!"

His fingers were forced open around the hilt as his palm tore. His sword went spinning high into the air.

Just as Lee Hyun was about to drive his sword toward Xue Jingxing's chest, Xue Jingxing formed a hand seal with his empty hand.

‘Hm?’

Shrieeeek–

The entire valley screamed at once.

The spare sword that had been knocked high into the air stopped and trembled in place. The white flying sword embedded in the cliff also tore itself free, scattering stone dust as it rose. And that was not all. Dozens of strands of silver-white sword qi left around the cliffs, waterfall, and deep pool during their earlier exchanges all surged into the air at once.

‘A sword formation?’

Dozens of strands of silver-white sword light intertwined in midair, enclosing Lee Hyun on all sides like a gigantic birdcage as they contracted around him.

At that instant,

Booom!

Just before the sword net fully interlocked, a shockwave from the Qi Sphere Barrier erupted from Lee Hyun's entire body in every direction, forcibly pushing back the closing silver-white sword net. In that opening, Lee Hyun swung the Profound Gate Sword at an unbelievable speed toward the sword lights trying to connect with one another.

Bang-bang-bang-bang!

With a series of bursting impacts, the silver-white sword lights filling the space around him shattered into fragments.

Meanwhile, Xue Jingxing, who had been blasted into the cliff by the Qi Sphere Barrier, belatedly saw the shattered motes of light raining down.

‘What in the world just hit me? Is this man really only at Foundation Establishment Stage 3? Even a demon beast wouldn't be this ridiculous!’

He had sparred countless times with the most formidable fellow disciples in the Dharma Protector Court, but never before had he been crushed by such unorthodox and brutally overwhelming force.

Xue Jingxing let out a hollow laugh and lowered both hands completely.

"I lost. This was your complete victory, fellow Daoist."

...

The two sat on a boulder beside the deep pool. Xue Jingxing applied Blood-Staunching Powder to his palm and wrapped it in cloth, then stared at his sword hilt for a moment.

"I can't remember the last time I was disarmed."

Lee Hyun's gaze shifted to his hand.

"Is the wound deep?"

"It'll heal in a few days."

Xue Jingxing opened and closed his hand, then turned his head toward Lee Hyun.

"Do you possess a Metal-attribute spiritual root?"

"No. I have a Wood, Fire, and Earth triple spiritual root."

Xue Jingxing's brows twitched slightly. He looked back and forth between the Profound Gate Sword and Lee Hyun, seeming to choose his words for a moment.

"Where did you learn your swordsmanship?"

Lee Hyun set his sword beside his knee.

"I was told that one of my ancestors was a grandmaster of the martial path in the mundane world. He supposedly reached the Profound Realm, and I've practiced the martial learning he left behind since childhood. I also obtained other inheritances while living as a rogue cultivator."

It was the same story he had once told Zhang Jingyi. Xue Jingxing likewise nodded slowly after hearing it.

"Martial arts from the mundane world... Even so, I doubt everyone who obtained that inheritance could have used it as you do."

He adjusted the cloth wrapped around his palm.

"Once you closed the distance, you kept switching between techniques and moves in rapid succession. It was difficult to respond. Now I understand why Shi Zhenheng lost."

Lee Hyun could not readily answer.

"Fellow Daoist Xue."

"Go ahead."

"Could you recommend a worthwhile Way of the Sword inheritance in our sect's Scripture Pavilion?"

Xue Jingxing thought for a moment.

"For a sword cultivator specialized in close combat like you...... I would suggest looking into the Great Unity Heavenly Dipper Sword Canon."

"The Great Unity Heavenly Dipper Sword Canon..."

As Lee Hyun repeated the name, Xue Jingxing continued.

"It's one of the finest Way of the Sword inheritances in our sect's Scripture Pavilion."

"Thank you."

Xue Jingxing rose to his feet.

"I'm the one who benefited today. If another opportunity arises, I hope you'll spar with me again."

...

Once the skill exchange was settled, Lee Hyun received another sixty contribution points.

After returning to Qingyu Ravine, Lee Hyun lay down in his residence and closed his eyes.

From the first silver-white arc drawn across the sky to the final sword formation, every sword path remained vivid in his mind even with his eyes shut.

Xue Jingxing had been stronger than he expected.

The moment when three streams of sword light pierced through two Spirit Light Shields in succession bothered him. Lee Hyun could achieve the same result by pouring in more spiritual power, but he was not confident he could manipulate sword qi separated from the blade with such precision. He had also broken the final sword formation before it could fully unfold, so he could not claim to have properly experienced its power.

The valley in the Huatian Secret Realm suddenly came to mind.

Guo Zhenming, heaven's prodigy of Haigu Island. The dark-red bone nail launched from his hand had pierced three layers of Spirit Light Shields even after its trajectory was knocked askew by a spear. It had torn through Lee Hyun's body-protecting spirit light as well, and in the end, it had been the Black Scale Inner Armor that saved him.

Even then, Lee Hyun had realized he was not invincible. Yet after returning, his countermeasures had amounted to practicing how to draw the Profound Iron Buckler more quickly and repairing his damaged magic tools.

He had never deeply examined how his defense had been breached, or whether there was a way to make it sturdier using the same amount of spiritual power.

Lee Hyun sat up.

The Square-Inch Step, One Ultimate, Six Swords, and Boundary-Cleaving Saber Art were still outstanding martial arts. They were supreme arts created by Profound Realm masters of the Qianyang Kingdom over the course of their lives, and Lee Hyun himself had practiced and refined them for many long years. He had even integrated the Earth-Origin Force and various techniques into them.

But he had assumed that was enough. Whenever he defeated an opponent, he took it as proof that his methods were correct, and any openings exposed during combat were patched over with his abundant spiritual power and other magic tools. Ever since he had become able to perform the martial arts ingrained in him with the body of a cultivator, he had spent fewer days seriously studying combat techniques than he once had.

Xue Jingxing was a cultivator who had not even lived eighty years. Lee Hyun had lived in this world for over fourteen hundred. He had not risked his life practicing the sword every single day, but the time he had accumulated was by no means short. It was difficult to readily accept that he had been outmatched in the variations of the sword.

‘No... The years contained within Xue Jingxing's sword are not merely eighty.’

How long had the sword cultivators of earlier generations, the ones who created the sword art he practiced, held swords in their hands? How many enemies had the cultivators who followed them fought while discarding flawed paths and finding better ones?

Some among them must have possessed talent no less impressive than the grandmasters of the martial path in the Qianyang Kingdom. They had lived longer than martial artists, flown through the skies, and fought enemies capable of wielding spiritual power.

Without realizing it, Lee Hyun had been underestimating combat among cultivators. It was a world where a higher realm meant stronger spiritual power, and a better magic tool meant greater might.

Because he had overcome those differences with his vast reserves of spiritual power and the supreme arts of the mundane world, he had taken too lightly the fact that there were also people beyond those advantages who had delved deeply into martial learning.

‘I've grown complacent. I haven't been relentless enough.’

Making a technique larger was not the same as making it sharper. Just as a Profound Realm martial artist had broken through a cultivator's defenses using the principle of One Point Pierces the Surface, Lee Hyun's own defenses could likewise be breached by an opponent with far less spiritual power than he possessed.

...

The next day.

The Inner Pavilion of the Scripture Pavilion.

Lee Hyun studied the list of sword inheritances for some time. Even after finding the name Xue Jingxing had mentioned, he did not decide immediately. He read the summaries and cultivation requirements of the neighboring sword arts as well before returning to the first entry.

《Great Unity Heavenly Dipper Sword Canon》.

Access required a staggering 370 contribution points.

Lee Hyun checked the price once more, then held out his identity token.

"I would like to view the Great Unity Heavenly Dipper Sword Canon."

The managing cultivator checked his identity token.

"Fellow Daoist Li Dongsan of Yanxia Peak. Proceed to inheritance chamber five."

...

By the time Lee Hyun emerged from the inheritance chamber, it was well past noon.

Even as he walked down the corridor, he reviewed what he had just read.

It began with methods for condensing and refining sword qi, followed by explanations of various sword forms, with later sections covering light splitting and sword formations. It required no particular spiritual root or constitution, but imposed strict demands on the practitioner's control of spiritual power and attainment in divine sense.

Even the opening method for condensing and refining sword qi resembled the way he had wrapped Spirit Aura around his sword blade, but its details were far more intricate.

After leaving the Scripture Pavilion, Lee Hyun headed for the Inner Alchemy Court instead of returning directly to Qingyu Ravine.

...

The Pill Recipe Pavilion of the Inner Alchemy Court.

Lee Hyun examined the pills taken by Foundation Establishment cultivators to overcome bottlenecks.

The Origin-Opening Pill, taken when advancing from Foundation Establishment Stage 3 to Stage 4. And the Profundity-Penetrating Pill, used to advance from Stage 6 to Stage 7. Both were Tier 2 pills, though the latter was more difficult to refine.

Access to the pill recipes cost one hundred and one hundred forty contribution points respectively. That was cheaper than the Foundation Establishment Pill recipe, but after spending so many contribution points on the sword canon just moments earlier, the prices still made him hesitate.

Lee Hyun checked his remaining contribution points. Between what he had already saved, the points from the Qinghe Valley mission, and those he had earned from this exchange, he could afford to view both pill recipes.

"I'd like to view the pill recipes for the Origin-Opening Pill and the Profundity-Penetrating Pill."

He had no intention of refining either immediately. When attempting a breakthrough in his lower dantian, he could begin by simply obtaining one or two finished pills.

But later, when his entire body reached the same bottleneck, there was no guarantee he would be able to obtain fifty Origin-Opening Pills or fifty Profundity-Penetrating Pills. He wanted to learn the necessary medicinal ingredients and alchemy methods in advance in preparation for that time.

Chapter 63

After deducting the contribution points from his identity token, the cultivator on duty pointed toward a small stone chamber farther inside.

“Go to the Third Inheritance Chamber.”

...

Click.

After the stone door closed, Lee Hyun infused divine sense into the jade slip on the stone pedestal and examined the pill recipe.

The main ingredient of the Origin-Opening Pill was Spirit-Storing Ginseng.

One root of Spirit-Storing Ginseng between 200 and 390 years of medicine age. A list of auxiliary medicinal ingredients followed beneath it.

Many of the names were familiar. Some were ingredients he had often processed at the Inner Alchemy Court, while others were things he had seen at the Spirit Materials Hall in Danxiao Immortal City.

‘I already have Spirit-Storing Ginseng, and the rest shouldn’t be difficult to obtain.’

In a good mood, Lee Hyun moved on to the next section. The refining method for the Origin-Opening Pill did not seem particularly complicated.

‘I think even I could manage this....’

He then pressed the second jade slip to his forehead and examined the pill recipe for the Profundity-Penetrating Pill.

The Profundity-Penetrating Pill required another main ingredient in addition to Spirit-Storing Ginseng.

Midnight-Noon Grass.

It had to be between 220 and 450 years of medicine age and used whole, with its roots, stem, and leaves intact.

The image of the spirit plant recorded in the jade slip appeared in his mind.

Midnight-Noon Grass had dark green leaves, with faint vermilion lines running along their veins.

Fortunately, its growing conditions were not demanding. It was a spirit herb that grew in warm places without sunlight, though its leaves readily rotted when exposed to cold wind.

‘I can grow this in the tunnel.’

The underground of this world was less hot than the Earth of his past life, but deep within the common soil stratum, there were no seasonal temperature fluctuations like those on the surface, and it remained fairly warm.

After memorizing the growing conditions of Midnight-Noon Grass, Lee Hyun examined the refining method for the Profundity-Penetrating Pill.

‘It looks harder than the Origin-Opening Pill, but... I’ll have chances to learn it in the future.’

Now that there would be records of him having studied both pill recipes, he would have opportunities to assist with refining those pills.

...

The next day, Danxiao Immortal City.

Lee Hyun visited the Spirit Materials Hall where he had previously bought Jade-Condensing Grass seeds.

“Do you have Midnight-Noon Grass seeds?”

“Yes. How many do you need?”

“Give me a hundred.”

The clerk headed toward the shelves farther inside and returned shortly afterward with a wooden box. Lee Hyun inspected the seeds inside, paid the spirit stones, and placed the box into his storage pouch.
