He also bought small samples of several auxiliary medicinal ingredients used in the Origin-Opening Pill and Profundity-Penetrating Pill. They were not for planting, but so he could compare the descriptions in the pill recipes against their actual medicinal potency.

After finishing his business in Danxiao Immortal City, Lee Hyun departed to the northwest. He had been granted a month of rest as well as permission to leave the sect, so he intended to use the opportunity to inspect Tunnel No. 3.

...

As he traversed mountains and rivers by alternating between the Reclining Escape Art and Skywalking Art, Lee Hyun slowly reviewed the contents of the Great Unity Heavenly Dipper Sword Canon in his mind.

The Great Unity Heavenly Dipper Sword Canon contained methods for condensing and refining sword qi, thirty-six basic sword forms, light splitting, and sword formations.

The mnemonic formula that encompassed the condensing and refining of sword qi and the application of sword forms within this inheritance was called the Great Unity Heavenly Dipper Sword Art.

The next stage, light splitting, was a technique for dividing sword light into multiple streams and controlling them separately. Each divided stream of sword light carried sword qi and could genuinely attack an opponent. The technique Xue Jingxing had used during their spar, dividing his sword qi into several streams and controlling them individually, also fell under light splitting.

Once one became proficient in light splitting, one could precisely control multiple streams of sword qi with a single sword and have them respond to one another, weaving them into a sword formation.

...

Eight days later, Tunnel No. 3.

After breaking through the rock wall, Lee Hyun opened his spirit-insect pouch.

Bzzzzzz–

Golden balls of fur poured out in a rush.

Fuzzbees soon flew in from the passage farther inside as well. Some touched antennae with those that had emerged first, while others circled around Lee Hyun’s sleeves and storage pouch.

“Have you all been well?”

When Lee Hyun took out Bonefuzz No. 1, the swarm grew even more excited.

“Go ride it and play. Just don’t go into the spirit fields.”

He opened the chest plate, and one fuzzbee darted inside.

Click.

Its six bone arms moved one after another.

The other fuzzbees landed on Bonefuzz No. 1’s head and shoulders.

Lee Hyun watched them for a moment.

Whenever possible, he took the fuzzbees to the Danxiao Sect in rotation.

He did not want the experiences of those that remained in the tunnel and those that traveled outside to become too different. It would be easier to bring them around if they all understood the same instructions to roughly the same degree.

The same applied to operating Bonefuzz No. 1.

There were always a few fellows that tried to get inside its chest first, but Lee Hyun never allowed any single one to monopolize it for long.

“Take turns riding it.”

...

Lee Hyun first inspected the water tanks, bamboo pipes, formation inscriptions, drainage channels, and other facilities before beginning his tour of the spirit fields.

「Spirit Field No. 1-1」

He slowly walked around the field, comparing the ledger against the actual plants.

“Eighty-one Bone-Rot Flowers, 281 Yin Soul Grass plants, 73 Purple Poison Orchids, 51 Earth Vein Flowers... average medicine age, 466 years... These fellows will soon become Tier 3 spirit plants, won’t they?”

He examined the lower portions of several mother plants. There were no spirit-insect eggs and no signs of disease.

Several fuzzbees were rolling around on the nearby soil.

“You’ve taken good care of them.”

Squeak.

...

He also inspected Spirit Fields No. 1-2 through No. 1-5.

“Across all four fields, that makes 431 Bone-Rot Flowers, 1,103 Yin Soul Grass plants, 291 Purple Poison Orchids, and 202 Earth Vein Flowers... with a medicine age of around 432 years... I can harvest the Yin Soul Grass for the Spirit-Calming Pills from here.”

...

「Spirit Field No. 1-6」

Round Yin Water Lotus leaves overlapped across the surface of the broad pond. Flowers and lotus pods rose here and there between the leaves, while young stems stretched toward open patches of water.

There was no point in counting the lotus leaves. The ledger distinguished them by mother plants that had independently rooted beneath the mud.

The older mother plants had a medicine age of around 412 years, while their descendants were about 122 years old.

Lee Hyun collected the ripe lotus pods, shelling and snacking on some of the seeds while storing the rest in his storage pouch.

...

「Spirit Field No. 1-7」

Six Stone Honey Peach trees spread their branches wide.

The three older trees had thick branches extending almost to the rock walls, while the three propagated from cuttings had also grown into respectable trees.

Their medicine ages were similar to those of the Yin Water Lotuses. The older trees were around 412 years old, while those planted later were roughly 122 years old.

Lee Hyun trimmed several branches that had begun touching one another and cut back a few that were pressing too close to the tunnel ceiling.

When he extended a hand, a Stone Honey Peach detached from its branch and flew into his palm.

He peeled it and took a bite. Cool, sweet juice spread through his mouth.

He picked the fully ripened Stone Honey Peaches and placed them into his storage pouch.

...

Spirit Fields No. 2-1 through No. 2-5 were all Spirit-Storing Ginseng fields.

“Five hundred fifty-two roots at 297 years of medicine age and 914 roots at 155 years... That’s more than enough for the Origin-Opening Pills and Profundity-Penetrating Pills....”

...

「Spirit Field No. 3-1」

The Ringless Divine Tree was still small.

“About sixty-three years since sowing, twenty-two years since it sprouted... and it has one more leaf....”

Lee Hyun looked back and forth between the drawing he had made in the ledger last time and the tree in front of him, then added a new drawing.

Next, he checked Spirit Fields No. 3-2 through No. 3-4, where three hundred Jade-Condensing Grass plants were growing. The first thirty he had planted were a little over seven years of medicine age, while the 270 planted later were around five years old.

...

At roughly twenty-five li (about 9.8 km) underground, the air grew warmer.

The three hundred Fire-Heart Orchids brought from the Huatian Secret Realm had been divided among Spirit Fields No. 3-5 through No. 3-7.

“Their medicine ages are mostly between nine and eleven years....”

Lee Hyun inspected the water tanks, bamboo pipes, formation inscriptions, drainage channels, heat-insulating stone slabs, Lesser Yang Stones, and everything else in order.

...

The last place he visited was the unnumbered test spirit field.

Spirit plants of varying medicine ages had been planted in separate small plots so he could study traces of bone age. Recently, he had also begun using part of the field to test the germination of newly acquired seeds.

“That’s the spirit-field inspection finished! I only need to make one new field now.”

...

He created the new field below and a short distance away from the cavern where the Jade-Condensing Grass was being grown. This location, eighteen li underground, was warm enough for Midnight-Noon Grass, so there was no need to descend all the way to twenty-five li.

After connecting the bamboo pipes and the formation inscriptions for supplying water, he took out one hundred Midnight-Noon Grass seeds, buried them in the soil at regular intervals, and cast the Germination Art.

After evenly moistening the soil with the Spirit Rain Art, he erected a wooden plaque as the final step.

「Spirit Field No. 3-8」

...

After finishing his inspection of the spirit fields, Lee Hyun dug up three Yin Soul Grass mother plants around 432 years of medicine age from Spirit Field No. 1-2 and brought them to the alchemy chamber twenty-five li underground.

He then took out the auxiliary medicinal ingredients he had purchased in Danxiao Immortal City one by one and began processing them.

...

The next day.

When he opened the lid, two round pills lay at the bottom of the pill furnace.

“It worked!”

After ruining his first two furnace batches, Lee Hyun succeeded in refining Tier 2 low-grade Spirit-Calming Pills for the first time on his third batch!

After resting thoroughly, Lee Hyun swallowed one Spirit-Calming Pill in the cultivation chamber. He immediately closed his eyes and began refining the medicinal strength according to the mnemonic formula for consuming the pill.

The Yin Soul Grass Lee Hyun had used was old for a Tier 2 spirit plant and therefore possessed strong medicinal potency, so the effect of the Spirit-Calming Pill was considerable as well. He felt a constant sense of pressure while assimilating its medicinal strength.

Even so, because he had already trained his primordial spirit and divine sense with the Spirit-Nourishing Pill and Spirit-Refining Essentials, he had little difficulty enduring the medicinal strength.

...

How much time had passed?

After thoroughly refining the medicinal strength, Lee Hyun opened his eyes.

“Oh....”

The increase in his divine sense was far more noticeable than when he had first taken a Spirit-Nourishing Pill.

Lee Hyun examined the remaining pill inside the jade bottle.

‘I should make around ten, then take them little by little while cultivating back at the sect.’

Two days later.

After harvesting six more Yin Soul Grass plants and repeating the refinement several times, Lee Hyun managed to secure ten Tier 2 low-grade Spirit-Calming Pills.

Having finished his business in the tunnel, Lee Hyun stopped at a city in the mundane world on his way back to the Danxiao Range.

As soon as he passed through the city gate, the rumble of cartwheels mingled with the cries of traveling merchants. Steam rose from restaurants along the streets, while crowds bustled through every alley.

Lee Hyun had a particular destination in mind.

A bookstore.

When he opened the door and stepped inside, the smell of paper and ink greeted him.

The shelves were divided among classics, collections of poetry and prose, geography books, and popular novels, while newly printed books were stacked high on tables near the entrance.

Lee Hyun stood in front of them and flipped through a book. After reading a few pages, he heard a young voice beside him.

“Mother, can’t you buy me this one?”

“Dear, you really should stop reading such trashy popular novels.”

“But all my friends have read it....”

“You need to read classical literature if you want to learn anything. Here, choose one from these.”

Lee Hyun turned his head without thinking.

The shelf the woman pointed to bore a sign reading Classic Masterpieces.

His eyes fell on the titles of the books beneath it.

《I Took In What I Thought Was a Demon Beast, but It Was a Prince of Qianyang Kingdom》

《I Became a Prisoner of Qianyang Kingdom, and Now I'm Popular》

‘Huh?’

Lee Hyun pulled out a book and examined the cover.

‘This is classical literature?’

Lee Hyun let out a quiet laugh.

He had read these books 909 years ago, back when they were still classified as popular novels.

The copy in his hand was a newly printed edition. The typeface had been changed to an archaic style unlike the one from centuries ago, and there was even a note beneath the title stating that the text had been annotated by a certain scholar.

「These classic masterpieces, once popular in the now-fallen Yunze Kingdom, reflect the emotions of the Yunze people during an era when they suffered repeated invasions by Qianyang Kingdom. Literature is a mirror reflecting its age, and...」

Beside him, the woman was placing a book into the child’s hands.

“You must learn the spirit of the ancients.”

“Yes....”

Lee Hyun returned to the shelves containing the newest popular novels.

“I’ll take everything from here to here.”

“Pardon? Are you certain? The books in this section haven’t been completed yet.”

“That doesn’t matter.”

...

By the time he returned to Qingyu Ravine, only a few days remained of his rest period.

Lee Hyun piled the books he had bought in one corner of his residence and lay down to read the popular novels.

...

His leave eventually ended, and life returned to its usual routine.

After several months, he began assisting not only with the Foundation Establishment Pill but also with the Origin-Opening Pill and Profundity-Penetrating Pill.

Once his alchemy duties for the sect were finished, he returned to Qingyu Ravine and trained in the Primordial One-Qi Art, Spirit-Refining Essentials, and Great Unity Heavenly Dipper Sword Art.

From time to time, he visited Xue Jingxing to ask about passages where he was stuck, and they occasionally had light sparring matches.

Even after that, he received permission to leave the sect about once every six months to visit Tunnel No. 3, and from time to time he convened a central meeting of the Two Heavens Society to keep the organization going.

Fifteen years later.

Lee Hyun purchased an Origin-Opening Pill in Danxiao Immortal City for eight mid-grade spirit stones. It was far cheaper than a Foundation Establishment Pill, and he could obtain one without spending contribution points. Contribution points were better saved for studying inheritances.

After returning to Qingyu Ravine and giving both his body and divine sense ample rest, Lee Hyun swallowed the Origin-Opening Pill and began circulating the Primordial One-Qi Art.

Hummmm–

Lee Hyun calmly held the rest of the spiritual power throughout his body steady while focusing on the movement within his lower dantian.

The light of the Qi-Gathering Formation gradually brightened, rapidly drawing the surrounding spiritual qi into Lee Hyun’s body. The dense spiritual power rotating within his lower dantian surged into motion along a new flow.

Then, at a certain moment.

Thump!

Lee Hyun’s long robe billowed slightly.

He continued his qi circulation until the flow of spiritual power within his lower dantian stabilized, then slowly opened his eyes.

“It worked!”

Foundation Establishment Stage 4.

His lower dantian had finally reached mid-stage Foundation Establishment.

After taking some time to stabilize his realm, Lee Hyun inspected his body internally. Then he took a wooden board from his storage pouch and began carving in Korean onto it.

【Age: 1,479】

【Realm: Foundation Establishment Stage 4 (Lower Dantian)】

【Spiritual Power: 1,420 → 1,452】

【Cultivation Art: Primordial One-Qi Art (Foundation Establishment Section)】

【Techniques (Minor Attainment): Great Unity Heavenly Dipper Sword Art, Spirit-Refining Essentials, Condensed-Essence Grasping Hand, Flame-Threading Art, Spirit-Guarding Essence-Protecting Method, ...】

【Techniques (Major Attainment): Skywalking Art, ...】

Once he had finished carving everything, he floated the wooden board in front of himself and admired it with satisfaction.

His gaze lingered for a moment on the words beside Great Unity Heavenly Dipper Sword Art.

‘Can I really call it Minor Attainment? It might still be Novice... Well, whatever. It’s not like anyone is going to inspect my wooden board....’

...

A few days later, at the communal Alchemy Hall.

When Lee Hyun entered, Liu Zhengyuan, who had been processing medicinal ingredients, looked up.

“Senior Brother Li.”

He stopped halfway through his greeting.

“Could it be...?”

“I reached Stage 4.”

“Congratulations!”

Fang Jiyun, who was farther inside, also turned and examined Lee Hyun’s aura before smiling.

“You’ve finally reached the mid stage. Did you use an Origin-Opening Pill?”

“Yes. I bought one.”

“Good. Tell Master at this month’s lecture as well. Now that you’ve reached mid-stage Foundation Establishment, you can be considered a proper pillar of Yanxia Peak.”

“You praise me too highly.”

...

Several months later.

After Yanxia Peak’s lecture ended, a few people remained behind.

Lee Hyun, Fang Jiyun, and Eldest Senior Brother Song Qiming.

Song Qiming was a Foundation Establishment Stage 9 cultivator. After Tao Wenqian passed away, he had naturally taken on the role of Eldest Senior Brother while handling various affairs around Yanxia Peak.

He spoke little and rarely showed much expression, but he was good-natured.

Tan Yunsheng watched the doorway through which the disciples had left, then placed a jade slip on the table.

“Dongsan. I need you to take on an external assignment this time.”

Lee Hyun cupped his hands.

“What kind of assignment is it?”

“We’ve decided to send alchemy personnel to Haimen Port on the southwestern coast of the Great Yan Kingdom. Go there and take charge of one of the alchemy rooms.”

Lee Hyun recalled the name Haimen Port.

It was a coastal port reached by traveling southwest from Qinghe Valley’s former Mountain Gate. Located on the border between Anling Kingdom and the Great Yan Kingdom, it was a major trade hub frequented by many cultivators as well as mortals.

Song Qiming spread a map beside the jade slip.

“The cultivation forces in the area have established a joint base. Our sect and the Biluo Sect have both agreed to contribute supplies and personnel.”

Several points were marked along the coastline on the map, and red lines had been drawn over a few of them.

Lee Hyun asked,

“Is this related to demon beast activity?”

“It is.”

Tan Yunsheng nodded.

“The affected area has expanded since Qinghe Valley first reported it. For the past few years, the damage has spread beyond the sea routes to small coastal islands and harbors as well.”

Song Qiming pointed to the southern section of the map.

“As the Nanming Twelve-Sect Alliance expands its influence over the sea routes toward Lan Kingdom and Cang Kingdom, merchant groups and cultivators pushed out of those waters have been searching for other routes. More of them are venturing into distant waters than before and encountering demon beasts.”

“Has the reason for the increase in demon beasts been discovered?”

Tan Yunsheng shook his head.

“Not yet. Our sect’s Intelligence Hall is investigating as well, but so far, there is no evidence that the demon beast appearances are connected to the Nanming Twelve-Sect Alliance.”

The Intelligence Hall was responsible for gathering reports from disciples dispatched throughout the region and information brought in by merchant groups. When necessary, it also sent people out directly to verify whether rumors were true.

Tan Yunsheng pointed to several of the red markings on the map.

“If the smaller sects are unable to cope and withdraw, the number of available sea routes will shrink even further. Then people and goods will become concentrated along the remaining routes, and when an incident occurs there, the damage will be even greater.”

“It would affect the transportation of medicinal ingredients used by our sect as well.”

“For certain ingredients, yes. But there is a larger problem than a slight increase in medicinal ingredient prices. If the coastal bases collapse, the sea routes and harbors leading toward Kun Kingdom will become difficult to keep safe as well. If the kingdoms of the mundane world are devastated and their populations decline, we lose children we might otherwise take in as disciples. What good is it if a child is born with a spiritual root but dies before we ever find them?”

Tan Yunsheng continued.

“Still, we cannot exactly send our sect’s Golden Core Elders to every stretch of coastline.... What they need locally are alchemists capable of adjusting medicinal potency according to the properties of different demon-beast poisons. And if you go, Dongsan, given how skilled you are in combat, I’ll feel somewhat more at ease. The others on our peak are far more dependable at alchemy than they are in a fight. I worry they would panic and get themselves injured even when facing demon beasts at the same realm.”

Song Qiming added calmly,

“That is why we have also requested personnel from the Dharma Protector Court. We cannot expect you to bring the junior disciples along while handling both alchemy and protection yourselves.”

Lee Hyun picked up the jade slip and examined its contents.

The deployment period was initially set at two years, after which they would be rotated out depending on local conditions and whether replacement personnel were ready.

Song Qiming would lead the group, while Lee Hyun would be responsible for the alchemy work. It also seemed likely that one Foundation Establishment cultivator from the Dharma Protector Court would accompany them.

Chapter 64

Lee Hyun withdrew his divine sense from the jade slip.

“When do we depart?”

“We’re planning to leave ten days from now. Wrap up your current duties and make your preparations in the meantime.”

Song Qiming pointed at the jade slip.

“It isn’t written here, but the Outer Alchemy Court will assign six Qi Refining disciples to work under you. Most of them are experienced in alchemy and handling medicinal ingredients, so you shouldn’t have much trouble working on-site. The formation masters, talisman makers, and artifact refiners from the other peaks have already gone ahead and started working.”

“Will you be staying there as well, Eldest Senior Brother?”

“I plan to stay for about the first month. Once we’ve put the lodgings and alchemy rooms in order and coordinated the work with the local cultivators, I’ll have to return.”

...

After returning to Qingyu Ravine, Lee Hyun looked over the jade slip detailing the assignment once more.

Haimen Port was a harbor roughly sixty thousand li west-northwest of the Danxiao Range. It did not seem particularly far on the map, but actually traveling back and forth would take quite some time.

‘It’s not far from Tunnel No. 3, so that’s not bad. It should also make Two Heavens Society activities easier. But....’

He took the Danxiao Sect identity token bearing the name Li Dongsan from his storage pouch.

He had passed the Special Selection for Skilled Practitioners as a thirty-five-year-old rogue cultivator at Qi Refining Stage 8, received a Foundation Establishment Pill and successfully broken through at seventy-seven, and was now posing as a 117-year-old mid Foundation Establishment cultivator.

Considering the lifespan of a Foundation Establishment cultivator, it would not seem strange for him to remain another hundred years or so.

Still, he was not sure whether merely making himself look older would be enough.

Even if he disguised his appearance with various disguise methods, if his qi and blood and physical condition remained unchanged while his fellow disciples grew visibly old and frail, someone close to him might eventually find it suspicious.

‘Another fifty years at most would probably be best.’

There were still things he would regret giving up if he left immediately.

His Master knew a great deal and was earnest about teaching him. His fellow disciples were decent people as well, and once he finished his routine duties, he was mostly free to do as he pleased.

Finding another place like this would be a task in itself.

Still, he had acquired the pill recipes for Foundation Establishment Pills, Origin-Opening Pills, and Profundity-Penetrating Pills, and had already secured propagation stock for growing the essential medicinal ingredients. He was no longer in the same predicament as before, where leaving the sect would leave him at a loss as to where he could obtain what he needed for cultivation.

‘Demon beasts.... Something about the situation feels suspicious. There’s always a chance I might not make it back from this external assignment, so I should spend my contribution points before I go.’

Over the past fifteen years, Lee Hyun had steadily performed his routine alchemy and auxiliary duties, occasionally taking on additional commissions as well, so he had accumulated quite a few contribution points.

After considering what he ought to obtain with them, Lee Hyun rose from his seat.

...

The Inner Pavilion of the Scripture Pavilion.

While examining the list of inheritances, Lee Hyun stopped in front of a jade slip.

Primordial One-Qi Art: Golden Core Section

It required 320 contribution points to access.

‘So it really is here.’

Strangely enough, the Primordial One-Qi Art was not classified as a cultivation art for personal practice, but was stored alongside inheritances from various fields of craft.

That was because Primordial True Qi could change its nature with relatively few restrictions, allowing some of its mnemonic formulas and principles to be applied to crafts such as formations and talisman crafting.

It was not an inheritance monopolized by the sect, either, and almost no one tried to cultivate it directly, so the access cost was relatively low for a Golden Core cultivation art.

Lee Hyun handed his identity token to the cultivator overseeing the area.

“I would like to access this.”

...

Inside the inheritance chamber.

Lee Hyun pressed the jade slip to his forehead.

The opening section described key formulas for gathering and stabilizing the true essence of Foundation Establishment Great Perfection and harmonizing one’s essence, qi and spirit before Core Formation. It was followed by mnemonic formulas for Core Formation and cultivation methods to use after forming a golden core.

Finally, there was an extensive section dealing with the Primordial Body. Unlike the Foundation Establishment Section, however, it was extraordinarily difficult, making it nearly impossible to understand on the spot. The annotations would make him feel as though he was beginning to grasp a passage, only for the very next section to leave him completely lost again.

‘For now, I need to memorize it perfectly. Once I leave, I can inscribe the contents onto a blank jade slip.’

Lee Hyun calmly committed even the sections he could not understand to memory.

...

After leaving the inheritance chamber, Lee Hyun went through the list of craft inheritances again.

This time, he chose an inheritance titled Record of Marine Demon-Beast Materials.

It covered methods for identifying and processing poison sacs, bile, bones, shells, and other materials harvested from demon beasts found in the sea.

The access cost was only thirty contribution points, so it was not expensive.

Next, Lee Hyun examined the inheritances concerning formations.

The spirit fields in Tunnel No. 3 were continuing to expand. Moreover, the medicine age of the spirit plants was steadily increasing, so relying solely on the fact that they were hidden deep underground made him somewhat uneasy.

Nothing had happened thus far, but there was no guarantee that would remain true forever.

His gaze stopped on one entry.

Spirit-Concealing Formation

It was a Tier-2 formation used to conceal underground cultivation cave abodes.

Lee Hyun read the description beneath it.

It could suppress the fluctuations of spiritual power leaking from a residence, while the formation itself specialized in concealing its aura among the surrounding earth qi. The deeper it was installed within layers of bedrock, the more effective it became. Since it borrowed the power of the local earth vein and terrain, it also consumed almost no spirit stones.

‘This would be perfect for the tunnel.’

The access cost was 140 contribution points.

Lee Hyun asked the managing cultivator,

“Is there anywhere that sells the formation plate and formation devices for this formation?”

“Not within our sect, as far as I know. This formation is only used to hide cave abodes and has weak defensive capabilities, so there isn’t much demand for it. On top of that, its formation plate and formation devices have to be custom-made to suit the local terrain. I doubt anyone sells premade sets. The inheritance contains the manufacturing methods, so you will either have to study the formation yourself using those as reference or commission a formation master.”

Lee Hyun thought for a moment.

Would he have to commission a formation master to make the formation plate and formation devices?

Having someone else make them would mean explaining every detail of the tunnel’s structure and terrain, which made him uncomfortable. And if he made different kinds of tunnels in the future, he would have to ask a formation master all over again.

‘No one has ever discovered the tunnels so far, so it isn’t urgent. I’ll access it for research purposes first and learn how to make the formation plate and formation devices later.’

Lee Hyun held out his identity token.

“I’ll access this one as well.”

...

The inheritance of the Spirit-Concealing Formation covered everything from methods for examining bedrock layers to the materials and artifact-forging methods for the formation devices, along with techniques for engraving restrictions into the formation plate.

Its contents were so extensive and thorough that the contribution points did not feel wasted in the slightest.

Lee Hyun memorized every diagram and annotation without missing anything before leaving the Scripture Pavilion. After returning to Qingyu Ravine, he accurately inscribed the contents of Primordial One-Qi Art: Golden Core Section, Record of Marine Demon-Beast Materials, and Spirit-Concealing Formation onto blank jade slips.

It was the fifth day since they had departed from the Danxiao Sect.

A flying boat soared beneath the clouds.

Lee Hyun, Song Qiming, and Ge Tianxiong of the Dharma Protector Court were seated on the deck. The Qi Refining disciples were either resting inside the cabins or checking the supplies entrusted to them.

Ge Tianxiong was a Foundation Establishment Stage 7 cultivator. He looked to be in his mid-forties, with a sturdy build and a short beard.

Setting down his teacup, he said,

“I heard about Fellow Daoist Li from Fellow Daoist Xue.”

“Fellow Daoist Xue Jingxing?”

“That’s right. He seemed rather baffled when he heard I’d be accompanying you as an escort. He asked why anyone would bother escorting Fellow Daoist Li.... He told me you’re probably the most skilled fighter among the Danxiao Sect’s Foundation Establishment cultivators. Is that true?”

Lee Hyun scratched his head.

“Surely not. Fellow Daoist Xue must simply enjoy praising others.”

“Fellow Daoist Xue? He’s never praised me even once.......”

“....”

“Anyway, hearing that you’re skilled in combat certainly puts my mind at ease.”

...

A few days later.

An endless expanse of blue appeared ahead of the flying boat.

It was the sea.

Lee Hyun walked to the edge of the deck.

The mountain ranges on land gradually sank lower as they stretched toward the sea, and a large harbor lay nestled between them. Inside the long breakwaters, ships of every size were packed together.

Small fishing boats came and went beside enormous merchant vessels with their sails lowered. Long lines of wagons and laborers filled the docks, and cultivators riding magic tools could be seen moving above them.

On the low hills west of the harbor, a long wall built from black stone enclosed the area.

Thick pillars stood at regular intervals atop the wall facing the sea, and a faintly glowing formation barrier stretched between them.

Characters were engraved above the fortress gate.

Jinghai Fort.

Originally, it had been a small stone fort protecting the harbor, but several powers had expanded it together. Inside the walls stood dozens of halls, warehouses, and workshops, connected by roads wide enough for cargo wagons to pass through.

A tall watchtower rose on the side facing the harbor, and several cultivators beneath it were inspecting the wagons entering and leaving.

...

The flying boat descended onto a broad open ground inside Jinghai Fort.

Two Foundation Establishment cultivators from the Biluo Sect and the Danxiao Sect cultivators who had been dispatched ahead of them came to greet the party. After confirming one another’s identity tokens and assignment documents, Song Qiming headed toward an inner hall with them.

Five Foundation Establishment cultivators from the Danxiao Sect were already staying there.

There was one formation master, one talisman maker, and one artifact refiner from various peaks, as well as one cultivator from the Dharma Protector Court responsible for security and escorts. The remaining person belonged to the External Affairs Court and was tasked with coordinating personnel and supplies while communicating with the local powers.

Including Lee Hyun and Ge Tianxiong, there would be seven Foundation Establishment cultivators stationed there permanently.

The Biluo Sect had also sent six Foundation Establishment cultivators. They had not sent any alchemists, but they did have cultivators capable of repairing formations, making talismans, and maintaining magic tools. Including the disciples assisting in each field and the personnel assigned to security, escort, and transport duties, the two sects alone had sent nearly two hundred people.

There were also cultivators from local minor sects and hired laborers staying there.

Lee Hyun led the Qi Refining disciples in unloading supplies from the boat.

“Do not break the seals on the medicinal ingredients. Move them to the inner storehouse as they are.”

“Yes, Martial Uncle Li!”

The disciples hurried into action.

The hall assigned to their group was located in the eastern part of Jinghai Fort.

A signboard reading Pill Refining Pavilion hung above the main entrance. Inside were four alchemy chambers, a Medicinal Ingredient Storehouse, and a spacious workroom for preparing medicinal ingredients. Beyond a small courtyard in the rear stood a row of rooms for the cultivators to live in.

Lee Hyun’s residence was a detached building with its own courtyard, situated farther inside.

The sea was visible through the windows, and the interior had a bedroom as well as a separate study furnished with bookshelves. An adjoining stone chamber even contained a Qi-Gathering Formation for personal cultivation.

‘Not bad.’

...

The next few days were somewhat busy.

First, Lee Hyun installed the Tier-2 mid-grade pill furnace and formation devices brought from the sect, then checked the quantity and condition of everything delivered to the Medicinal Ingredient Storehouse. He also examined the pill recipes previously used locally and the records concerning demon-beast poison.

The formation master and artifact refiner who had arrived earlier inspected the burners and restrictions connected to the pill furnace. There was no earth fire available here, so the burners had to be ignited by inserting spirit stones into their formations, or else an alchemist had to use a fire-element technique personally.

After testing the heat, Lee Hyun designated areas for preparing medicinal ingredients and storing completed pills.

An elderly Qi Refining cultivator who had been working locally handed Lee Hyun a thick ledger.

“This is the current backlog. Most of it consists of Detoxification Pills and Blood-Staunching Pills, along with a smaller amount of pills that replenish qi and blood.”

The elderly cultivator led Lee Hyun into a separate stone chamber.

The jade caskets arranged on the stone table contained poison sacs, dried clots of blood, broken demon-beast bones, and other materials. Each casket had a slip of paper attached recording where and when it had been obtained, along with the demon beast’s appearance.

“We recognize some of the species, but others are ones we’ve only encountered recently. We were afraid that if we processed them recklessly on our own, we might ruin the medicinal ingredients....”

“You did well.”

...

After a few days, Lee Hyun had more or less organized the work under his responsibility.

The local alchemists continued making the pills they were familiar with, while the Danxiao Sect disciples divided the backlog and inspection work among themselves.

The Tier-1 alchemists who had worked in the Outer Alchemy Court were generally capable, as one would expect from disciples of a great sect.

Only Tier-2 demon-beast materials, specimens that were difficult to process using existing methods, and pill recipes that required adjustments to their formulation were brought to Lee Hyun.

As for demon-beast materials he had never seen before, he could compare them against local records and experiment with small quantities until he found the proper method of processing them. No one pressured him to produce an immediate answer. The Foundation Establishment cultivators of the Biluo Sect and Danxiao Sect were effectively kings here, so the local merchant groups and minor sects could not casually rush them.

As long as he met the assigned quota, the rest of his time was his own.

Even so, Lee Hyun intended to do what he could as a Tier-2 alchemist for the local cultivators and mortals.

...

About fifteen days later.

The six disciples gathered in the medicinal-preparation room were staring at the stone table.

In front of Lee Hyun lay a poison sac taken from a demon beast he had never seen before. Fine blue veins crisscrossed its surface like a net, while tiny bubbles continuously formed in the mucus inside.

One disciple cautiously spoke.

“Martial Uncle Li, we have no idea how to process this ourselves.”

Lee Hyun read through the processing notes the disciple had written, examined the poison sac, and then took it into the alchemy chamber.

A low, broad pill furnace rested atop the stone platform.

Lee Hyun first activated the furnace’s restrictions. Then, with a sweep of his hand, the poison sac floated into the air. It split open above the furnace, allowing the thick blue liquid inside to pour down.

Lee Hyun moved his fingers while examining the qi within it using the Aura-Reading Art and Poison-Discerning Art.

Whoosh–

One of the three divided flames unraveled into fine flame threads. The flame threads crossed over one another until they densely covered the top of the pill furnace, while the remaining two flames entered the furnace and began heating the poisonous liquid.

The Qi Refining disciples could only stare openmouthed at the wondrous technique they were seeing for the first time.

As the poisonous liquid swelled, a blue mist rose from it. The moment the mist tried to escape the furnace, the flame curtain linked to the restrictions curved inward and forced it back inside.

A short while later, the material inside the furnace separated into three portions: a clear liquid, a sticky mass, and blackened powder.

Lee Hyun poured the refined liquid and the sticky mass into separate jade bottles.

He examined the remaining powder once more. After confirming that the Poison-Discerning Art detected no lingering reaction from it, he withdrew his hand.

“Seal these two bottles for research. There is no toxic qi left in the powder, so it can be discarded.”

One disciple stood with his mouth open for a moment before bowing his head.

“That was incredible. But may I ask the name of that technique you used to divide the flames into several streams? Could we access it at the Scripture Pavilion as well?”

“Ah, this?”

Lee Hyun shaped the flame above his palm into a crane and made it flap its wings, drawing exclamations from the Qi Refining disciples.

“It’s called the Flame-Threading Art. Only disciples of Yanxia Peak are permitted to learn it. You won’t find it in the Scripture Pavilion.”

“Yanxia Peak....”

“Do not try imitating it recklessly. Fire-element techniques have considerable killing power.”

“Yes!”

The disciples carried the jade bottles out

Someone spoke quietly dozens of zhang away, but Lee Hyun could hear them with his divine sense.

“He blocked the pill furnace with a curtain of flame so the poisonous mist couldn’t spread outside. That really was an incredible technique....”

“But how is he already so good at processing demon-beast poison when he’s only been here a short while? Are all Tier-2 alchemists like that?”

As Lee Hyun listened, he purged the lingering traces clinging to his body with the Detoxification Art and Cleansing Art.

In truth, Lee Hyun was exceptionally skilled at detoxification.

After all, the Bone-Rot Flowers, Purple Poison Orchids, and Yin Soul Grass he had handled for over a thousand years were all poisonous medicinal plants. Of course, he still had to learn the properties of unfamiliar demon-beast poisons from scratch. But separating only the toxic qi little by little while preserving the medicinal potency had long since become second nature to him.

...

When Lee Hyun reached the courtyard in front of his residence, he found a small jade casket sitting on the table. Opening it revealed several round pieces of white flesh inside.

“What is this?”

A disciple in the courtyard answered.

“It’s the meat of an Azure-Shelled Clam, a Tier-1 spirit creature. The merchant group that delivered medicinal ingredients today left some for us. Everyone at the Pill Refining Pavilion shared it, and we set aside your portion, Martial Uncle.”

Lee Hyun picked up a piece with his chopsticks.

After using the Aura-Reading Art and Poison-Discerning Art to check it for poison or any sinister qi, he put it in his mouth. The flesh was tender, with a sweet taste lingering at the end.

“Delicious.”

“I’ll get more the next time I go out to the harbor.”

“There’s no need. Finish your assigned work first, then get some rest.”

“Yes.”

After the disciple withdrew, Lee Hyun leaned back against a long chair.

When he opened his spirit-insect pouch, a small ball of golden fur crawled out. The fuzzbee prodded the clam meat on the table, then, apparently uninterested, crawled into his sleeve. Lee Hyun put the fuzzbee back into the spirit-insect pouch and took a popular novel from his storage pouch.

‘I’ve got it easy.’

He ate another piece of clam meat and turned the page.

About a month after their arrival, Eldest Senior Brother Song Qiming returned to the main sect after finishing the work of coordinating their duties.

Before leaving, Song Qiming called Lee Hyun aside.

“If something happens that you cannot handle, report it to the main sect. There is no need to try solving everything with only the people stationed here.”

“Yes.”

Even after Song Qiming departed, the Pill Refining Pavilion continued operating smoothly.

The demon-beast materials whose processing methods Lee Hyun had already organized were handled by the juniors, who added their own annotations to the records as they worked. Only unfamiliar specimens were set aside separately.

Ge Tianxiong would occasionally stop by for tea on his way back from patrolling the area around the harbor or escorting a convoy.

...

A few days later.

Shiwan Market, northeast of Haimen Port.

The cultivator market sat among low, rocky hills. Rogue cultivators traveling to and from Haimen Port came there to buy and sell goods or rest for a while. Old shops lined both sides of the road, while stalls in the open spaces displayed jumbled piles of dried medicinal ingredients, chipped magic tools, demon-beast bones, and hides.

It had originally been a small market in decline, but the recent appearances of Tier-2 demon beasts and the frequent passage of Foundation Establishment cultivators had gradually begun breathing life back into it.

The Dongshun General Store, tucked deep within an alley, was one of the least conspicuous shops there. Cracked medicine mortars and empty jars were piled in front of the entrance, and an elderly clerk dozed beneath a faded signboard.

In the underground stone chamber beneath it, masked cultivators had gathered.

Soon, the floor rippled, and a cultivator in purple robes rose from below. All seven people immediately stood.

“We pay our respects to the Society Head.”

From beneath the Badger mask, Lee Hyun’s gaze swept over them.

Compared to the time a Tier-2 gu warrior from the Black Sun Office of Qianyang Kingdom had infiltrated under the guise of Black Sable, every member attending the central gathering had since been replaced. Though the same masks remained, the voices and mannerisms were different. The previous members had either died of old age or retired after handing their duties over to successors.

Lee Hyun sat in the seat of honor.

“Report.”

First came reports concerning vein seats and contact points.

Afterward, they discussed exchanges and transactions involving various magic tools, talismans, pills, and other goods.

Lee Hyun allowed the members to trade freely among themselves and did not involve himself. His realm and skills had risen considerably, and he now had access to the Danxiao Sect’s various resources, so the items handled by these members were almost entirely useless to him.

The rogue cultivators around this area who made use of vein seats and residual-vein pockets were mostly Qi Refining cultivators. Those at Foundation Establishment or above were rare.

‘Should I raise the caliber of the membership? Well, the information gathered by members moving around in different places is still useful....’

After various matters were discussed, the member wearing the Red Crab mask spoke last.

“Society Head. What do you think about establishing a useful connection in Haimen Port?”

“With whom?”

“I hear there is a Tier-2 alchemist dispatched there from the Danxiao Sect. His name is Li Dongsan.”

“And?”

“If we could recruit him, I believe it would greatly benefit the Two Heavens Society members nearby. With your abilities, Society Head, recruiting a Foundation Establishment cultivator should be nothing.”

Black Crow snapped at him.

“Idiot. He’s a Foundation Establishment alchemist from a great sect. Do you have any idea what could happen if we brought someone like that into the Two Heavens Society?”

“Hmph. The depths of our Two Heavens Society are endless, and our influence spans several cultivation nations. You’re the newcomer here, so it seems you simply don’t understand. Perhaps even the Danxiao Sect is insignificant compared to the Two Heavens Society’s true power.”

Lee Hyun stared gravely at Red Crab.

‘The Two Heavens Society is not that powerful....’

Lee Hyun looked back over his past actions, wondering whether he had cultivated too much of an air of mystery around the organization, but Red Crab seemed to be an exception.

“Red Crab, do not recklessly act in the name of the Two Heavens Society. Our depths may be boundless, but that does not mean they are yours to wield.”

“My apologies.”

“Do not attempt to recruit cultivators from great sects. And report any new developments concerning the nearby demon beasts, Qianyang Kingdom, or anything else of note.”

“Yes!”

Fifteen days later.

Ge Tianxiong came to find Lee Hyun while he was studying the formation inscriptions of the Spirit-Concealing Formation in the rear courtyard of the Pill Refining Pavilion.

He held a fragment of blue shell in one hand.

“Fellow Daoist Li, could you take a look at this?”

Lee Hyun accepted the piece of shell.

Its edges were charred black, while dark green mucus had dried along the inner surface.

“The toxic qi is quite strong.”

“I heard a merchant ship was attacked yesterday along one of the nearby sea routes. The attackers were Tier-2 demon beasts called Ironback Sea Crocodiles. Some local Foundation Establishment cultivators nearby tried to drive them off once, but they failed.”

Ge Tianxiong took a map from his storage pouch.

A chain of small islands lay a little over two hundred li southwest of Haimen Port. A red mark had been drawn over the narrow waterway between them.

“They’ve settled around here.”

“How many are there?”

“Three have been confirmed. The largest one was apparently around late Tier 2. Their poisonous mist makes them difficult to approach, and if they get cornered, they dive underwater.”

“Are you going to subjugate them?”

“I’m planning to go tomorrow. One of the local Foundation Establishment cultivators who went there before will guide us, and two Biluo Sect cultivators have agreed to join us in hunting them. Would you come with us as well, Fellow Daoist Li? It would help if you could examine the toxic qi. And of course, if we could borrow those sword skills Xue Jingxing told me about, that would be even better.”

“Very well.”

...

The next morning.

Five Foundation Establishment cultivators left Haimen Port and headed southwest.

The coastal cliffs and small harbors gradually receded behind them.

The once-clear seawater darkened into a deep navy blue.

The cultivator guiding them pointed ahead.

“There.”

A half-destroyed merchant ship was wedged between two small islands.

Then a dark blue-black armored back rose from beneath it, lifting the enormous hull to one side.

Crack–

With the sound of the ship’s bottom splitting apart, an enormous snout emerged above the surface of the water.

Chapter 65

Planks torn from the bottom of the ship spilled across the surface of the sea. An Ironback Sea Crocodile thrust its head through the shattered hull and opened its jaws, spewing dark green poison mist mixed with seawater.

"Spread out!"

At Ge Tianxiong's shout, two more columns of water erupted behind the merchant ship. Two more Ironback Sea Crocodiles emerged from the spray.

Lee Hyun was about to check their positions when he felt a slight movement inside his spirit-insect pouch. The fuzzbees, which had been quiet until moments ago, had suddenly grown restless.

'Hm?'

Before he had time to wonder why, the green poison mist came rolling toward them on the wind.

When the mist touched the body-protecting spirit light of a local cultivator who had moved ahead, the surface of the spirit light immediately began to corrode with a hiss. As the man hurriedly retreated, several streams of flame sprang from Lee Hyun's fingertips.

Fwoosh–

The long flame threads crossed through the air, forming a loose net. The poison mist thinned for a moment when it collided with the flames, but the green fog, heavy with seawater, kept surging in behind it.

Rather than forcing the net of fire to spread wider, Lee Hyun thrust his left hand forward.

Boom!

The broad Qi Sphere Barrier violently swept away the poison mist and droplets of seawater. For a moment, the view between the group and the demon beasts cleared.

"Now!"

A Biluo Sect cultivator shouted the word and hurled a jade-colored ring. The ring expanded in midair and wrapped around the neck and forelegs of the largest Ironback Sea Crocodile at once. As the beast twisted its body in resistance, fierce sparks flew from the ring's surface.

Another Biluo Sect cultivator sent several flying swords at the eye of a smaller crocodile.

Clang!

The sword tips bounced off its tough eyelid, but while the creature's eye was closed, a local cultivator circled around and slashed its foreleg.

Ge Tianxiong descended straight toward the large Ironback Sea Crocodile. A saber light nearly ten zhang (about 33 m) long shot from his thick saber and crashed down onto its armored back with a thunderous roar.

Craack–

Fragments of shattered armor flew in every direction. The crocodile violently shook its head, tearing free of the jade-colored ring, then slapped the surface of the sea with its tail and twisted toward the water.

But Lee Hyun's sword light pierced through the curtain of water it had thrown up.

Swoosh!

The first sword light cut off its escape route, and the second mercilessly pierced the softer joint between the plates of its back armor.

As the Ironback Sea Crocodile's body listed to one side, Ge Tianxiong's saber fell once more onto its shattered back armor.

Crunch!

With the sound of bones breaking, blood and green fluid sprayed into the air.

Once the largest beast fell, the other two did not last long.

One tried to flee underwater, only to be overturned belly-up by the combined assault of the Biluo Sect cultivators. The other attempted to burrow beneath the ruined merchant ship, but Lee Hyun's sword light severed both of its forelegs.

Ge Tianxiong's final descending blow split its head open.

The surroundings fell silent.

...

Three demon-beast corpses floated on the surface of the sea. As shattered planks and pieces of dark blue armor drifted among the waves, the group began moving the corpses onto a broad nearby reef.

Lee Hyun was hauling one of them up when another faint vibration came from his spirit-insect pouch.

Buzz. Buzzz.

'Why have they been acting like this since earlier? Could there be spirit insects inside these demon beasts?'

Lee Hyun stepped back several paces and fired sword light at the Ironback Sea Crocodile's belly. Its abdomen split open, spilling hot blood and entrails.

Lee Hyun used the Qi Sphere Barrier to push away the splattering filth and fishy stench, then used the Condensed-Essence Grasping Hand to pull the incision apart.

Ge Tianxiong came over and peered inside.

"Is there anything useful? That one over there didn't have a demon core...."

"Let's check the venom sac first."

Lee Hyun alternated between the Aura-Reading Art and Poison-Discerning Art. It was not difficult to distinguish the organs where toxic qi had gathered densely, and their shapes mostly matched what he had read in the Record of Marine Demon-Beast Materials.

However, something he had never seen in the jade slip was attached beneath the venom sac.

It was a small pouch. From within its thin membrane came faint fluctuations of spiritual power distinct from the demon beast's residual demon power.

He carefully cut through the surrounding flesh, revealing a long, pale insect.

Threadlike tissues extended from its head and tail into the demon beast's body. Whenever the insect twisted, the strands squirmed along with it.

"A parasitic spirit insect?"

Ge Tianxiong's expression changed. Hearing him, the other cultivators gathered around the corpse as well.

Lee Hyun carefully examined the spirit insect's aura. Perhaps because its host was dead, its spiritual power was rapidly weakening, but it was unquestionably a Tier-2 spirit insect.

'It's somewhat similar to the Life-Bound Gu of Qianyang Kingdom....'

He thought of the Meridian-Linking Jade Silkworm and the spirit insects he had brought back from beneath the Anling Kingdom's royal palace, but its appearance was not exactly the same as any of them.

One of the Biluo Sect cultivators pointed to the flesh beside the spirit insect.

"It doesn't seem to have gotten in there naturally."

Two tiny silver needles were embedded there. A faint pattern ran along the fine thread connecting the needles.

Without touching the needles, Lee Hyun cut away the surrounding tissue along with them. He placed the entire piece into a jade casket, affixed a sealing talisman, then looked over the remaining corpses.

"We should inspect the others as well."

...

Similar traces were found in the other two. The spirit insect in one had been sliced apart by sword qi, while the other had already stopped moving.

Even so, the tissues connecting them to the demon beasts' bodies and the tiny silver needles remained intact.

Ge Tianxiong placed the three jade caskets side by side and stared at them for some time.

"I've heard that the gu warriors of Qianyang Kingdom carry spirit insects inside their bodies."

A Biluo Sect cultivator nodded.

"I was thinking the same thing. But I don't know whether they use the same method on demon beasts."

Lee Hyun looked away from the sealed jade caskets.

"For now, I think we should send them back to the sect headquarters. We can't hastily conclude that this is Qianyang Kingdom's doing."

"Let's do that."

The group recorded the location where the beasts had been captured, their appearance, and the properties of their poison mist.

After returning to Jinghai Fort, they handed the jade caskets and records over to the cultivator in charge at the External Affairs Court.

They decided to sell the remaining demon-beast corpses to a local merchant guild.

After selling all three corpses, Lee Hyun's share came to thirty mid-grade spirit stones.

He briefly considered taking some of the bones to use in making bone puppets, but the cultivators were already discussing a price for the corpses as a whole, so he did not go out of his way to ask for them.

After fighting Tier-2 demon beasts himself, he felt that it would not be particularly difficult to hunt them alone whenever he needed bones.

...

A little over a month later, word arrived that the sect headquarters had received the specimens and records.

However, no separate instructions concerning the matter were issued to the cultivators at Haimen Port. Nor did they learn what the sect headquarters had discovered.

...

A few days later.

Clouds hung low over the sea. Black reefs stretched in a long chain among the waves, and not a single ship could be seen beyond them.

Lee Hyun landed on the highest reef.

As his divine sense swept through the cracks between the submerged rocks, it caught a long, thick presence.

'Down there?'

He flicked a finger, sending a small ball of fire between the rocks. A moment later, an explosion rang out and a column of water shot upward. Beneath it, a body covered in blue scales writhed.

A thick sea serpent raised its head. It was an Azure-Scaled Sea Serpent.

According to the Record of Marine Demon-Beast Materials, it was a demon beast with sturdy vertebrae and scales that could be used as materials for magic tools. The spiritual pressure coming from the creature before him had reached the late Tier-2 level.

"It's fairly large."

The Azure-Scaled Sea Serpent opened its jaws, and a compressed stream of water shot out at tremendous speed.

Swoosh!

Immediately after Lee Hyun stepped aside, the upper portion of the reef where he had been standing was sliced clean away.

The water pressure was formidable, but Lee Hyun had no intention of giving the beast time to catch its breath.

He kicked off the reef and rapidly closed the distance. The Profound Gate Sword traced an arc through his hand, and the sword light split gracefully, throwing the Azure-Scaled Sea Serpent's senses into disarray.

Crack-crack-crack!

The flashing sword light split apart the sea serpent's tough scales. The instant it thrashed in pain and struck the surface of the sea, Lee Hyun had already reached the side of its neck.

Slice–

Finely honed sword qi slipped smoothly through the gaps between its vertebrae.

Thud!

The enormous head plunged into the seawater first, followed by the body, which struck the surface with a tremendous splash while spraying blood.

'The swordsmanship I'm used to really is more comfortable.'

Lee Hyun put away the Profound Gate Sword and reviewed the brief exchange. For now, the One Ultimate, Six Swords he had honed over many years was still far more familiar than the Great Unity Heavenly Dipper Sword Art.

Just then, the fuzzbees inside his spirit-insect pouch began moving restlessly. Lee Hyun hauled the Azure-Scaled Sea Serpent's corpse onto the reef and examined it, eventually detecting a spirit insect beneath its neck.

This one also contained an insect connected to the body through flesh and thin strands of tissue. Two small silver needles were embedded beside it as well.

He removed the tissue to which the spirit insect was attached along with the surrounding flesh and sealed it in a jade casket. He then took out six flying swords and began dismantling the Azure-Scaled Sea Serpent's corpse.

He first collected the bile and usable scales, then separated and sealed the parts whose toxicity and medicinal potency needed to be examined individually.

Once the remaining flesh had been stripped away, a thick, long spine was revealed.

The pale, solid bones were permeated with resilient demon power. Even scraping them with a blade left only a shallow scratch.

'These bones are good.'

They also matched the qualities described as desirable in the Profound Yin White Bone True Scripture. Properly processed, there was more than enough material to make an entire puppet. Lee Hyun sorted and collected the bones according to their intended uses, washed the traces from the reef with seawater, and left.

After that, he continued making occasional trips out to sea while avoiding other people's notice. After several hunts, a sizable pile of Tier-2 demon-beast bones had accumulated inside his storage pouch.

Not every Tier-2 demon beast carried a spirit insect. Even so, if he hunted several, he would usually find one or two, and each time Lee Hyun collected the spirit insects.

...

Tunnel No. 3.

When Lee Hyun took out the jade caskets, balls of golden fur crowded around his arms and shoulders. Their buzzing grew noticeably louder before he had even finished undoing the seals.

Buzzz–

"Wait."

Lee Hyun washed a stone bowl with the Spirit Rain Art, then placed the spirit insects inside.

Those still alive twisted their bodies and tried to crawl toward the edge, but there was no escaping the fuzzbees circling the bowl.

As the three existing Tier-2 fuzzbees approached first, Lee Hyun stopped them.

"Don't eat everything yourselves. Share."

Squeak squeak!

The moment he moved his hand away, the small golden swarm descended upon the stone bowl.

A short while later, the bowl was spotless. The fuzzbees, their bellies swollen round, landed one by one on the earthen floor nearby. A few simply sprawled out and went to sleep.

Lee Hyun examined their auras one after another. There was no noticeable change yet.

'I'll have to keep bringing more.'

He then inspected the spirit fields, water tanks, bamboo supply pipes, and other facilities before taking out Bonefuzz No. 1.

Lee Hyun examined the bone puppet's shoulders and chest. There was an issue that had bothered him ever since he first placed a fuzzbee inside it.

Was having a fuzzbee operate a Six-Armed Bone Puppet with six arms and two legs really the best approach?

'Maybe it's about time I changed its shape.'

...

A few days later, a Foundation Establishment artifact refiner stationed at Jinghai Fort came to the Pill Refining Pavilion.

He opened the jade bottle Lee Hyun handed him, examined the contents, and nodded.

"This will be more than enough. It's much clearer than the last batch."

"Warm it first, then use it a little at a time. If you pour it all on at once, you may damage the surface of the spirit material."

"Understood. You've saved me some trouble."

The jade bottle contained a liquid Lee Hyun had produced by refining demon-beast venom. The artifact refiner intended to use it while processing materials for a magic tool.

As Lee Hyun watched him put away the jade bottle, he asked several questions that had been troubling him about joining spirit materials and connecting restrictions.

One question led to another, as each answer raised a new doubt. The conversation grew somewhat lengthy, but the artifact refiner did not seem to mind, since it also gave him a chance to confirm the properties of the material he intended to use.

After that, whenever Lee Hyun spent time with formation masters or talisman makers, he also took opportunities to ask questions and discuss formation inscriptions, talisman inscriptions, restrictions, and related matters.

"Fellow Daoist Li, you've had quite a lot of questions lately."

"There were parts I couldn't understand just by reading on my own."

"We ask you plenty about alchemy ourselves, so it benefits us both."

...

After returning to his quarters, Lee Hyun took out the jade slips containing the Profound Yin White Bone True Scripture, Introductory Guide to Soul Stone Inscription, and Spirit-Concealing Formation. Beside them, he opened the book containing Guo Zhenming's annotations.

Reading them again while recalling the explanations he had heard from artifact refiners, formation masters, and talisman makers, he gradually began to understand passages he had previously memorized without even knowing what they meant.

'At this point, I think I could modify Bonefuzz No. 1 or build a new Bonefuzz based on its structure....'

Producing the formation devices and formation plate for the Spirit-Concealing Formation was still beyond him. He would need to become both a Tier-2 formation master and an artifact refiner for that, and such a goal remained far out of reach.

...

Tunnel No. 3.

Lee Hyun laid out the demon-beast bones.

The clear, gentle Primordial True Qi gathered over his hand gradually took on a gloomy quality before transforming into Profound Yin White Bone True Qi.

As he wrapped the bones in that true qi and refined them, faint smoke rose from their surfaces. The remaining impurities fell away, and the rough surfaces slowly became smooth.

Following the method recorded in the inheritance, Lee Hyun cut the bone materials and shaped the surfaces that would be joined together.

...

Three months later, in Tunnel No. 3 once again.

Bonefuzz No. 1 stood before Lee Hyun, looking completely different from the Six-Armed Bone Puppet it had once been.

The body that had once stood upright like a human had been replaced by a rounded torso about two chi (about 66 cm) long. A low head was attached to the front, and three pairs of legs extended from either side of its body.

The puppet looked just like a wingless fuzzbee!

Replicating the beating of wings, however, was difficult. For flight, Lee Hyun intended to adapt the existing restrictions and draw power from spirit stones instead.

The fuzzbee inside pressed itself against the bone plate beside the soul stone. A moment later, the joints began clicking, and the legs moved one after another.

At first, Bonefuzz took cautious steps one at a time. Before long, it began walking across the cavern.

Unlike when it had controlled the Six-Armed Bone Puppet, its movements were extremely nimble!

"Oh...."

Bonefuzz stopped in front of Lee Hyun and raised one of its forelegs. From inside its torso came a cry that sounded almost boastful.

Squeak squeak!

Lee Hyun smiled and nodded.

"Does this body suit you better?"

Squeak!

...

Once the first modification succeeded, the next projects became much easier. Over the following few months, Lee Hyun built Bonefuzz No. 2 and Bonefuzz No. 3 in succession.

During that time, the fuzzbees also began to change. As he continued feeding them the spirit insects he brought back from each demon-beast hunt, one fuzzbee after another began showing signs of breaking through to Tier 2!

Like the three that had broken through before them, they dug small holes in the cavern walls and disappeared inside. When they finally emerged after being out of sight for some time, both the glow surrounding their fur and the aura emanating from their bodies had changed.

The fuzzbees that became Tier-2 spirit insects grew considerably stronger.

However, there was a limit to how much spiritual power their tiny bodies could contain, so they were still nowhere near strong enough to play a major role against Foundation Establishment cultivators, Tier-2 gu warriors, or demon beasts.

Even so, there were plenty of uses for them. For one thing, there were now more fuzzbees capable of controlling Bonefuzz puppets.

They would also be a great help if Tier-2 spirit insects ever invaded the spirit fields.

...

By the time his assignment was nearing its end, the number of Tier-2 fuzzbees had already surpassed fifty. Along one side of the cavern stood ten bone puppets in a row, from Bonefuzz No. 1 through Bonefuzz No. 10.

He could obtain bones through hunting, but soul stones and the spirit materials required for inscriptions did not simply appear on their own.

Between purchasing the materials he lacked and remaking failed components, a considerable portion of the spirit stones he had earned from hunting had been spent.

When Lee Hyun opened the covers on the puppets' torsos, the fuzzbees swarmed toward them. Those that made it inside settled into position, while the ones that arrived too late circled the open covers.

Click. Click-click.

The ten bone puppets rose one after another. Watching a line of identical bone puppets move together gave them something of the grandeur of an army!

Lee Hyun watched them with satisfaction for a while before turning toward the fuzzbees still waiting for their turn.

"They do look impressive... but they cost too many spirit stones."

He held out his hand, and the fuzzbees that had failed to secure a Bonefuzz landed on his arm.

"I've thought about it, and making one for every single one of you is a little much. All the spirit stones I earn hunting demon beasts would disappear just like that...."

Squeak squeak!

The fuzzbees cried out in unison. Lee Hyun instructed the ones already riding inside the puppets to give up their places after a set amount of time. For now, they had no choice but to compromise by taking turns.

Once he had built up a reasonable number, Lee Hyun's attention shifted to Bonefuzz's performance. Walking and running had become fairly natural, but aside from ramming enemies with their bodies or legs, the puppets had no proper means of attack.

'Should I equip them with magic tools?'

He quickly shook his head.

'Giving every Bonefuzz its own magic tool seems excessive. It would be better to build in a technique that can hit an enemy from a distance. If I can apply the same spell formula to multiple Bonefuzz puppets, that should reduce the work later on.'

Lee Hyun recorded the idea and decided to devote more time to researching it.

...

Then, one day.

Masked cultivators gathered in the underground stone chamber beneath Dongshun General Store in Shiwan Market. Wearing his Badger mask, Lee Hyun sat in the seat of honor and listened to their reports.

The topics varied widely, from relocating vein seats and admitting new members to rising prices in certain cultivator markets. Lee Hyun asked additional questions whenever necessary.

'The south will only become more turbulent... and even considering the day I eventually leave the Danxiao Sect, it would be better to establish a foothold in the north ahead of time.'

Once the reports were finished, Lee Hyun spoke.

"From now on, our Two Heavens Society will expand its influence northward. Establish contact bases there as well, and look for ways to increase both our membership and the number of vein seats."

Black Crow raised his head.

"Do you mean the Xuan Kingdom?"

"Starting there would be fine, and you may also investigate other nations farther north. Compared to the forces the Two Heavens Society will one day encompass, our current scale is only the beginning. You will have to become its great pillars."

Lee Hyun slowly looked around at the members.

"Approach this as though you are laying the foundation for an empire where even your descendants will serve the Two Heavens Society and many families will live for generations. Plan and carry out the details according to your individual circumstances."

At that moment, Red Crab spoke as if he had been waiting for the chance.

"So the time has finally come. I knew such an order would be given one day. It must mean the Two Heavens Society has already grown so large in the south that there is nowhere left for us to expand."

'Hm?'

"In that case, we'll need to establish ourselves in the north as well so we don't fall behind the other existing members. Thank you for giving us this opportunity."

"Of course. There is no need for further expansion southward at present. But even as our influence grows, our chain of commands and reports must never be severed. Manage the organizations under your charge properly, and do not neglect the rules for maintaining secrecy."

Black Crow examined the map spread before him.

"I know several members who travel to the Xuan Kingdom for trade. I'll use them to begin expanding into a few cultivator markets there."

"Do so."

"However, it will take time to establish ourselves."

Lee Hyun nodded.

"There is no need to rush. Whether it takes ten years or a hundred."

The members cupped their hands in unison.

"We shall carry out your command."

Two years had passed since Lee Hyun was dispatched to Haimen Port.

When he first discovered spirit insects resembling Life-Bound Gu inside the Ironback Sea Crocodiles, he had wondered whether it might lead to friction with Qianyang Kingdom.

However, nothing else occurred that required Lee Hyun's involvement. The sect headquarters remained silent.

When the replacement alchemist arrived from the sect headquarters, Lee Hyun went through the Medicinal Ingredient Storehouse, pill furnaces, ledgers, and records of the Pill Refining Pavilion with him as part of the handover.

On the day before his departure, he held a modest drinking gathering with the Foundation Establishment cultivators he had befriended, sharing spirit wine with them.

...

Ten days later, Danxiao Sect.

Accounting and reports began as soon as he arrived.

Once he finished, he climbed halfway up Yanxia Peak. Halls and small pavilions appeared here and there among the ancient pines, and Tan Yunsheng greeted him while seated on a broad stone terrace.

"Dongsan, you've worked hard. Rest for about seven days first."

"Thank you."

After his rest, Lee Hyun returned to his familiar routine.

Once he completed his regular alchemy duties, he cultivated his cultivation art in Qingyu Ravine and studied various arts whenever he had time. He also continued wrestling with the problems in the Puppet Art that he had been unable to solve at Haimen Port.

Occasionally, he was dispatched to Haimen Port again. Each time, he participated in demon-beast subjugations and performed his alchemy duties, but at least while Lee Hyun was there, no particularly major incidents occurred.

Meanwhile, the Two Heavens Society gradually expanded northward.

In the beginning, even though it operated through separate cells, Lee Hyun, as society head, had known most of its members. But as each organization admitted new members, who then formed smaller organizations of their own, that began to change.

Now, there were quite a few members whose names and areas of operation were all he ever received in reports. Rather than trying to personally keep track of every lower-ranking member, Lee Hyun focused on ensuring that communication with the leaders of each organization remained intact.

As attendance at the central meetings increased, he stopped gathering everyone at once and instead divided them into several groups for their reports.

The rules and operating procedures that had been refined through trial and error since the days of the Qutian Society proved enormously helpful in keeping the Two Heavens Society together.

The greater its influence became, the more rules its members had to follow. Yet thanks to those rules, members who had never even seen one another's faces could operate across different regions while remaining connected as a single organization.

It was the forty-eighth year since Lee Hyun had returned to the Danxiao Sect after completing his first assignment at Haimen Port.

The cultivation chamber in Qingyu Ravine.

Thump.

The light of the Qi-Gathering Formation flared violently once, then subsided. Only after the spiritual power in his lower dantian stopped surging did Lee Hyun slowly open his eyes.

"Done!"

It had been almost thirty years since he reached Stage 5.

Lee Hyun was in an excellent mood.

He observed his body for a moment, then took out a wooden board from his storage pouch for the first time in ages. He erased several characters he had carved there long ago and added a new record.

【Realm: Foundation Establishment Stage 4 → Stage 6 (lower dantian)】

【Spiritual Power: 1,452 → 1,548】

...

A few days later, in the communal Alchemy Hall of Yanxia Peak.

When Lee Hyun entered, two Foundation Establishment cultivators who had been preparing medicinal ingredients rose to their feet.

"Greetings, Senior Brother Li."

Lee Hyun nodded and was about to pass when one of them cautiously held out a jade bottle.

"Senior Brother, could you take a quick look at this?"

"What is it?"

"My refined medicinal liquid keeps turning cloudy."

Lee Hyun opened the jade bottle and examined the state of the medicinal liquid and the medicinal potency remaining within it.

"The medicinal ingredients you used didn't contain enough moisture. You dried them too much."

The young cultivator hurriedly wrote it down. After explaining a few more things to the two of them, Lee Hyun went farther inside.

Liu Zhengyuan, who had been organizing a list of medicinal ingredients, looked up and widened his eyes. His sideburns were now streaked with white.

"You've reached Stage 6. Congratulations, Senior Brother."

"Thank you."

...

Lecture Hall.

Lee Hyun entered and took his usual seat near the front.

'It's been a long time.'

As he adjusted the end of his sleeve, he looked down at the back of his hand. Through his disguise method, he had made it look somewhat thinner than before.

He had mixed white into his hair as well and deepened the wrinkles around his eyes.

Li Dongsan was now 167 years old. Even for a Foundation Establishment cultivator, that was no longer young.

When Tan Yunsheng entered, the disciples rose in unison. After taking his usual seat of honor, his gaze settled on Lee Hyun.

"Dongsan. I heard you've reached Stage 6?"

"Yes, Master."

"Well done. Don't overexert yourself while stabilizing your realm."

"I'll keep that in mind."

Tan Yunsheng and Lee Hyun's fellow disciples congratulated him on reaching Foundation Establishment Stage 6, but none of them attached much significance to it.

At his age, there was no hope of breaking through to Golden Core from Foundation Establishment Stage 6. For an ordinary cultivator with a triple spiritual root, it was the expected outcome.

Li Dongsan had now become one of Yanxia Peak's core disciples, but practically no one expected him to one day become a pillar of the sect.

His fate was no different from that of most Foundation Establishment cultivators.

When Tan Yunsheng began his lecture, Lee Hyun cleared away his stray thoughts.

About half a shichen (about one hour) later.

A disciple in the back row was about to raise his hand with a question when a streak of light flew in from outside the Lecture Hall.

It was a voice-transmission talisman.

Tan Yunsheng stopped speaking and caught it. As the talisman burned away at his fingertips, his eyes closed briefly. When he opened them again, his expression had changed.

"We'll stop here for today."

One disciple cautiously asked,

"Master, has something happened?"

"There has been a major clash in southern Cang Kingdom."

Tan Yunsheng's voice dropped.

"A Nascent Soul Elder of the Wangu Sect returned gravely wounded after fighting cultivators from the Nanming Twelve-Sect Alliance. Because of that incident, an envoy sent by the Wangu Sect has just arrived at our sect headquarters."

Someone quietly drew in a breath.

A Nascent Soul cultivator had been gravely wounded?

Everyone present was a Foundation Establishment inner disciple. Not one of them was a fool.

If the Wangu Sect of Cang Kingdom fell, Kun Kingdom to its north would be next.

If war broke out among Tier-4 cultivation nations, Foundation Establishment cultivators would be little more than moths flying into a flame!

The disciples could feel the clouds of war gathering over Kun Kingdom. A creeping sense of foreboding rose into their chests.

The relaxed atmosphere in the Lecture Hall grew heavy with tension.

Tan Yunsheng rose from his seat.

"For the time being, anyone who needs to leave the sect is to inform me first."

The disciples stood and bowed. Tan Yunsheng left the Lecture Hall at a faster pace than usual.

Chapter 66

At dawn the next day, outside the cave abode in Qingyu Ravine.

Lee Hyun lay on his back with his fingers interlaced behind his head, listening to the waterfall as he gazed up at the stars in the night sky.

‘A Nascent Soul cultivator was seriously injured....’

To a Foundation Establishment cultivator, a Nascent Soul cultivator was like a natural disaster, an existence one could not even dream of defying.
