Tan Yunsheng rose from his seat.

“Orders have come from the main mountain. At dawn tomorrow, we will withdraw from Qingshi Market.”

Beside him, Liu Zhengyuan quietly exhaled. It sounded as though some of his tension had eased.

But another Elder immediately continued.

“Our withdrawal route is north. We are heading for the Xuan Kingdom.”

Liu Zhengyuan’s expression stiffened.

Someone at the back of the hall asked,

“Are we not returning to the main mountain?”

Tan Yunsheng shook his head.

“The main mountain is preparing to withdraw as well.”

Many did not immediately understand what he meant.

“...You mean we’re vacating the Mountain Gate?”

A disciple in the front row asked.

Tan Yunsheng gave a short answer.

“Yes.”

An Elder of the Biluo Sect stood.

“The Seniors engaged the Nanming Twelve-Sect Alliance in battle. Those who came from the north also lent their strength, but it was not enough to reverse the tide.”

Tan Yunsheng added,

“The Nanming Twelve-Sect Alliance had more Nascent Soul cultivators than we expected. We failed to properly assess how much their strength had grown since they seized the Lan Kingdom long ago. Once those who crossed the sea later joined them as well, the balance tipped against us. One of our sect’s Supreme Elders also suffered injuries to his dharma body. I am told he will need to recuperate for some time.”

The Biluo Sect Elder continued.

“They discussed whether the main mountain could still be defended if the fighting continued, and ultimately settled on terms for withdrawal.”

He gestured, and a rolled sheet of paper on the table unfurled and floated into the air.

「The Wangu Sect, Danxiao Sect, and Biluo Sect will hand over their main mountains and major strongholds within the agreed period. The Nanming Twelve-Sect Alliance will not pursue the withdrawing Nascent Soul cultivators.」

The hall erupted in murmurs.

“All the spirit veins....”

“They’re even handing over the main mountains?”

“Quiet.”

The voices died down.

The Elder looked over the disciples.

“For now, the primary targets are the Tier 4 spirit veins of our main mountains and the surrounding strongholds. Each sect is deciding the details of which supplies to remove and how to withdraw its personnel. Here, you need only prepare to leave Qingshi Market. Until the withdrawal is complete, Nascent Soul cultivators from both sides will not intervene in fighting among Golden Core cultivators, Tier 3 gu warriors, and those below those levels.”

Song Qiming asked,

“Does that mean Golden Core cultivators, Tier 3 gu warriors, and those below them may continue attacking one another?”

“Yes.”

A disciple asked,

“Could the Supreme Elders travel with us....”

“No.”

Tan Yunsheng answered.

“The agreement also stipulates that Nascent Soul cultivators will not escort the withdrawal columns. The Supreme Elders have already left the battlefield, and we Golden Core Elders will lead those who remain.”

Yue Wugou clenched the hand resting on his knee.

“So even after taking our spirit veins, they intend to chase us down and steal our possessions?”

The Biluo Sect Elder did not deny it.

“The Nanming Twelve-Sect Alliance refused our demand that their disciples be forbidden from pursuing us as well. Many cultivators must have joined them in hopes of earning battle merits and spoils. The twelve sects are unlikely to make all of them give up their share. In any case, they won the war. It is not something we are in a position to decide.”

“....”

“On the other hand, their Nascent Soul cultivators will not attack us either. Without that condition, we would even have had to fear Nascent Soul cultivators appearing along our withdrawal route. The Supreme Elders have done as much as they could for your sake. The other side likewise does not want Nascent Soul cultivators from our side roaming around slaughtering their disciples. In exchange, both sides have agreed to stay their hands.”

Lee Hyun organized the situation in his mind.

The Nascent Soul cultivators would no longer intervene.

But they could still encounter Golden Core cultivators or Tier 3 gu warriors. There would also be Foundation Establishment cultivators and Tier 2 gu warriors pursuing them from behind.

To those people, the storage pouches and cargo carried by the retreating cultivators would look like spoils waiting to be claimed.

Tan Yunsheng’s voice remained calm.

“That is all that has been decided. What we must do now is get out safely.”

He waved a hand, and a map unfolded in midair.

A route leading north from Qingshi Market lit up. Several strongholds were marked along the way.

“We and the Biluo Sect will travel together for part of the route. We will also join up with personnel from nearby strongholds.”

He pointed to the first rendezvous point.

“The advance party will leave today to scout the route. Everyone else will load the cargo by tonight and depart before daybreak. The grand formation will remain active until the rear guard has withdrawn.”

Another Elder added,

“Move any supplies that have already been packed as they are. Do not waste time dismantling equipment that cannot be taken with us. People and the supplies necessary for travel take priority.”

The Elders explained the rendezvous points and order of movement.

There were many questions.

Whether they would be able to meet the fellow disciples who remained at the main mountain.

Whether cultivators from nearby cultivation clans could bring their families with them.

Where the contribution points they had accumulated until now could be settled.

But the Elders gave negative answers to most of them.

They could not say whether anyone would be able to join up with fellow disciples from the main mountain. There was no time to fetch family members who were far away, and they were told that making use of their contribution points would likewise be difficult.

...

After the meeting ended, the Yanxia Peak disciples followed Tan Yunsheng to a separate hall.

As soon as the doors closed, Liu Zhengyuan finally voiced the question he had been holding back.

“Master. Has the Xuan Kingdom agreed to let us enter?”

“Yes. The Azure Cloud Sect, Taixuan Sect, and Jinding Sect have agreed to allow the fleeing disciples passage and temporary refuge. However, they have not agreed to provide us with a new place to settle.”

The disciples’ attention gathered on him again.

“The spirit veins there already have owners. Those three sects have no intention of giving us land where we can simply reestablish our former power wholesale. If we wish to obtain a spirit vein and establish ourselves, we will have to negotiate separately with those who control them.”

Mei Sujun asked,

“Then has it still not been decided where we will stay?”

“That is correct.”

Silence fell for a moment.

Yue Wugou muttered quietly,

“If the Nanming Twelve-Sect Alliance advances farther north, won’t the Xuan Kingdom be in danger too? And if cultivators from the Cang Kingdom and Kun Kingdom cross into their territory, that must cause problems for them as well. Why didn’t they help more actively?”

“They are not as desperate as we are.”

Tan Yunsheng pointed toward the upper portion of the map.

Beyond the Cang Kingdom and Kun Kingdom, the land spread broadly to the east and west. The Xuan Kingdom lay within that widened expanse, with several other borders extending around it.

“The Kun Kingdom lies on a peninsula, but from the Xuan Kingdom onward begins the gateway to a vast continent stretching east and west. The circumstances are different there. To attack that region, they would also have to consider the movements of several neighboring cultivation nations. Most of the surrounding sects follow the orthodox path, so they will not welcome demonic path forces from across the sea establishing themselves nearby. The Nanming Twelve-Sect Alliance also needs to divide up the newly captured spirit veins and secure the territories it has occupied. The Xuan Kingdom likely believes the alliance will find it difficult to shoulder that burden as well and immediately continue its advance north.”

“Even so....”

“They still sent three Nascent Soul cultivators. That was a considerable effort on their part. It seems they simply were not willing to risk having their own Nascent Soul cultivators seriously injured merely to defend our Mountain Gate.”

Yue Wugou could say nothing more.

Tan Yunsheng continued.

“The Xuan Kingdom has also obtained a promise from the Nanming Twelve-Sect Alliance that they will not pursue us into Xuan territory. First, we must make it there.”

Song Qiming looked at Tan Yunsheng.

“Master, where do you intend to go?”

Tan Yunsheng did not answer immediately.

He studied the map on the table for some time before slowly speaking.

“First, I should find somewhere for all of you to rest.”

He looked around at his disciples.

“I have already sent word to some old acquaintances. But I still do not know whether any of them will have a place capable of taking in our entire Yanxia Peak family. I intend to look into other possibilities as well.”

Tan Yunsheng was both a Golden Core cultivator and a Tier 3 alchemist. An alchemist of his caliber was a rare existence in the cultivation world, so finding somewhere for himself alone to stay would not have been particularly difficult. There was no shortage of forces throughout the human realm that would welcome him.

The problem was bringing along all the disciples who had followed him. Most spirit veins suitable for settling safely already had owners, and few places would accept so many disciples all at once.

Fang Jiyun asked cautiously,

“Should we find separate places to stay....”

“We can discuss that after reaching the north.”

Tan Yunsheng cut in.

“Do not start worrying about splitting up already. For now, think only about getting out of here safely. Qiming, check the roster of disciples who came to Qingshi Market and make sure everyone is accounted for.”

“Yes.”

“The rest of you, inspect the flying boats and the supplies we will be transporting. Hurry.”

“Understood.”

Chapter 69

Early the next morning.

Several large flying boats hovered low over the open ground north of Qingshi Market. Cultivators hurried back and forth between them, carrying the last of the cargo aboard.

The flying boat carrying the Danxiao Sect's alchemists was positioned in the center of the fleet.

The cargo on deck had already been firmly secured, and the Qi Refining disciples were gathered inside the cabin.

While Song Qiming checked the roster, Fang Jiyun and Chen Xiaoying inspected the restrictions throughout the vessel.

When Lee Hyun came aboard, Yue Wugou raised a hand.

"Junior Brother Li. Over here."

Beside him, Mei Sujun was watching the cabin entrance. Before long, Liu Zhengyuan came aboard late, dragging a shield as tall as himself. Meeting her gaze, he awkwardly hunched his shoulders.

"Sorry I'm late."

Soon afterward, Tan Yunsheng descended onto the deck.

"Is everyone aboard?"

Song Qiming folded the roster.

"Yes."

Tan Yunsheng looked over the cabin and deck in turn.

At his waist hung the small gourd he had carried when they first set out from the main mountain.

"If a battle breaks out along the way and we get separated, head for the rendezvous point we agreed on. Don't go wandering around trying to hitch a ride on some other flying boat."

The disciples bowed their heads.

"Yes."

...

Before long, the lead flying boat began moving north.

The lamps along the edges of its deck went out one after another. The flying boats behind it also rose into the dark sky while maintaining their spacing.

The enormous grand formation surrounding Qingshi Market trembled faintly. Then, the instant the final flying boat at the rear passed through, it faded away in midair and went completely dark. The halls and pavilions that had once kept the market bright through the night were plunged into pitch-black darkness in an instant.

...

That afternoon, six flying boats from the Biluo Sect and Danxiao Sect joined them from beyond the eastern mountain range. By evening, when forces withdrawing from another stronghold also linked up with the fleet, the number of Golden Core Elders escorting them had risen to four.

There was Tan Yunsheng, a long-bearded Elder from the Biluo Sect, a newly arrived blue-robed Elder from the Danxiao Sect, and a female cultivator from the Biluo Sect.

The people's expressions brightened.

With the soaring auras of four Golden Core Elders seeming to pierce the heavens, the heavy atmosphere inside the flying boats gradually eased. With this much strength, they believed they could break through even if they encountered an ambush.

...

For an entire day, the fleet continued north without rest.

The Foundation Establishment cultivators took turns inspecting the flying boats' restrictions, while the Qi Refining disciples rested in the cabins and replaced spirit stones whenever the order came. Twice, attackers appeared along the way, but after witnessing the fleet's might, they withdrew without daring to approach.

They were less than a day from the border of the Xuan Kingdom.

Clang―

At the sharp peal of a bell from one of the flying boats, every cultivator on deck looked up at once.

At the exact moment the four Golden Core Elders shot into the air between the flying boats, the dark clouds in the southern sky twisted into a gigantic vortex and tore apart.

Boom!

Along with a pulse of magical power like the heartbeat of the heavens themselves, a massive black beast broke through the clouds and emerged.

Its frost-sharp claws squeezed and burst the clouds apart, and its body, dozens of zhang long (well over 100 m), was covered in black scales. A man in a billowing black robe stood atop the head of the thick-horned flood dragon.

"It's the Fuhai Sect!"

"That demon beast is an Ink-Scaled Flood Dragon...!"

Before the shout had even ended, an overwhelming pressure descended from the sky.

Three figures appeared behind the flood dragon.

One was a Tier-3 gu warrior from the Qianyang Kingdom, dark-red veins writhing beneath his skin. Another was a Golden Core cultivator holding an enormous bow carved from bones stripped from a living creature, with a bird's head attached to one end that was still rolling its eyes. The last was a gaunt Golden Core cultivator carrying a massive pitch-black coffin tightly bound in chains and talismans.

Four Golden Core-level cultivators and an upper Tier-3 demon beast had appeared.

The spiritual pressure hanging overhead alone made the flying boats' defensive light screens creak, and several Qi Refining disciples inside the cabins coughed up blood. Their qi and blood had been thrown into turmoil by the divine senses and waves of magical power radiating in every direction from so many Golden Core-level beings.

"It wouldn't do to send you off on your little outing empty-handed, now would it?"

The Fuhai Sect cultivator's mocking voice had barely cut through the air when the Golden Core archer drew his bowstring.

Whoom!

Three red rays shot through the air and embedded themselves ahead of the fleet. The connected formation inscriptions violently seized control of the surrounding wind-aspect spiritual power. The currents supporting the vessels twisted, pressing the flying boats downward.

Creeeak!

The lead flying boat lost its balance and plunged downward. At that instant, a fourth arrow tore through the air toward the hull.

BOOM!

The bronze mirror deployed by the female cultivator of the Biluo Sect knocked the arrow aside. The deflected red light struck a distant mountain peak and pulverized the entire summit.

Clank!

Taking advantage of the opening, the coffin-bearing cultivator released the chains.

The moment the coffin lid opened, yin qi cold enough to freeze the marrow poured out, and a corpse with flesh hardened like bronze stepped forth.

A Bronze-Armored Corpse whose eyes and mouth had been sewn shut with golden thread.

The monster had been a Golden Core cultivator in life. As it stepped upon the empty air, dense corpse qi and spiritual pressure violently swept the surrounding clouds aside.

"Keep heading north! If you stop here, the entire fleet will be slaughtered!"

Tan Yunsheng's shout struck the disciples' eardrums. The stopper of the small gourd he had taken from his waist popped open.

Fwoosh!

The instant a tiny spark leaped out, dazzling blue light pierced the dark clouds brought by the Ink-Scaled Flood Dragon and illuminated the surroundings. Every beat of the firebird's wings, transparent as blue glass, devoured heaven-and-earth spiritual qi at a terrifying rate. The entire sky a hundred zhang ahead of it was swallowed by a net of blue flame.

"Azure Void Glass Flame?!"

The cultivator riding the Ink-Scaled Flood Dragon formed a hand seal in shock, and the flood dragon spat out a gigantic water dragon. Yet wherever the water dragon touched the Azure Void Glass Flame, it instantly vaporized into white mist, and the explosively surging steam blanketed the sky.

Bang!

The firebird darted through the momentary opening and grazed the flood dragon's scales. Dozens of black scales, harder than steel, melted and fell away, and even the exposed flesh beneath them began to burn.

The flood dragon's agonized roar shook heaven and earth.

GRAAAAH!

Meanwhile, the Nine-Section Emerald Jade Vine cast out by the elderly Biluo Sect Elder shot into the sky. Hundreds of enormous jade-green vines spread outward and intertwined into a forest, blocking the enemies' path.

BOOM! CRACK!

The Qianyang Kingdom gu warrior's blood spear tore through the forest of vines, while the Bronze-Armored Corpse smashed into it, unleashing thunderous explosions.

Even as the fleet sped north at full speed, the storms of magical power raging behind them tossed the flying boats around like fallen leaves. When Lee Hyun looked back, he clearly saw the middle of a distant mountain peak beneath the clashing Golden Core cultivators sliced cleanly away at an angle.

...

No sooner had they escaped the Golden Core cultivators' battlefield than ambushers swarmed up from the surrounding mountain ranges like hornets.

"Enemies to starboard!"

"Block the flying swords!"

BOOM! BOOM! BOOM!

Under the barrage of flying swords and firebolts coming from every direction, one flying boat at the rear had its stern torn away and burst into flames. As disciples spilled from the falling vessel, Mei Sujun's silk and Lee Hyun's Condensed-Essence Grasping Hand reached out in turn, pulling them to safety.

Clang!

The instant Lee Hyun's Profound Gate Sword knocked aside a flying blade diving toward his face, the now-empty flying boat shattered into pieces and plummeted to the ground.

Signals flared one after another from the boats ahead, and Song Qiming immediately seized the formation plate.

"We split up too!"

As the fleet broke apart in every direction, Yanxia Peak's flying boat skimmed beneath the clouds and plunged between the mountain ridges.

...

A desperate flight that lasted one shichen (two hours).

But the enemies, having caught the scent of blood, were relentless. Just as they were circling around a valley to the northeast, two gray-scaled Tier-2 demon beast birds, together with twelve Foundation Establishment cultivators and gu warriors, completely blocked the flying boat from both front and rear.

"We push through! Don't slow down!"

Song Qiming frantically poured spiritual power into the formation plate, while Fang Jiyun plastered talismans over the restrictions on the cracked hull. Yue Wugou and Mei Sujun also drew their weapons.

And at that moment, the balance of the aerial battle shattered all at once.

Twang!

An archer's purple arrowhead came hurtling in and smashed into Liu Zhengyuan's shield.

BOOM!

The impact crumpled metal and drove Liu Zhengyuan to one knee, opening a fatal gap in their defenses.

A gu warrior who had concealed his presence below the valley immediately shot upward through that opening. With savage Gu Origin True Qi wrapped around the tip of his spear, he charged straight toward the underside of the flying boat, into the blind spot directly beneath the cabin.

He was radiating spiritual pressure at the level of an early Golden Core cultivator!

He was an early Tier-3 gu warrior.

However, beneath his torn clothing was a deep sword wound running from his chest to his left shoulder, and blood was still flowing from the injury he had yet to properly close. Only the body-protecting spirit light around that area flickered with obvious instability.

Lee Hyun moved at once.

'Dammit, why is a Tier-3 gu warrior here?'

Whoosh!

Liu Zhengyuan's shield had been knocked aside, while Mei Sujun's silk was entangled with one of the demon birds.

Lee Hyun vaulted over the railing and threw himself beneath the hull, compressing spiritual power into the Profound Gate Sword. It was already too late to block the incoming spear shadow head-on.

Flash!

Lee Hyun's sword slid obliquely along the spear shaft. The gu warrior's spear tip, which had carried all its force toward piercing the flying boat, veered aside by about a handspan and tore a long gash through the restriction and outer hull beneath the vessel.

As the gu warrior tried to pull his spear back from the unexpected interference, Lee Hyun slid his blade along the point of contact and drove into his opponent's guard.

His target was the gaping wound in the man's chest.

Clang!

The Gu Origin True Qi surging through the spear shaft nearly tore apart Lee Hyun's grip on the sword hilt.

But Lee Hyun did not let go.

The Great Unity Heavenly Dipper Sword Qi that he had compressed to a single point until the very end flashed, piercing straight through the wavering spirit light over the wound.

"Ghk!"

Blood burst from the gu warrior's chest.

He reflexively twisted aside and managed to avoid having his heart pierced, but the wound he had barely managed to close split open again all the way to his shoulder. The Gu Origin True Qi he had painstakingly brought under control began leaking violently away.

The instant Lee Hyun pulled his sword free, he used the recoil from his Qi Sphere Barrier to propel himself backward.

The spear shaft swung by the gu warrior grazed the tips of his feet, and that counterattack alone blew apart an entire section of the nearby cliff.

'One mistake and I'm dead!'

The gu warrior stopped his sinking body against a nearby rock face and tried to soar upward again. But true qi surged backward from his torn chest, and he spat out a clot of blood before dropping to one knee.

In that brief opening, the flying boat rounded the bend in the valley.

Lee Hyun also shot upward alongside the hull and returned to the deck.

The disciples on deck had only stumbled from the impact beneath the hull and had failed to properly witness the brief clash. Before they could even regain their footing, attacks once again poured in from every direction.

Clang!

Yue Wugou's iron plaque knocked aside a demon bird's claws and flew wide through the air. At that instant, another gu warrior slipped into his blind spot and unleashed countless strands of insect silk.

Hum!

Lee Hyun twisted his left hand inside his sleeve.

A brief surge of Earth-Origin Force dragged the gu warrior sideways, and Yue Wugou's iron plaque, which had been flying wide, smashed directly into the man's collarbone.

Crunch!

"AAARGH!"

As the insect silk scattered with his scream, Yue Wugou's second iron plaque crushed the man's back and sent him plummeting below.

But there was no time to rest.

BOOM! CRACK!

The other demon bird threw its massive weight against the bow of the flying boat.

The railing shattered, sending splinters of wood raining everywhere, and Liu Zhengyuan, who had been bracing his shield, coughed up blood as the bone in his shoulder was crushed.

"Junior Brother Liu!"

Chen Xiaoying shouted as the jade ruler she launched smashed into an enemy cultivator's side and sent him falling.

While Mei Sujun's silk wrapped around the demon bird's neck and hurled it away from the vessel, Lee Hyun slid down along the broken outer plating at the stern.

The Profound Gate Sword flashed in his hand.

Great Unity Heavenly Dipper, Twelfth Form: Bending Turn.

An archer who had been drawing his bow at the thinned light screen beneath the flying boat had his wrist effortlessly severed by Lee Hyun's sword qi as it curved through the air.

"Aaagh!"

Before the scream had even ended, a cultivator carrying a shield refined from human skin charged in.

But Lee Hyun's arm moved with unbelievable speed.

His sword light split the shield apart, and the cultivator's head flew from his shoulders.

Amid the spray of blood mist, Lee Hyun snatched the man's storage pouch and returned to the deck.

Seeing their companions fall one after another, the enemies widened their distance the instant he landed.

The archer with the purple bow, apparently their commander, retreated and shouted.

"Don't engage the sword cultivator! Punch through the side of the boat!"

"Once the boat crashes, everything aboard is ours!"

The enemies seemed to believe that if they simply shot down the battered flying boat from a distance, all the storage pouches and wealth carried aboard it would fall into their hands.

The remaining enemies lowered their altitude together and began unleashing wave after wave of attacks on the flying boat.

BOOM! BOOM! BOOM!

Under the rain of magic-tool attacks, the deck rocked violently enough to overturn, and the cabin ceiling collapsed as the disciples screamed.

Even the defensive barrier sustained by the formation plate began to flicker.

At this rate, the flying boat would be blown apart in midair.

'I need to take that guy out first.'

Lee Hyun stepped onto the railing.

"Junior Brother Li!"

"I'll be right back."

Bang!

Before the words had even finished, Lee Hyun shot into the air like a bolt of lightning.

The archer sneered and aimed his bow at the sword cultivator who had leaped into open air.

At the same time, a gu warrior sprayed a web of insect silk from his palm, blocking Lee Hyun's path.

But then,

Hum!

Lee Hyun clenched his left hand hard in midair.

The gu warrior blocking his path pitched forward as though dragged by a magnet.

The web of insect silk collapsed in the wrong direction, completely obstructing the archer's view behind him instead.

"You bastard...!"

Slice!

Before the archer could even finish cursing, the gu warrior's head flew off.

Lee Hyun burst through the spray of blood, and the startled archer fired three arrows at his face in rapid succession.

Thwip-thwip-thwip!

The purple arrows flew fast enough to scorch the air.

BOOM!

Lee Hyun's Qi Sphere Barrier pressed against the first arrow and knocked it off course.

The spinning Profound Iron Buckler knocked away the second.

The final arrow slid along the blade of the Profound Gate Sword, throwing off sparks with a skin-crawling shriek.

SCREEECH!

By the time the sparks grazed his cheek, Lee Hyun had already closed to directly beneath the archer's chin.

'What a monster...!'

Despite his shock, the archer reacted quickly and hurled away the bow in his hands, a high-grade magic tool.

The restrictions engraved into the bow released, and the weapon exploded on the spot.

BOOOOM!

'You didn't expect that!'

Using the raging flames as a shield, the archer retreated and had just pulled his most treasured supreme-grade magic tool bow from his storage pouch when it happened.

With the Profound Iron Buckler held before him, Lee Hyun tore straight through the flames without hesitation.

His sword was already thrusting toward the archer.

The startled man hastily raised his bow, and bow and sword collided, releasing a violent shockwave.

CLAAANG!

Disbelief spread across the man's face.

Lee Hyun's sword had pierced straight through the joint in the bow stave.

Crack!

The sturdy spirit bow shrieked as it broke in two.

The sword tip continued forward, shattering the man's body-protecting spirit light and plunging deep into his chest.

Spurt!

"Urgh...."

The focus vanished from the man's eyes as his heart was pierced.

Lee Hyun kicked the corpse away and spun around, swinging his sword horizontally toward a demonic cultivator who had tried to ambush him from behind with a flying sword.

Flash!

A crescent of sword light carved through the air and cleanly separated the cultivator's upper and lower body.

Blood rained from the sky.

Lee Hyun caught up to the flying boat far ahead and lightly landed on the deck.

Drops of blood fell steadily from the tip of his sword.

"......."

With even their commander killed in an instant, the remaining demon birds and demonic cultivators recoiled in horror and climbed higher into the sky.

None of them dared approach the flying boat again.

"Full speed ahead!"

At Song Qiming's roar, the flying boat thundered forward and slipped into a gorge between the mountains.

...

Only after flying for another shichen and completely leaving the mountain range behind did the cultivators aboard the flying boat collapse to the deck, gasping for breath.

Liu Zhengyuan clutched his shattered shoulder and barely managed to set his shield down with trembling hands, while Yue Wugou sat against the blood-soaked railing and tossed a Qi-Restoring Pill into his mouth.

"...Junior Brother Li."

Yue Wugou looked up at Lee Hyun with dazed eyes.

"That archer?"

"I killed him."

"Good, good.... The bastard deserved to die...."

At Lee Hyun's calm reply, Yue Wugou let out a hollow laugh and muttered to himself.

Perhaps the release from the crushing tension had finally brought his exhaustion to its peak, because he kept repeating the same words blankly.

...

As the sun began sinking toward the west, the long mountain range gradually lowered.

Beyond the countless mountain ridges they had crossed, broad plains and a majestic river unfolded beneath the flying boat.

Song Qiming's hand stopped as he compared the terrain ahead with the map spread before him.

The people on deck rose to their feet, and the disciples inside the cabin began emerging one by one.

Far away, enormous pillars of light towered over the mountain ridge marking the border.

Beneath them, the flags of three sects fluttered above the fortified pass.

The Azure Cloud Sect, the Taixuan Sect, and the Jinding Sect.

Several flying boats that had arrived before them were already descending in a line below.

After sending a voice-transmission talisman toward the pass to announce their identities, Song Qiming glanced back at the southern sky.

There was still no sign of Tan Yunsheng or the other Elders.

"The Xuan Kingdom...!"

At someone's tearful cry, the battered flying boat slowly began descending toward the pass, bathed in the sunset glow of relief.

Chapter 70

When the half-wrecked flying boat touched down, a plank that had barely been clinging to the edge of the deck fell away.

Thud.

The Qi Refining disciples emerging from the cabin flinched at the sound.

“Please disembark slowly.”

A Qi Refining cultivator from Xuan Kingdom dressed in blue enchanted robes approached the flying boat. Several Qi Refining cultivators carrying stretchers followed behind him.

While Mei Sujun and Chen Xiaoying handed over the injured, Song Qiming took out his identity token and the personnel roster.

“I’m Song Qiming of Yanxia Peak, Danxiao Sect. We withdrew from Qingshi Market.”

“Qingshi Market....”

The other man looked up from the roster he had been flipping through.

“It says here that Elder Tan Yunsheng was leading your group.”

“He stayed behind to fight Golden Core cultivators from the Nanming Twelve-Sect Alliance. We don’t know where he is now.”

The Xuan Kingdom cultivator pointed toward the long halls on the northern side of the clearing.

“We’ll take the injured over there. The rest of you, please confirm your headcount first. If any fellow disciples who were separated from you arrive later, we’ll let you know.”

...

The checkpoint was already packed with people.

Inside one of the halls was a Foundation Establishment cultivator from the Danxiao Sect’s Infirmary who had arrived earlier. He sat Liu Zhengyuan down, cut away the clothing stuck to his shoulder, and examined the wound with his divine sense.

“Your meridians aren’t severed. However, you must not channel spiritual power forcefully through this arm for the time being.”

The cultivator used a technique to set the shattered bone fragments back into place. While Liu Zhengyuan gritted his teeth and endured the pain, the cultivator gave him medicinal liquid containing dissolved Tier 2 Bone-Forging Powder, then placed a hand on his shoulder.

As the blue light of the Wood-Aspect Healing Art seeped into the wound, the swelling rapidly subsided and the torn flesh knitted together.

“Keep circulating your qi like this and absorb the medicinal strength. You should be able to move your arm again in a few days.”

...

Even after sending the others to their temporary lodgings, Song Qiming remained in the clearing for quite some time.

Whenever he saw light approaching from the south, he raised his head, but the only arrivals were flying boats that had been scattered or small groups of Foundation Establishment cultivators flying in together.

As the night deepened, the lamps around the clearing lit up one by one.

Just then, the cultivators atop the checkpoint rose to their feet.

Three streaks of light were approaching through the southern sky.

“It’s the Elders!”

Song Qiming flew out first, and the Yanxia Peak disciples waiting outside the hall quickly followed him.

Three people descended into the clearing.

Tan Yunsheng, the long-bearded Elder from the Biluo Sect, and the female Biluo Sect cultivator who wielded the bronze mirror.

The blue-robed Elder from the Danxiao Sect was nowhere to be seen.

The left sleeve of Tan Yunsheng’s enchanted robe was almost entirely gone. A long, charred mark ran across his exposed arm, and the gourd at his waist had lost much of its former luster.

The other two Golden Core cultivators were in even worse shape than Tan Yunsheng.

“Master!”

When Song Qiming approached, Tan Yunsheng raised a hand.

“I’m fine. What about the children?”

“Zhengyuan injured his shoulder and is being treated, but his life is not in danger. Most of the junior disciples from Yanxia Peak only suffered minor injuries. As for the Qi Refining outer disciples... quite a few of them lost their lives.”

“I see.”

Soon afterward, a Golden Core cultivator from Xuan Kingdom appeared and escorted the Elders inside. Tan Yunsheng gave Song Qiming a brief instruction before following them.

“Look after the children. I’ll go assess the situation first.”

...

Three days later.

A Golden Core Elder of the Danxiao Sect visited their checkpoint.

He had been part of the group that evacuated the sect headquarters earlier. He said that the people and supplies transported aboard several flying boats had entered Xuan Kingdom through different checkpoints and had already been divided among several strongholds farther inside the kingdom.

The checkpoint where Lee Hyun’s group had arrived primarily received cultivators coming from Qingshi Market and western Kun Kingdom.

It seemed that most of those who had crossed over from the Wangu Sect had taken other routes.

...

That afternoon, the Yanxia Peak disciples gathered in a large room at their temporary lodgings.

Tan Yunsheng, whose complexion had improved, sat in the seat of honor. A sealed letter bearing the seal of the sect headquarters lay before him.

“The Supreme Elders have decided on a course of action.”

The disciples straightened.

“One Supreme Elder is recuperating, while the other is contacting acquaintances and looking into what can be done from here. For the time being, they have concluded that rebuilding the Danxiao Sect’s headquarters somewhere else in the near future will be difficult.”

Liu Zhengyuan asked,

“Would moving to another kingdom be difficult as well?”

“How could we find a place capable of housing two Nascent Soul cultivators, several Golden Core Elders, and countless disciples? Spirit veins of that scale already have owners wherever you go.”

Tan Yunsheng looked down at the sealed letter.

“Under the current circumstances, we can no longer maintain the sect in the same form as before.”

Song Qiming asked quietly,

“Then what will happen to the disciples?”

Tan Yunsheng raised his head.

“Starting today, each of you may seek your own residence and livelihood. You may join another sect or leave to become a rogue cultivator. You will not be punished under the sect rules for doing so.”

The room fell silent.

One disciple’s lips moved hesitantly.

“Is the Danxiao Sect... going to disappear?”

“The Supreme Elders remain, and so does our sect’s inheritance. Some Elders also intend to carry on our lineage elsewhere.”

Tan Yunsheng paused for a moment.

“However, from now on, the sect headquarters will no longer be able to provide you with residences or cultivation resources. There will be no more regular missions, nor contribution points awarded in return. Some of the supplies managed by the various peaks and divisions will be sorted out and distributed, while the inheritances will be entrusted to those who intend to carry them on.”

Yue Wugou clenched and unclenched his hands over his knees.

“If the sect headquarters is rebuilt someday, will we return?”

“Who knows... I have no idea when such a thing might happen. Even I don’t know where the Supreme Elders or the sect master will go, or what they intend to do from now on.”

Tan Yunsheng looked around at his disciples.

“Even if the day comes when the Danxiao Sect is rebuilt, no one who has already established themselves in another sect will be forced to return.”

Lee Hyun touched the identity token at his waist.

‘I didn’t think it would end like this.’

He had expected to be the one to leave the Danxiao Sect first, only for the Danxiao Sect to collapse before he could.

Tan Yunsheng also explained the conditions they had to observe while in Xuan Kingdom.

They were forbidden from seizing the spirit veins of existing sects or clans by force. They could negotiate with the owners to buy or lease a spirit vein, but establishing a new Mountain Gate required separate consultation with the power governing that region.

...

Only a few days after the sect’s decision was announced, the number of visitors to their temporary lodgings increased sharply.

They had come to recruit talent.

Foundation Establishment stewards from the Azure Cloud Sect and Jinding Sect asked the disciples about their spiritual roots and ages.

They said cultivators with a single spiritual root would immediately be accepted as inner disciples if their age and realm were suitable. Those with dual spiritual roots, as well as cultivators with mutated spiritual roots and relatively few root attributes, could also receive favorable treatment if they met the same conditions.

The cultivators from the Taixuan Sect asked more questions about practical skills.

After checking what kinds of pills they could refine, what level of formations they could repair on their own, and how much experience they had cultivating spirit plants, they immediately requested interviews with several cultivators.

The Golden Core Elders were all exceptional cultivators and seemed to be receiving decent offers from various sects, but disciples like Lee Hyun had no way of knowing the detailed terms of those negotiations.

...

Lee Hyun received an offer as well.

The Taixuan Sect asked whether he was interested in working with spirit plants and alchemy. However, because he had triple spiritual roots and was advanced in age, they said he would have to serve as a Foundation Establishment steward in the Outer Gate.

Lee Hyun read through the terms.

“I’ll think it over.”

The other man did not look particularly disappointed.

“There are so many alchemists from the Danxiao Sect that the opening may be gone soon. Are you sure you want to hold off?”

“Yes.”

After the man left, Yue Wugou peered at the document Lee Hyun had received.

“Tsk... No one knows how to recognize your true worth. Fools, all of them.”

“Haha. I really am fine with it.”

...

The disciples gradually began making different choices.

One young disciple with dual spiritual roots kept reviewing the terms offered by the Azure Cloud Sect.

A fellow disciple beside him asked,

“Are you really thinking of joining them?”

“I haven’t decided yet.”

“Couldn’t we settle somewhere among ourselves?”

“Where?”

“Hmm...”

Every disciple had different circumstances.

Some needed to search for family members who had lived in Kun Kingdom, while others intended to seek shelter with cultivation clans they had not contacted in years. There were even disciples who planned to return to life as rogue cultivators.

...

Five days later.

Tan Yunsheng gathered his disciples and said,

“I’ve decided to accept a position as a guest elder with the Taixuan Sect. It seems I’ll also have opportunities to conduct research with their alchemists. They appear to have quite a few medicinal ingredients and pill recipes that I have never worked with before.”

For the first time in a long while, strength returned to his voice.

“If any of you wish to come to the Taixuan Sect, tell me. I’ll see if I can find a position for you. However, it will be difficult for all of us to live together on one peak as we did before. You’ll likely be assigned to different places according to your skills and cultivation realms.”

Tan Yunsheng slowly looked over his disciples.

“I’m sorry I cannot look after all of you. I am your Master, but I am also a cultivator who still dreams of pursuing the immortal path. There is still much cultivation I wish to pursue. This battle also made me painfully aware of my shortcomings. I am not in a position where I can afford to spend my time somewhere without a Tier 3 spirit vein.”

Tan Yunsheng was not particularly old among Golden Core Elders, and he was still a cultivator who could aspire to the Nascent Soul realm.

Song Qiming was the first to cup his hands.

“I’m glad things worked out, Master.”

The other disciples offered their respects in turn.

Several Yanxia Peak disciples, including Chen Xiaoying, who possessed dual spiritual roots, were already considering offers they had received from the Taixuan Sect.

A few days later, those among them who had received favorable terms decided to follow Tan Yunsheng together with Chen Xiaoying.

Fifteen days later.

Heiwu Market in southwestern Xuan Kingdom.

It had originally been a quiet place, but its streets were now packed with cultivators who had crossed over from the south.

People wearing the enchanted robes of the Danxiao Sect and Biluo Sect were common sights, and spirit-insect pouches still bearing the Wangu Sect’s insignia could occasionally be seen as well.

Goods hastily put up for sale were piled high along the roadside.

There were old pill furnaces, damaged formation plates, and broken magic tools, but most of the goods were spoils taken from cultivators of the Nanming Twelve-Sect Alliance.

Long lines had formed at the shops selling pills deeper inside the cultivator market. Meanwhile, a cultivator selling magic tools from a roadside stall could not attract a single customer.

“Hold on. Aren’t you interested in this flying sword?”

“Who would buy it at that price now? Ownerless magic tools are lying around everywhere.”

Off to one side, two cultivators began arguing while haggling over an item, but they stopped as soon as a cultivator patrolling the market appeared.

Rumors had been circulating for days that bandit cultivators were prowling outside the market.

Lee Hyun passed through the crowd and entered a medicinal-ingredient shop.

Song Qiming, Fang Jiyun, Yue Wugou, and Mei Sujun were seated inside.

The medicinal-ingredient merchant across the table spread out a map.

“This is Xu Kingdom.”

A vast territory was marked to the west of Xuan Kingdom, while even farther west, forests and mountain ranges seemed to cover the rest of the map.

「Cangmang Forest」

“Isn’t there a sect in Xu Kingdom with a Nascent Soul cultivator?”

When Song Qiming asked, the merchant nodded.

“There is a great sect called Baoguang Temple. It is the greatest power in Xu Kingdom. However, unlike the three great sects of Xuan Kingdom, it does not often interfere in the affairs of smaller sects.”

“You mean we may claim a spirit vein and establish a Mountain Gate?”

“As long as you do not seize one that already has an owner. In particular, there are still quite a few undeveloped Tier 2 spirit veins along the eastern frontier of Cangmang Forest.”

The medicinal-ingredient merchant pointed to several small dots on the map.

“These are all sects or clans established by Foundation Establishment cultivators. Some were founded by several people joining forces, while others were established by people who migrated here from other kingdoms.”

Yue Wugou crossed his arms.

“If it’s such a good place, why are there still unclaimed spirit veins?”

The merchant laughed.

“Demon beasts come down frequently. Obtaining a spirit vein and making a living there are two different matters.”

“What level are the demon beasts?”

“Along the frontier, they’re generally Tier 2 or below. If a Tier 3 demon beast appears, the monks of Baoguang Temple take action. That’s why few of them settle in the area for long.”

Mei Sujun asked,

“If we report one to Baoguang Temple, will they immediately come and deal with the Tier 3 demon beast?”

“That I cannot say. It’s not as if the monks are standing by, ready to come the moment they’re called. That’s why even small sects generally prepare defensive formations and somewhere to retreat to whenever possible.”

The merchant pushed the map slightly closer.

“There are several places around here where I source medicinal ingredients. If you wish, I can introduce you so you can go there first and ask about the local circumstances yourselves.”

...

After leaving the medicinal-ingredient shop, the group found seats at a teahouse on the outskirts and spread the map out again.

Lee Hyun asked,

“Are you truly thinking of going there?”

“We haven’t decided yet.”

Song Qiming looked toward the western side of the map.

“But I think it might be nice for us to establish a small Mountain Gate of our own and spend our later years there.”

Fang Jiyun set down his teacup.

“A trading company in Xuan Kingdom offered me a position. The terms weren’t bad. But if I joined them, I would spend the rest of my life managing someone else’s medicinal ingredients and pill furnaces. I simply couldn’t bring myself to feel interested.”

“Would joining a sect be any different?”

Yue Wugou spoke.

“Who would offer people of middling aptitude like us particularly good treatment?”

Mei Sujun looked at him.

“There’s no need to sell yourself short.”

“Well, that’s true. Still, I’m tired of working under someone else.”

Song Qiming continued,

“We should be able to earn spirit stones through alchemy. There’s no need to build a large herb garden from the start either. We could secure a small spirit vein, establish cave abodes and an alchemy room, then trade with a nearby cultivator market.”

“We’ll need a defensive formation as well.”

“Indeed. It would also be good if an artifact refiner and formation master came with us. I’ve seen quite a few fellow disciples from other peaks who have nowhere else to go, so I intend to ask whether they’re interested.”

Lee Hyun studied the map.

A small Mountain Gate where Foundation Establishment cultivators could live together, built around a Tier 2 spirit vein.

It seemed they intended to create a small power of their own.

Most of the cultivators who had failed to receive appealing recruitment offers from Xuan Kingdom’s great sects were disciples who had joined the Danxiao Sect long ago.

Those whose cultivation realms were low for their age and aptitude, and who therefore had little hope of breaking through to Golden Core, were treated less as people worth nurturing and more as manpower that could be put to immediate use, even if they possessed useful skills.

For people who had once been inner disciples of the Danxiao Sect, that was quite a blow to their pride.

Song Qiming turned his gaze toward Lee Hyun.

“What does Junior Brother Li plan to do?”

“I was planning to live as a rogue cultivator.”

“I thought as much.”

Song Qiming looked disappointed.

Lee Hyun glanced at his other fellow disciples.

‘Hmm... Is it really all right to let them go off like this?’

To his eyes, these naive fellow disciples were like ducklings charging toward the water the moment they saw it.

They had spent most of their lives under the sect’s protection, so he had his doubts about how well they would adapt to settling in unfamiliar lands without anyone backing them.

‘Something about this doesn’t sit right...’

Lee Hyun set down his teacup.

“I’ll go with you for now.”

“Really?”

Yue Wugou raised his head.

“Yes. I’ll stay with you for a while, just until you settle in. After that, I intend to leave and take care of my own affairs.”

Song Qiming looked at him for a moment before nodding.

“Even that much would be a tremendous help.”

“With the fearsome Junior Brother Li along, mere Tier 2 demon beasts won’t stand a chance.”

Yue Wugou laughed, and Mei Sujun immediately replied,

“Senior Brother, you should learn how to hunt demon beasts from Junior Brother Li before he leaves.”

“Did I say I wouldn’t? I was thinking exactly the same thing.”

Lee Hyun scratched his head.

‘I just need to keep an eye on them for a little while.’

He thought of the location of Tunnel No. 3 and the route he had traveled so far.

Although he had entered Xuan Kingdom, he was actually closer to Tunnel No. 3 than he had been while at the Danxiao Sect headquarters.

If he went as far as the area near Cangmang Forest west of Xu Kingdom, the distance would grow again, but there was still plenty of water stored in the tanks.

Even excluding the half year he had spent at Qingshi Market and the time since the evacuation, his calculations said the supply should last at least another two years.

‘It’s not as if I have to stay with their sect forever. If settling down looks like it’ll take a long time, I can just make a few trips back to Tunnel No. 3 in the meantime...’

...

The tenth day after arriving at Heiwu Market.

Almost everyone who intended to leave had decided on a destination.

Among those who planned to follow Song Qiming to Xu Kingdom were several Foundation Establishment cultivators from other peaks. Two cultivators skilled in formations, two artifact refiners, one talisman maker, and one sword cultivator from the Dharma Protector Court joined them. Around eighty Qi Refining disciples who had asked to be taken along were also accepted.

...

The next morning.

A flying boat hovered over the clearing outside Heiwu Market.

It was not the same vessel they had ridden from Qingshi Market. That flying boat would have cost too much to repair, so they had removed and sold whatever useful components remained.

The new flying boat was smaller and older than the previous one, but it could carry around a hundred people, and its restrictions were intact.

As the flying boat slowly rose, Yue Wugou shook the railing.

“This should do.”

Song Qiming turned his gaze forward.

“We head west.”

The flying boat accelerated beneath the clouds.

Fifteen days later.

After traveling one hundred thousand li (about 39,200 km) westward from southwestern Xuan Kingdom, the group’s flying boat entered western Xu Kingdom.

Xu Kingdom had vast plains and cities.

Small temples could occasionally be seen on the low hills beside the road. Some were places where mortals burned incense, while spirit light flowed above the Mountain Gates of others.

But the farther west they traveled, the fewer human settlements they encountered.

The forests between the cultivated fields gradually grew broader, until eventually every mountain peak and valley was covered in deep green.

The distant mountain ranges vanished into clouds and mist, with no end in sight.

It was Cangmang Forest.

...

A cultivator market east of the forest.

Two monks in yellow enchanted robes stood atop the walls. Beside the gate was a large stone stele engraved with the prohibitions that had to be observed in this region.

Lee Hyun descended from the flying boat and stopped in front of it.

「Do not intrude upon the territory of another Mountain Gate or clan.

Do not enter areas forbidden by Baoguang Temple without permission.

When securing a new spirit vein, report its location to a nearby stronghold so that territorial boundaries do not overlap.」

Below that were further rules concerning demon beasts.

「Upon discovering a demon beast of Tier 3 or above, report it to Baoguang Temple.

Do not recklessly take eggs or newborns.

Do not release poison or burn the forests to exterminate entire groups of demon beasts.

Refrain from killing unless necessary to protect your residence or spirit fields.」

Yue Wugou tilted his head after reading the last part.

“Why does it forbid killing them?”

A rogue cultivator in gray robes passing nearby laughed.

“Be careful. If you go so far as to destroy their nests, the monks will come looking for you.”

“Are we not allowed to fight even when defending a spirit vein?”

“You can kill them then. What else are you supposed to do if you can’t drive away a creature that attacks people? They merely want you to drive it off if you can.”

The rogue cultivator added,

“If you bring Baoguang Temple news of a Tier 3 demon beast, the monks will be delighted. Especially if it’s one that should have formed a demon core.”

...

Before choosing a spirit vein where they would settle, the group visited a trading company in the cultivator market to gather information.

Dried medicinal ingredients and demon-beast carapaces were piled in the rear courtyard.

When the owner of the trading company heard they were from the Danxiao Sect, he immediately invited Song Qiming and several others into an inner room.

After Song Qiming and Fang Jiyun discussed spirit veins and the medicinal-ingredient trade with him, Yue Wugou asked about what they had heard earlier.

“Why is Baoguang Temple so eager to hunt Tier 3 demon beasts? Are they really doing it out of Buddhist compassion to save all sentient beings?”

The owner refilled his teacup.

“Because of the demon cores. Baoguang Temple is said to possess a special secret method for using Tier 3 demon cores to refine Golden Core Condensing Pills.”

Fang Jiyun’s hand froze.

“Golden Core Condensing Pills!? You mean the Golden Core Condensing Pills needed for a breakthrough to Golden Core?”

“Yes. Though I don’t know the specific pill recipe.”

Song Qiming said,

“Then Baoguang Temple must have a great many Golden Core cultivators.”

“It does. There isn’t a single sect in Xu Kingdom that tries to contend with Baoguang Temple.”

The owner pointed toward the carapaces piled outside.

“When the monks hunt demon beasts, they take the demon cores and any useful materials first. Whatever remains is released to trading companies like ours.”

Yue Wugou laughed as though he found the whole thing absurd.

“Wait, they use demon cores for alchemy themselves, yet tell us to refrain from killing?”

“Haha. If everyone kills off all the smaller ones, there will be fewer beasts left to form demon cores later.”

The owner’s answer was perfectly matter-of-fact.

“That’s why they particularly dislike people taking eggs or newborns. Hunting itself is forbidden in some areas deeper inside the forest.”

Mei Sujun set down her teacup.

“Then....”

“Well... you may want to watch what you say in front of the monks.”

The owner laughed.

“Some of them genuinely do dislike pointless killing. Baoguang Temple is enormous, so naturally all sorts of people belong to it.”

...

Fang Jiyun still seemed preoccupied by the mention of Golden Core Condensing Pills.

“If they possess such a secret method, wouldn’t cultivators from other kingdoms come here trying to buy Golden Core Condensing Pills?”

“Many do, in fact. But there are rumors that those pills have a problem.”

“What sort of problem?”

The owner lowered his voice slightly.

“They say cultivators who achieve Core Formation with them find it difficult to reach the Nascent Soul realm. Exactly what goes wrong is not known outside the temple.”

“You mean they damage one’s cultivation foundation?”

“Some say that, while others claim there is another reason. I don’t know. I only tell customers what I’ve heard, because pretending to know more would only risk offending the monks who come here to buy goods.”

Lee Hyun drank his tea as he listened.

Golden Core Condensing Pill.

For a moment, he remembered Senior Brother Tao Wenqian receiving that pill and sharing drinks with his fellow disciples.

It was a pill that even the Danxiao Sect could not easily refine.

‘Does that mean demon cores can substitute for the main ingredient? Wait, then if I could obtain that pill recipe... I wouldn’t need to spend years growing the main ingredient for Golden Core Condensing Pills in Tunnel No. 3. If I hunted enough Tier 3 demon beasts to make more than fifty Golden Core Condensing Pills, couldn’t I break through to Golden Core throughout my entire body?’

Lee Hyun was briefly tempted, but the rumor that achieving Core Formation with Baoguang Temple’s Golden Core Condensing Pills made it difficult to progress to the Nascent Soul realm bothered him.

Besides, only his lower dantian had reached Foundation Establishment Stage 6. The rest of his body was still merely at Qi Refining Stage 9. There were still many things he needed to master and temper first, so this was not something he needed to investigate in a hurry.

The owner continued,

“Even so, plenty of people seek them out. Setting the Nascent Soul realm aside, how many cultivators have no path to Core Formation at all? Golden Core cultivators can live for more than five hundred years, while the Nascent Soul realm is practically legendary to begin with, beyond the reach of most... To the majority of cultivators, Baoguang Temple’s Golden Core Condensing Pills are every bit as precious as ordinary Golden Core Condensing Pills.”

Song Qiming nodded.

The owner set down the teapot and took out a map.

“More importantly, you said you were searching for somewhere to settle. Let me first show you the areas that have only recently become available for development.”

...

Song Qiming and the owner spoke for quite some time.

In short, two months earlier, the monks of Baoguang Temple had subjugated a Tier 3 demon beast that had settled nearby. Afterward, rogue cultivators exploring the surrounding region had discovered several new Tier 2 spirit veins.

The group paid the trading company spirit stones for the information and decided to send several Foundation Establishment cultivators ahead to investigate the area.

...

Four days later.

Lee Hyun sat on the edge of a cliff, looking down into a valley where a stream ran through the depths below.

His fellow disciples were busy inspecting various locations for a place to establish their new settlement, but Lee Hyun merely wandered around as though he were watching someone else’s affairs.

In truth, he intended to leave soon, and his fellow disciples were already grateful that Lee Hyun had accompanied them this far. They made no effort to trouble him by consulting him over every detail of establishing the new Mountain Gate.

Lee Hyun intended to protect his fellow disciples if a Tier 2 demon beast appeared, but after arriving, he found there were no demon beasts in the immediate vicinity at all.

With everyone else bustling around while he alone remained carefree, he felt strangely out of place.

Lee Hyun took out a map of Xu Kingdom from his storage pouch.

His hand stopped as he examined the various place names in the surrounding region. One of them sounded familiar.

‘Hm? This place...’

It was a place name he had seen not long ago in a report submitted by members of the Two Heavens Society.

Lee Hyun had ordered the society to expand northward roughly fifty years ago. Since then, the Two Heavens Society had increased its number of strongholds in Xuan Kingdom, while some members had also advanced into Xu Kingdom along the western trade routes.

Lee Hyun pointed back and forth on the map between the cultivator market where the Two Heavens Society had a stronghold and the valley where he now stood.

They were not very far apart.

‘Come to think of it, I’ve never met the members in this area in person. Before I return to Tunnel No. 3, I should hold a meeting here.’

Chapter 71

One month later.

Two pillars had been erected at the entrance to the valley.

Qi Refining disciples carried timber back and forth between the pillars, which did not even have doors yet. From deeper inside came the ceaseless sounds of stone being cut and roofs being raised.

A signboard hung above the two pillars, bearing three characters.

Yanxia Sect.

“So you settled on this name in the end.”

Song Qiming nodded at Lee Hyun’s words.

“I asked the fellow disciples from the other peaks as well. They all said it was fine.”

“We couldn’t come up with anything better, either.”

Yue Wugou, who stood beside them, spoke.

Lee Hyun looked deeper into the valley.

His fellow disciples were adapting better than he had expected.

Song Qiming had informed a nearby Baoguang Temple outpost of the spirit vein’s location and the name of their newly established sect, while Fang Jiyun had negotiated terms for purchasing medicinal ingredients from merchant houses in the cultivator market.

The formation masters who had come with them installed a concealment formation to hide the sect and defensive formations to protect their residences. The artifact refiners were making the equipment needed for the alchemy chamber and furnishings for the disciples’ quarters.

It would take more time to properly cultivate the spirit fields, but they could still practice alchemy with purchased medicinal ingredients.

A few days earlier, they had delivered their first commissioned batch of pills. Once money began coming in, everyone’s expressions brightened considerably.

‘This should be good enough.’

Lee Hyun made several rounds of the surrounding area. He saw no demon beasts that could threaten them. There were no demon-beast dens or unusual presences either in the lower reaches of the valley or in the underground rock layers.

Of course, there was no guarantee that nothing would ever happen, but he could not stay here forever waiting for a demon beast that might never come.

These people were not children. They were full-fledged Foundation Establishment cultivators from the Danxiao Sect. Lee Hyun decided to stop treating them like children.

That evening, Lee Hyun drank tea with Song Qiming.

“I’ll head out tomorrow morning.”

“I see. Has it already come to that?”

Fang Jiyun, who had been organizing the account books beside them, stopped what he was doing.

“You’re leaving already?”

“Didn’t we agree from the start that I would leave once I saw you properly settled in?”

“That is true, but....”

Song Qiming handed Lee Hyun a small jade token.

“Whenever rogue cultivator life gets dull, come visit us. We’ll always have a place for you to stay.”

“Haha, I will.”

...

The next morning.

Several people came outside the sect to see him off.

Yue Wugou patted Lee Hyun on the shoulder.

“Next time you come, bring some good spirit wine with you.”

“Shouldn’t Senior Brother be the one buying it for me?”

“I have a sect to build now, don’t I? I can’t go spending spirit stones carelessly.”

As Yue Wugou shamelessly made excuses, Mei Sujun shot him a sidelong glance.

“If you send Junior Brother Li on errands like that, won’t he find it too troublesome to ever come back?”

Lee Hyun snickered.

Fang Jiyun gave him a fist-and-palm salute.

“Junior Brother, thank you for everything. May fortune accompany you on the road ahead, and may you attain longevity.”

“I owe Senior Brother Fang a great deal as well. May the road ahead be smooth and prosperous for you!”

After offering his final farewell to Song Qiming, Lee Hyun rose into the air.

The sect and its new signboard gradually receded into the distance.

Three days later.

The backyard of a general store in a small cultivator market.

Lee Hyun sat in a chair wearing a white deer mask.

The Qi Refining cultivator across from him stood straight-backed with both hands clasped respectfully.

“Elder White Deer. Your guide will arrive shortly.”

“Very well.”

Lee Hyun raised his teacup.

The identity he was using this time was that of a Two Heavens Society Elder whom the society head had sent to Xu Kingdom.

Of course, no such Elder had originally existed.

He had invented him himself!

Word had already been sent through the existing contact network that Elder White Deer, trusted by the society head, was coming to inspect the situation in Xu Kingdom, and a gathering had been arranged accordingly.

The members here had never even seen the society head in his badger mask, so there was no need for Lee Hyun to appear under the society head’s identity himself.

‘Come to think of it, isn’t the meeting place underneath here?’

Lee Hyun examined the ground beneath his feet.

He had assumed they would descend beneath the storeroom as usual, or use some hidden passage beside a well.

Instead, the guide opened another back door and led him out of the cultivator market.

‘Just where is this meeting place...?’

...

After leaving the cultivator market and traveling along the edge of the Cangmang Forest, they came upon a valley filled with mist between two cliffs.

At the designated spot, the guide raised a spirit tablet, and a faint light spread outward. A section of the cliff blocking their path soon rippled like water.

There was a road beyond it.

Following the road inward revealed several low halls, storehouses, and a broad open yard one after another. A small flying boat undergoing repairs sat off to one side of the yard.

‘...?’

Lee Hyun turned his gaze toward the inner cliff, then stopped for a moment.

A gigantic badger clung to the cliff face.

It was a stone statue that looked five or six zhang (about 16.5–19.8 m) tall. With its forepaws planted on a boulder as it gazed down over the valley, it looked surprisingly majestic.

‘...What the hell is this?’

A familiar phrase had been carved into the stone tablet beneath it.

「Approach this as though you are laying the foundation for an empire where even your descendants will serve the Two Heavens Society and many families will live for generations.」

Lee Hyun stared at it for a moment.

Those were his own words.

‘.......’

He had tossed them in almost as an afterthought while telling them to expand their influence northward.

Seeing Lee Hyun staring at the statue, the guide carefully explained.

“It was erected so that we would never forget the Society Head’s words.”

“I see.”

Lee Hyun walked farther inside.

Masked cultivators were waiting in front of one of the halls.

The person standing at the front wore a heron mask. The aura flowing from his body was at mid-stage Foundation Establishment.

He bowed deeply.

“I am Heron, in charge of affairs in western Xu Kingdom. Greetings, Elder.”

The members behind him bowed in unison.

...

The reports began.

On the map spread across the table, cultivator markets, spirit veins, and trade routes had been marked in different colors.

Heron began by explaining the underground vein seats.

“There are three places we stopped using last year. Demon beasts began passing through them, and after investigating, it appeared that a Tier 2 demon beast had settled nearby. We temporarily assigned the members to other vein seats and refunded the spirit stones corresponding to their unused time.”

When Lee Hyun nodded, Heron continued.

“Things are a little different here compared to the south. Finding a Tier 2 spirit vein itself is not particularly difficult. The problem comes after we find one.”

He pointed to several markings on the map in turn.

“There are too many demon beasts.”

A cultivator beside him wearing a brown mountain-goat mask spoke.

“Our clan didn’t have enough people to guard our spirit fields, so we began taking turns going out with two neighboring clans. Somehow, they ended up joining the Two Heavens Society as well. Membership continued to grow that way, and now thirteen cultivation clans are connected to the Two Heavens Society in one way or another.”

Lee Hyun looked at the map again.

‘The Two Heavens Society has turned into an alliance of rogue cultivator clans...’

They had initially begun by using underground vein seats, just as the original Two Heavens Society did, but Tier 2 spirit veins were not particularly rare in this region. There was no reason they could not simply settle aboveground.

As the environment changed, so did the Two Heavens Society’s way of operating.

In this harsh land where demon beasts appeared frequently, the underlying strength of the Two Heavens Society manifested in a different way. It became the central point around which nearby people joined forces.

The Two Heavens Society’s members could pool their medicinal ingredients for sale, making it easier to negotiate with merchant houses, and they could also obtain supplies or seeds difficult to find here through members in other countries.

Since joining brought tangible benefits, the Two Heavens Society gained more and more members.

“But it would be unwise for the Two Heavens Society to become too visible. Does everyone in each clan know about the Society?”

“No. Only the clan head and a few people responsible for communications know. Everyone else believes we are simply clans that trade with and help one another. We strictly observe the original rules.”

Heron paused briefly.

“Much of what we do now is different from what the Society originally did, so I was uncertain how you would view it, Elder.”

Lee Hyun leaned back in his chair.

“You should operate according to the circumstances here. As long as information about the Two Heavens Society and its members does not leak, I have no objection.”

“Thank you.”

Reports followed regarding Baoguang Temple’s patrol zones, forbidden areas, and the demon beasts that had recently been subjugated. Thus far, Baoguang Temple had never taken issue with anyone connected to the Two Heavens Society.

“Never interfere with or provoke Baoguang Temple.”

“I will keep that firmly in mind.”

The discussion then moved on to cultivators arriving from the south.

Large numbers of cultivators from the Danxiao Sect, Biluo Sect, and Wangu Sect had poured into Xuan Kingdom, but not many had made it as far as Xu Kingdom yet.

“When accepting cultivators from the south, vet them according to the existing rules.”

Lee Hyun thought for a moment before adding,

“Avoid friction with cultivators from the Danxiao Sect whenever possible. They have many alchemists, so establishing good trade relations with them should prove useful.”

“Understood.”

...

After the reports were finished.

“Take a look at these for me. I’d like them appraised. See whether they can be sold here as well.”

Lee Hyun began taking items out of several storage pouches.

A set of curved flying blades appeared on the table. Next came a gourd, two shields, a pair of bracers, and a short spear. All of them were high-grade magic tools.

When various Tier 2 talismans began piling up after them, one of the nearby members hurriedly brought over another small table.

Next came mid-grade magic tools and spare weapons. Bottles containing all sorts of pills, including Qi-Restoring Pills and Detoxification Pills, were lined up as well. There were even several bottles of cultivation pills intended for Foundation Establishment cultivators.

As magic tools and pill bottles continued appearing without end, another member hurriedly carried over a large third table.

Lee Hyun nodded and opened the next storage pouch. A split human-skin shield dropped onto the table.

Clack.

Blue Toad, who had been preparing an account book at one side of the room, flinched.

Blackened, shriveled tendons were visible between the severed layers of human skin. Beside it lay an intact heart-protecting mirror, the spare magic tool of the cultivator who had wielded the human-skin shield.

The belongings of the gu warrior who had sprayed insect silk in front of the archer also came out. A short sword, two flying blades, spirit materials used to repair magic tools, containers filled with demon blood and medicinal powder. There were even pills for replenishing qi and blood and a travel spirit token from Qianyang Kingdom.

Next came a long box. When the lid opened, a metallic gleam was revealed inside. Eight magic-tool-grade arrows.

There were also two spare bowstrings, unfinished arrowheads, and spirit materials used for bow repairs.

Then came a bow broken cleanly in two. Heron’s gaze stopped on the severed ends.

“This is....”

It was a supreme-grade magic tool.

Its joint had been destroyed, but the quality of the remaining restrictions and spirit materials was unmistakable.

Lee Hyun put the broken bow away again.

“Hmm... this wasn’t one I meant to sell.”

Last came a flying sword, a mid-grade defensive magic tool, and several wooden boxes.

They had belonged to the demonic cultivator who had died trying to ambush him from behind.

The flying sword had merely lost its owner and remained perfectly intact. Papers listing the names and weights of the spirit materials were attached inside the wooden boxes.

All three tables were full.

Among the spoils Lee Hyun had obtained from the cultivators of the Nanming Twelve-Sect Alliance, he had already set aside the spirit stones and anything worth researching. He had only taken out what remained.

The things he did not take out included the first half of the 《Mist-Condensing Art》, records on raising Life-Bound Gu, an unfinished shell magic tool, a Mirage Clam pearl, shell fragments with formation inscriptions still intact, and various spirit materials. He also put the broken bow limbs he had just taken out into that storage pouch.

He had separately kept a jade slip called the 《Spirit Bow and Arrow Maintenance Record》, which he had found in one of the storage pouches acquired while escorting the flying boat.

It described how to straighten warped bow limbs, how to adjust where force concentrated after changing a bowstring, and how to inscribe connected restrictions onto flexible spirit materials that repeatedly bent and flexed.

Once he had laid out all the spoils he intended to sell, excluding everything he had set aside, the hall fell silent.

...

The members gathered around the tables and began appraising the items.

Their hands moved faster and faster.

Blue Toad felt chills run down his spine as he examined the spoils.

There were far too many unused talismans.

‘What in the world... Did his enemies not even have time to use their talismans or flee while fighting the Elder?’

He looked at the split human-skin shield lying on the table. Its perfectly smooth cut was frightening enough, but somehow the intact heart-protecting mirror and flying sword beside it felt even more horrifying.

‘Were they taken down before they could even use their magic tools? These aren’t newly bought items, either. There are signs of use on the grips and straps...’

Blue Toad cautiously asked,

“Elder. Did you... bring all these from the south?”

“Yes. I ran into a few troublesome fellows on the way here, so I picked up some things.”

The Elder answered as though it were nothing of consequence.

‘On the way here?’

The words echoed through Blue Toad’s mind.

What kind of places had Kun Kingdom and Cang Kingdom become?

They were lands where great sects had abandoned their sects and fled, and where rumors said even Golden Core cultivators had died.

Yet while passing through such places, he had collected this much loot from demonic cultivators.

‘A mere Elder of the Two Heavens Society is this powerful...?!’

...

Heron did not jump to conclusions as quickly as the newly initiated Blue Toad.

Spoils could be obtained through many different means.

They might have belonged to people the Elder had personally killed, or they might have been divided among several other Elders.

That was not what mattered.

Why had the Elder before him brought out items like these on his very first visit?

‘This is... a test!’

Could they identify magic tools from the south? Would they recklessly pay full value for suspicious goods? Did they know where each different kind of item should be sold?

‘Of course. What is the most important quality a member of an organization that rules the world from the shadows must possess? The ability to safely fence stolen goods and make a huge profit from them!’

Despite belonging to the secretive Two Heavens Society, Heron had only ever handled extremely wholesome and legal(?) affairs until now. The thought that he had finally been entrusted with something shady filled him with tremendous excitement.

This was exactly the sort of work a ruthless and terrifying organization, the kind he had long dreamed of, ought to be doing!

...

After carefully inspecting everything with the other members, Heron brought the account book over to Lee Hyun.

“Elder. Here are the appraisal results.”

As Lee Hyun examined the account book, Heron continued.

“There is no need for you to wait long, Elder. We can pool the Society’s reserve funds with spirit stones from members who wish to purchase the goods and buy everything from you ourselves. We can offer three hundred mid-grade spirit stones.”

‘Huh? That much?’

“Very good.”

Heron nervously studied Lee Hyun’s reaction.

“...Are you certain we may proceed with that amount? Did we appraise everything correctly?”

“Hmm? Is there a problem?”

“No. We will have everything prepared by tomorrow morning.”

“Then do so.”

Lee Hyun poured himself some tea.

‘It would’ve been a hassle to sell all this at a cultivator market... This worked out nicely.’

...

The next day.

After receiving the spirit stones, Lee Hyun gifted some of the empty storage pouches to the members and finished packing his belongings.

The cumbersome pile of spoils had vanished cleanly.

“You people are... truly impressive.”

Heron bowed.

“If you entrust such matters to us in the future, we will not disappoint you.”

“There is no need to work for my sake. Simply keep the Two Heavens Society safe and follow the rules.”

Heron straightened his posture.

‘He holds the position of an Elder within the organization, yet refuses to pursue personal gain... Just how terrifying must the society head be for even someone like him to watch his conduct so carefully?’

Lee Hyun watched the members dividing up the stolen goods among themselves with satisfaction.

‘Creating the Two Heavens Society really was worth it.’

It earned him spirit stones, gathered information, and now it even sold off his odds and ends for him.

What a useful organization.

...

A city in Xu Kingdom.

Lee Hyun stood inside a bookstore.

The shelves held many books he had never seen in Kun Kingdom. There were stories about the demon beasts and rogue cultivators of the Cangmang Forest, as well as adventure tales about monks vanquishing monsters.

“I’ll take everything from here to here.”

...

Lee Hyun headed southeast through Xu Kingdom.

He avoided large cultivator markets and roads crowded with cultivators, periodically checking the terrain and the surrounding presences as he traveled.

Unlike war-torn Kun Kingdom, however, Xu Kingdom was largely peaceful.
