After taking a roundabout route of more than one hundred thousand li (about 39,200 km), a familiar mountain range finally appeared.

It was a remote land at the far northwestern edge of Kun Kingdom.

Lee Hyun surveyed his surroundings for a while before sinking beneath the ground.

...

Tunnel No. 3.

Ssssk.

Squeak?

The fuzzbees swarmed around him.

When Lee Hyun held out a hand, the first one to reach him landed on the back of it. The latecomers squeezed in beside it.

“Have you all been well?”

Squeak, squeak!

When he opened the spirit-insect pouch, the fuzzbees that had traveled with him poured out, making the cavern even noisier.

Lee Hyun first filled the water tank with the Spirit Rain Art, then disconnected one of the bamboo water pipes, washed out the inside, and reinstalled it.

After that, he inspected the passages connecting the spirit fields, storage room, and cavern one by one.

Once he confirmed that nothing was wrong, a warm, comfortable feeling washed over him, as though he had finally returned home.

‘Home really is the best.’

Lee Hyun went to the storeroom and set down several storage pouches.

He then took out the popular novels he had bought and neatly arranged them on the shelves. Seeing the shelves filled with new books made anticipation rise within him at the thought of setting off on adventures through their stories.

“I should savor them.”

Next, he organized his jade slips.

《Definitive Explanation of Formations》, 《Commentary on Formation Deployment by Terrain》, 《Spirit Material Refining Method》, 《Comprehensive Guide to Magic-Tool Restrictions》, 《Essentials of Restriction Inscription》

These were inheritances he had acquired by spending every last contribution point before leaving the Danxiao Sect.

Beside them, he placed the 《Profound Yin White Bone True Scripture》 and 《Introductory Guide to Soul Stone Inscription》 that he had been studying for some time, along with the book containing Guo Zhenming’s annotations.

He also took out the jade slip for the 《Spirit-Concealing Formation》.

‘I should start building this soon.’

To do that, he first needed to properly master the basics of Tier 2 formations and artifact-refining art.

In the past, he had lacked inheritances and had been burdened with alchemy work assigned by the sect.

Now he had inheritances to study and nothing but time.

The various cultivators of the Nanming Twelve-Sect Alliance had even provided him with plenty of spirit materials for practice.

He sorted the spoils he had kept instead of selling into separate compartments beneath the workbench.

...

A few days later.

A Bonefuzz lay beside the workbench.

Lee Hyun examined the legs on either side of its torso.

Then he held one of the broken bow limbs from his spoils in one hand and pressed lightly on its tip with the other.

‘It’s remarkably tough.’

Examining the severed end, he saw that several different spirit materials had been layered thinly together. Different materials had been used for the outer and inner sections, with fine restrictions running between them.

As he compared it against the explanations in the 《Spirit Bow and Arrow Maintenance Record》, its structure gradually began to make sense.

Lee Hyun lifted one of Bonefuzz’s legs.

A faint click came from within as he bent and straightened the joint.

‘Could I use this here as well?’

Bonefuzz could already fly, but there was still plenty of room for improvement in the way it pushed off the ground. Its movements were somewhat stiff when abruptly changing direction or darting forward low to the ground.

What if it could store force in its legs and release it all at once?

‘If I can make them like these bow limbs, it should reduce the impact when it lands as well. But if they bend too easily, would they fail to support the torso under strain? There’s a lot to study.’

...

Lee Hyun then made the rounds of the spirit fields, checking the medicine age of the spirit plants and reviewing his long-term plan for refining Foundation Establishment Pills.

610 years later.

The cultivation chamber of Tunnel No. 3.

Faint spirit light flowed from Lee Hyun’s entire body as he lay on the ground.

The light lingered briefly over his skin before sinking back inside.

Hooooo―

Lee Hyun slowly exhaled.

Even after opening his eyes, he remained still for quite some time.

His divine sense traveled from the tips of his toes to the top of his head, then swept through the depths of his body once more.

No trace of underdeveloped energy remained anywhere.

“Finally... my entire body has reached Qi Refining Great Perfection!”

He clenched and unclenched his hand.

His lower dantian remained at Foundation Establishment Stage 6.

Over the long years, he had cultivated the rest of his body, which had previously remained at the beginning of Qi Refining Stage 9.

Of course, he had not spent all 610 years lying in the cultivation chamber.

He tended the spirit fields, practiced techniques, made magic tools and broke them, then melted the broken ones back down again.

He completed the Spirit-Concealing Formation using formation devices he had personally refined, and he installed new components in Bonefuzz’s legs based on the structure of the bow limbs.

Occasionally, he went aboveground to obtain necessary supplies or buy books.

Although Tunnel No. 3 remained his base, he usually cultivated at a Two Heavens Society vein seat comparable to a Tier 2 spirit vein. Had he only needed to fill a single lower dantian, the cultivation might have taken just over a decade, but filling his entire body required dozens of times more spiritual qi.

As he traveled back and forth between the vein seat and the tunnel to cultivate, this much time had passed before he knew it.

Lee Hyun took a stone tablet from his storage pouch. The wooden board he had used as a handmade status window kept rotting, so he had replaced it with stone.

After smoothing away several old characters with the Soil-Softening Art, he engraved new ones with the Yang Metal Art.

【Age: 2,141】

【Realm: Foundation Establishment Stage 6 (lower dantian), Qi Refining Great Perfection (rest of body)】

【Spiritual Power: 1,548 → 1,908】

【Constitution: Primordial Body, Qi Refining Great Perfection】

He looked down at the stone tablet.

“I’m over two thousand years old now.”

...

Spirit Field No. 3-2.

Lee Hyun knelt beside a Jade-Condensing Grass plant and carefully brushed away the soil.

A jade-colored bulb appeared among its roots.

‘Its medicine age is... around 230 years.’

The Jade-Condensing Grass had finally reached the medicine age specified in the Foundation Establishment Pill recipe. Taking care not to damage the bulb or fine roots, Lee Hyun dug out a generous amount of soil around one plant and transferred it onto a jade tray.

...

Spirit Field No. 2-3.

Rather than taking roots from the spirit field containing the Spirit-Storing Ginseng he had planted first, Lee Hyun selected suitable roots from a field established later.

The Spirit-Storing Ginseng planted earlier had already exceeded the maximum medicine age specified in the Foundation Establishment Pill recipe.

He then descended to Spirit Field No. 3-5, where the Fire-Heart Orchids were cultivated.

Behind the stone slabs erected to keep them from directly receiving the heat of the earth-fire vein, the Lesser Yang Stones steadily produced lesser yang qi.

The fine lines inside the Fire-Heart Orchids’ red petals were vivid.

Lee Hyun sat before them and repeatedly checked their medicinal potency.

They possessed the same properties as those he had seen in the Huatian Secret Realm.

“These are ready too.”

He placed the prepared Fire-Heart Orchid onto a separate jade tray.

All three main ingredients had been gathered.

...

The alchemy chamber of Tunnel No. 3.

The three main ingredients and twenty-six kinds of supplementary medicinal ingredients had been laid out.

Hummm―

As the formation inscriptions on the floor lit up, earth fire flowed through the burner and gathered beneath the pill furnace.

Lee Hyun formed a hand seal, and the flames split into countless fine strands.

Flame-Threading Art.

Countless flame threads crossed over one another.

His command of the Flame-Threading Art was so refined that if the disciples of Yanxia Peak at the Danxiao Sect long ago had seen him, they might have mistaken it for Golden Core Elder Tan Yunsheng himself using the technique.

Lee Hyun’s hands began moving in a dazzling blur.

...

A few days later.

Despite his extraordinary mastery of techniques and his skill as a Tier 2 alchemist, Lee Hyun failed to refine the Foundation Establishment Pill three whole times!

No wonder it was renowned as such a difficult pill to refine.

Even so, after repeatedly recalling the sight of Tan Yunsheng refining it, Lee Hyun succeeded in producing Foundation Establishment Pills on his fourth attempt.

Clack.

When he opened the lid, a beautiful auspicious glow briefly illuminated the surroundings, and two ivory-colored pills floated upward.

Only after checking them several times with both his divine sense and the Aura-Reading Art did Lee Hyun finally smile.

“It worked.”

These were the first Foundation Establishment Pills he had ever refined himself.

...

One month later.

Small jade bottles stood in a row atop the table.

Each bottle bore a Spirit-Sealing Talisman, and beside them were records of the date of refinement and the pill-inspection results.

After checking the final bottle, Lee Hyun closed the account book.

72 Foundation Establishment Pills.

“This should be enough.”

There were still plenty of main ingredients left in the spirit fields, so if he ran short, he could simply make more.

Lee Hyun closed the burner, checked the formation inscriptions, and left the alchemy chamber.

...

A few days later.

After resting thoroughly, Lee Hyun lay in the center of the cultivation chamber.

He had ordered the fuzzbees not to come near the cultivation chamber and had closed the stone door.

After one final inward examination of his body, Lee Hyun took out the first Foundation Establishment Pill.

Gulp.

Lee Hyun held the medicinal strength back from rushing into his lower dantian and focused it on a small region outside it. Once that part of his body began refining spiritual qi into liquid true essence on its own, he stabilized it thoroughly before moving on to the next region.

...

Time passed.

One by one, the bottles containing Foundation Establishment Pills emptied.

...

One year later.

A faint mist drifted through the cultivation chamber.

Hummm―

At some point, Lee Hyun felt something strange.

He had moved only one part of his body, yet his entire body responded along with it.

Thump.

Stone dust on the floor of the cultivation chamber floated lightly into the air.

Lee Hyun remained motionless as he digested the final medicinal strength of the Foundation Establishment Pill and refined the newly absorbed spiritual qi.

At last, a mysterious radiance bloomed from his entire body, and his reclining form naturally floated into the air.

Lee Hyun opened his eyes and smiled.

“It has been a long journey.”

Now that not only his lower dantian but his entire body could produce liquefied spiritual power, the flow of drawing in and sending out spiritual power from head to toe became far smoother.

‘I see. I already had a great deal of spiritual power before, but because it existed in different states, there must have been a bottleneck in its flow.’

Lee Hyun turned upright and set his feet on the floor, then took the stone tablet from his storage pouch.

Light from the Yang Metal Art flowed from his fingertips.

【Age: 2,142】

【Realm: Foundation Establishment Stage 6 (lower dantian), Foundation Establishment Stage 1 (rest of body)】

【Spiritual Power: 1,908 → 3,672】

【Constitution: Primordial Body, Foundation Establishment Stage 1】

【Cultivation Art: Primordial One-Qi Art (Foundation Establishment Section)】

【Techniques (Major Attainment): Great Unity Heavenly Dipper Sword Art, Spirit-Refining Essentials, ...】

【Techniques (Perfection): Skywalking Art, Condensed-Essence Grasping Hand, Flame-Threading Art, Spirit-Guarding Essence-Protecting Method, ...】

【Skills: Alchemy Tier 2, Formations Tier 2, Artifact Refining Tier 2, Puppet Crafting Tier 2, Spirit-Plant Cultivation Tier 2, Insect Control Tier 2】

Lee Hyun set the stone tablet against the cultivation chamber wall and admired it for a long while.

He was savoring the sight of his accomplishments.

“Excellent!”

Chapter 72

A few days later.

Scritch. Scritch.

At the faint sound from the tunnel wall, Lee Hyun turned his head.

A hole sealed with earth and hardened mucus was cracking open from the inside. A moment later, two short forelegs poked through the gap.

Crack.

Dry earth crumbled away.

A ball of golden fur poked its head out. It paused halfway through, then kicked its hind legs about as though its rump had gotten stuck.

Lee Hyun widened the entrance slightly with his finger.

Plop.

The fuzzbee dropped onto his palm and shook itself off. Its newly exposed fur was still a little damp, and a transparent membrane clung to the tips of its wings.

“You slept for quite a while this time.”

Squeak.

A familiar response came through the Spirit-Nurturing Seal.

Lee Hyun examined its body. He could sense the stable aura of a Tier 2 spirit insect within it.

It was one of the three fuzzbees that had mutated long ago after eating Meridian-Linking Jade Silkworms.

...

Over the years, Lee Hyun had also learned a fair amount about fuzzbee ecology.

Fuzzbees that had remained active for a long time would gradually eat less and move more sluggishly, until one day they dug small burrows into the wall. After sealing the entrance with earth and mucus, they would remain out of sight for years at a time.

At first, he had thought they were dead.

But after confirming that spiritual power and life force were still circulating steadily inside them, Lee Hyun had refrained from carelessly opening the burrows.

When they finally emerged again much later, they left behind thin husks.

The spiritual power and soul within them remained unchanged. The Spirit-Nurturing Seal was still intact, and they had forgotten neither the commands they had learned nor the knack for controlling Bonefuzz.

They were undergoing long periods of dormancy while gradually replacing their aging tissues.

After searching through the countless jade slips and books he had acquired over the years, he learned that there were indeed spirit insects capable of living for extremely long periods.

Even among Tier 2 spirit insects, lifespans and growth cycles varied greatly from species to species.

He had never found any records of spirit insects resembling fuzzbees, so he still had no idea how long they could live.

However, although several generations had already come and gone among the smaller fuzzbees in the spirit fields, those that had first reached Tier 2 were still alive, repeatedly falling into these long sleeps and awakening again.

...

Lee Hyun used the Spirit Rain Art over a stone bowl, then mixed in a little Hundred-Flower Honey.

The resulting liquid was one of the few things fuzzbees ate besides spirit insects.

Still sluggish after waking from its long sleep, the fuzzbee gripped the rim of the bowl with its forelegs and drank for quite some time. Once its abdomen had grown plump, it stretched its wings a few times before flying toward the workbench.

A Bonefuzz puppet that had just finished undergoing inspection lay there with its chest cover open.

Zip.

The fuzzbee slipped inside.

Click.

Bonefuzz took two steps and briefly stumbled, but quickly regained its balance. It then crouched low and lightly sprang onto the workbench.

Squeak!

Lee Hyun smiled.

“You wake up after all this time and immediately climb back in? Is it really that much fun?”

Bonefuzz raised one foreleg.

At the sound it made, fuzzbees began appearing from all over. Several that saw the first one inside circled around the closed chest cover.

“All right. It’s been a while, so let’s go out for a stroll.”

Buzzzzz―

...

A rocky mountain several hundred li (well over 100 km) from Tunnel No. 3.

Deep within layers of interlocking rocky ridges was a long, narrow valley. It was difficult to see inside from the outside, and the valley floor was covered not with water but with broken stones and dry sand.

Lee Hyun surveyed the surroundings for a while. After confirming that there were no people or demon beasts nearby, he opened his storage pouch and took out the Bonefuzz puppets.

He currently had forty-eight Bonefuzz puppets, and their designs had changed considerably compared to long ago.

The bone plates covering their backs and chests had been divided into sections so they could be easily replaced, while separate components reinforced the areas most prone to impacts. Curved plates made by layering different spirit materials had also been fitted inside their legs.

They were the result of his research into the broken bow limb he had obtained from the archer and the Spirit Bow and Arrow Maintenance Record.

Lee Hyun opened the bodies of the Bonefuzz puppets, and the fuzzbees pouring out of the spirit-insect pouch entered them with practiced ease.

Those that failed to claim a Bonefuzz settled on Lee Hyun’s shoulders and arms instead.

When Lee Hyun stretched out a hand, a round stone buried in the sand floated into the air.

“Bring it back.”

He threw the stone deeper into the valley.

Twang!

The springy plates inside their legs bent like bowstrings, then snapped straight.

The Bonefuzz in front shot forward low enough to skim the ground, then used a boulder blocking its path as a foothold and launched diagonally into the air.

The Bonefuzz puppets behind it scattered in unison.

While one chased the stone in a straight line, two others alternated between kicking off the cliffs on either side, racing ahead as though tightening an encirclement.

Hummm―

The Bonefuzz that reached the landing point first activated its flight-suppressing restriction, causing the stone slicing through the air to lurch sideways and be dragged toward it.

Another Bonefuzz barreling in from the opposite side activated its restriction as well. The two pulls locked against each other, holding the stone taut in midair.

Taking advantage of the opening, another Bonefuzz sprang up from below like a shadow, swiftly snatched the stone with its forelegs, and hugged it against its chest.

Squeak!

With a triumphant cry, it abruptly changed direction and fled, while the other Bonefuzz puppets gave chase.

Lee Hyun stared at them in disbelief.

“I told you to bring it to me....”

The Bonefuzz carrying the stone slid behind a massive boulder. But when the group burst out from the opposite side, the stone was already in another one’s arms.

A swarm of round bodies came pouring after it.

Clatter-clatter-clatter!

The lively sound of bony legs striking rock walls echoed throughout the valley.

Whenever they changed direction sharply, the plates inside their joints flexed and straightened. Any puppet that lost its balance in midair used its flight restriction to right itself before kicking off the cliff again.

Their movements as they stole the stone and shook one another off were far more agile and coordinated than before. It might have looked like simple play, but their mobility and control over rough terrain had improved tremendously.

One of the fuzzbees on Lee Hyun’s shoulder squeaked loudly beside his ear.

Squeak-squeak-squeak-squeak-squeak!

“All right. You can have a turn next time.”

...

Quite some time later.

The sand was covered in a chaotic web of Bonefuzz footprints.

Lee Hyun seized the stone and pulled it toward himself. Two Bonefuzz puppets that stubbornly refused to let go were dragged along with it.

“That’s enough playing. Come out.”

Their chest covers opened, and balls of golden fur emerged before flying back into the spirit-insect pouch.

Lee Hyun put the empty Bonefuzz puppets into his storage pouch, then finally returned the fuzzbees clinging to his body to the spirit-insect pouch as well.

The valley fell silent.

“Now, then....”

It was time to examine his own body.

Lee Hyun’s feet rose into the air.

The instant he tilted his body slightly forward, the cliffs of the valley seemed to be sucked backward at terrifying speed.

Whoosh―

Before the sound of his passage through the air could even catch up, the rocky ridge that had been far in the distance was suddenly right before his eyes.

His body turned at a right angle in midair.

He flipped over, plunged downward, then shot upward again in the next instant.

After achieving Whole-Body Foundation Establishment, being in the air felt so natural that there hardly seemed any reason to keep his feet on the ground at all.

Lee Hyun came to a complete stop in midair and drew the Profound Gate Sword.

Shing.

The black line running down the center of the blade glowed white-hot and let out a piercing sword cry.

Swish.

He casually slashed the sword diagonally.

Flash!

Sword light split the air and swept across the opposite cliff.

A hair-thin crack appeared where the sword light passed, and the house-sized upper section of the cliff revealed a perfectly smooth cross-section as it slid free into the air.

Just before the enormous mass of rock plunged to the ground, Lee Hyun extended his left hand.

Humm!

A giant hand formed in midair as he unleashed the Condensed-Essence Grasping Hand.

It was on an entirely different level from before. What had once been a translucent shape now looked almost solid, with a faint blue sheen.

Boom!

The giant hand shot out as though tearing into the mountainside and caught the falling section of cliff in midair. Even after the giant hand took the full force of its tremendous fall, not a single finger so much as trembled.

Lee Hyun closed his hand.

BOOOOM!

The rock crumbled like clay under the giant hand’s grip, exploding with a thunderous roar as countless fragments burst in every direction.

Lee Hyun did not retreat even as the debris hurtled toward him.

Fwoosh!

Using the spherical light screen of the Qi Sphere Barrier as its framework, the flames of the Flame-Threading Art instantly expanded into a curtain of fire.

Hissssss―

Every falling rock fragment that touched it glowed red, softened, and melted away in midair. Molten stone and scorching winds churned beyond the curtain, yet not so much as a speck of dust reached Lee Hyun inside the flames.

After withdrawing the fire, Lee Hyun looked down at the Profound Gate Sword in his hand.

Trrring....

The blade was trembling faintly. The restriction running through its center had been unable to withstand the influx of spiritual power and was giving off thin wisps of smoke.

It was sturdy even among high-grade magic tools, yet this was what happened when Lee Hyun poured his spiritual power into it all at once.

‘It can’t handle it.’

Magic tools were divided into low grade, mid grade, high grade, and supreme grade.

Among supreme-grade magic tools, those made with especially outstanding materials and craftsmanship were often called exceptional supreme-grade magic tools. Even cultivators at late Foundation Establishment or Great Perfection could not easily obtain one.

Anything better belonged to an entirely different category and was no longer called a magic tool, but a magic treasure.

Magic treasures were made primarily from Tier 3 or higher spirit materials and required the magical power and nurturing of a Golden Core cultivator during refining, making them incomparably more precious than magic tools.

Because of that, when a rogue cultivator without any backing had just achieved Core Formation, it was common for them to continue using an exceptional supreme-grade magic tool because they could not obtain a magic treasure.

‘Both the quality and quantity of my spiritual power have changed. I need at least a supreme-grade magic tool, or perhaps an exceptional supreme-grade magic tool.’

Lee Hyun put the Profound Gate Sword into his storage pouch.

He could buy a finished one, or if he obtained suitable spirit materials and a crafting method, he could try making one himself.

However, becoming a Tier 2 artifact refiner did not mean he could freely make every supreme-grade or exceptional supreme-grade magic tool.

Just as even a Tier 2 formation master was most familiar with the formations they primarily studied, refining a particular supreme-grade magic tool required separate research into how to weave together suitable restrictions and harmonize the properties of multiple spirit materials.

‘I have plenty of time. I can think it over slowly.’

After erasing the traces of his spiritual power from the surroundings, he disappeared beneath the ground.

...

A few days later, in the storeroom of Tunnel No. 3.

Lee Hyun opened the pouches containing his spirit stones one after another.

Approximately 1,200 mid-grade spirit stones.

They had accumulated from the spoils he had acquired through battle over the years, along with the spirit stones he earned by selling spirit plants and pills.

Some were also his share from brokering trades as society head of the Two Heavens Society or supplying its members with the items they needed.

Even though he kept his margins small for the members’ convenience, the steady flow of transactions brought in spirit stones little by little.

In truth, the profits accumulated that way over some six hundred years had been much greater. At one point, he had possessed nearly twice as many spirit stones as he did now.

However, he had spent almost all the profits he earned as society head of the Two Heavens Society on learning various crafts and disciplines.

His biggest expenses had been soul stones, cinnabar and refined demon-beast blood for inscribing formation inscriptions and restrictions, and high-grade spirit materials for Bonefuzz frames. The mid-grade spirit stones consumed in operating the Bonefuzz puppets were no small expense either.

Thus, once the number of Bonefuzz puppets approached fifty, he stopped increasing their numbers and focused instead on repairing and improving the ones he already had.

Lee Hyun looked at the pile of failed components beneath the workbench.

‘At least I still have what I learned from all that...’

Another cultivator in his situation might have cut spending on Bonefuzz even further, but Lee Hyun’s spirit fields were filled with expensive spirit plants. If he wanted, he could simply sell them for more spirit stones, so he considered maintaining his current stock of mid-grade spirit stones more than enough.

‘Still... this time I should sell off a few spirit plants. I need to get a supreme-grade or exceptional supreme-grade magic tool...’

Lee Hyun walked through his spirit fields, considering which spirit plants to sell.

Several varieties had passed five hundred years of medicine age and become Tier 3 spirit plants. Selling only a few of them would likely bring in a considerable number of spirit stones.

The oldest were in Spirit Field No. 1-1.

The mother plants he had originally planted were already approaching seven hundred years of medicine age.

‘Selling even a few of these later should give me more than enough spirit stones.’

Guyan Market in northwestern Kun Kingdom.

Above the city gate hung a black flag embroidered with silver waves.

Lee Hyun followed the line inside.

The walls had grown taller.

When he had last visited a little over ten years ago, the stalls that now stood within the walls had still been spread across the open ground outside. New halls lined both sides of the streets, and the paving stones had been laid evenly enough for carts to pass.

Spirit tablets belonging to various merchant groups hung beside the toll station. Some even bore the name of the Nanming Sea.

More than six hundred years had passed since the Nanming Twelve-Sect Alliance took control of Kun Kingdom and Cang Kingdom.

During that time, the alliance had suffered several internal conflicts over the division of spirit veins. Long-serving Elders died, new Nascent Soul cultivators emerged, and the balance of power shifted.

Factions that had once belonged to the same sect sometimes split apart and raised separate banners, while sects that had declined severely came under the protection of other sects.

The sects of neighboring cultivation nations such as Xuan Kingdom had also reinforced their border strongholds. After several clashes, they established boundaries neither side would cross.

The name Nanming Twelve-Sect Alliance still remained, but for the time being, there were no signs that it intended to expand its territory further.

As time passed, the wartime tension also faded from Kun Kingdom, and the coming and going of merchant groups became commonplace.

In the Kun Kingdom of the present day, disputes over taxes and the prices of goods were far more common than anything else.

...

“We have this month’s entire quota prepared. However, the price of powdered Azure-Horn Deer is higher than last time....”

“The official procurement price is fixed.”

The gray-robed cultivator did not look up from the ledger.

The shopkeeper pressed his lips shut.

“...Understood.”

The clerks beside him began unloading wooden crates.

Not far away, two patrol cultivators were twisting a rogue cultivator’s arms behind his back as they dragged him away.

“I’m telling you, I paid first!”

“You can tell the Steward that.”

The onlookers made way on their own when the patrol cultivators approached.

The streets were crowded and business seemed brisk, but whenever someone wearing the insignia of the Nanming Twelve-Sect Alliance appeared, everyone around them became guarded.

...

Once Lee Hyun realized that Guyan Market was not suitable for trading Tier 3 spirit plants, he lost interest. After leaving the cultivator market, he stopped by the nearby county seat.

He had visited the place from time to time over the past six hundred years, yet even the city’s name had changed again since his last visit.

Women gathered around the well, while the aroma of grain dough baking over small roadside ovens drifted through the streets.

People stood in front of the government office, checking their names on a newly posted notice.

“Looks like the Gu-Rearing Institute is recruiting people again this year.”

“Think my second son could become a gu warrior if he went there?”

Lee Hyun passed through the crowd and entered a bookstore.

Many of the books on the shelves featured stories set at sea.

They told of mysterious islands, underwater cave abodes, and cultivators traveling between islands atop bizarre spirit beasts.

It was no longer unusual at all for place names from the Nanming Sea to appear in popular fiction in Kun Kingdom.

In those stories, the demonic cultivators of the Nanming Sea were usually cultured and dashing. They drank fine wine, settled grudges without hesitation, and often handed jade slips to protagonists who had lost their way.

Lee Hyun pulled out one book and flipped through a few pages.

‘This one might actually be entertaining.’

Beside it was another book collecting old accounts from the cultivation world.

He spotted the name Danxiao Sect and opened it, only to find a brief description of it as one of Kun Kingdom’s sects that had already vanished.

Below that was a note stating that several alchemy lineages of Taixuan Sect, along with small sects in Xuan Kingdom and Xu Kingdom, had carried on its inheritance.

Lee Hyun read for a moment before closing the book.

“I’ll take this one too.”

The shopkeeper approached.

“That one isn’t a novel, but a history book. I’m afraid it won’t be very entertaining...”

“I know.”

A little over twenty days later.

Lee Hyun entered western Xu Kingdom for the first time in quite a while.

Along the way, he passed through several cultivator markets and Two Heavens Society contact points, where he also confirmed the date of the gathering to be held in the west.

There was still plenty of time before the gathering.

While heading west, he changed course in front of a low mountain range.

A familiar stream ran down the slope and into the valley.

Lee Hyun took a small jade token from the storage pouch at his waist and brushed his thumb over its surface.

Eldest Senior Brother Song Qiming had given it to him long ago.

...

Yanxia Sect’s Mountain Gate stood atop a flight of stone steps.

Doors and a roof had been added where there had once been only pillars, and a low wall extended behind them.

Beyond the Mountain Gate was a courtyard where medicinal ingredients were laid out to dry. Higher up the slope stood tier upon tier of halls and disciples’ residences.

Thin smoke from the alchemy chamber drifted through the valley.

‘They’ve managed surprisingly well all this time.’

Lee Hyun gazed at the scene for a while.

During the first few decades, he had visited several times, but afterward, he stopped coming because of how old Li Dongsan should have been by then in the eyes of outsiders.

A very long time had passed since he had last personally entered this valley.

The Qi Refining disciple guarding the Mountain Gate rose to his feet.

“Greetings, Senior. What brings you here?”

Lee Hyun held out the jade token.

“I brought something belonging to someone with ties to this place. May I see your sect master?”

The disciple examined the jade token, then called another disciple from inside.

A short while later, a Foundation Establishment cultivator descended to the Mountain Gate.

He appeared to be a man in his forties. His clothes were neat, and his fingertips bore faint traces of handling medicinal ingredients.

“I am Xu Zheng’an, the sect master of Yanxia Sect.”

He cupped his hands, and Lee Hyun returned the greeting.

Xu Zheng’an accepted the jade token and examined both sides before sending his divine sense into it. When a faint pattern appeared within the token, his expression changed.

“May I ask... what relationship do you have with Senior Li Dongsan?”

“His inheritance passed through several generations before reaching me.”

Xu Zheng’an looked at the jade token once more.

“Please, come inside.”

...

Xu Zheng’an was the sixth sect master of Yanxia Sect.

The sect was still relatively small.

The disciples made their living primarily through alchemy and preparing medicinal ingredients, while a few learned formations and artifact-refining arts to maintain the sect’s various implements.

Two Qi Refining disciples were carrying medicinal ingredients across one side of the courtyard.

Xu Zheng’an led Lee Hyun into one of the halls.

It was the Ancestral Hall, where memorial tablets and portraits were enshrined.

Song Qiming.

Fang Jiyun.

Yue Wugou.

Lee Hyun’s gaze moved over the names one by one.

Beneath each was a brief account of their deeds and the years of their birth and death.

Mei Sujun’s memorial tablet was there as well. Beside it was a record somewhat longer than those accompanying the other tablets.

The only Golden Core cultivator in Yanxia Sect’s history.

She had supported the sect for many years and expanded its dealings with Baoguang Temple.

‘Come to think of it, I vaguely remember hearing that Senior Sister Mei had achieved Core Formation....’

Lee Hyun accepted a stick of incense and placed it before the tablets.

Xu Zheng’an waited silently beside him.

After leaving the Ancestral Hall, they headed to the neighboring building.

It was where documents from the sect’s founding and old artifacts were kept.

Several paintings hung on the walls.

Lee Hyun stopped in front of one of them.

「Founding Benefactor Li Dongsan」

The man in the painting was enormous.

Compared with the people painted beside him, he looked to be around nine chi (about 3 m) tall. His shoulders were broad, his arms thick, and he held a sword as tall as a man in one hand.

That much was fine.

The problem was his eyes.

Piercing blue sword light streamed from both of them.

‘...Who is this supposed to be?’

Lee Hyun stared at the painting for a moment.

Xu Zheng’an explained.

“No portrait from his lifetime survived, so later generations painted this based on accounts of his deeds.”

“His deeds?”

“The records left by Ancestral Master Yue Wugou describe them in detail. They say that every time he swung his sword, enemy cultivators fell one after another.”

Lee Hyun read the inscription beneath the painting.

「His gaze was like a sword, and his enemies dared not meet his eyes.」

Xu Zheng’an asked cautiously,

“Is it very different from what you were told he looked like?”

“Haha... I wouldn’t know either.”

...

While they were drinking tea, Xu Zheng’an brought over a small ledger.

“There is something I need to give you.”

He pointed to an entry in the ledger.

“These items were left with instructions that they be handed over if a successor of Senior Li Dongsan ever came here. They have been on the handover list for a very long time.”

Lee Hyun set down his teacup.

“What are they?”

“Would you like to visit somewhere first?”

...

On a low hill behind the sect.

Stone monuments stood in rows beneath old trees.

Xu Zheng’an stopped in front of one of them.

It was Yue Wugou’s grave.

Beside the gravestone was a round stone lid half buried in the earth.

Xu Zheng’an formed a hand seal, and a small formation inscription around the edge of the lid lit up. The earth shifted aside and the stone lid rose.

A narrow stone coffer lay beneath it.

Xu Zheng’an took out a wine jar.

Several layers of Spirit-Sealing Talismans covered the black earthenware jar. The outermost talisman was not particularly old, but those farther inside had yellowed with age.

A thin stone plaque was tied around the neck of the jar.

「To be given to Junior Brother Li or his successor if either comes.」

Xu Zheng’an said,

“We replaced the Spirit-Sealing Talismans at regular intervals. The seal beneath them is still intact.”

“I see.”

“I’m told Ancestral Master Yue buried this separately because it was excellent spirit wine. He drank every last drop of his own share... and ordered everyone not to touch this one.”

The corner of Lee Hyun’s mouth twitched slightly.

Xu Zheng’an set down the wine jar and two cups.

“I’ll return for you shortly.”

He descended the hill.

...

Lee Hyun removed the seals from the wine jar.

When he pulled out the stopper, a rich, mellow fragrance drifted out.

He poured one cup and placed it in front of the gravestone, then filled his own.

“So you did end up buying it after all, Senior Brother.”

Lee Hyun raised his cup.

The wine was surprisingly smooth.

...

That evening.

A wine jar and a small wooden box sat on the table in the guest room Yanxia Sect had provided.

Inside the wooden box were a letter from Mei Sujun and a jade slip.

Xu Zheng’an had said that the sect also kept a copy of the jade slip, so Lee Hyun was free to take the original and the letter with him.

Lee Hyun unfolded the paper.

The handwriting was small and neat.

「To Junior Brother Li.

If the person reading this letter happens to be your successor, you can skip the beginning and dismiss it as the pointless ramblings of an old cultivator. The jade slip I enclosed should at least be of some help to anyone learning alchemy.

I have no idea how likely it is that this will ever reach you in person.

Still, every now and then, I found myself thinking that if it was you, perhaps you were still alive somewhere, advancing your realm. Even long ago, whenever something difficult happened, you were always the calmest of us. You seemed somehow like someone who stood beyond the passage of time itself.」

Lee Hyun turned to the next page.

「The sect we founded has held together surprisingly well.

At first, we all thought we could earn spirit stones as long as we practiced alchemy, but even securing medicinal ingredients on time proved difficult. Only then did we realize how fortunate the environment at Danxiao Sect had been, with its countless spirit fields and spirit-plant cultivators.

Senior Brother Fang, Senior Brother Yue, and Senior Brother Song had a rough time of it.」

Lee Hyun chuckled under his breath.

The letter contained all sorts of little stories, such as the time Yue Wugou got an upset stomach after improperly preparing demon-beast meat, and how Song Qiming passed on the position of sect master but continued teaching disciples even in his later years.

It also recorded who passed away first and what those left behind did afterward.

Mei Sujun did not dwell on any of it with lengthy lamentation. She had simply written down their names and what had happened in a calm, matter-of-fact way.

...

「I eventually succeeded in Core Formation, late though it was.

I used Baoguang Temple’s Golden Core Condensing Pill.

That opened a new chapter in my life. Thanks to it, I was able to do many of the things I had wanted to do.

Later, when I looked down at the sect from the sky, I found it a little funny. After forming my golden core, my standards rose, and the valley where I had lived suddenly looked rather rustic.

Even then, I rarely felt as though I had time to spare.」

At that moment, the sound of leaves rustling in the wind came from outside the window.

Lee Hyun read the rest.

「I also discovered something interesting about the Golden Core Condensing Pill.

If you are still alive, then you have probably already formed a golden core or nascent soul, so this may not be of much help. But after going to all the trouble of researching it, I felt I wouldn’t be satisfied unless someone learned what I had found.

And if the person reading this is your successor rather than you, perhaps it will be useful.

The claim that using this pill for Core Formation completely cuts off the path to Nascent Soul does not appear to be entirely accurate.

This is not something I guessed on my own. I asked Baoguang Temple’s alchemists as well, and repeatedly compared the records they had accumulated over many years with the changes in my own golden core.

I wrote the details in the jade slip.

I also left behind a few other things I found useful while practicing alchemy, so whether it is you or your successor, I hope whoever needs them can make use of them.

Wherever you are, take care of yourself. I hope you live happily.」

The letter ended there.

Lee Hyun folded the paper, placed it back inside the wooden box, and closed the lid.

Then he sat by the window and drank a little more of the wine Yue Wugou had left behind.

...

At dawn the next day.

Lee Hyun withdrew his divine sense from the jade slip.

Several sheets of paper were spread across the table.

He redrew on them the diagram of a golden core he had just seen.

At intervals of several decades, Mei Sujun had examined her own golden core and repeatedly drawn the same section.

In the later diagrams, some of the lines gradually grew fainter.

They were demon markings.

...

Baoguang Temple’s Golden Core Condensing Pill was a pill that borrowed the power of a demon core to aid Core Formation.

During the alchemy process, repeated refinement stripped away the demon beast’s fierce aura and impurities, but not every trace remaining in the demon core could be erased.

There remained a structure in which demon power had been condensed in a fixed pattern over long years. The Golden Core Condensing Pill used part of that very structure to help a cultivator’s true essence condense into a golden core.

Some called it a trace of demon intent.

It did not mean that the thoughts or soul of a living demon beast remained. What lingered was the pattern by which spiritual power had flowed and gathered within the demon core.

After Core Formation, those traces took root within the cultivator’s golden core as well, and the portions visible on its surface were known as demon markings.

The problem came afterward.

To form a nascent soul, one normally had to merge one’s qi and spirit, that is, one’s spiritual power and primordial spirit, within the golden core. Only after breaking through the golden core could they be reborn as a nascent soul.

However, the externally borrowed structure of the demon markings interfered with that transformation.

The magical power that needed to merge with the cultivator’s primordial spirit continued to preserve the original flow pattern inherited from the demon core.

Because the demon markings were connected to the golden core’s internal structure, they could not simply be scraped away from the surface. Removing them required changing the flow itself.

The natural method for removing the demon markings was to nurture the golden core for a long time with one’s own magical power and, by following refining formulas, gradually assimilate those foreign flow patterns until they became one’s own.

That exact process was recorded in the series of diagrams Mei Sujun had drawn.

Baoguang Temple had apparently been observing the same phenomenon for a very long time.

The problem was that the refining took far too long.

The speed of refining differed from cultivator to cultivator. However, based on Baoguang Temple’s accumulated records and the rate at which demon markings faded, changing the structure of the entire golden core was estimated to require roughly one thousand years.

A Golden Core cultivator, on the other hand, could live at most six hundred years.

Moreover, they did not gain a fresh six hundred years of life from the day they achieved Core Formation. Cultivators who formed their cores late had already used up a considerable portion of their lifespan beforehand.

Naturally, their lives ended before the demon markings could disappear.

That was why the belief had spread that cultivators who used Baoguang Temple’s Golden Core Condensing Pill would find it difficult to reach Nascent Soul.

Lee Hyun rubbed a fingertip over the lines on the paper.

‘If these records are really correct... then this pill isn’t a problem for me at all, is it?’

Chapter 73

Lee Hyun leaned back in his chair.

Spread across the table were sheets of paper onto which he had copied Mei Sujun's diagrams of the golden core.

That the demon markings had actually faded was an observed fact. The estimate that it would take roughly a thousand years to remove them completely had been reached after cross-checking Baoguang Temple's records.

It might not take exactly a thousand years, but whether it was eight hundred or twelve hundred made little difference to Lee Hyun.

Then another thought suddenly occurred to him.

'Wait. I'll probably have to take around fifty Golden Core Condensing Pills....'

Lee Hyun looked down at the golden core drawn on the paper.

'Don't tell me it'll take fifty thousand years?'

For a moment, he felt faint.

The thought of forming a golden core and then spending fifty thousand years doing nothing but grinding away at the demon markings made even Lee Hyun feel strange.

'It probably isn't that simple. I'll have that much more magical power to refine them with as well....'

But for now, there was no way to know which possibility was correct.

Mei Sujun could hardly have conducted her research while accounting for the Primordial Body, which turned the entire body into something like a dantian.

Lee Hyun wrote a small note in one corner of the paper.

「Time required to refine demon markings during Whole-Body Core Formation.」

If he could solve that problem, Baoguang Temple's Golden Core Condensing Pills would suit him extremely well.

Obtaining Tier-3 demon cores would not be easy, but securing fifty ordinary Golden Core Condensing Pills seemed even more daunting.

He recalled when Eldest Senior Brother Tao Wenqian had received his Golden Core Condensing Pills.

Even the Danxiao Sect, renowned for its alchemy, had only managed to produce four pills after twenty-seven years. Lee Hyun had also heard that the alchemy had been delayed because one of the main ingredients had been nearly impossible to obtain.

Even if Lee Hyun acquired the pill recipe, he would first have to figure out where to obtain those medicinal ingredients and how to cultivate them.

Even if the required medicine age of the main ingredient was only five hundred years, he would have to grow it for roughly fifteen hundred years in his current underground spirit field. He could cultivate in the meantime, of course, but he still did not know whether he could provide all the necessary growing conditions.

Baoguang Temple, on the other hand, was already producing Golden Core Condensing Pills steadily.

All that remained was to learn more about their production method and the nature of the demon markings.

'Once my entire body reaches around mid Foundation Establishment, I'll start looking into this in earnest. If I can enter Baoguang Temple by then....'

Lee Hyun thought for a moment and touched his hair.

'Would I have to shave my head?'

He imagined himself sitting before a pill furnace in Buddhist robes.

It felt a little strange.

'Well... I can worry about that when the time comes.'

Lee Hyun organized the papers, then placed Mei Sujun's jade slip and a letter into a wooden box.

...

Two days later.

Lee Hyun left the Yanxia Sect.

During his stay, he had discussed alchemy with Xu Zheng'an and read some of the disciples' records on preparing medicinal ingredients.

The Yanxia Sect possessed several formulas he had never seen in the Danxiao Sect. They were recipes that had been modified over several generations in an attempt to replace the ingredients in existing pill recipes with medicinal ingredients found in the Cangmang Forest.

Lee Hyun was given a copy of one of them.

In return, he taught them a technique for extracting toxic qi from poisonous herbs without drawing out their medicinal potency along with it, and left behind a pouch of spirit stones as a gift.

"Thanks to your preserving these records for so long, I've obtained something precious. Please accept this as a small token of my gratitude."

Xu Zheng'an repeatedly declined before finally accepting the pouch.

He accompanied Lee Hyun all the way beyond the Mountain Gate, then clasped his hands together.

"I am glad to know that Senior Li Dongsan's inheritance still lives on. If you ever pass nearby again, please visit us."

"I will."

Over the next month or so, Lee Hyun passed through several Two Heavens Society contact points in the Xu Kingdom and Xuan Kingdom.

He attended their gatherings not as Badger, the Society Head, but in the capacity of an Elder.

Reports followed on the condition of the vein seats, goods being traded, and rumors from various regions. What caught Lee Hyun's attention was an auction being held in northern Kun Kingdom.

"An exceptional supreme-grade magic tool is appearing?"

"Yes. The auction is being held by Jiubao Pavilion in Huichuan Market. We've heard that the Sinking Moon Sword will be among the items offered this time."

"The Sinking Moon Sword?"

A member wearing a white weasel mask held out a thin booklet.

The cover bore the title 《Nanming Hundred Artifacts Register》.

It was a book compiled by merchant groups and appraisers of the Nanming Sea, selecting one hundred renowned magic tools from throughout the territory of the Nanming Twelve-Sect Alliance and recording their histories and capabilities.

Magic treasures were not included.

Cultivators differed in their opinions about the rankings of the magic tools listed within, but no one disputed that anything worthy of inclusion was a rare masterpiece.

Just how many Foundation Establishment cultivators did the Nanming Twelve-Sect Alliance have now?

Its territory stretched across countless archipelagos and small continents beyond the Nanming Sea, as well as the Lan Kingdom, Cang Kingdom, Qianyang Kingdom, and Kun Kingdom. There had to be tens of thousands of Foundation Establishment cultivators at the very least.

And among those tens of thousands of Foundation Establishment cultivators, how many had no magic tool at all? If anything, most probably owned two or more.

For something to rank among the hundred most renowned magic tools across all of them, even if the list was ultimately nothing more than a ranking game among Foundation Establishment cultivators, there could be no doubt that its quality was extraordinary.

The member opened the booklet to one page.

「8th Place, Sinking Moon Sword」

Lee Hyun looked over the illustration and read the description beneath it.

The blade was long and straight. Fine lines extending all the way to its tip overlapped like faint ripples, though it was difficult to make out what was distinctive about them from the illustration alone.

One passage in the description caught his eye.

「Possesses a resilient sword body and can retract its sword light, concealing it deeply.」

"When is the auction?"

"Midway through next month. However, whether everything written in the book is true...."

"I can see for myself."

Northern Kun Kingdom, Huichuan Market.

Tall stone bridges spanned the place where two rivers converged.

Ships laden with goods brought up from the south were moored along the riverbanks, while flying boats descended one after another onto docks carved into the mountainside.

Foundation Establishment cultivators were a common sight in the streets.

There was an old man wearing several spirit-beast pouches with their openings tied shut by red cord, a man carrying a long, narrow coffin on his back, and even a female cultivator from whose sleeves came the chirping of insects.

There were rogue cultivators dressed plainly as well, but among those heading toward the larger halls, many had concealed their faces.

Lee Hyun also wore a gray robe and a dark mask.

He had arrived at Huichuan Market three days earlier, entrusted four spirit plants to Jiubao Pavilion's appraisal office, and received an explanation of the auction.

Jiubao Pavilion had offered to buy them outright on the spot, but Lee Hyun wanted them put up for auction.

He wanted to see for himself what kinds of people needed his spirit plants, and how badly.

...

The auction hall stood in a spacious building at the center of the cultivator market.

Eight bronze-colored pillars stood before the entrance. The eyes of the beasts coiling around them glowed red, while Foundation Establishment cultivators beneath them checked invitation tokens and entrance fees.

When Lee Hyun presented one mid-grade spirit stone and his consignment spirit tablet, the steward inspected the tablet and handed him a small numbered bidding token.

"Section D, No. 57. The proceeds from your consigned items can be settled together with the cost of anything you purchase."

A female Qi Refining cultivator in a blue skirt soon approached.

"Senior, this way, please."

She led Lee Hyun into a broad chamber.

The seats were arranged in tiers around a high platform in the center. A small table and tea had been set at every seat, while thin curtains of restrictions hung on both sides to prevent divine sense from intruding freely.

On the second floor were lavish private rooms concealed behind thick blinds and formation screens. They were occupied by direct-line members of major sects and people from influential cultivation clans. Those without any special background, like Lee Hyun, naturally gathered on the first floor.

As the sound of chains scraping across the floor came from one of the private rooms, the female cultivator guiding him slowed for a moment, but soon continued walking as though nothing had happened.

"Inject spiritual power into the numbered bidding token and your bid will appear above the platform. You may also call out your bid directly or transmit it through the token."

"Understood."

Lee Hyun sat down.

When the man seated ahead and to his right adjusted his sleeve, something resembling a tiny human face briefly appeared on the inside of his wrist before vanishing again.

To the left, a helmeted cultivator and a white-haired old man stared at one another.

An icy tension hung between them.

But when a Jiubao Pavilion steward walking past turned his head toward them, both men looked away as though by prior agreement.

...

A short while later.

The lamps above the platform brightened.

A middle-aged cultivator with a neatly trimmed beard stepped onto the platform and gave a light fist-and-palm salute in all directions. The man possessed the aura of Foundation Establishment Great Perfection.

"Thank you, fellow Daoists, for traveling so far to join us. I am a steward of Jiubao Pavilion and will be presiding over today's auction."

The murmuring gradually subsided.

"All items have been appraised by our pavilion. Unless otherwise stated, any residual ownership imprints and tracking measures have also been removed. If you have questions, ask before placing the winning bid. We cannot accept returns simply because you decide you dislike your purchase afterward."

Several cultivators chuckled quietly.

"All bids will be denominated in mid-grade spirit stones."

The steward gestured behind him.

"Now, let us begin with the first item."

Two attendants came up carrying a silver tray.

On it lay two long pieces of bone and six black jade bottles.

The steward picked up one of the bones and snapped it in two.

Crack.

The dry sound echoed through the hall.

He dripped a drop of black liquid from one of the jade bottles onto each broken surface.

The liquid stretched into sticky threads, linking the two surfaces. When he pressed the bone pieces together and channeled spiritual power through them, the black strands seeped inside.

A short while later, the steward grasped both ends of the repaired bone and slowly bent it before letting go. The bone, which had curved like a bow, straightened again.

"Supple Bone Glue. It is refined from the secretions of the Half-Jointed Bone Creature, which lives in the deep trenches of the Nanming Sea. Its advantage is that it fills cracks in spirit materials without making the joint excessively rigid."

Several cultivators in the front rows straightened in their seats.

Lee Hyun also studied the bone carefully.

'Could I use that to repair Bonefuzz...?'

A cultivator asked,

"How much more durable is it than ordinary bone glue?"

"When tested on the same spirit material, it withstood more than three times as much repeated bending. Detailed test records will be included. Six bottles as one lot. Starting bid, thirty."

"Forty."

"Forty-eight."

The bids immediately began climbing.

An old man with a braided beard called sixty, and a female cultivator wearing bone rings on every finger called seventy-two.

Lee Hyun lost interest as he watched the price rise. It would be far cheaper to hunt a Tier-2 demon beast himself, refine its bones, and replace the entire damaged section.

"Eighty."

"Eighty-eight."

"Ninety-six."

A brief silence followed.

The steward tapped a small jade gavel.

Tap.

"Sold to the fellow Daoist in Section D, No. 132."

...

The next item was a round crystal case.

It was half-filled with red liquid, within which two eyeballs moved slowly.

"Twinborn Blood Eyes. These were refined while still alive from the eyes of a pair of Blood-Eyed Fish born together."

When the steward removed one eyeball from the case, an attendant received it and carried it behind the hall.

The steward placed the remaining eyeball on his palm. Fine blood vessels crawled between his fingers, and the pupil contracted sharply once.

"The attendant in the rear courtyard has just flipped over a plaque. It has a blue background with a white crane painted on it."

A short while later, the attendant returned holding a blue plaque bearing the image of a white crane.

"Place one eye wherever you wish, and you can see that location through the other. On open ground, we have tested them at up to thirty li (about 11.8 km). The range decreases when rock or metallic strata lie between them."

A voice came from behind the blinds on the second floor.

"Can they be implanted into a human body?"

"Anywhere with blood circulation."

The steward continued without batting an eye.

"However, if you leave one implanted in someone else's body for too long, you may one day find that its owner has changed. The essential formula for rearing and controlling them will also be included."

The bidding proceeded quickly.

Two masked cultivators took turns raising the price, until one of the private rooms on the second floor finally bid one hundred eighty and won the item.

...

The mood changed slightly when the third item appeared.

Resting on the silver tray was a piece of wood less than one chi (about 33 cm) long. Its exterior was charred black, but a faint yellow glow seeped from the cut surface.

When the steward placed a few wood shavings into a small incense burner, smoke rose from it.

"This is heartwood from Mind-Calming Wood that formed part of the Dharma Assembly Hall of a Baoguang Temple subsidiary residence for three hundred forty years. It came from a beam removed when the residence was expanded, and only the section most deeply infused with incense-offering qi was selected."

A cultivator wearing a red headscarf snorted.

"You're selling those bald monks' wood in a place like this?"

The steward looked at him and smiled.

"Resentful spirits do not care where something came from. You may burn it, or carve it into small tablets and carry them with you. It is particularly useful when bonding a soul banner or clearing the lingering consciousness from a corpse puppet. As you can see from its thickness, there is enough to make four tablets and still have some left over for incense."

"One hundred."

"One hundred twenty."

The cultivator in the red headscarf, who had scoffed moments earlier, immediately raised his hand.

"One hundred fifty!"

In the end, the piece of wood went to another cultivator for two hundred sixty.

...

Several more items followed.

A Black Jade Flying Blade capable of holding and firing three different types of poisonous liquid.

A shell that, when submerged in water, emitted mist carrying its owner's breath and body heat.

And a coffin divided into nine compartments.

When the lid opened, cold corpse qi spilled across the floor.

Models of corpse puppets had been placed inside, and the nature of the yin qi could apparently be regulated separately in each compartment.

"Have you been forced to carry your painstakingly raised corpse puppets separately because their corpse poisons are incompatible? With this, you can place them all in the same coffin. The restrictions are divided so that even if poison leaks from one compartment, it will not spread to the others."

Three cultivators carrying coffins on their backs leaned forward almost simultaneously.

...

A short while later.

Two attendants placed a broad jade casket on the platform.

When the lid opened, layers of ivory-colored petals were revealed.

The steward raised his voice slightly.

"Next is one of the more precious spirit plants brought in today. A Bone-Rot Flower mother plant with a medicine age of approximately six hundred ninety years!"

The atmosphere in the audience changed in an instant.

Even the soil around the Bone-Rot Flower's roots had been preserved intact. A faint bone-white spirit light flowed from its thick roots, while poisonous pollen gathered within the stamens glittered like tiny crystals.

The steward loosened the restriction along the edge of the jade casket slightly.

Whoosh–

As a thin cloud of ivory poisonous pollen rose, several cultivators in the front row immediately activated their body-protecting spirit light.

The steward closed the restriction again.

"Its medicine age is sufficient for use as the main ingredient in Tier-3 Bone-Forging Powder. The medicinal potency of its petals and stamens is rich, and the growth points on its roots remain completely intact."

Divine sense descended from one private room on the second floor.

Several other strands of divine sense also swept over the jade casket.

"Steward!"

An old cultivator near the back craned his neck in disbelief and shouted.

"Not even one fine root is broken, and the soil is intact! This wasn't harvested and stored. It looks as though it was dug straight out of a spirit field this very morning!"

"Your eye is keen."

The steward smiled.

"Some of you may wish to use it as a medicinal ingredient, but those who possess spirit fields should pay attention to the fact that this is a mother plant. Opportunities to obtain a Tier-3 poisonous herb mother plant in such vigorous condition are exceedingly rare."

Murmurs erupted throughout the hall.

"They're putting a living mother plant nearly seven hundred years old up for sale?"

"Did someone raid a newly discovered secret realm or something?"

"No, something like that must have a great sect behind it!"

Lee Hyun suppressed a dry laugh.

"Starting bid, five hundred. Please increase each bid by at least twenty."

"Five hundred twenty."

"Five hundred sixty."

The initially cautious bidding soon accelerated.

Once it passed six hundred, only four bidders remained.

The female cultivator wearing bone rings, an old man in a silver mask, and two private rooms on the second floor.

"Seven hundred."

"Seven hundred forty."

"Eight hundred."

The female cultivator pressed her lips together.

The old man in the silver mask inspected the roots inside the jade casket once more before speaking.

"Eight hundred fifty."

A reply immediately came from the second floor.

"Nine hundred."

The old man remained silent for some time.

The steward looked around the seats.

"Nine hundred. Opportunities to obtain a Tier-3 Bone-Rot Flower mother plant that can be replanted and cultivated are not common in this region."

No one bid higher.

The jade gavel descended.

Tap.

"Sold to the fellow Daoist in Section A, No. 3."

...

The Purple Poison Orchid came next.

Fine silver lines covered the surface of its purple bulb like a net.

The steward slowly turned the jade tray.

"This one has also exceeded six hundred ninety years of medicine age. If you intend to refine Purple Venom Extract, look at the condition of the bulb before the leaves. The inside is neither soft nor hollow."

Cultivators wearing green gloves showed particular interest in the Purple Poison Orchid.

It sold for eight hundred.

Competition over the Yin Soul Grass was fiercer.

As its ink-black leaves slowly unfurled inside the jade casket, divine sense extended from several parts of the audience almost simultaneously.

As though he had been waiting for that, the steward said,

"You have surely sensed its medicinal potency yourselves. The greatest difficulty in continuing to cultivate Yin Soul Grass of this age is preventing the yin qi within its leaf veins from becoming turbid. As you can see, the flow is exceptionally even."

Lee Hyun was a little surprised.

'That was a problem?'

There had never been any particular trouble in the tunnel.

He had simply endured the poisonous pollen, watered the plants, and let the fuzzbees devour the spirit insects.

The Yin Soul Grass sold for one thousand mid-grade spirit stones.

When the Earth Vein Flower appeared last, fewer people showed interest.

Instead, those who did bid persistently asked how much of the roots had been preserved.

"The main root hasn't been severed anywhere?"

"No. It has been coiled inside."

When an attendant opened the lower section of the jade casket, several layers of slender roots were revealed, wound together.

The steward carefully unfolded them all the way to the tips.

"An Earth Vein Flower this old can be used even in a high-grade spirit field. However, as you are transplanting roots that have already settled into one place, I recommend preparing the qi of the new soil beforehand."

Two cultivators in red robes competed to the end, and the Earth Vein Flower sold for two hundred.

'Even that goes for two hundred.'

Lee Hyun had no intention of selling Earth Vein Flowers in large quantities, but he had brought one along because he was curious about their value.

The four spirit plants had sold for a combined total of two thousand nine hundred mid-grade spirit stones.

Even after deducting the commission, it was a fortune greater than the entire wealth of an ordinary Foundation Establishment Great Perfection cultivator.

An ordinary rogue cultivator could risk his life for an entire lifetime and still never lay hands on this many spirit stones, yet Lee Hyun had earned them from just four plants dug out of a corner of his spirit field.

Only then did Lee Hyun relax and lean comfortably back in his chair.

'I have plenty of funds now.'

...

More than two shichen (about four hours) after the auction began.

All the attendants withdrew from the platform, and the steward personally carried out a long sword case.

The low murmurs from the audience faded.

The case was made of black wood. Instead of decorations, several layers of seals covered its surface, and the clasp gave off a dull silver gleam.

The steward removed the seals one by one.

Click.

The lid opened.

A longsword lay upon black silk inside.

The blade was a little over four chi (about 1.3 m) long.

It was neither excessively broad nor narrow, tapering straight and sharp toward the tip. Patterns like ripples holding moonlight overlapped faintly across its surface.

It was unmistakably a silver-gray sword, yet when one's gaze shifted slightly, one side of the blade seemed to sink into darkness. Looking again, that section appeared perfectly normal.

Lee Hyun narrowed his eyes.

The steward lifted the sword.

"I imagine many of you have been waiting for this."

He slowly turned the blade.

"Eighth place in the Nanming Hundred Artifacts Register. The Sinking Moon Sword."

Quiet exclamations rose throughout the audience.

The steward waited a moment, as though enjoying their reaction.

"This magic tool is famous for having collided head-on with the magic treasure of an early Golden Core cultivator and emerged completely intact. The appraisal record from that incident, along with records from two subsequent inspections of the sword body, will be included."

The steward held the sword horizontally for all to see.

Lamplight flowed in a long line across the blade.

"One of its primary materials is Supreme Yin Cold Iron. It is a precious spirit material of which only one jin can be obtained by refining five thousand jin (about 3,000 kg) of Profound Nether Iron Ore. In addition, finely ground Moon Shadow Stone powder was used while quenching it ninety-nine times."

The faint ripple patterns along the blade brightened slightly.

"The amount of spiritual power it can handle is exceptionally high, enough that even a mid-stage Golden Core cultivator can use it. Those of you who have experienced the sword body or restrictions giving out first while condensing and refining powerful sword qi will understand the value of this sword."

The steward infused the sword with spiritual power.

Hummm–

Clear light filled the blade.

A moment later, the steward formed a different hand seal, and the light along the blade gradually faded. Even the outline perceived through divine sense became indistinct.

"Moon Shadow Stone disrupts the energy perceived by divine sense. The Light-Retracting Restriction engraved into the blade complements it exquisitely, allowing the sword to deceive both the eyes and divine sense."

An attendant activated the formation plate on the platform, causing small flames to appear around the steward.

Mist scattered between the flames, and thin beams of light passed back and forth in several directions.

None were powerful, but each emitted a different fluctuation of spiritual power.

The steward moved the sword among them.

Lee Hyun followed the first few trajectories, then raised an eyebrow slightly.

'Interesting.'

The steward withdrew the sword qi.

"It also contains Tier-2 Thick Earth Refined Metal. Thanks to this, not only is the sword body exceptionally sturdy, it is also highly capable of recovering from damage. Scratches and minor cracks can be repaired easily as long as you can handle basic fire control. What use is acquiring a masterpiece of a magic tool if you're too afraid of damaging it to use it properly?"

The steward left the Sinking Moon Sword floating above its case.

"The consignor succeeded in Core Formation and is now preparing a life-bound magic treasure. As they intend to raise funds for that purpose, they will not accept trades for other items."

He looked around the hall.

"Starting bid, six hundred mid-grade spirit stones. Please increase each bid by at least twenty."

The numbered bidding tokens lit up before he had even finished speaking.

"Six hundred forty."

"Seven hundred."

"Seven hundred eighty."

"Eight hundred forty!"

Lee Hyun did not enter the bidding immediately.

Even after the price exceeded eight hundred, six people were still bidding.

He wondered if there were really so many people who used swords, but some among them did not look particularly skilled in swordsmanship.

One did not have to be a sword cultivator to want a good magic tool.

Lee Hyun channeled spiritual power into his numbered bidding token.

"One thousand fifty."

A voice came from the second floor.

"One thousand one hundred fifty."

The sword-bearing cultivator in the front row hesitated, then lowered his hand.

No further bid came from the other private room.

Lee Hyun spoke.

"One thousand three hundred."

A brief silence followed.

A blind on the second floor trembled slightly.

"One thousand four hundred."

"One thousand five hundred."

The steward waited with the jade gavel in hand.

The Sinking Moon Sword floated above its case, shedding an elegant glow.

A moment later, the blind of one private room on the second floor was roughly swept aside, revealing a man dressed in an enchanted robe patterned with blue scales.

With one hand resting on the railing, he looked down at Lee Hyun, who sat in a corner of the first floor. His narrow chin was raised arrogantly, and displeasure filled his long, slanted eyes.

"Fellow Daoist from Section D, No. 57."

Lee Hyun looked up.

The man was at Foundation Establishment Great Perfection. Two blue rings adorned his fingers.

"I am Wei Zongyue of the Fuhai Sect. This sword is something my Master, Perfected Xuanzhao, has had his eye on for quite some time." [TL Note: The exact Hanja for 현조진인 has not been revealed yet. Depending on the characters used, 진인 could also be translated as “Daoist Master”, “Perfected” or “Perfected One”, so the title may be adjusted if later chapters clarify it.]

Gasps spread through the hall.

"The Fuhai Sect?"

"Perfected Xuanzhao? Isn't he that famous Golden Core Elder?"

"Then that's Wei Zongyue, his true-inheritance disciple...."

Hearing the murmurs around him, one corner of Wei Zongyue's mouth curled upward. He looked at Lee Hyun, sitting among the common seats with his face concealed, as though he were an insignificant gnat.

"How dare you covet something the Fuhai Sect has set its sights on? If you know your place and withdraw now, I will overlook the discourtesy of hiding your face and butting in."

The surrounding cultivators shook their heads as they looked at Lee Hyun, some with pity and others with ridicule.

Lee Hyun looked away from the man at the railing and lightly tapped his numbered bidding token.

"One thousand six hundred."

The hall fell as silent as though cold water had been poured over it.

Wei Zongyue's smile froze.

The Jiubao Pavilion steward cleared his throat awkwardly, then immediately acknowledged the bid.

"Section D, No. 57 bids one thousand six hundred."

A vein bulged on Wei Zongyue's forehead. He was sitting in a private room on the second floor and had even invoked his Master's name, yet some nameless rogue cultivator from the first floor had rebuffed him to his face?

"Seeing as even Perfected Xuanzhao's name means nothing to you, I suppose you aren't a fellow practitioner from Nanming."

Lee Hyun did not answer.

"Could you be a spy sent by one of the northern sects to investigate our affairs? Otherwise, how could anyone dare humiliate the Fuhai Sect like this on Kun Kingdom soil!"

Several cultivators snorted at Wei Zongyue's words.

It was hardly unusual for cultivators from the Xuan Kingdom to frequent markets in Kun Kingdom, and Jiubao Pavilion had never forbidden cultivators from orthodox path sects from entering.

Still, no one stepped forward to intervene. Watching people quarrel over an expensive sword was rather entertaining.

Just as Wei Zongyue released killing intent as though he might make a move at any moment, Lee Hyun remained leaning against his chair and raised his right hand. A pale white energy rose from the back of it.

Hummm–

A chilling fluctuation of spiritual power slammed into the surroundings.

"Urgh?!"

The cultivator seated directly beside him retreated together with his chair. Even the man nearby who had been radiating cold killing intent moments earlier turned pale and instinctively activated his body-protecting spirit light.

It was Profound Yin White Bone True Qi, terrifyingly pure and no weaker than the true qi of a Foundation Establishment Great Perfection cultivator.

"Does that answer your question?"

Lee Hyun's voice was calm, but fear had entered the eyes of the cultivators around him.

"Profound Yin White Bone True Qi?"

"He's from the Yin Bird Sect!"

"His true qi is condensed to that degree... Is he from Haigu Island's direct lineage?"

The demonic fiends of the Yin Bird Sect's Haigu Island were notorious even within the Nanming Twelve-Sect Alliance for their madness.

Wei Zongyue stared at Lee Hyun for a while longer, his jaw tight.

The steward on the platform lightly tapped his jade gavel.

Tap.

"Our pavilion does not inquire into anyone's origins. Will you continue bidding?"

Wei Zongyue slowly sat down.

"One thousand six hundred fifty."

Lee Hyun answered immediately.

"One thousand seven hundred."

Wei Zongyue's face turned mottled red and blue with humiliation.

"One thousand seven hundred fifty."

"One thousand eight hundred."

There was not the slightest wavering in Lee Hyun's voice.

This time, the silence stretched on.

After waiting long enough, the steward spoke.

"One thousand eight hundred."

No one raised the price.

"Any further bids?"

Wei Zongyue gripped his armrest so hard it seemed ready to break, but eventually withdrew his hand.

The jade gavel descended.

Tap.

"The Sinking Moon Sword is sold to the fellow Daoist in Section D, No. 57."

After the auction ended.

Lee Hyun was shown into a separate small room.

The sword case rested on the table.

The Foundation Establishment steward from Jiubao Pavilion opened the settlement ledger and went over each amount one by one.

After confirming the items, Lee Hyun received his spirit stones.

Despite buying such an expensive sword, he now had more mid-grade spirit stones left than he had possessed before coming to the auction.

He took the Sinking Moon Sword in his hand.

He greatly liked the way it settled naturally into his grip.

As he slowly infused it with spiritual power, the restrictions within the blade responded one after another. He had not even bonded with it yet, but there was no obstruction in the flow.

Lee Hyun placed the sword case, scabbard, and sword into his storage pouch.

...

He remained in Huichuan Market for several more days.

A Tier-3 grand formation covered the cultivator market, so he could not slip out underground, and there were still not many cultivators leaving through the main gate.

He rented a workshop, engraved his ownership imprint into the Sinking Moon Sword, and examined the accompanying essential formula for its operation.

Mastering the Light-Retracting Restriction would require practice, but he already had no trouble wielding the sword with his existing sword techniques.

...
