“Indeed. It reveals the fullness and purity of one’s primordial yang. The longer someone has preserved it intact, the stronger the reaction.”

The monk ran a hand along the mirror’s rim.

“Ordinarily, someone who has preserved it well for several decades will produce a red light. Among those who have guarded their primordial yang while cultivating for over a hundred years, some even produce a golden light.”

“Can it tell a person’s age as well?”

“Not exactly. The reaction also varies according to one’s constitution and cultivation art. Some show golden light while still young, while others may spend a hundred years alone and produce only a faint red glow.”

The old monk sat down again and held out the mirror.

“Place your hand on it and channel a little spiritual power into it.”

Lee Hyun placed his hand on the mirror.

Hummm.

The lotus blossoms engraved around its rim lit up. A red glow appeared for a moment, then deep golden light flooded the mirror’s surface.

The monk straightened.

“Oh...!”

At that moment, a white speck appeared in the center of the golden light.

It expanded in the blink of an eye.

Flash!

“...!”

Every shadow inside the Guest Hall vanished.

Beneath the table, behind the chairs, even inside the shrine niche, everything was washed completely white. It was as though a tiny sun had descended onto the mirror.

Lee Hyun immediately removed his hand.

The radiance faded. Silence returned to the Guest Hall, and the scent of incense once again filled the air.

“.......”

The monk stared at the mirror with his mouth slightly open.

Lee Hyun looked down at it as well.

‘I didn’t expect it to react this strongly.’

After a moment, the monk picked up the Yang Essence Mirror.

He examined the formation inscriptions around the rim and on the back in turn. Only after channeling spiritual power into it and checking it for quite some time did he carefully set it back down.

Lee Hyun asked,

“Did I pass?”

“.......”

The monk looked at Lee Hyun’s face again. Somehow, his calm expression seemed suffused with profound meditative absorption!

“When you see a beautiful woman... what goes through your mind?”

“I think she is beautiful.”

The monk slowly nodded.

“And yet you are not captivated by her....”

He exclaimed in admiration.

“To think your innate primordial yang could be this pure. What rare innate cultivation aptitude. Perhaps some affinity remains from a past life in which you practiced pure conduct for many years.”

‘I didn’t do anything particularly special in my past life....’

“A Foundation Establishment cultivator in the prime of his vitality who stays away from women without even considering it an ordeal!”

The monk pressed his palms together.

“What a truly precious affinity.”

“Then, my admission....”

“I permit it. Your name shall be entered among the inner disciples of the Lotus Court.”

The monk immediately picked up his brush.

“This old monk’s Dharma name is Huitan. If you have no objections, enter my lineage. I will personally teach you the Clear Yang Purifying Fire Art.”

Lee Hyun thought for a moment.

There was certainly no harm in taking a Golden Core cultivator who could teach him alchemy as his Master. Besides, had he not come to Baoguang Temple for the sake of alchemy in the first place?

He rose and bowed respectfully.

“Please guide me, Master.”

“Hoho. Good, good.”

The brush moved rapidly across the document.

Lee Hyun waited for a moment before asking,

“Are there no other tests I need to take?”

“What sort of tests?”

“Things like bone age or spiritual roots.”

Huitan looked puzzled instead.

“You are practically a Buddha in the flesh already. What importance could those things possibly have?”

“.......”

That afternoon.

Thin trails of smoke rose from an incense burner inside a small Dharma hall deep within the Lotus Court.

Huitan placed a wooden tablet two fingers wide in front of Lee Hyun. Nothing had yet been written on its surface.

“Every disciple who enters our court makes at least one vow. The same goes for those who previously practiced other cultivation arts. One must first learn how to obtain vow power before one can properly cultivate our court’s inheritance.”

Lee Hyun examined the wooden tablet.

Fine formation inscriptions ran between the grain of the wood.

“Can it be any vow?”

“Do not choose carelessly. The nature of the vow power you obtain changes according to what you vow.”

Huitan opened a booklet beside him. It contained examples of various vows and accounts of what had happened to the cultivators who made them.

A vow to shave one’s head at fixed intervals and never grow out one’s hair.

A vow to preserve one’s primordial yang.

A vow never to leave any offering one received uneaten.

There was even a vow to rise before sunrise.

“It is best to choose something proven. Vows that countless practitioners have upheld for many years also have well-established essential formulas for handling the vow power they produce. Refusing to grow one’s hair and preserving one’s primordial yang are examples.”

When Huitan turned the page, it showed examples of people who had ruined their cultivation by making excessively ambitious vows.

Lee Hyun read a few lines, then closed the booklet.

“I will preserve my primordial yang.”

“As expected!”

A satisfied smile spread across Huitan’s face.

“It is also the vow most compatible with the Clear Yang Purifying Fire Art.”

He engraved words onto the wooden tablet and handed it to Lee Hyun.

“A vow is not something made merely with words. You must engrave it into your heart according to the mnemonic formula I am about to teach you. Once a vow you have upheld takes root in your primordial spirit, you will be able to add vow power whenever you wish and create a new kind of strength.”

After hearing the mnemonic formula, Lee Hyun closed his eyes.

The scent of incense grew stronger.

A long while later, his divine sense lightly touched the wooden tablet.

“I vow to preserve my primordial yang intact.”

Hummm.

The characters engraved on the vow tablet glimmered faintly.

Lee Hyun felt an extremely fine thread form along the outside of his primordial spirit.

Whenever he tried to grasp it, it faded, but whenever he recalled the oath he had just made, it became clear again.

Huitan nodded.

“Well done.”

“Will I begin to generate vow power now?”

“Think of it as having planted a seed. As you keep your vow and cultivate according to the mnemonic formula, it will gradually accumulate.”

He pointed to the vow tablet.

“If you break your oath, a crack will appear in the tablet. At that point, you will no longer be able to produce Buddha-Light True Qi. When the heart that broke the vow falls out of harmony with the vow power accumulated from keeping it, your true qi may even reverse its flow and injure you if the clash is severe enough.”

Lee Hyun carefully placed the tablet into his storage pouch.

Huitan took out two jade slips.

“You are already a Foundation Establishment cultivator, so you have no need for another cultivation art for spiritual power. One of these is the 《Buddha-Light Heart Art》, the mnemonic formula for cultivating vow power and adding it to spiritual power. The other is the 《Clear Yang Purifying Fire Art》.”

Lee Hyun accepted the jade slips.

Huitan opened his palm, and a faint golden energy appeared above it.

“True qi created by adding the power of a vow is broadly called Vow-Powered True Qi. Among those forms, the true qi cultivated through our Baoguang Temple’s Buddha-Light Heart Art is called Buddha-Light True Qi.”

The golden energy slowly flowed between his fingers.

“It excels at suppressing heart demons and resentful spirits, as well as subduing violent demon power. It is also useful against vicious ghostly entities controlled by demonic cultivators and other sinister energies.”

Huitan withdrew his hand.

At that moment, the smoke rising from the incense burner gathered behind the Buddha statue.

When Lee Hyun looked over, Huitan explained,

“That is incense-offering qi. Incense offerings gathered from temples throughout the Xu Kingdom are also channeled into Baoguang Temple. They are used to maintain the grand formation and nurture magic tools, and they can aid cultivation as well. However, only monks who walk the Dao of Incense Offerings can control them.”

On the way out of the Dharma hall, Lee Hyun looked beyond the wall.

Rows of tall tiled roofs stretched into the distance, surrounded by restrictions far denser than those elsewhere.

“Is that part of the Lotus Court too?”

“That is where important pills such as Golden Core Condensing Pills are refined.”

“Can disciples enter as well?”

“Of course. But first, you must accumulate sufficient merit and prove yourself someone who can be entrusted with the work.”

Huitan lightly patted Lee Hyun’s shoulder.

“Do not rush. If you have the affinity, your chance will come.”

...

Lee Hyun’s residence stood on a low peak to the east of the Lotus Court.

Beyond a small courtyard stood three halls side by side, with a garden of bamboo and stone behind them.

Inside were a cultivation chamber, a study, and even a guest room for receiving visitors.

“Am I really allowed to use such a nice place by myself?”

The monk guiding him laughed at Lee Hyun’s question.

“Our Baoguang Temple is hardly poor. You are a Foundation Establishment cultivator, a Tier 2 alchemist, and a talent Monk Huitan has praised to no end. We can hardly make you share a room with the young disciples, can we?”

It was the same guest-receiving monk who had guided him at the Mountain Gate when he first arrived. His Dharma name was Mingxiu, and Lee Hyun had already decided to address him as Senior Brother.

“Do I not need to receive a separate Dharma name?”

“You may take one if you wish, but there is no problem with continuing to use your current name. There are many disciples like that in our temple.”

Mingxiu pointed to the restriction beside the door.

“Use your spirit tablet to open and close it. When leaving the sect, just inform the Guest Hall roughly where you are going and when you expect to return. As long as you do not disappear and leave your assigned duties unattended, there will be no issue.”

Lee Hyun nodded.

It seemed comfortable enough.

Just then, footsteps sounded behind them.

A round-faced monk entered the courtyard. When Mingxiu waved, he immediately walked over.

“Is this the new Junior Brother Li?”

“That’s right.”

“Oh....”

The round-faced monk studied Lee Hyun closely.

“To think a jewel of a talent like you had been living as a rogue cultivator. How fortunate that fate brought you to our temple.”

“You flatter me.”

When Lee Hyun gave a fist-and-palm salute, the monk shook his head gravely.

“Junior Brother must be even more careful with his conduct from now on.”

“Yes?”

“I mean that you must guard your primordial yang well.”

Mingxiu nodded too.

“Indeed. You cannot let your guard down just because you have entered our court.”

He took a thin picture album from inside his robe. Lee Hyun’s gaze shifted toward it.

When Mingxiu opened the album, there was a painting of a female cultivator standing beneath a willow tree.

The woman in the painting slowly blinked. Even the hem of her clothes seemed to sway in the wind.

The workmanship was quite impressive.

“This is Senior Sister Xu from the Life-Release Court.”

“I see.”

“Do not linger beside her too long when she is feeding the spirit beasts. If she smiles and starts talking to you, your heart may easily waver.”

“Senior Sister Xu is beautiful even when she isn’t smiling.”

When the round-faced monk added that, Mingxiu nodded.

“That is true.”

He turned to the next page.

This time, a female cultivator with her hair tied in a red ribbon held a spear.

“This is Junior Sister Lu from the Demon-Subduing Court. Be even more careful around her.”

“Is there some problem?”

“She has the dangerous habit of looking people straight in the eyes when she speaks.”

Lee Hyun looked at the painting.

The female cultivator in the picture was staring straight back at him as well.

Mingxiu lowered his voice.

“Especially if she asks you to spar, do not agree too readily.”

“Because I might get injured during the spar?”

“You might end up seeing her brush back her hair as she wipes away sweat, from up close.”

The round-faced monk sighed deeply.

“That would indeed be dangerous.”

‘.......’

Lee Hyun pointed at the picture album.

“Why are you carrying something like this around?”

Mingxiu’s expression did not change in the slightest.

“It is a cultivation aid.”

“I see.”

“I look through it often to temper my heart.”

Mingxiu closed the album.

At that moment, the round-faced monk grabbed his wrist.

“Wait. It looks like a new page was added at the back.”

“Ah, this is....”

The two leaned over the picture album together.

Lee Hyun waited for a moment, then went inside his residence first.

Three months later.

The cultivation chamber on the eastern peak of the Lotus Court.

Lying down, Lee Hyun raised a finger and gathered clear energy at its tip.

It was Primordial True Qi.

Then an extremely faint golden hue seeped into it.

Hummm.

The energy above his finger became slightly heavier and denser.

Lee Hyun brought his hand closer to his face and examined it.

‘It worked.’

It was Buddha-Light True Qi.

Primordial True Qi could originally be transformed into various kinds of true qi as long as he understood the appropriate Dharma teaching and mnemonic formula.

That was how he had produced Profound Yin White Bone True Qi and used it to refine Bonefuzz.

At first, however, he had been unable to produce Buddha-Light True Qi properly.

He could reproduce its color and the flow of spiritual power. Yet the energy he produced lacked the distinctive quality he had sensed in Baoguang Temple’s true qi.

The reason was simple.

He had possessed no vow power.

‘If I had to classify it, Buddha-Light True Qi isn’t a power derived purely from qi. Are qi and spirit acting together....?’

Over the past three months, Lee Hyun had cultivated the Buddha-Light Heart Art while accumulating vow power.

Although only a short time had passed since he made his vow and began cultivating it, the speed at which his vow power accumulated was far greater than expected.

According to Huitan, the vow power gained from preserving one’s primordial yang was also affected by the fullness and purity of one’s innate primordial yang. Even cultivators practicing the same mnemonic formula could obtain different amounts of vow power.

With primordial yang that had remained completely intact for over two thousand years, there could hardly have been a more suitable vow for him.

Once he had accumulated enough vow power, the rest was not difficult.

He adjusted the flow of his Primordial True Qi according to the mnemonic formula and added vow power to it. Only then did proper Buddha-Light True Qi form. There was no need to change the cultivation art he already practiced.

He sat up and this time activated the Clear Yang Purifying Fire Art.

Fwoosh.

A tiny pale-golden flame formed at his fingertip. Looking closely, its center was almost white.

When Lee Hyun lowered the fire control, the flame shrank to the size of a fingernail.

He brought over a jade dish containing a little demon blood left over from Refining practice. As he brought the flame close, dark crimson energy rose from its surface.

Sizzle.

Thin smoke drifted upward.

Lee Hyun extinguished the flame and examined the demon blood.

The turbid energy had been greatly reduced, while the medicinal potency that needed to remain had been preserved surprisingly well.

The Clear Yang Purifying Fire Art was a fire technique that used the purity of primordial yang to kindle Buddha-Light True Qi into yang fire.

It could also burn away sinister energy, but its greatest use was undoubtedly Refining.

‘Is it normally this effective?’

Lee Hyun stared at the dish for a moment.

‘Who would have thought staying away from women would help with something like this?’

He lowered his spiritual power even further and repeated the experiment. He was deliberately practicing how to suppress the effects of the Clear Yang Purifying Fire. He was worried that if it worked too well, he might be dragged into some unexpected trouble.

...

Five days later.

The Lotus Court’s communal alchemy chamber.

A bowl containing a demon beast’s marrow fluid sat in front of Lee Hyun.

Huitan examined the bowl and flicked his finger, sending a thread of flame into it.

Murky, threadlike strands rose within the dark crimson marrow fluid.

As the flames passed between them, the strands broke apart and turned to smoke.

“Try it yourself.”

Lee Hyun summoned the Clear Yang Purifying Fire and sent a small flame beneath the marrow fluid.

Sssss.

The turbid energy slowly rose and vanished.

Lee Hyun lowered the fire control, but even when touched by only the faintest flame, the malevolent energy within the marrow fluid quickly dispersed.

‘I need to reduce it a little more.’

As soon as he withdrew his hand, Huitan lifted the bowl.

“That’s it!”

“Is it satisfactory?”

“Your primordial yang is one thing, but your skill at handling fire is excellent. You make teaching worthwhile.”

Huitan opened the jade casket beside him. Inside lay a demon core with a crack across its surface.

“With demon cores, what you preserve is especially important. You must remove the violent energy while preserving the cohesive structure required for a Golden Core Condensing Pill.”

“Does that structure remain even after Core Formation?”

“Indeed. Those are what we commonly call demon markings. If you remove those as well, the Golden Core Condensing Pill itself loses its effectiveness.”

...

Life at Baoguang Temple was comfortable.

The Lotus Court contained many cultivators skilled in all manner of arts.

The cultivation arts they practiced and the vows they had made were all different.

One monk had apparently vowed to praise someone at least once every day.

On days when he had nothing in particular to praise, he would visit the medicinal-ingredient storeroom and compliment the disciples there for drying the medicinal herbs well or arranging the medicine bottles neatly.

Lee Hyun would sometimes receive praise from him merely for sitting quietly nearby.

Once he finished the regular practical training and the Refining work assigned to him, the rest of his time was largely his own.

Lee Hyun cultivated at his residence, read popular novels, and practiced the Clear Yang Purifying Fire Art.

Occasionally, he went out to purchase necessary supplies or run the Two Heavens Society.

Then one day, Huitan handed him a small jade token.

“Go to the Scripture Pavilion.”

“Am I allowed to examine the inheritances?”

“You have grown accustomed to handling vow power. It is time to see what sort of Dharma teaching suits you.”

Lee Hyun accepted the jade token.

“How do I earn the contribution points needed to examine them?”

Huitan shook his head.

“Baoguang Temple has no such thing as contribution points.”

“Then how....”

“You learn whatever you have affinity with.”

...

The monk overseeing the Scripture Pavilion looked at the jade token and nodded.

“So you are Senior Brother Huitan’s disciple. Come this way.”

On the second floor where he led him, books and jade slips were arranged across long shelves.

“You may examine the inheritances on this floor.”

“What about the other floors?”

“You do not have affinity with those yet.”

A strange thought suddenly occurred to Lee Hyun.

‘Could someone secretly be keeping track of some kind of affinity score?’

...

《Palm of Compassion》

Lee Hyun examined the first jade slip.

It was a palm technique that concentrated Buddha-Light True Qi in the palm before releasing it.

When the monk in the illustration thrust out his palm, the rock opposite him collapsed from within.

Lee Hyun picked up the next jade slip.

《Fist of Deliverance》

A note written at the very beginning caught his eye.

「Send demonic creatures onward with one’s fists and guide them onto the path of reincarnation.」

For some reason, the explanation sounded frightening.

Beside it was another technique called 《Demon-Subduing Seal》.

It involved forming a hand seal to concentrate Buddha-Light True Qi, then bringing down a golden seal. It was said to be useful for suppressing resentful spirits and ghostly entities.

Lee Hyun read the descriptions of several more techniques before picking up a jade slip placed a short distance away.

《Sumeru Visualization Scripture》

It contained far more material than the ones he had examined earlier.

It was an inheritance that used one’s vow as its foundation and shaped Buddha-Light True Qi into the form of a Dharma guardian. An explanation stated that only if one’s vow remained as unshakable as Mount Sumeru would the form built upon it remain intact.

‘There’s too much here. I’ll have to look at this again later.’

One side of the shelves contained body-refining arts.

《Mighty Vajra Body》

It strengthened the sinews and bones through spirit medicines and formations. It was not a cultivation art that raised one’s realm, but even within the same realm, it allowed the practitioner to exert far greater strength and withstand attacks from magic tools.

However, the deeper one cultivated it, the more precious the required spirit medicines became.

Lee Hyun looked at the enormous list of necessary materials, shook his head, and reached for the next inheritance.

《Arhat Golden Body》

It was a cultivation art that infused Buddha-Light True Qi deep into the flesh, tempering the skin, muscles, and skeleton in sequence.

Once completed, the golden radiance surrounding the body would not easily fade, and the cultivator could withstand attacks from magic tools with their bare body.

Lee Hyun looked at the diagram toward the back.

Thin lines originating inside the body overlapped in layer after layer beneath the skin.

Strangely enough, something about it felt familiar.

He flipped back and forth through the diagram.

‘I’ve seen this somewhere....’

After studying it for a long time, he stopped upon seeing a note beside the diagram.

「Some of the golden-body mnemonic formulas in the main text were taken from the ancient methods contained in the Golden Core section of the 《Primordial One-Qi Art》.」

‘Huh?’

Lee Hyun began examining the contents again from the beginning.

At the front of the inheritance was a lengthy passage explaining the origins of the Arhat Golden Body.

When he first looked through it, he had skimmed past that section because it mostly listed ancestral masters from long ago and traced the lineage of the inheritance.

Lee Hyun slowly reread one passage.

「The Arhat Golden Body transmitted today is a Dharma teaching modeled after the Leakless Golden Body of antiquity.」

Leakless Golden Body.

An unexpected explanation followed beneath it.

The golden-body arts of antiquity differed from those of the present day in the very foundation of their cultivation.

In an age when heaven-and-earth spiritual qi was abundant, cultivators who made their entire bodies into a dantian bound all the spiritual power accumulated throughout their bodies into a single flow and underwent Core Formation.

The ancient Daoist tradition called this method Embracing Unity and Returning to the Elixir.

It meant embracing the energy of the entire body as one and condensing it into an elixir without allowing it to scatter.

A cultivator who underwent Core Formation in this manner did not form a separate, small golden core within the body.

The entire body itself became a single golden core.

The interior of that golden core extended throughout the entire physical body, while its outer boundary, the core shell, overlapped the layer of the skin.

The Buddhist practitioners of antiquity developed their golden-body arts upon this foundation.

A body in which the energy inside and outside the flesh flowed as one, and in which the core shell at the body’s surface and the flesh and blood received magical power together.

That was the foundation of the Leakless Golden Body.

Things changed in later generations.

The years and resources required to raise the entire body to Foundation Establishment Great Perfection and form a golden core from there became excessive.

Cultivators therefore began focusing their cultivation on the narrow region of the lower dantian.

It was far faster to use the spiritual power that would otherwise have been required to fill the entire body to first raise the realm of the lower dantian, and breaking through a major realm also extended one’s lifespan.

Sects of the Buddhist tradition chose the same path.

Even after the method of forming a small golden core in the lower dantian became widespread, records describing the might of the golden bodies of antiquity remained.

Monks of later generations repeatedly infused magical power and vow power into their flesh and engraved linked golden inscriptions across the surface of their bodies in an attempt to recreate those ancient golden bodies.

Over the long years, numerous cultivation arts were created, and the Arhat Golden Body was one of them. The text also described the limitations that arose during that process, along with the mnemonic formulas added by ancestral masters to compensate for them.

Lee Hyun touched one of the lines in the diagram with his finger.

‘So that’s why it looked familiar.’

He recalled the Golden Core section of the 《Primordial One-Qi Art》 that he had obtained long ago from the Danxiao Sect.

The latter half, which dealt with the Primordial Body, contained an unusual number of passages that were difficult to understand.

At the time, he had assumed they were simply complex essential formulas for breaking through into the Golden Core realm.

But now that he compared them with this diagram, he realized those passages described how to form a core shell across the entire body.

They were essential formulas for creating a body capable of cultivating the ancient Leakless Golden Body!

If one formed a golden core in the lower dantian, its boundary would arise within the lower dantian.

But what if the entire body was bound together and underwent Core Formation as one?

Then that boundary would have to form at the surface of the body.

Lee Hyun read the next annotation.

「Forming cores in several places and linking them afterward is not the embracing unity meant by this method. From the moment condensation begins, the entire body must be embraced as one.」

His eyes narrowed.

This was important.

When Lee Hyun achieved Whole-Body Foundation Establishment, he had absorbed the medicinal strength of the Foundation Establishment Pills one body part at a time.

He had done something similar when breaking through to Foundation Establishment Stage 4.

But it seemed he could not use the same method for Core Formation.

If one part of his body condensed first into an independent golden core, a core shell would form around that region.

He might still be able to raise the rest of his body into the Golden Core realm afterward, but it would no longer become the single unified body required by the ancient golden-body arts.

Lee Hyun read the annotation several times.

It did not mean that he had to swallow all the pills at once.

He could absorb their medicinal strength in sequence. However, during that process, he had to prevent any single part from condensing ahead of the others while preparing sufficient true essence throughout his entire body.

The final condensation absolutely had to occur as one throughout the whole body.

‘Then I can’t form a golden core in my lower dantian first this time.... I’ve gone to all the trouble of following a cultivation method from antiquity. It’d bother me if I missed the chance to create a Leakless Golden Body, wouldn’t it?’

However, to create the Leakless Golden Body, he first had to reach Whole-Body Foundation Establishment Great Perfection and then secure a sufficient quantity of Golden Core Condensing Pills.

‘The question is whether taking more Golden Core Condensing Pills will increase the time needed for refining the demon markings by the same amount....’

Lee Hyun thought for a moment, then looked at the Arhat Golden Body diagram again.

In the end, the Arhat Golden Body was merely a crude imitation of the Leakless Golden Body.

But the path to achieving the original still remained open to him.

‘A true golden body....’

TL Note: Then can we assume there won't be any romance in this novel?

Chapter 78

Lee Hyun remained in the Scripture Pavilion for quite some time even after setting down the jade slip of the Arhat Golden Body.

He reread the annotations on the Leakless Golden Body and compared them with the passages he remembered from the Golden Core section of the Primordial One-Qi Art.

After that, he picked up the inheritances one by one again. Even if he had no intention of learning them right away, there was no harm in knowing what they contained.

They might prove useful someday, or help him understand other techniques.

From that day onward, Lee Hyun spent several days going back and forth to the Scripture Pavilion, carefully examining every inheritance he was permitted to read.

Whenever there were sections too difficult to memorize in one sitting, he returned to his residence to organize what he remembered, then came back the next day to check them again.

...

A few days later.

Lee Hyun's residence on the eastern peak of Lotus Court.

Several blank jade slips lay on the table.

Lee Hyun picked one up and pressed it to his forehead. As his divine sense seeped into it, text and diagrams were inscribed one after another within the previously smooth jade slip.

After a long while, he lowered the jade slip and closed his eyes for a moment.

‘This is incredibly difficult.’

It was the Sumeru Visualization Scripture.

The mnemonic formula was long, but the visualization diagrams were even harder to memorize than the text. He had to know every detail precisely, from the sacred image's posture and the positions of its fingers to the patterns engraved on its implements.

It was not an inheritance that could be used merely by remembering the general appearance.

Simply put, it was a technique for manifesting a Dharma manifestation outside one's body.

At Foundation Establishment, one could begin visualization cultivation by imprinting the sacred image upon the mind. Once sufficiently proficient, it was even possible to manifest a faint figure outside the body.

However, that was nothing more than an illusory Dharma manifestation.

It could imitate the motions of extending its arms and swinging its implements, but it could neither strike an enemy nor block a magic tool.

It was different from the Condensed-Essence Grasping Hand, which shaped spiritual power into a hand to seize objects. The Dharma manifestations of the Sumeru Visualization Scripture required complex flows to run throughout the entire body and all of their implements, and those flows had to be supported by the magical power of a Golden Core cultivator.

The first stage that could actually be used in battle was the Four Heavenly Kings manifestation, which could be formed at the Golden Core realm.

The pipa-bearing Nation-Guarding Heavenly King manifestation.

The sword-bearing Growth Heavenly King manifestation.

The Wide-Seeing Heavenly King manifestation, bearing a dragon and a jewel.

The All-Hearing Heavenly King manifestation, bearing a parasol and pagoda.

It was customary to begin by choosing one of the four for visualization and learning the divine ability possessed by that Dharma manifestation.

One could disrupt an enemy's divine sense with the music of the pipa, unleash ferocious slashes with the sword, coil around an enemy with the form of the dragon, or imprison them beneath the pagoda.

Those who cultivated the scripture deeply enough could even manifest the divine abilities of several Heavenly Kings at once.

In one of the diagrams he had copied into the jade slip, a translucent giant surrounded a monk's body. When the monk moved his arm, the Dharma manifestation's arm moved with him, and its enormous palm slammed into the rock face opposite him.

In another diagram, a Heavenly King raised a pagoda.

A golden boundary descended beneath it, and the movements of the demonic creature rampaging inside slowed.

‘Perfect for holding something down while I beat it up!’

The Sumeru Visualization Scripture passed down by Baoguang Temple contained mnemonic formulas all the way through the Nascent Soul realm.

At that stage, the new Dharma manifestation one could wield was the Immovable Wisdom King manifestation.

The cultivator sat cross-legged at the center of the Dharma manifestation, which was surrounded by a flaming halo. The manifestation held a sword and a noose in its hands, yet in contrast to its wrathful face, the monk seated within wore a serene expression.

The Heavenly Kings manifestations of the Golden Core realm largely followed the cultivator's own movements.

At the Nascent Soul realm, however, the limbs and implements of the Dharma manifestation could each be moved independently around the nascent soul. Even while the monk sat with his eyes closed, the Wisdom King's sword swung and its noose shot outward as though alive.

Beside the diagram was a brief annotation.

「Borrow the form of wrath, but do not forget your vow or allow yourself to be swept away by personal anger.」

Lee Hyun pondered that passage several times.

He understood what it meant. What he could not grasp was how one was supposed to keep one's own mind serene while pouring power into a wrathful form.

‘That's something for the Nascent Soul realm. There's no need to worry about it yet.’

Maintaining a Dharma manifestation also required no small amount of magical power and vow power. Using the divine abilities imbued in its implements consumed even more.

It was said that at Baoguang Temple, when a monk who followed the Dao of Incense Offerings operated the Mountain-Guarding Grand Formation to supply incense offerings, they could sometimes manifest a Heavenly King fifty zhang (about 165 m) tall, or a Wisdom King a hundred zhang tall.

However, maintaining such an enormous Dharma manifestation for long was difficult.

It was useful when defending the sect or attacking a wide area all at once, but under normal circumstances, the manifestation was usually condensed to a size the cultivator could comfortably sustain.

The annotations toward the end briefly mentioned Dharma manifestations that could be used after reaching Spirit Transformation, but did not contain the mnemonic formulas for those stages.

Lee Hyun set down the jade slip and examined the other inheritances.

He had also secured the Palm of Compassion, Fist of Deliverance, Demon-Subduing Seal, Mighty Vajra Body, and Arhat Golden Body, but he had no intention of cultivating all of them.

As Lee Hyun saw it, a significant number of Baoguang Temple's inheritances had one major drawback: they depended on Buddha-Light True Qi containing vow power.

The Buddha-Light True Qi he currently produced relied on his vow to preserve his primordial yang. In other words, if that vow were broken, he would no longer be able to use the techniques that depended on it.

‘I haven't had any affinity with women so far... but something unexpected could always happen.’

He did not want a power bound by such a condition to become his primary means of combat.

‘The Mighty Vajra Body requires far too many resources. I'd be better off using those resources to advance my whole-body cultivation. I can just study the martial principles behind the Palm of Compassion and Fist of Deliverance. I don't need the Arhat Golden Body either... because I'm going to create the Leakless Golden Body.’

One of the advantages of the Leakless Golden Body he intended to achieve was that it did not depend on Buddha-Light True Qi or vow power.

That was because the Leakless Golden Body had never been a cultivation method belonging to the Buddhist tradition in the first place. It was a result produced through the process of forming a golden core with the Primordial Body of the Primordial One-Qi Art.

Rather, the Arhat Golden Body was something monks had created after seeing the Leakless Golden Body and attempting to imitate its advantages.

Therefore, once Lee Hyun created the Leakless Golden Body, even if his vow were broken afterward, the golden-core structure established throughout his entire body and the resulting physical strength would remain intact.

There was no need for Lee Hyun to cultivate the Arhat Golden Body.

‘Let's start with the Demon-Subduing Seal and Sumeru Visualization Scripture.’

The Demon-Subduing Seal could suppress resentful spirits and ghostly entities, making it useful for Lee Hyun, who currently had no particular means of dealing with them.

The Sumeru Visualization Scripture would not help him in a fight right away, but it belonged to an entirely new area that did not overlap with his existing combat methods, so he decided to cultivate it as well.

Of course, both techniques depended on Buddha-Light True Qi.

But that did not matter if he used them only as supplementary methods rather than his primary means of combat. Moreover, the visualization cultivation of the Sumeru Visualization Scripture consisted of imprinting sacred images upon the mind, so at least that portion should remain even without vow power.

Having finished his thoughts, Lee Hyun put the jade slips away for the time being.

‘Now I need to gather information on demon markings.’

Three years later.

Lee Hyun followed Huitan into the Inner Alchemy Chamber of Lotus Court to participate in the alchemy of a Golden Core Condensing Pill.

Restrictions far thicker than those in the communal alchemy chambers covered the walls and floor. The burner inside was closed, yet a faint heat could be felt merely from stepping into the stone chamber.

Two disciples who had arrived earlier pressed their palms together in greeting.

“Greetings, Martial Uncle Huitan.”

Huitan nodded, and Lee Hyun greeted the two as well.

Both were late Foundation Establishment cultivators.

One of them was a Senior Brother who went by the Dharma name Mingzhen. Lee Hyun had encountered him several times during Refining practice. He was skilled at processing the flesh and blood of demon beasts and had already assisted with other alchemy sessions in the Inner Alchemy Chamber.

At the center of the stone chamber stood a waist-high stone platform, above which a blue demon core the size of an adult's fist slowly rotated.

Black energy flowed between the six golden sealing rings wrapped around its surface.

The faint sound coming from it resembled both the wind and the distant weeping of many people at once.

Lee Hyun's gaze lingered on the demon core.

It was a Tier-3 demon core.

A thin monk standing beside it raised his hand and pressed down on one of the golden sealing rings.

Hummm.

The weeping subsided.

“Everyone, come closer and take a look.”

It was Elder Huijue, a Golden Core cultivator and Tier-3 alchemist overseeing this batch of Golden Core Condensing Pills.

He pointed at the demon core.

“It came from an aquatic demon beast that lived in Heishui Pool. Resentful-spirit energy and toxic qi are heavily entangled within it, so processing it is somewhat troublesome.”

Black energy writhed beneath the surface of the demon core.

“The stronger resentful spirits and the more violent demon power have already been suppressed. Your task is to remove the baleful qi remaining in the outer layer.”

Huijue moved a fingertip. A narrow gap opened between the golden sealing rings, revealing blue, threadlike strands within.

The threads seemed tangled, yet continued in a consistent direction. Clumps of black energy were lodged between them like drops of ink.

“The blue must remain.”

Huijue's fingertip pointed to the black portions.

“This must be removed.”

He looked around at the disciples.

“If anything goes wrong, I'll intervene, so there's no need to be too nervous.”

The first disciple stepped forward and kindled a golden flame at his fingertip.

Whoosh.

As the flame seeped between the golden sealing rings, the black energy shrank back.

However, a faint poisonous mist soon rose from the demon core's surface. The disciple increased the flame slightly, causing the mist to vanish, but the blue threads beneath it trembled as well.

Huijue curled a finger.

Tap.

A golden sealing ring rotated and pushed the flame away.

“That will do.”

The disciple withdrew his hand.

“My apologies.”

“You did nothing wrong. You were merely a little slow in adjusting the flame after seeing how the baleful qi moved.”

After letting them examine the section that had been treated, Huijue opened the restriction over another area.

This time, Mingzhen stepped forward.

His Clear Yang Purifying Fire was much more finely controlled than that of the previous disciple.

The flame slowly followed the edge of the black energy. A thin wailing sound emerged from within the demon core, but Mingzhen's flame did not waver.

After some time, the black stain had diminished by roughly half.

Mingzhen did not try to press deeper and withdrew the flame.

Huijue nodded.

“Good. You didn't overreach.”

Mingzhen wiped the sweat from his forehead.

“I don't think I can handle the deeper portion.”

“This old monk can take care of that. You did exactly what could safely be entrusted to you.”

Finally, Lee Hyun stepped forward.

His master, Huitan, spoke from behind him.

“Do as you normally do.”

Lee Hyun nodded and examined the flows within the demon core.

Black energy clung in a thin film between the blue threads.

‘This seems easy...’

A small flame formed at his fingertip.

The center of the pale golden flame was almost white.

Lee Hyun spread his fingers slightly, and the flame split into several flame threads that flowed between the golden sealing rings.

It was a feat made possible by the Flame-Threading Art.

Still, many people knew how to divide flames into multiple strands, so those watching merely thought Lee Hyun was highly skilled.

Huijue's gaze settled on his fingertips.

The thin flames moved in different directions within the demon core.

Where the baleful qi had gathered thickly, they brightened slightly. Within narrow gaps where blue threads intertwined, they dimmed until they were almost invisible.

Ssssss.

As one strand of black energy burned away, the blue thread that had been pinned beneath it regained its original flow and quivered lightly.

Lee Hyun immediately shifted the position of the neighboring flames. He left room for the blue thread to move while slowly stripping away only the black stain clinging behind it.

Huijue's hand stopped above the golden sealing rings.

There was no need to intervene.

‘Was his name Li Dongsi? This fellow really is skilled!’

Some time later.

Lee Hyun withdrew his hand.

The blue threads were clearly revealed where the black stains had vanished. Even the baleful qi embedded deep within the narrow gaps had been removed, yet the pattern formed by the threads had barely changed.

The stone chamber fell silent for a moment.

Huijue drew the demon core closer and examined the section Lee Hyun had Refined several times.

Mingzhen also tilted his head slightly and peered at it.

“He even removed the baleful qi deeper inside... yet the underlying pattern is almost completely undamaged.”

Huijue slowly nodded.

“Indeed.”

The corners of Huitan's lips rose.

“What did I tell you?”

“I had heard he was good.”

Huijue looked at Lee Hyun.

“But he's even better than I expected! I didn't know he could divide his Clear Yang Purifying Fire like that while maintaining such precise fire control over each individual strand.”

Lee Hyun pressed his palms together.

“You flatter me.”

Huitan spoke with a satisfied expression.

“His primordial yang is so pure that he can remove baleful qi even with his fire control kept that low. My disciple is practically at the level of a man who's never even held a woman's hand.”

‘...’

Huijue snorted.

“Maybe he just hasn’t met the right woman yet.”

“What are you talking about?”

“I mean he might think differently after seeing Young Lady Wang smile.”

Huitan's expression stiffened.

“Don't entertain such foolish ideas. What good would come of snuffing out such a precious flame?”

...

After the disciples finished processing the outer layer, Huijue and Huitan stepped in to Refine the baleful qi deeper within and remove the toxicity that had seeped deep between the condensed structures.

Lee Hyun watched every detail of their methods.

After several days of Refining and compounding, the pill furnace was finally opened.

A pill glowing with a faint golden hue rose through the mist.

It was a Golden Core Condensing Pill.

Lee Hyun's gaze remained fixed on the pill.

Huijue placed it on a jade dish and used his magical power to draw out a trace of its medicinal strength.

The medicinal fragrance grew richer.

Within the faint energy rising into the air, Lee Hyun saw a familiar flow.

It resembled what had been inside the demon core, but the energies of multiple medicinal ingredients had been added, making it far gentler and more stable.

“Can you see it?”

Huijue asked.

“Yes.”

“This is what helps condense true essence.”

After finishing his explanation, Huijue held out a small spirit tablet to Lee Hyun.

“From now on, take on Refining work in the Inner Alchemy Chamber. You'll begin by processing the outer layers. Learn the other steps by watching from the side.”

“Thank you.”

When Lee Hyun accepted the spirit tablet, Huitan added from beside him.

“There are Refining records in the study inside. Before handling an unfamiliar material, be sure to read them. There can be differences depending on the demon core.”

“Are there also records of the cultivators who took the pills?”

Huijue's gaze turned toward Lee Hyun.

“There are. Is there something you're curious about?”

“I'd like to know how much of the demon markings remain when someone takes several Golden Core Condensing Pills.”

Huijue thought for a moment.

“I'm not sure about that myself. Golden Core Condensing Pills are precious, so there probably aren't many people who've received and taken several... Still, when you have time, go look through the records.”

...

That evening.

Lee Hyun sat in a small study inside the Inner Alchemy Chamber.

Several jade slips lay on the table.

The species of demon beast, the state of its demon core, the medicinal ingredients and Refining methods used, and the quality of the completed pill.

Baoguang Temple had also recorded what happened after each Golden Core Condensing Pill was made.

They documented the recipient's realm and age, whether their Core Formation succeeded, and what form the demon markings took. Some cultivators continued examining their own golden cores at regular intervals even after Core Formation and sent back records of their findings.

Many of the diagrams were more detailed than those Lee Hyun had seen in Mei Sujun's jade slip.

Lee Hyun first selected cases in which cultivators had taken two or more Golden Core Condensing Pills.

Fortunately, several such records remained.

The amount and form of the remaining demon markings varied from person to person, but taking more Golden Core Condensing Pills did not necessarily make the refining process slower.

There were even cases in which the demon markings faded more quickly than in cultivators who had taken only one pill.

‘If that's the case... isn't this fine?’

Lee Hyun laid out in sequence the diagrams one cultivator had submitted over several decades. The demon markings had not been erased one location at a time. Instead, the foreign flows throughout the golden core had gradually faded together as the years passed.

‘So taking fifty Golden Core Condensing Pills wouldn't mean spending fifty thousand years refining them.’

...

The next day.

Just to be certain, Lee Hyun asked his master Huitan about the matter.

“Is my guess correct?”

Huitan looked down at the diagrams his disciple had spread out, then nodded.

“You don't pick out the demon markings and erase them one by one. Following the refining formulas, you circulate your magical power evenly throughout the entire golden core. Changes occur simultaneously everywhere that magical power flows. You should still have some time before Core Formation. Are you already curious about things like this?”

“I heard that Elders who achieved Core Formation using Golden Core Condensing Pills have difficulty breaking through to Nascent Soul. If this problem can be solved, I thought it might be a great help to Baoguang Temple.”

“You really... just how much merit are you trying to accumulate? I certainly hope you find a way through this problem so this master of yours can break through to Nascent Soul!”

“Did you also achieve Core Formation using a Golden Core Condensing Pill, Master?”

“I did.”

Lee Hyun pressed his palms together.

“This disciple will think about whether there is a way to accelerate the refining.”

“Hoho, I was only joking. Countless people have already studied the problem without solving it.”

...

After returning to his residence, Lee Hyun took out the Golden Core section of the Primordial One-Qi Art and examined its contents closely.

‘Based on everything I've learned so far, it should be worth preparing for Core Formation with this method while using Golden Core Condensing Pills.’

To do that, he first needed to learn the pill recipes.

However, a problem arose when it came to learning the recipes for the Golden Core Condensing Pill.

Or, more precisely... there were far too many different Golden Core Condensing Pill recipes.

The characteristics of a demon core differed between every species of Tier-3 demon beast, so the alchemy method had to be adapted accordingly.

Even if Lee Hyun became stronger in the future, there was no guarantee he would be able to obtain enough Tier-3 demon cores from a single species. Therefore, he needed to observe the alchemy process for as many different kinds of Tier-3 demon cores as possible.

‘At this rate, I'll have to stick around Baoguang Temple for quite a while... I need to watch them process as many kinds of demon cores as possible, don't I? Well, I have plenty of time anyway, so it doesn't matter...’

Fortunately, the Golden Core Elders of Baoguang Temple permitted Foundation Establishment alchemist disciples to naturally learn the pill recipes while observing the alchemy of Golden Core Condensing Pills.

In truth, the Golden Core Condensing Pill recipes themselves were not particularly precious to Baoguang Temple.

The greatest problem was the simple fact that their key ingredient was a Tier-3 demon core.

Those who needed Golden Core Condensing Pills were cultivators at Foundation Establishment Great Perfection, yet cultivators at that realm could not hunt Tier-3 demon beasts. Without the assistance of a Golden Core cultivator, obtaining one was something they could only dream of.

Unless, of course, someone appeared who could easily slay Tier-3 demon beasts while still at Foundation Establishment Great Perfection.

...

And so Lee Hyun continued visiting the Inner Alchemy Chamber and learning the process for refining Golden Core Condensing Pills.

Every different type of demon core gave him something new to learn, so even after finishing his assigned Refining work, he often stayed to watch the Elders continue with the remaining steps.

He also steadily continued cultivating the Demon-Subduing Seal and the Sumeru Visualization Scripture.

From time to time, he left the sect to handle matters concerning the Two Heavens Society and tend to the spirit fields and fuzzbees of Tunnel No. 3.

Before he knew it, ten years had passed.

Lee Hyun's residence on the eastern peak of Lotus Court.

Lee Hyun reclined on a long couch by the window, reading a popular novel.

On one side of the table lay the Refining records he had organized that morning, while beside them was a stack of books he had yet to open.

He had already finished his assigned work for the day.

Just as the protagonist of the novel was about to open a treasure chest in an undersea ruin, a faint vibration came from the restriction outside the door.

Lee Hyun raised his head.

‘Who is it?’

A young monk stood outside his residence.

“Elder Huitan has summoned you.”

Lee Hyun slipped a bookmark into the novel and rose from his seat.

...

Several jade slips and a folded letter lay in Huitan's study.

The seal on the letter bore the name of an unfamiliar country.

Haiguang Kingdom.

It was a mortal kingdom on the southern coast under the protection of Xu Kingdom's cultivation world.

“Sit.”

Huitan held out a jade slip.

“This is a report from the south.”

Lee Hyun sat down and sent his divine sense into the jade slip.

Tier-2 aquatic demon beasts had been appearing along various parts of Xu Kingdom's southern coastline and attacking people.

The first report had come from Baisha Port in Haiguang Kingdom.

Five fishing boats had failed to return, and enormous bite marks had been found on wreckage washed ashore.

Not long afterward, demon beasts began coming all the way into the shallows.

Monks from local temples stepped forward and moved the people away from the coast, but Qi Refining cultivators were incapable of dealing with Tier-2 demon beasts. For now, all boats had been forbidden from sailing, and the residents of coastal villages were being relocated inside nearby cities.

Similar reports had also come from other ports some distance from Baisha Port.

Several mortal kingdoms along the coast had rushed to request aid from Baoguang Temple, and the temple had decided to dispatch disciples to save the sentient beings there.

Lee Hyun examined the latter portion of the jade slip.

There were illustrations recording the demon beasts' appearances and movements.

One was a turtle-shaped demon beast with a thick shell, while the other was a water snake with a long, slender body and red stripes.

Huitan spoke.

“This water snake normally even preys on that turtle. Yet they attacked the boats together, and when the monks approached, they retreated in the same direction.”

“They may be spirit beasts under someone's control.”

“That's why the Demon-Subduing Court isn't treating this as a simple demon-beast extermination either. They intend to determine whether a beast tamer is controlling them or whether some other method is being used.”

Huitan paused briefly, then added,

“Lotus Court has decided to send people this time as well. They'll examine the traces remaining in the demon beasts' flesh, blood, and meridians, and preserve any necessary materials to bring back.”

Huitan looked at Lee Hyun.

“The temple said they would like you to make the trip. When they were discussing whom to send, Junior Brother Huijue strongly recommended you. It seems he thinks quite highly of the Refining skills you've shown over the years.”

A hint of pride could be heard in Huitan's voice.

Lee Hyun studied the demon beasts drawn on the jade slip for a moment longer, then recalled the rearing records of the Life-Bound Gu he had obtained long ago.

Just because demon beasts that normally did not get along were moving together did not necessarily mean gu insects were involved. But if gu had been implanted in them to control them, it would explain the situation.

‘Is the Dongming Sect of the Nanming Twelve-Sect Alliance making a move?’

Lee Hyun readily agreed.

“Understood.”

‘If the Dongming Sect is controlling demon beasts by implanting gu in them... they'd make excellent food for the fuzzbees...’

Huitan nodded in satisfaction when Lee Hyun agreed so readily.

...

On the day of departure, in front of the Mountain Gate.

“Junior Brother, over here.”

Lee Hyun turned his head at the clear voice, like jade beads rolling across a silver tray.

It was Wang Shulin, Elder Huijue's direct disciple.

She was stunningly beautiful.

Her eyes were gentle and the corners of her lips naturally curved slightly upward, giving her a strangely captivating air that made people feel good simply looking at her, even when she was not smiling.

Far from shaving her head, she had loosely pinned half of her lustrous, jet-black hair up with a jade hairpin, while the rest cascaded softly over her slender shoulders and down her back.

Her attire was equally far removed from dull monastic robes. Her silk enchanted robe, woven in subtle shades of jade and white, fluttered like wings whenever the wind blew. Each time she moved, wrists as pale as white jade showed between her sleeves, accompanied by a delicate fragrance.

She stared openly at Lee Hyun for a moment before her eyes curved into crescents and a mischievous smile appeared on her face.

“So you're the famous Primordial Yang Layman, Junior Brother? Master told me about you. Looks like I won't be bored.”

Watching from some distance away, Huitan grabbed Huijue by the sleeve.

“Huijue, you wretched bald monk! You've really set your mind on snuffing out my disciple's flame!”

“Hohoho, Senior Brother Huitan, really now. Wouldn't a young man and woman going together to save sentient beings also be a fine immortal affinity? Hm. If his Dao heart is as unyielding as vajra, how could a mere woman's smile possibly shake it?”

Chapter 79

Wang Shulin smiled, as though she was already used to their masters bickering.

“Come on. They’re always like that, so there’s no need to pay them any mind.”

“Yes.”

A small flying boat hovered over the open ground before the Mountain Gate. A female cultivator was already standing on the deck, her hair tied high with a red cord.

The sleeves of her dark navy enchanted robe were fastened tightly around her wrists, and a black spear case was strapped across her back. The head of a spear, hung with six iron rings, protruded from the top of the case. She had been gazing down the mountain with one hand resting on the railing, but turned when the two approached.

‘Ah, so that’s her.’

Lee Hyun recognized the face from Senior Brother Mingxiu’s picture album. She was a beautiful woman with a pleasant, refreshingly straightforward air.

Cultivators were generally better-looking than mortals.

Even Qi Refining cultivators benefited from a degree of marrow cleansing, and by the time one reached Foundation Establishment, not only did blemishes disappear from the skin, but facial asymmetry and irregularities in the bone structure were largely corrected as well.

For example, Li Dongsi appeared to cultivators to be somewhere in his forties, while his actual age was estimated to be between forty and a hundred. But that was merely the impression he gave by the cultivation world’s exacting standards. To a mortal, he would have looked no older than his late twenties or early thirties.

The effect was even more pronounced among female cultivators. Once the flaws in their appearance disappeared, even a little makeup was enough for them to be called peerless beauties by the standards of the mundane world.

Some even went out of their way to obtain and take pills such as Appearance-Preserving Pills to make themselves look younger. As a result, they generally looked younger or more beautiful than male cultivators.

This was one of the reasons certain monks of Baoguang Temple who had sworn to preserve their primordial yang suffered all the more!

The female cultivator from the Demon-Subduing Court before him did not seem to have made any particular effort to beautify herself, but perhaps because she had broken through to Foundation Establishment at a young age, she looked remarkably youthful.

Wang Shulin raised a hand toward the flying boat.

“Senior Sister Lu, have you been waiting long?”

“I only just got here.”

The female cultivator gave Lee Hyun a slight greeting.

“I’m Lu Hongyan of the Demon-Subduing Court. I’ll be handling the escort this time.”

“I’m Li Dongsi of the Lotus Court. I’ll be in your care, Senior Sister Lu.”

Lee Hyun could sense the aura of late Foundation Establishment from Lu Hongyan. Wang Shulin was around Foundation Establishment Stage 6, so Lu Hongyan was considerably stronger. He had also heard that Lu Hongyan had entered the sect several years before Wang Shulin.

“You two focus on examining the materials. If any demon beasts appear, I’ll take the front.”

After confirming that both of them were aboard, she activated the flying boat’s restrictions.

The vessel slowly rose into the air.

...

Mountain ranges stretched endlessly beneath the clouds.

Whenever the flying boat descended, they could see terraced fields arranged like steps and villages strung out along the waterways. Many of the villages had small temples at their centers.

Lee Hyun gazed down at the scenery for a while before taking a book from his storage pouch.

It was a popular novel he had not yet finished.

“What are you reading?”

As Wang Shulin sat down beside him, a faint fragrance drifted over on the wind.

“A novel.”

“Is it good?”

“It’s decent enough. I tend to read just about anything.”

Wang Shulin tilted her head slightly toward the open book. A lock of her hair slipped down and brushed against his arm.

“Mind if I read along?”

“Hmm... Shall I take out another novel for you?”

“That sounds like too much trouble. I’ll just read what you’re reading.”

Lee Hyun looked at her.

Up close, her eyelashes were long. When she smiled, her eyes curved gently, and a playful glimmer danced in her clear pupils.

‘She really is beautiful. But I can’t let my two-thousand-year record end now! I have to stay strong.’

Ever since witnessing the power of the Clear Yang Purifying Fire, Lee Hyun had developed the strange goal of preserving the record he had built up over all those years.

In terms of his past life, it was like reaching thirty without ever dating anyone and then discovering that doing so really had given him the ability to use magic.

He could actually produce Buddha-Light True Qi from his hands, and its power grew stronger with every passing year. Once he became fascinated by that ability, suppressing his interest in the opposite sex was not particularly difficult.

Wang Shulin met his gaze for a moment, then the corners of her lips rose.

“Master made it sound as if you were completely uninterested in romance.”

“Haha. I’m simply focused on cultivation...”

Wang Shulin let out a soft laugh, and Lu Hongyan, who was piloting the flying boat, glanced back at them.

...

Quite some time later.

As soon as Lee Hyun closed his book, Wang Shulin spoke as though she had been waiting for him to finish.

“Last time, when I was working on the inside of the golden ring, I tried doing it the way you do. It was much easier.”

“It’s only a minor trick.”

Wang Shulin took out a small notebook and flipped through several pages. She opened it to a page containing drawings of a demon core’s cross-section and the flow of flames, asked him a couple of questions, then jotted down a few notes in the margin.

“No wonder Senior Martial Uncle Huitan treasures you so much when you have skills like this.”

“It’s all because Master taught me well.”

“Still, he goes too far with all that talk about primordial yang. You have desires too, don’t you?”

Wang Shulin lowered the notebook onto her lap.

“By the way, do you plan to keep that vow forever?”

“Hmm... It hasn’t been very long since I made the vow. From the records left by the Seniors, preserving one’s primordial yang seems to be one of the most powerful ways to generate vow power.”

“What if you change your mind later?”

“I suppose I’ll think about it when that happens.”

“Apparently, there’s also a way to cultivate vow power without making vows.”

Lee Hyun turned his gaze toward her.

“How?”

“There’s an inheritance like that on the third floor of the Scripture Pavilion. It’s called the Sutra of Refining Intent into Vow.”

At the front of the flying boat, Lu Hongyan turned her head.

“Junior Sister Wang, you read that too?”

“Only the preface. Master once sent me up there to look for some records, and the title sounded strange, so I took a look.”

Wang Shulin turned back to Lee Hyun.

“Did you know? Even if you keep an oath, vow power won’t accumulate unless you’re consciously aware that you’re keeping it. What do you think that means? It means it isn’t as though heaven itself is keeping track of who keeps their oaths and handing out vow power.”

“Uh... Then what matters isn’t simply whether you actually keep the oath, but your own state of mind?”

“Right. A Dharma teaching refines your conviction that you’ve kept your vow and turns it into vow power. So vow power can be considered a kind of mental power. It isn’t something only sects of the Buddhist tradition, like our Baoguang Temple, can use. Cultivators skilled in sorcery or incantations can wield similar powers.”

“Does the Sutra of Refining Intent into Vow create vow power in a different way?”

“That inheritance uses visualization and spirit refinement to nurture a mind seal within the primordial spirit. Once it becomes stable enough, it can generate vow power without relying on a vow that requires adhering to a particular course of action.”

Lu Hongyan asked,

“If it’s that good, why don’t they teach it?”

“Because it’s too difficult and takes too long.”

Wang Shulin gave a small shrug.

“Plenty of people cultivate it for decades without managing to establish a proper mind seal, and establishing one isn’t the end of it either. Forcing an unstable mind seal into use can injure the primordial spirit, so it has to be refined for a long time afterward as well. By comparison, if you simply make a vow and keep your oath, you can use Buddha-Light True Qi with similar effects in a much shorter time.”

“I see. Better to spend that time learning a different inheritance. Time is spirit stones, after all.”

Wang Shulin laughed and nodded at Lu Hongyan’s remark.

Lee Hyun was silent for a moment.

‘So that’s how it works. If I learn that, I won’t have to keep clinging to my vow forever. I can just cultivate it slowly...’

Wang Shulin added,

“If you’re interested, look it up sometime. If fate allows, you might get a chance to read it. But learning it won’t automatically erase the vow you’ve already made. I heard you’d also have to separately learn how to withdraw the vow power you’ve accumulated. And it’s also true that preserving your primordial yang benefits the Clear Yang Purifying Fire Art.”

“I see.”

Wang Shulin placed a small drawing board on her lap.

The rooftops and trees of a village they had passed earlier were drawn on it.

“You learned to paint as well?”

“Mm. It’s actually related to my vow.”

Wang Shulin answered as she moved her brush.

Instead of ink, golden Buddha-Light True Qi suffused the tip of the brush.

“I vowed to draw one thing I’ve never drawn before with my own hand every day.”

“That’s a good vow. It must be useful for sharpening your powers of observation.”

“Exactly. It comes in handy during fights too.”

“In fights?”

“This brush is a magic tool. If I draw a crane with fire, it flies out and attacks my enemy. If I draw a tiger, it charges out and bites them.”

“That’s remarkable.”

The sheets of paper stacked beneath the drawing board depicted things like an unknown insect, a broken teacup, and a twisted tree branch.

The tip of her brush moved along the tree’s slender branches.

A while later, Wang Shulin raised the brush and examined her drawing.

“This tree really is shaped strangely!”

She suddenly stood up and struck an absurd pose.

Lu Hongyan looked at her.

“Do you really have to act it out with your whole body?”

Lee Hyun asked,

“Senior Sister Lu, what vow did you make?”

“I vowed not to hide the mistakes I make in battle. Win or lose, I record them.”

Lu Hongyan pointed to a small booklet at her waist.

“Do you show it to other people?”

“No. I’m pretty much the only one who reads it.”

“And that still counts as a vow?”

“Surprisingly, yes. People have a tendency to deceive even themselves and rationalize their mistakes. Facing those things head-on is quite difficult.”

She spoke calmly.

“When I win, it’s easy to think I won because I was skilled, and when I lose, to blame it on my opponent having a better magic tool or better luck. But I may have been luckier than I realize, and my opponent may have been unlucky. Most importantly, when it sounds like an opponent was simply lucky, that’s often because they were being modest when they described what happened. Thanks to this vow, I’m not only producing Buddha-Light True Qi, I’m improving my actual skills more quickly as well.”

“That’s a good vow.”

“The downside is that I need to fight often to create opportunities for my vow power to grow. If I’m not careful, that can turn into a dangerous habit of throwing myself into deadly situations. It’s important not to let your own vow control you.”

...

As sunset approached, Wang Shulin spread out a fresh sheet of paper.

With the brush handle held between her teeth, she looked around. Her gaze passed over the sky, the clouds, the railing, and Lu Hongyan before finally settling on Lee Hyun.

“I haven’t drawn Junior Brother Li’s face yet.”

A short while later, Wang Shulin stopped her brush and looked back and forth between the picture and Lee Hyun.

“That’s strange...”

“What is?”

“Your face doesn’t have many distinctive features. Maybe I’d say it leaves a sort of vague impression...”

“Haha...”

Lee Hyun realized it was because of his Seven-Aspect Disguise Method.

‘I should research disguise arts a little more too.’

Several days later, Baisha Port in Haiguang Kingdom.

It lay roughly thirty thousand li (about 11,760 km) south of Baoguang Temple.

Small houses stretched beyond a wooden palisade erected along the coast. Flat stones weighed down the roofs, and wooden posts for hanging fishing nets out to dry stood in every alley.

But perhaps all the nets had been taken down, because when the flying boat entered the air above the port, the only thing stirring was a lone scrap of cloth.

Two boats remained at the docks. One had a large section torn from its side, while the other lay tilted on the beach with its hull exposed.

Lee Hyun examined the underside of the damaged boat.

A thick scale was lodged between the planks.

“Have you come from the main temple?”

An elderly monk in gray robes approached from a low hill behind the port, accompanied by two young monks.

All three were Qi Refining cultivators. The elderly monk had reached Qi Refining Great Perfection, but in the presence of three Foundation Establishment cultivators, even his steps were noticeably cautious.

Lu Hongyan lowered the flying boat and showed her spirit tablet.

“I’m Lu Hongyan of Baoguang Temple’s Demon-Subduing Court. These two have come with me from the Lotus Court.”

The elderly monk pressed his palms together and bowed until he was nearly bent in half.

“This humble monk is Yuanwu, abbot of Hai’an Temple. This humble monk and the others lacked the strength to handle the matter ourselves and have troubled the Immortal Masters to journey so far.”

Dried mud stained the hem of his robes, and one sleeve had been patched with a piece of new cloth.

“Have all the residents been evacuated?”

“Yes. The last cart left three days ago. They’re staying inside the city to the north now.”

“Good.”

Wang Shulin spoke.

“You’ve been keeping the demon-beast carcasses, I hear?”

“We have no intact specimens. They are not demon beasts this humble monk and the others are capable of killing. We did recover a few that washed ashore already dead, however....”

“Show us those first.”

...

A stone chamber behind Hai’an Temple.

When the sealing talisman on the door was removed, a fishy stench seeped out.

A turtle’s hind leg, fragments of a shattered carapace, and part of a water snake’s torso lay on a stone table. A preservation formation was running, but the materials were in poor condition.

Yuanwu explained,

“They say the water snake coiled around the boat while the turtle rammed it from below. When this humble monk and the others approached using talismans, the two withdrew eastward together.”

Lee Hyun examined the carapace fragments and the water snake’s torso in turn. He saw neither gu insects nor silver needles.

‘Could it really have nothing to do with the Dongming Sect?’

There was too little left, however, to conclude from this alone that the creatures had not been controlled.

“Have they appeared again recently?”

At Lu Hongyan’s question, Yuanwu nodded.

“Yesterday around sunset, we saw two turtles on an offshore sandbar. We did not dare approach them carelessly.”

“Show us where.”

...

A little over a hundred li east of the port.

Narrow channels ran between sandbars exposed by the receding tide. In every pool left behind by the sea, small fish moved about, flashing their silver bellies.

Lu Hongyan lowered the flying boat.

“There they are.”

Two shapes like black boulders huddled together at the end of the sandbar.

When Lee Hyun swept them with his divine sense, one slowly moved.

It was a turtle.

Its carapace was nearly three zhang (about 9.9 m) long. Seaweed and barnacles clung to its shell, and hook-like claws grew from the ends of its thick feet.

“Dark-Armored Sea Turtles. The big one looks like it’s late Tier 2.”

Lu Hongyan spoke.

Lee Hyun looked at the channel between the two turtles.

There was a long red line beneath the water.

“There’s a snake as well.”

“Mm. I saw it.”

Lu Hongyan landed on a rocky stretch of coast and put the flying boat into her storage pouch.

“Let’s take those three down first.”

A palm-sized bronze incense burner floated out of Wang Shulin’s sleeve.

It stood on three short legs, and its lid was shaped like a closed lotus. When she infused it with spiritual power, the petals opened, revealing a glowing red ember inside.

She held a brush in her other hand.

“I’ll keep the smaller one pinned down. Please leave the head intact. We need to see whether it was being controlled.”

“Got it. Junior Brother Li, watch the water snake.”

Lu Hongyan flicked two fingers and pointed into the air.

Thoom!

The spear case on her back burst open, and a long spear tore through the air.

Its six iron rings shrieked as a piercing whistle split the air.

It crossed dozens of zhang in an instant. Golden Buddha-Light True Qi flowed like lightning along the shaft of the flying spear.

The Dark-Armored Sea Turtle raised its head.

Whoooosh!

A torrent of murky water erupted from its mouth like a cannon shot.

“Break through!”

The instant Lu Hongyan stabbed her fingers downward through the air, Wang Shulin’s brush scattered sparks behind her.

She slashed the brush through the air, sketching a neck and wings. The crimson ember inside the incense burner spewed fierce flames that swallowed her brushstrokes.

Fwoooosh!

Just as the long spear twisted in front of the torrent and expanded to three zhang in length, a blazing fire crane swept in low.

Boom!

The long spear slammed down on the turtle’s back, crushing the barrier of water surrounding its carapace.

Golden ripples spread from the point where the spearhead struck. A low sutra chant sounded, and each successive ripple shattered another layer of the water barrier, spraying enormous sheets of water in every direction.

Hidden by the spray, the fire crane swept in and lashed flames across the smaller turtle’s face.

Hissss―

The shallow seawater boiled in an instant, filling the air with thick, fishy steam. Blinded, the smaller turtle recoiled in fright and tucked in its head.

But the larger one, a late Tier 2 demon beast, was different.

Grrrrrr!

With a piercing roar, all the seaweed clinging to its shell stood on end. Seawater surged upward from every nearby pool and gathered into a spinning water wheel as large as a house.

The fierce vortex repeatedly knocked aside the long spear as it tried to strike the creature’s flank. Sparks flew from the spearhead as it scraped across the carapace and glanced away.

Then an enormous water wheel, tearing up the entire sandbar in its path, hurtled toward the rock where the three stood.

“Up!”

Lu Hongyan rose first, and Lee Hyun and Wang Shulin split to either side and flew into the air.

Rumble!

The water wheel swept directly beneath their feet and tore away the entire edge of the rocky outcrop. Spray and gravel flew in every direction, stinging their cheeks.

When the surging seawater collapsed one of the fire crane’s wings, the smaller turtle seized the opening and burst through the spray.

“Not so fast!”

As Wang Shulin descended, she turned her brush sideways and drew a long stroke.

The fire crane’s body instantly unraveled and transformed into a low, elongated wall of fire.

Terrified by the flames blocking its path, the creature twisted away from the scorching sand. But directly behind the larger turtle was a blind spot with no room to escape.

“Got you!”

A vajra shot from Lu Hongyan’s sleeve, trailing golden light as it fell over the heads of the two turtles.

Hummm!

The vajra swelled to three zhang long and released an enormous wave of spiritual power.

A huge golden circle spread beneath it. As though crushed beneath an invisible millstone, the two creatures’ feet sank deep into the sand. Sand was forced outward all around them, and even the current the larger turtle had been gathering was crushed apart.

But the larger turtle desperately raised its head.

Its thick neck stretched taut, and a mass of blue water swelled inside its mouth, brimming with toxic qi.

Lu Hongyan crooked her finger downward, and the circling long spear plunged like a bolt of lightning.

Boom!

The spear, dyed golden, drove into the creature’s open mouth, pierced through its neck, and buried itself in the sandbar. Blood erupted like a fountain, and the gathering mass of water burst apart without strength.

Amid the reek of blood, Lee Hyun caught sight of a red line at the edge of his vision. It was slicing through a shallow channel as it slipped away.

‘The water snake!’

It was trying to escape across the tidal flats while the turtles held their attention.

Lee Hyun reached out, and the gigantic hand formed by the Condensed-Essence Grasping Hand split through the surface of the water in an instant.

The water snake twisted its body.

Shwaaak!

Dozens of water needles burst from the surface and rained toward Lee Hyun’s face.

Clang!

A turquoise shield plate swept in front of him and shattered the needles to pieces.

Meanwhile, the giant hand plunged beneath the surface and clamped tightly around the water snake just below its head.

Splash!

A body that looked at least five zhang long was hauled into the air. The water snake thrashed its tail violently around the giant hand’s wrist, while dark red mist seeped from its gaping mouth.

Just before the poison mist could spread, Lee Hyun lightly flicked a finger.

Slice.

A flash of silver sword light shot from his sleeve and grazed the back of the snake’s neck, cutting cleanly through the joint between two vertebrae.

Its long body writhed several times before going limp.

As Lee Hyun dragged the carcass onto the sandbar, he wrapped the escaping poison mist in flames and burned it away.

The Sinking Moon Sword had already returned to his storage pouch.

Thoom!

At that moment, Lu Hongyan’s long spear tore free from the larger turtle’s neck and traced a crimson arc through the air. It pierced the smaller turtle through the back of the neck, still pinned beneath the vajra, and buried itself in the sandbar.

The surroundings fell silent.

...

Lu Hongyan recalled the vajra and washed the blood from the tip of her long spear in the seawater.
