After shrinking the spear back to its original size and returning it to the case on her back, she examined the larger turtle’s foreleg, which had been hidden beneath its carapace.

“It was already injured? Come to think of it, its reactions were strange from the start.”

Lee Hyun approached to inspect it as well. A deep chunk had been gouged from its thick flesh. Dark, clotted blood crusted the edges, and some of the muscle deeper inside had been severed.

When Wang Shulin shifted the turtle’s body slightly, a similar wound appeared on the opposite side of the carapace.

“You didn’t inflict these wounds, did you, Senior Sister?”

“No.”

Wang Shulin took out a small piece of paper and marked the locations.

Lu Hongyan turned toward the water snake Lee Hyun had moved aside.

“Junior Brother Li, you’re surprisingly good in a fight.”

“I was fortunate.”

Lee Hyun washed the remaining sand from the water snake’s body.

The fellow had a long wound along its flank as well.

...

The three moved the carcasses onto a flat stretch of rock along the nearby coast.

A low cliff extended behind them, and a narrow path wide enough for a person to walk along ran to the left.

While Lu Hongyan kept watch over the surroundings, Wang Shulin and Lee Hyun divided the carcasses between themselves.

Wang Shulin straightened out the water snake’s body, inserted needles at each point she intended to cut, and sliced beneath the scales.

She collected the flowing blood directly into jade bottles and tied off the meridians around the venom sac in advance.

Lee Hyun examined the turtle’s neck and the inner side of its carapace.

‘If there were a gu insect, the fuzzbees should react...’

The spirit-insect pouch remained quiet.

Still, Lee Hyun examined the carcass thoroughly, just in case.

The location where a gu insect was implanted varied depending on the method and the host.

In the demon beasts he had captured long ago at Haimen Port, he had found spirit insects beneath the venom sacs or around the neck. The breeding records for Life-Bound Gu also described methods that used other locations where meridians converged.

He opened each suspicious area in turn.

But even after employing several detection methods, including his divine sense, Aura-Reading Art, and Keen Hearing Art, then dissecting the carcass himself, he found nothing.

‘Looks like the fuzzbees won’t be getting a meal.’

...

Quite some time later, Wang Shulin called to Lee Hyun.

“Junior Brother Li. Come look at this.”

A piece of flesh cut from the water snake’s flank lay in front of her.

Several thin meridians beneath the wound had turned black.

“At first I thought the fellow’s own poison had seeped into them, but the reaction is different.”

Wang Shulin dripped a drop of medicinal liquid onto it. The reddish mucus slowly turned clear, but the blackened sections remained unchanged.

Lee Hyun activated the Aura-Reading Art and examined the interior.

“It seems to be demon power from another demon beast.”

Lee Hyun placed a piece of flesh he had cut from the turtle’s foreleg beside it, and the same energy revealed itself within those meridians.

Wang Shulin spread two sheets of paper beside them, each marked with the locations of the injuries. They showed the marks on both sides of the carapace and on the water snake’s flank.

Lu Hongyan had approached without them noticing and looked down at the papers.

“...Claws?”

“It looks as though something grabbed them and then lost its grip. The same demon power remains in the wounds too.”

“There were no traces of gu insects either. It doesn’t look like someone was controlling them and making them move together.”

At Lee Hyun’s words, Lu Hongyan turned toward the sea.

“Does that mean there’s something around here capable of attacking Tier 2 demon beasts?”

All three felt a vague sense of unease.

“Let’s head back for now. Don’t search any farther.”

They were hurriedly gathering the venom sac, demon blood, and pieces of carapace when a sloshing sound came from below the rocks.

Lee Hyun looked down and saw that a stone which had been visible beneath his feet moments earlier was now underwater.

‘Is the tide coming in already?’

But something was wrong.

The seawater was not flowing inward. Instead, it was swelling upward in a broad curve from farther offshore.

A black back broke the surface.

A Dark-Armored Sea Turtle.

Then another appeared behind it.

“Senior Sister.”

Before Lee Hyun could finish calling out, Lu Hongyan was already taking the flying boat from her storage pouch and activating its restrictions.

As the three boarded, the vessel lifted away from the rocks.

Its altitude had changed only slightly, yet the sea looked completely different.

Black shadows filled every channel beyond the sandbars.

There were far more than one or two.

Lee Hyun extended his divine sense, then his expression hardened.

Ten, twenty.

There were dozens within sight alone. Beneath the surface, the auras of Tier 2 demon beasts surged toward them like waves.

“We’re heading north immediately.”

Lu Hongyan turned the bow of the flying boat.

Wang Shulin summoned her incense burner and took out a voice-transmission talisman with her other hand.

“Yuanwu. A horde of Tier 2 demon beasts is converging on the eastern coast. Evacuate the temple and retreat to the city. Immediately.”

As soon as she finished speaking, the talisman streaked westward, leaving a trail of light behind it.

BOOM!

At that exact moment, the surface below the rocks exploded, and a demon beast with a blue dorsal fin burst from the water and slammed into the underside of the flying boat.

Thud!

A turquoise shield plate flashed beneath the vessel and deflected the impact at an angle.

Thrown off course, the demon beast’s massive body crashed into the cliff opposite them.

Rumble!

With a deafening crash, the sheer rock face collapsed.

“Keep going.”

With a single gesture, Lee Hyun sent two more shield plates spinning into place, completely covering the underside and right side of the flying boat.

Wang Shulin’s brush danced, tracing dazzling arcs.

Using the fierce flames erupting from the incense burner, she drew a huge ring in the air, infused it with spiritual power, and hurled it toward the sea behind the flying boat.

Rrrrrumble!

The flames exploded outward in a circle the instant they struck the surface. An enormous volume of seawater boiled in moments, sending up a dense wall of scalding steam that completely obscured the vision of the dozens of demon beasts leaping after them.

The flying boat shot over the top of the cliff at tremendous speed.

Yet even as Lu Hongyan accelerated, she could not tear her gaze away from the sea.

The outer waters from which the demon beasts had come.

Several li away, a reef was slowly sinking beneath the surface.

No.

Something behind the reef was rising to its feet.

A long, massive arm emerged, and its fingers closed around the rock. The reef, large enough to be clearly visible even from this distance, crumbled helplessly in its grasp.

Shaking seawater from its body, an enormous ape straightened its back.

The fellow was covered in brown fur, while scales grew across its chest and belly. When it lowered its webbed hands, the waist-deep seawater split apart to either side.

Thoom―

The instant it looked in their direction, a headache struck all three of them as though lightning had exploded inside their skulls. Chilling killing intent and crushing pressure washed over them.

A tremendous wave of divine sense had swept across the entire coastline.

“A Tier 3 demon beast....”

Lu Hongyan’s voice dropped.

The flying boat accelerated again.

Lee Hyun looked back and judged the distance. It was still far away. He did not know how fast that thing could move through the sea, but if they flew farther inland now....

Whoooosh―

At that moment, a shadow passed over the flying boat.

All three of them looked up almost simultaneously.

Above the mountain ridge running parallel to the coast.

Dark blue-black wings slowly tilted beneath the clouds.

It was a bird.

Long feathers like spearheads extended from the tips of its wings. Two pale streams of wind trailed far behind its tail.

As the creature banked, the forest below flattened in a single direction as though struck by a typhoon.

A sharp, tearing demonic qi, entirely different from that of the ape in the sea, rolled along the mountain ridge.

Wang Shulin’s brush froze.

“Two Tier 3 demon beasts...?”

Chapter 80

Instead of answering, Lu Hongyan poured spiritual power into the flying boat's restriction, and the vessel shot above the mountain ridge.

At that moment, dark blue wings sliced through the air beneath the black clouds.

Whoooosh―

The monstrous bird circling overhead folded its wings tight and plunged downward.

A pale gale spiraled behind its long tail as its mountain-sized body hurtled down at a terrifying speed.

“Lower our altitude!”

At Wang Shulin's scream, the flying boat tilted so violently it nearly rolled onto its side.

Blue-green shield plates shot out one after another from Lee Hyun's sleeve.

In an instant, four shield plates interlocked like gears above the flying boat, forming a defensive barrier.

BOOOOM!

Dozens of wind blades burst from the tips of the bird's wings and slammed head-on into the shield plates.

The impact shook even the flying boat's defensive barrier. One of the spirit stones embedded in the railing shattered with a crack, and the vessel was violently shoved backward through the air.

The mountain ridge behind them was cleanly cleaved along a diagonal line.

Collapsing rocks and trees thundered down and swallowed the forest. Amid the deafening roar, Lu Hongyan shouted.

“I'll take us down!”

The flying boat plunged in an almost vertical dive.

Just as they dropped to a perilously low altitude, nearly brushing the treetops, Lee Hyun looked back and frowned.

The ape that had been in the sea was gone.

‘When did it...!’

BOOM!

With a ground-shaking crash, an enormous figure dropped onto the coastal cliff like a bolt of lightning.

A Tier 3 demon beast, the Scale-Armored Sea Ape.

The ape, whose chest and belly were covered in scales, sprang up the instant it landed.

BANG!

Bedrock shattered beneath its feet as the hulking figure, wreathed in surging demonic qi, bounded through the air and crashed down onto the next mountainside.

The impact of its landing alone ripped massive trees out by the roots. The distance between it and the flying boat vanished in the blink of an eye.

Lee Hyun swung the Six-Leaf Shield around behind the flying boat.

Whoosh―

A huge boulder torn free and hurled by the ape ripped through the air toward them.

A shield plate knocked it aside at an angle, sending the deflected boulder crashing into the forest below and throwing up a towering cloud of dust.

To make matters worse, the monstrous bird was circling overhead again.

Without slowing, it swept through a huge arc and turned back toward the front of the flying boat.

Lu Hongyan gritted her teeth.

“Junior Sister Wang, take the controls!”

Wang Shulin took control of the flying boat without hesitation.

“Where should I take us?”

“That low valley ahead! If we climb, we'll be easy prey for the bird!”

Lu Hongyan pulled a faded yellow talisman from her storage pouch.

A crescent-shaped blade had been drawn across it in blood-red ink. The patterns along its edges had been worn faint by the passage of time, but the aura slumbering within still felt keen enough to cut flesh.

Lee Hyun's gaze fixed on it.

‘A talisman treasure?’

A talisman treasure was a consumable trump card created when a high-level cultivator of the Golden Core realm or above sealed a portion of the power of one of their techniques or magic treasures into a special talisman.

They were usually bestowed upon descendants by the elders of a cultivation clan, precious treasures meant to be used only when one's life was hanging by a thread.

Lu Hongyan held the talisman upright between both hands as though pressing her palms together in prayer.

“Buy me a little time. I'll tear that bird apart first.”

Spiritual power poured from her entire body into the talisman like a waterfall, and the blade inscribed upon it began to radiate light as though it had come alive.

Lee Hyun rearranged the shield plates and replied.

“Leave it to me.”

The flying boat slipped into a narrow gorge within the valley.

While controlling the flying boat's restriction, Wang Shulin sent an incense burner floating into the air. The brush in her other hand swept through the air, spreading a curtain of crimson flames.

Fwoooosh!

Flames surged from the stern and filled the forest behind them.

The ape pursuing close behind roared and thrust out its massive arm, ripping the flames apart with ease.

Broken tree trunks came raining down and battered the stern of the flying boat without mercy.

At the same time, a shadow descended from overhead.

Screeeech!

The monstrous bird's hook-like talons tore through the air toward the bow. At that instant, Lee Hyun's eyes flashed.

CLAAANG!

Its talons scraped across three overlapping shield plates in a shower of sparks.

The tremendous weight abruptly forced the flying boat downward.

Treetops scraped against the bottom of the vessel with an eerie grinding sound. Wang Shulin bit her lip and poured spiritual power into the restriction, but the unbalanced vessel could not easily regain altitude.

Lee Hyun grasped at the air, and the Condensed-Essence Grasping Hand surged up from below, forcefully pushing against the underside of the flying boat. Only then did the vessel barely regain its altitude.

Lee Hyun considered the situation.

‘Even with Senior Sister Lu's talisman treasure, I doubt she can handle more than one...’

The alternating assaults of Tier 3 demon beasts from the air and the ground were immensely dangerous.

Had he been alone, he would have hidden underground with the Earth Escape Art long ago, but he had fellow disciples to protect now.

“Almost done!”

Large beads of sweat rolled down Lu Hongyan's forehead.

The silver blade emerging between her hands had already taken solid form, growing to the size of a forearm. The talisman paper was beginning to char black.

Wang Shulin shouted.

“It's coming back!”

The monstrous bird shot through a narrow gap in the gorge and spread both wings wide. Dozens of wind blades howled viciously between its blue-tinged feathers.

Without hesitation, Lee Hyun overlapped all six plates of the Six-Leaf Shield in front of the flying boat.

Clatter-clatter!

CLANG! CLANG-CLANG-CLANG!

Countless sparks sprayed like rain across the shield plates blocking the flying boat.

The cliffs on both sides exploded with thunderous booms, sending rocks raining down.

The monstrous bird drove itself forward with its enormous body, still whipping up winds with its wings as its vicious beak and talons bore down on them.

At that moment, Lu Hongyan's eyes snapped open.

“Be torn apart!”

BAAANG―

Silver sword light shot straight from her fingertips.

The monstrous bird sensed danger instinctively and twisted its wings, but it was already too late.

The sword light sliced through the demonic light barrier around its wing as easily as cutting tofu and pierced straight through the joint beneath.

SPLASH!

Dark blue feathers and blood sprayed in every direction like a fountain.

The bird's ear-splitting shriek shook the gorge. Its enormous body lost its balance and skimmed diagonally over the flying boat before crashing into the mountainside, sweeping away dozens of trees and boulders at once.

At that moment, the talisman treasure in Lu Hongyan's hand crumbled into ash.

Screeeech......!

With one wing left in tatters, the monstrous bird barely managed to rise. It glared resentfully at the flying boat.

When Lee Hyun silently aimed the Six-Leaf Shield at it again, the creature flapped its wings and staggered into the air, retreating toward the sea.

Lu Hongyan breathed heavily as she brushed the ashes from between her fingers.

“I poured every last bit of the talisman treasure's power into that attack... and still couldn't kill it.”

“Driving it away was enough.”

The instant Lee Hyun answered,

RUMBLE!

The forest behind the gorge collapsed as though struck by a landslide.

The ape trampled through the trees, leaped over the flying boat, and dropped like a thunderbolt into their path.

“Watch out!”

Wang Shulin sent the flying boat into a sharp turn, but she could not evade it completely.

BOOOOM!

Two enormous fists smashed into the floor of the gorge.

Debris and dust erupted like a waterfall and battered the flying boat's defensive barrier without mercy. Part of the stern's outer wall was torn away, and the vessel lurched violently.

As the ape rose from the dust, terrifying demonic qi billowed from between the scales covering its chest.

Lu Hongyan stepped forward to block the roaring beast with her long spear leveled, but having just used the talisman treasure, the flow of her spiritual power was visibly weaker.

Lee Hyun looked between the hulking creature blocking their path and his two Senior Sisters.

‘If there's only one...’

Having made his decision, Lee Hyun spoke calmly.

“Senior Sister Lu, I have a talisman treasure as well.”

Both women immediately turned toward him.

“You have a talisman treasure?”

“It's a sword-type talisman treasure. Once activated, sword qi will burst in every direction, so the two of you should take the flying boat and leave the gorge first.”

“No. While you're preparing to activate it, we'll draw its attention...!”

Lee Hyun shook his head firmly.

“My talisman treasure doesn't take long to activate. Having the flying boat nearby will only get in my way. I'll keep that thing occupied, so go on ahead!”

Before he had even finished speaking, Lee Hyun kicked off the deck and shot into the air.

The blue-green shield plates followed behind him like shadows.

The ape's yellow eyes immediately swung toward Lee Hyun. Its enormous hand swept through the air as though trying to swat a flying insect.

Whoosh!

The instant Lee Hyun dodged as lightly as a feather, the plates of the Six-Leaf Shield overlapped and slammed heavily into the side of its wrist.

BANG!

The giant arm was knocked outward, creating a momentary opening.

Wang Shulin steered the flying boat through the gap, skimming past the ape and escaping the gorge.

“We'll wait beyond the mountain! If it gets too much, get out of there immediately!”

Lu Hongyan's shout faded into the wind.

Without looking back, Lee Hyun widened the distance between himself and the ape.

The instant he confirmed that the flying boat's presence had disappeared beyond the ridge, his gaze turned cold.

He drew a scabbard from his storage pouch and pulled out a silver-gray sword.

Shing.

It was the Sinking Moon Sword.

Lee Hyun lowered the tip of the blade.

BOOM!

The ape kicked off the ground and charged. An arm as massive as a house swept horizontally through the air.

The six shield plates lined up in front of Lee Hyun and blocked the blow.

BOOOOM!

An enormous impact surged through the Six-Leaf Shield.

Lee Hyun twisted the angles of the shield plates, diverting the brute force toward the cliff while simultaneously slipping beneath the ape's armpit.

BANG!

The cliff exploded, and amid the shower of stone dust, the silver-gray blade flashed like lightning.

CLANG!

White sparks burst across the thick demonic light and scales. The blade failed to bite deep, sliding away after leaving only a shallow line.

Grrrrrr!

Baring its teeth, the ape brought its free left hand crashing down from above.

As the palm descended over him like a black cloud, Lee Hyun slid backward across the ground.

BOOM!

The earth caved in like a crater, and a storm of dirt swept outward in every direction.

As though determined not to let the retreating Lee Hyun escape, the ape lowered its shoulder, stretched out its right arm, and charged again.

At that instant, an anchor of Earth-Origin Force formed in Lee Hyun's left hand as he retreated.

Hummm!

An invisible, crushing shackle snapped into place around the ape's wrist.

The immense gravitational force applied without warning yanked the huge arm off course.

Startled by the unfamiliar phenomenon, the ape shook its arm, but that momentary delay was more than enough for Lee Hyun.

The tremendous spiritual power accumulated throughout Lee Hyun's limbs, skeleton, and the meridians across his entire body surged all at once.

The Sinking Moon Sword's Light-Retracting Restriction lit up, and the outline of the blade blurred into the radiance.

Hummmmmm―

Lee Hyun's figure blurred.

Great Unity Heavenly Dipper, Thirty-First Form: Split Light Unites as One.

Whoooosh―

Dazzling light erupted in every direction, throwing the ape's vision into disarray.

Every one of those countless lights was sword light. The sword lights that filled the air accelerated all at once, then converged into one directly before the ape's eyes!

Flash!

Radiance intense enough to sting the skin engulfed the ape in pure white.

SPLAAASH!

A massive wound split diagonally from its shoulder to the opposite flank, spraying dark red blood through the air.

“KYAAAAAGH!”

The ape reeled backward with an agonized scream. Yet the ferocity of a Tier 3 demon beast was not so easily broken. Even as blood poured from its body, it swung its left arm in one final desperate struggle.

CLAAANG!

The shield plates, which had not had time to form a proper defensive formation, were knocked helplessly away, and at point-blank range with nowhere to evade, the enormous fist slammed hard into Lee Hyun's side.

BANG!

At that moment, dazzling light swelled beneath his robe.

Crack!

A thin membrane like a shed skin emerged around Lee Hyun's body and caught the fist.

A spirit molt of the Three-Molt Silkworm Robe.

The molt absorbed the otherwise fatal impact in his place and shattered into pieces.

The recoil sent Lee Hyun flying. After spinning several times through the air, he landed lightly on the ground.

A dull pain lingered in his side, but neither his bones nor his internal organs had been injured.

Without the Three-Molt Silkworm Robe, the blow would have broken at least five or six ribs.

Lee Hyun stared coldly at the ape.

The ape clutched its torn chest, bloody foam bubbling from its mouth. Wet, gurgling sounds escaped between its ragged breaths.

The savagery in its eyes slowly gave way to fear.

Realizing it had chosen the wrong opponent, the ape hurriedly turned and tried to flee toward the coast. Lee Hyun kicked off the ground.

Without even looking back, the fleeing ape tore up a boulder and hurled it behind itself.

The incoming rock smashed against the Six-Leaf Shield and shattered, and a silver-gray flash cut through the air between the fragments.

The ape spun around and hurriedly raised an arm to guard its neck.

Sword light carved deeply into its forearm, knocking the enormous hand aside. At that instant, the Sinking Moon Sword flashed again.

Shaaak―

This time, the sword light followed the wound already gaping across its chest and slipped smoothly inside.

The ape's pupils went slack, and its body stiffened.

The wet, bloody rasp leaking from its throat ceased.

BOOOOM!

Its enormous body toppled helplessly onto its side.

The raging demonic qi dispersed, leaving a long plume of dense dust billowing into the air.

Without approaching, Lee Hyun thoroughly examined the corpse with the Aura-Reading Art and his divine sense.

Only after confirming that its qi and blood had completely ceased and its primordial spirit had dissipated did he slowly descend to the ground.

The valley looked as though a natural disaster had swept through it.

An entire section of forest had been ripped apart, and deep sword marks scarred the cliffs.

Lee Hyun dusted off his clothes and checked beneath his robe. Of the three silkworm-cocoon embroideries sewn into the inner lining of the Three-Molt Silkworm Robe, one had lost its light and turned pitch-black.

‘Good thing I prepared an exceptional supreme-grade magic tool.’

He could never afford to let his guard down. The mere thought of what might have happened if even one more Tier 3 demon beast had been present was horrifying.

Lee Hyun approached the fallen ape below its neck.

From within its sturdy rib cage, he sensed a condensed mass of demon power pulsing more intensely than its heart had.

A demon core.

The demon core of a Tier 3 demon beast, something a Foundation Establishment cultivator could hardly even dream of obtaining alone.

...

When the flying boat cautiously returned above the valley, Lee Hyun was standing atop a bloodstained boulder, steadying his breathing.

Wang Shulin, leaning against the deck railing and looking down, stared wide-eyed.

“...No way.”

The enormous corpse of the ape lay sprawled across the valley floor.

Lu Hongyan was the first to leap from the flying boat. Her sharp gaze swept over Lee Hyun from head to toe.

“Junior Brother Li, are you hurt?”

“I'm fine.”

Wang Shulin followed her down and clicked her tongue at the horrific wound torn across the ape.

“A talisman treasure can be this powerful...? What realm was the Senior who made that sword-type talisman treasure in, for it to kill a Tier 3 demon beast?”

“I was fortunate. The talisman treasure's sword qi pierced its vital point cleanly.”

“What about the talisman treasure? Was it completely consumed?”

At Lu Hongyan's question, Lee Hyun put on a bitter expression and nodded.

“It turned into a handful of ash.”

Lu Hongyan let out a deep sigh.

“I suppose it would have. Mine was consumed just crippling one wing... Junior Brother, you really paid a heavy price.”

“If Senior Sister hadn't driven off the bird, I wouldn't have survived either.”

Lee Hyun calmly changed the subject and pointed toward the corpse.

“Let's deal with this first. Other demon beasts may come once they smell the blood.”

The two women immediately agreed and got to work.

While Lu Hongyan kept watch over their surroundings, Wang Shulin took a large jade casket, preservative medicinal liquid, and several Spirit-Sealing Talismans from her storage pouch.

Lee Hyun's sword cut into the ape's chest, and a deep glow burst from between the thick bones.

A demon core the size of an adult's fist.

Even outside the body, energy like a whirlpool in a blue sea seemed to pulse beneath its surface.

Wang Shulin swallowed a gasp of amazement.

“It's completely undamaged! It's only at the early Golden Core level, but... it's high grade.”

Lee Hyun carefully held out the demon core. Wang Shulin quickly accepted it, placed it inside the jade casket filled with medicinal liquid, and closed the lid.

The two of them attached several Spirit-Sealing Talismans to it.

They then stripped away the Tier 3 demon beast's valuable scales, tendons, and bones, quickly preserving everything they could.

After dividing the last of the boxes among their storage pouches, the three left the area without delay.

...

By the time the flying boat emerged from the valley, the black clouds had cleared, and a crimson sunset spread across the sky, staining the edge of the sea.

Lee Hyun leaned against the stern railing and pressed a hand to his aching side. Wang Shulin glanced at him and asked,

“Want some medicine? Are you sure you didn't bruise something?”

“I've already taken a pill, so I'm fine.”

“If it hurts even a little, don't hide it. Tell me.”

“Yes, Senior Sister.”

Lu Hongyan, who had been sitting in a corner of the deck, took a small booklet from her robe and wrote down several lines before stopping her brush.

“I shouldn't have taken off in the flying boat in the first place.”

When Lee Hyun looked over, she continued with self-reproach written across her face.

“There was a flying beast lurking overhead, yet I recklessly raised our altitude first. If Junior Brother Li hadn't blocked that first attack, the boat would have been destroyed and all of us would have died.”

“It was a sudden ambush.”

Wang Shulin tried to console her, but Lu Hongyan firmly shook her head.

“Handling unexpected situations like that is the responsibility of whoever's in command.”

She dipped her brush in ink, added another line, and closed the booklet.

“What did you write?”

At Lee Hyun's question, Lu Hongyan gave a bitter smile.

“That we didn't make it back alive because my judgment was sound. I wrote that much of it was simply my good fortune in having Junior Brother Li with us.”

When the three reached a temple in a nearby city, Abbot Yuanwu and the young monks were still tending to refugees scattered throughout the area.

Yuanwu had gone pale upon hearing that two Tier 3 demon beasts had appeared. When he received the report that one had been driven off and the other slain, his jaw dropped, and he could not find a word to say.

...

Three days later, a Golden Core Elder and elite disciples dispatched by Baoguang Temple's Demon-Subduing Court arrived.

Lu Hongyan's verbal report, Wang Shulin's meticulously drawn diagrams of the demon beasts, and tissue samples submitted by Lee Hyun were handed over to the Elder.

No traces of gu insects or sorcery were found in the demon beasts' bodies. The Elder also raised the possibility that something had driven them in from the distant sea. However, the evidence gathered so far was insufficient to determine the cause.

The Elder gave his orders.

“The Demon-Subduing Court will handle matters from here. The three of you are to return immediately and rest.”

Only then did the three return to Baoguang Temple with their minds at ease.

...

A few days later.

After receiving a full report on the incident, Huitan clicked his tongue.

“I sent you to investigate Tier 2 demon beasts, and instead you came back after risking your lives against Tier 3 demon beasts... Well, you made it back alive, and that's what matters. Take a break from alchemy for the time being and focus on recovering.”

“Thank you for your consideration, Master.”

“You said you brought back the demon core, didn't you?”

“Yes.”

“Come with me. Let's go see Junior Brother Huijue.”

...

The appraisal chamber beside the Inner Alchemy Chamber.

Huijue removed the seals from the jade casket with solemn care.

As the demon core rose into the air, radiating blue light, the appraisal chamber filled with the faint sound of waves and dense demonic qi.

“There's no doubt. It came from a Scale-Armored Sea Ape.”

Huijue sent a trace of magical power into the demon core and exclaimed in admiration.

“It's only early Tier 3, but its internal pattern is undamaged. It can be used as a primary ingredient for a Golden Core Condensing Pill.”

He continued.

“Li Dongsi, are you thinking of keeping it for when you begin preparing for Core Formation?”

“I'm considering it.”

“In that case, I'd advise against it.”

Huijue pointed to the internal pattern within the demon core.

“Unlike while it's inside a demon beast's body, once a demon core is removed, its energy will inevitably leak away over time no matter how thoroughly it's sealed, and its internal pattern will eventually break down. Unless you're about to attempt Core Formation soon, it's better to put it through Refining as quickly as possible.”

‘Of course. Besides, one pill won't be anywhere near enough for me...’

Lee Hyun had no idea how many years it would take to cultivate his entire body to Foundation Establishment Great Perfection.

Even if he made a Golden Core Condensing Pill in advance, nearly all of its medicinal strength would have dissipated by the time that many years passed.

For now, it was better simply to sell it.

“Would the temple be willing to buy it?”

Huijue nodded.

“Of course! The sect is always short on ingredients for Golden Core Condensing Pills, so we'll pay you generously. We'll buy all the scales and bones from the carcass as well.”

...

A few days later, the accounts were settled.

The sect commended the three for their contributions and also compensated Lu Hongyan with spirit stones for the talisman treasure she had consumed. Lee Hyun declined separate compensation for his loss, saying the proceeds from selling the demon beast materials were more than sufficient.

In truth, the amount he received from selling the demon core and other materials exceeded the value of an ordinary talisman treasure.

...

At the end of that month, Huijue summoned Lee Hyun to a corner of the Inner Alchemy Chamber, where Lee Hyun assisted him with the Refining process for a Golden Core Condensing Pill.

The demon core of the Scale-Armored Sea Ape Lee Hyun had slain melted inside the pill furnace, surrounded by several rings of golden magical power.

The baleful qi surrounding the demon core dispersed within the flames. The internal pattern revealed beneath remained intact as it absorbed the energies of the refined medicinal ingredients one after another.

The essences of various spirit plants fused together in a dazzling display.

Before long, the energies of the medicinal ingredients gathered around the demon core's internal pattern and merged into one, finally congealing into a Golden Core Condensing Pill that gave off a faint golden glow.

Lee Hyun observed every step of the process closely and committed it to memory.

Three months passed.

The southern coast regained its peace thanks to the Demon-Subduing Court's large-scale purge, and the ports that had been closed came back to life.

Aside from those encountered by Lee Hyun's group, only a couple more Tier 3 demon beasts appeared, and the exact reason behind the demon beasts' unrest was never discovered.

Lee Hyun's daily life returned to normal.

The damaged spirit molt of the Three-Molt Silkworm Robe also fully regenerated through nurturing with spiritual power.

...

One day, work in the alchemy chamber ended earlier than usual.

After washing his hands and stepping into the corridor, Lee Hyun heard a familiar voice.

“Junior Brother Li.”

He turned to see Wang Shulin approaching with light steps.

“Finished early?”

“Yes. Do you still have work left, Senior Sister?”

“No, I'm done too. Um... before you go, just a moment.”

Wang Shulin glanced around, then stepped close to Lee Hyun.

Along with a faint fragrance, her pale hand suddenly slipped inside Lee Hyun's sleeve.

When Lee Hyun closed his hand, his fingers found a jade slip.

“What is this?”

“Who knows?”

She gave him a mischievous smile.

Lee Hyun sent a trace of spiritual power into it, and bold golden script appeared at the beginning of the jade slip.

Sutra of Refining Intent into Vow

Lee Hyun's pupils trembled.

“This is...”

“You asked me about it on the flying boat back then, remember? You seemed very interested in methods of cultivating vow power without relying on vows.”

Wang Shulin fidgeted with her fingers as she added,

“Don't worry. I didn't secretly take it out of the Scripture Pavilion.”

“Can I really accept something this valuable...?”

“Ahem. It simply means this jade slip was fated to come into Junior Brother Li's hands. What is there to worry about?”

Chapter 81

Wang Shulin puffed out her chest proudly.

“I also found the annotations left by the seniors and the related essential formulas in the latter part, so I included those too. I separated the overlapping lines in the visualization diagram and drew them out individually, so it should be easier to understand if you compare them with the original.”

Lee Hyun pressed the jade slip to his forehead and examined it.

Sure enough, just as Senior Sister Wang had said, the inheritance of the 《Sutra of Refining Intent into Vow》 was followed by meticulously written annotations and diagrams. The densely tangled lines had been separated into several layers, with tiny notes marking which part of the original each corresponded to.

Perhaps because she was such a gifted artist, even the copied contents of the jade slip carried an elegant artistic touch.

“...This is a precious gift. I’ll study it carefully and take every word to heart.”

Wang Shulin peered at his face, then burst out laughing.

“Look at the corners of your mouth twitching.”

“Were they?”

“Mm-hm.”

She took a step back, her jade-green robes fluttering lightly.

“Carelessly making or releasing vows can damage your primordial spirit, so work your way up from the basics. Don’t jump ahead and start practicing the essential formulas at the back first.”

“I’ll keep that in mind.”

Wang Shulin smiled, looking a little embarrassed, then turned away. Sunlight fell across her back as she hurried off with quick little steps.

Lee Hyun remained standing there for a moment.

‘A celestial maiden...?’

It was already enough that she had obtained such a precious inheritance for him, yet she had even searched out the related essential formulas, organized them, and gone to the trouble of making everything easier to read.

She was probably still thinking about what had happened on the coast not long ago. Lu Hongyan and Li Dongsi had even used up precious talisman treasures during the fight, so Senior Sister Wang likely wanted to repay him in her own way.

‘That must be it.’

Lee Hyun put the jade slip into his storage pouch.

Wang Shulin was kind enough to make him wonder whether she might have feelings for him, but getting his hopes up only to end up disappointed on his own would leave a bitter taste.

Lee Hyun decided not to read too much into it. Even so, he took the jade slip out twice more on the way back to his residence.

...

The 《Sutra of Refining Intent into Vow》 was quite difficult.

Lee Hyun lay on a long bench reading the jade slip, only to return to the beginning several times.

Understanding the principles and actually putting them into practice were two different things.

The Sutra of Refining Intent into Vow did not depend on following prescribed rules of conduct, as a vow did.

Instead, one established a mind seal within the primordial spirit and refined it over a long period, creating a foundation from which vow power could arise on its own.

Merely picturing the form of the mind seal for a moment accomplished nothing.

The mind seal had to remain stable even when the practitioner was thinking about other things or using techniques. That was why prolonged cultivation was required to stabilize the mind seal even after it had been established.

‘Good thing I learned the Spirit-Refining Essentials.’

He was already accustomed to dividing his divine sense into several streams and controlling them without allowing them to interfere with one another. He had also continued training himself to imprint complex sacred images into his mind while practicing the Sumeru Visualization Scripture, so in terms of foundation alone, he was no worse than any other Foundation Establishment cultivator.

At the back of the jade slip was a separately copied 《Vow-Releasing Essentials》.

It described how to loosen the bond between an established vow and the primordial spirit, then gradually gather and retain the vow power cultivated through that bond

‘She even included this... I really am grateful.’

If he sufficiently stabilized the new mind seal before using this essential formula to release his vow, he would be able to preserve the vow power he had cultivated even if he later lost his primordial yang.

He had no intention of giving up his primordial yang right away, but he liked having the option available to him in the future.

...

After that, perhaps because Wang Shulin felt they had grown closer, she began visiting Lee Hyun’s residence from time to time.

At first, it was to discuss the Sutra of Refining Intent into Vow or alchemy.

...

Time gradually passed.

Lee Hyun practiced alchemy, cultivated, and occasionally visited his tunnels or the Two Heavens Society’s bases.

One thing had changed.

Whenever he returned to Baoguang Temple, his steps unconsciously became a little quicker.

For some reason, merely thinking about Senior Sister Wang made him feel strangely buoyant.

...

The first mind seal of the Sutra of Refining Intent into Vow stabilized faster than expected.

His primordial spirit and divine sense, tempered over many years, proved enormously helpful.

Afterward, Lee Hyun began studying how to release his vow.

He generated vow power from the new mind seal, used it to form Buddha-Light True Qi, cast techniques, depleted his divine sense, recovered it, and repeated the process again and again.

Only after he had tested it thoroughly did he begin practicing the Vow-Releasing Essentials.

One day, at Wang Shulin’s residence.

Wang Shulin, who was reclining beside Lee Hyun on a long bench, pressed a fingertip against his cheek.

“Strange.”

“...”

Lee Hyun looked at her for a moment before speaking.

“There’s something I want to show you, Senior Sister.”

“What?”

Instead of answering, Lee Hyun used the Cleansing Art to remove all his makeup, then released his disguise art.

The wrinkles around his eyes faded, while the contours of his cheeks and jaw gradually shifted. A moment later, a young man who looked not even twenty years old sat before Wang Shulin.

Wang Shulin’s finger twitched.

“...This is your real face?”

“Yeah.”

She stared at Lee Hyun’s face for a long while. Reaching out, she touched his cheek, then tilted her head slightly to inspect his profile as well.

“You were this young?”

“I happened to get a Youth-Preserving Pill when I was young.”

“Then why did you deliberately make yourself look older?”

“Hmm... because it saves me from having to explain unnecessary things?”

He still could not bring himself to reveal the secret of his agelessness.

Wang Shulin studied his face once more, then suddenly pouted.

“Then later on, I’ll be the only one who looks old....”

“You look younger than I do, Senior Sister.”

“Liar.”

“It’s true.”

The corners of Wang Shulin’s lips slowly curved upward.

...

At one of the Two Heavens Society’s contact bases in the Xu Kingdom.

Wearing his White Deer mask, Lee Hyun placed a small pouch of spirit stones on the table.

“Find me a Youth-Preserving Pill or Appearance-Preserving Pill. Something whose quality and efficacy are beyond doubt.”

Pills known as Youth-Preserving Pills or Appearance-Preserving Pills genuinely existed in the cultivation world. From the moment one took such a pill, one’s outward appearance would cease to age.

They only preserved appearance, however. They did not change one’s lifespan or bone age.

Many people coveted such pills, but most cultivators spent every spirit stone they obtained on cultivation resources and could never afford one themselves.

The main ingredients were rare, and demand was less consistent than for cultivation pills, so few alchemists specialized in refining them. That made obtaining a proper one more difficult than expected.

“How many do you require?”

“One pill will suffice. If the seller insists on selling them only by the bottle, however, purchasing several is fine.”

The cultivator across from him made a brief entry in a ledger.

“I’ll make inquiries.”

...

Some time later.

Wang Shulin accepted the small jade bottle Lee Hyun held out to her.

“What’s this?”

“A Youth-Preserving Pill.”

Wang Shulin removed the stopper. There were three pills inside the jade bottle.

Her eyes widened. After staring down at the bottle for a moment, her expression crumpled slightly, almost as though she were about to cry.

“......Where did you find something this precious? I looked around the cultivator market too, but they were incredibly hard to find.......”

“You seemed worried about it, Senior Sister. It wasn’t that difficult.”

She burrowed into Lee Hyun’s embrace.

“Thank you.”

Twenty years after he began practicing the Sutra of Refining Intent into Vow.

A cultivation chamber on the eastern peak of the Lotus Court.

Lee Hyun lay down while slowly guiding the medicinal strength of a Profundity-Penetrating Pill.

For some time, he had focused on strengthening his Primordial Body and mastering techniques, but recently he had concentrated on breaking through the bottleneck that had kept his lower dantian at Foundation Establishment Stage 6.

The spiritual power within his lower dantian compressed, then relaxed again.

As the pill’s medicinal strength blended into that flow, subtle changes began occurring in the place that had remained blocked for so long.

Lee Hyun did not rush. He simply repeated the same circulation again and again.

Several days later.

Hummm―

Lee Hyun’s reclining body gently rose into the air. A halo of light spread from his entire body and brightly illuminated the cultivation chamber before being drawn back inside him.

As his body slowly descended to the floor, Lee Hyun opened his eyes.

Foundation Establishment Stage 7.

His lower dantian had finally entered late Foundation Establishment!

He straightened his posture, then circulated his newly refined spiritual power through his meridians. The flow was smooth, and the same quantity of spiritual power now contained considerably more strength than before his breakthrough.

Once the circulation of his spiritual power had become natural, Lee Hyun took the stone tablet from his storage pouch.

Light flickered from his hand. Some of the characters blurred away, and new ones were engraved in their place.

【Age: 2,208】

【Realm: Foundation Establishment Stage 7 (lower dantian), Foundation Establishment Stage 4 (rest of body)】

【Spiritual Power: 7,396 → 7,460】

‘Now I can openly go around as a late Foundation Establishment cultivator.’

More than thirty years had already passed since he entered Baoguang Temple.

During that time, he had gradually raised his publicly displayed cultivation to Stage 5 and then Stage 6. Between Baoguang Temple’s excellent cultivation environment and the income he earned as a Tier-2 alchemist, rising from Stage 4 to Stage 7 was hardly conspicuous.

Lee Hyun admired the stone tablet for a moment before returning it to his storage pouch and leaving his residence.

His feet naturally carried him toward a nearby peak.

...

The restriction opened as soon as he arrived before Wang Shulin’s residence.

It happened before he could even knock.

“Finished?”

Wang Shulin hurried out from inside.

Her hair flowed over her shoulders like silk.

Her face was as youthful as when they had first met, and her expression was even brighter and more vibrant than back then, making her exceptionally beautiful.

The moment she saw Lee Hyun, she broke into a radiant smile, unable to hide her delight. Then she came to a stop in front of him and widened her eyes.

“You broke through? Stage 7?”

“Yeah.”

“Did you come to me first?”

“Where else would I go?”

Instead of answering, Wang Shulin threw herself into Lee Hyun’s arms.

Her fresh scent enveloped him as he held her.

After burying her face against his chest for a moment, Wang Shulin looked up, smiling brightly as she tugged at his hand.

“Want to have some spirit tea before you go?”

...

Three days later.

A guest came to Wang Shulin’s residence.

The restriction outside the door chimed softly twice.

After waiting for a moment, Lu Hongyan folded her arms.

“Junior Sister Wang.”

When there was no answer from inside, she spoke again.

“Junior Brother Li is in there too, isn’t he? Open the door.”

A moment later, the door opened.

Wang Shulin was hurriedly tying up her hair, her face flushed red. Lee Hyun had already used the disguise art to restore his usual face and was fastening his long robe with a dazed expression, though his clothes somehow sat rather awkwardly.

Lu Hongyan gave the two of them a sidelong look, as though she had expected exactly this.

“Good grief. So busy clinging to each other in broad daylight that you couldn’t even hear me....”

“Senior Sister!”

Wang Shulin flushed and waved her hands, but Lu Hongyan merely snickered and stepped through the doorway.

“I thought Junior Brother Li Dongsi was completely hopeless with women... I suppose the saying is true: the quietest spirit cat is always the first to sneak into the herb garden... I heard you mastered that difficult Sutra of Refining Intent into Vow in less than ten years just so you could stay close to Shulin? She never stops singing your praises, and I suppose she wasn’t entirely exaggerating.”

Wang Shulin clapped a hand over Lu Hongyan’s mouth.

“Someone might hear you! I gave you a Youth-Preserving Pill, and you promised to keep quiet!”

“Mmph... All right...”

Lee Hyun scratched his head, but he could not think of anything to say in his defense.

Lu Hongyan passed between them and entered the guest room.

While Wang Shulin prepared tea, Lu Hongyan placed a thin booklet on the table.

“The Yunzhou Dao Symposium is being held.”

Lee Hyun sat down.

“The Dao symposium?”

“It’s an exchange gathering held every sixty years by the various sects of the Nine Kingdoms of Yunzhou. This time it’ll be held in the Jing Kingdom, north of the Xuan Kingdom. Baoguang Temple has decided to send people as well.”

Wang Shulin set down a teacup.

“The Dao symposium where the disciples hold sparring matches?”

“Right. The Elders meet with other Elders, while the disciples pit their techniques and martial learning against one another.”

Lu Hongyan opened the booklet.

It contained a list of candidate disciples Baoguang Temple might send.

Lee Hyun’s gaze stopped on a familiar name.

Li Dongsi.

“...My name is here too?”

“Martial Uncle Huitan recommended you. Apparently, they’re only planning to choose two from the Lotus Court.”

Lee Hyun turned to Wang Shulin. She nodded.

“Go without worrying about me. Master said that during the next batch of Golden Core Condensing Pills, I’ll be allowed to handle the blending of the medicinal ingredients myself. I don’t want to miss an opportunity like this either. I’m going to use the chance to learn properly.”

Lu Hongyan stared at Lee Hyun and Wang Shulin in disbelief.

“You two are already checking in with each other before going anywhere? Anyone would think you were married. Junior Brother Li, do you want to go?”

“There must be plenty of people with higher cultivation than me.”

“With your skill, you’re more than qualified to be a candidate.”

Lu Hongyan picked up her teacup.

“I saw how you fought on the coast. Even twenty years ago, you managed to hold out while deflecting the attacks of a Tier-3 demon beast. Now you’ve even reached late Foundation Establishment. Even leaving aside the talisman treasure you used, that was impressive enough.”

Lee Hyun considered it for a moment.

The prospect of observing the combat methods of cultivators from unfamiliar sects at close range intrigued him.

It would be an entirely different experience from practicing techniques alone or sparring with familiar fellow disciples.

There would be no need to fight to the death either. These were friendly sparring matches held under the watch of Elders, and continuing to attack an opponent after they surrendered was strictly forbidden.

From Lee Hyun’s perspective, the only real downside was having to be separated from Wang Shulin.

Wang Shulin was beautiful. Whenever she saw him, she smiled first, and when no one else was watching, she naturally reached for his hand. Lee Hyun had grown quite accustomed to that affection.

They spent nearly every day together, so merely thinking about not seeing her for a while already left him feeling strangely empty.

But they couldn’t always be together, and from time to time, he still had duties to fulfill for the sect.

...

Huitan examined Lee Hyun’s aura and nodded.

“You truly have reached the late stage.”

“Yes, Master.”

“Good. I’ll concede that my disciple hasn’t become so blinded by women that he’s abandoned his cultivation.”

“.......”

Huitan gestured toward the stone table beside him.

A jade dish covered by a preservation restriction held dark crimson marrow fluid from a demon beast.

“Start by preparing this.”

Lee Hyun sat down and conjured a flame at his fingertips.

The pale golden fire split into slender strands and seeped into the marrow fluid.

Huitan watched in silence.

There was a difference from when Lee Hyun had first entered the temple.

Back when he had preserved his primordial yang intact, even an almost invisible wisp of flame had been enough to purge the baleful qi.

Now, he had to push his fire control a little higher. Losing his primordial yang had weakened the Clear Yang Purifying Fire.

Purging the same amount of baleful qi required more spiritual power than before, but that posed no difficulty whatsoever for Lee Hyun with his Primordial Body.

His control of the flames had also become far more precise, allowing him to preserve the medicinal potency despite the increased heat. Thread-fine flames wove through the marrow fluid, burning away only the baleful qi.

His many years of practicing the Flame-Threading Art shone through here as well.

His vow power had also been preserved completely. The mind seal he had stabilized before releasing his vow now served as its foundation, so the strength of his Buddha-Light True Qi had not suffered.

Sssss.

The dark crimson energy dispersed like smoke.

After a long while, Lee Hyun withdrew his hand. Huitan pulled the jade dish closer and inspected it.

The old monk’s eyebrows twitched briefly.

“...Excellent.”

Huitan set the dish down and looked at him.

“It is excellent, but...”

“Yes.”

“Losing your primordial yang still feels like a waste.”

Lee Hyun gave an awkward smile.

“It doesn’t interfere with Refining.”

“I know. That is why I did not stop you. It is not as though our temple has any precept forbidding Dao companions.”

Before Lee Hyun could speak, Huitan continued.

“Still, when I was young, at least I understood how precious primordial yang was. Somehow, even after falling for a woman, you continue cultivating and practicing alchemy without missing a beat, so I cannot even find anything to lecture you about. That makes you all the more irritating.”

“...It’s because Master taught me well.”

“As expected. You must be so excellent because you’re my disciple.”

Huitan stroked his beard.

He took a small jade token from a drawer, pressed it to his forehead, infused it with divine sense, then placed it on the table.

“It is time you learned some new techniques. Go to the Scripture Pavilion. If you present this token, you may study two inheritances on the third floor.”

“Thank you.”

As Lee Hyun accepted the jade token, Huitan added one final remark.

“And you should attend the Dao symposium. Before we are alchemists, we are cultivators. Seeing the methods of other sects will be useful.”

“I will.”

“You will be traveling as part of a group, so there is no need to feel pressured.”

...

The third floor of the Scripture Pavilion was quieter than the floors below.

The restrictions covering its shelves were far thicker than those on the second floor.

After checking the jade token Huitan had given Lee Hyun, the monk in charge gestured toward the shelves.

“Choose two.”

“Yes.”

Lee Hyun wandered between the shelves until he reached a section containing inheritances related to attacks on the primordial spirit.

‘Come to think of it, I know the Spirit-Guarding Essence-Protecting Method, so I can defend against divine-sense attacks. I’ve also learned the Spirit-Refining Essentials, so I’m used to stabilizing and dividing my divine sense. Yet I don’t actually have a method for attacking someone else’s primordial spirit with divine sense.’

After some time, his hand stopped before a jade slip.

《Spirit-Jolting Needle Method》

It was a Dharma teaching for infusing divine sense with vow power, condensing it into a fine point, and forming a Spirit-Jolting Needle that pierced an opponent’s consciousness.

Thanks to the foundations provided by his Primordial Body and martial arts, Lee Hyun was exceptionally strong in physical combat, while his abundant spiritual power also made him proficient in battles of techniques. Considering the three elements of essence, qi and spirit, it was now time for him to acquire an offensive method involving the primordial spirit.

Of course, defeating a powerful opponent of the same realm in a single strike with a divine-sense attack would be difficult. But such a technique did not need to destroy the primordial spirit outright to be useful.

Simply disrupting an opponent’s consciousness at the instant they formed a hand seal or controlled a magic tool would already be highly effective.

Lee Hyun reread the explanation several times before setting the jade slip aside as his first choice.

While browsing another set of shelves, he found the section containing escape arts.

He had already learned the Earth Escape Art and Water Escape Art long ago, so he had no need for them.

Among the Five Elements escape arts were the Fire Escape Art and Wood Escape Art as well, but the one that caught his attention most was the Metal Escape Art.

A technique that allowed the body to pass through metal or along ore veins where metal qi was densely concentrated.

Its difficulty was extremely high and mastering it would be far from easy, but Lee Hyun, already a master of the Earth Escape Art, found himself drawn to it.

If he learned this as well, he would be able to find paths through ore veins that were difficult to traverse with the Earth Escape Art alone.

...

Fifteen days later.

The Lotus Court held a simple sparring match to make the final selection of disciples who would participate in the Yunzhou Dao Symposium.

Mingzhen stood opposite Lee Hyun.

He was the Senior Brother who had studied the Refining of the Golden Core Condensing Pill alongside him. A late Foundation Establishment cultivator, Mingzhen was highly skilled at controlling several magic tools simultaneously.

A small bronze mirror floated above Mingzhen’s head. Lee Hyun likewise summoned the Sinking Moon Sword and deployed the Six-Leaf Shield.

As Mingzhen formed a hand seal, blue rays poured from the bronze mirror. Bands of light sealed off Lee Hyun’s left and right, while two flying blades shot through the gaps with an ominous whistle.

It was a clean, seamless combination.

Clang! Claang!

Two plates of the Six-Leaf Shield knocked the flying blades away. At that instant, Mingzhen’s mirror rotated, and blue light bound one shield plate, slowing its movement.

The moment the corner of Mingzhen’s mouth lifted―

Lee Hyun did not even consider recalling the slowed shield plate. Instead, he used it to block Mingzhen’s view and drove straight through the opening without hesitation.

Whoosh!

Frost-bright sword light erupted from the Sinking Moon Sword and shot in a straight line between the two flying blades.

“Urgh!”

Startled, Mingzhen flung out a hand. A small shield shot upward in haste and barely managed to knock aside the Sinking Moon Sword’s sword light.

Boom!

He did not even have time to feel relieved.

Amid the sword light that shattered against the shield’s edge, a single concealed strand of blue sword qi curved inward like a snake.

By the time Mingzhen hurriedly retreated, it was already too late.

A cold chill.

The sword qi, carrying a lofty, austere force without stirring so much as a breath of wind, stopped one cun (about 3.3 cm) from the nape of his neck.

The Elder watching from outside raised a hand.

“Enough.”

Cold sweat beaded on Mingzhen’s skin as he let out a helpless breath.

“I lost.”

Lee Hyun withdrew his sword qi and pressed his palms together.

“Thank you for the guidance.”

Mingzhen rubbed his chest and clicked his tongue.

“Guidance? Hardly. Junior Brother Li, your talent for combat is absurd. I’m glad you aren’t my enemy. For a moment, I thought I was fighting a ghost.”

Lee Hyun was slightly taken aback.

By now, he had completely mastered the Great Unity Heavenly Dipper Sword Art. He could conceal sword qi among countless streams of sword light and even form a sword formation with it.

What he had not expected was for a late Foundation Establishment Senior Brother to completely fail to react to a single strand of sword qi before Lee Hyun even deployed the sword formation.

‘I see. I’ve lost my sense of what’s normal for a Foundation Establishment cultivator... If I don’t want to attract too much attention at the Yunzhou Dao Symposium, I need to practice holding back.’

After the sparring matches ended, Lee Hyun and Senior Brother Mingyun, who excelled in formations, were ultimately selected to represent the Lotus Court.

...

Over the next two months, Lee Hyun went about his usual routine while learning his new Dharma teachings and preparing for the Dao symposium.

Gathering his divine sense and shaping it into a Spirit-Jolting Needle was relatively easy.

That was because he had refined his primordial spirit for many years, and the mind seal of the Sutra of Refining Intent into Vow was already stable.

What remained difficult was breaking through the divine-sense defenses of a fast-moving opponent and disrupting their consciousness at precisely the right moment in actual combat.

Even when he practiced with Lu Hongyan while both of them lowered their power and prepared beforehand, he often missed the proper timing to strike as soon as their exchanges sped up.

The Metal Escape Art was even harder.

But Lee Hyun felt no impatience whatsoever.

Most of the astonishing proficiency he took pride in with his techniques had been accumulated over long years. He had never expected himself to become immediately proficient with newly learned techniques.

He had time to spare, after all.

Before departure, he stopped by Tunnel No. 3 to check the spirit field and filled the water reservoir with the Spirit Rain Art. He also made sure to inspect the fuzzbees and Bonefuzz.

...

The night before departure.

Wang Shulin lay in Lee Hyun’s arms reading a popular novel. She stopped turning the pages, took his hand, and idly played with his fingers one knuckle at a time.

“Don’t go getting yourself mixed up in anything dangerous for no reason.”

“Mm.”

The next morning.

A large flying boat floated above a plaza on the eastern side of the mountain range where Baoguang Temple stood.

Several layers of golden patterns shone beneath the hull, while the image of a lion standing atop clouds was carved into the high prow.

Many disciples had already gathered in the plaza.

Cultivators from the Demon-Subduing Court had long spears and sword scabbards strapped to their backs, while others stood beside long cases containing magic tools.

Elsewhere, monks with unusually thick arms and shoulders spoke in low voices. A faint golden sheen flowed across the skin exposed beyond their enchanted robes.

They were disciples of the Vajra Court, which primarily practiced body-refining techniques.

A short distance away sat cultivators of the Concentration and Wisdom Court. Some had their eyes closed, while others rolled small prayer beads between their fingers.

The Concentration and Wisdom Court specialized in the in-depth study and practice of Dharma teachings on meditation, visualization, and spirit refinement. Its inheritances ranged from the Soul-Seizing Art, which used divine sense to shake an opponent’s soul, to methods for condensing a Dharma manifestation. As befitted a great sect of the Buddhist tradition, Baoguang Temple possessed profound foundations in Dharma teachings concerning the mind and primordial spirit.

One disciple from the Life-Release Court continuously stroked the ears of a small beast held in his arms.

The creature looked docile, but whenever it yawned, sharp demonic qi leaked from between its teeth.

‘There are beast tamers too...’

Lee Hyun looked around.

There were twenty-four participants in all.

Even though he had entered the sect more than thirty years ago, most of the faces were completely unfamiliar to him.

‘I really have spent all my time in the Lotus Court.’

Near the plaza, disciples of the Guest Reception Hall were directing the accompanying personnel as they boarded and moved their baggage.

A steward from the Discipline Hall checked the delegation roster while handing out spirit tablets.

Lee Hyun turned his gaze beyond the plaza.

Halls and cultivation grounds covered the distant peaks. Other flying boats traveled between them, while disciples who had finished their dawn practice descended the long stairways.

Baoguang Temple was enormous.

It truly was a great sect that presided over temples and frontier outposts throughout the Xu Kingdom, maintaining order across lands inhabited by countless cultivators and mortals.

His comfortable daily life in the Lotus Court was only a tiny part of it.

“Junior Brother Li!”

Lu Hongyan raised a hand from the deck.

Several cultivators from the Demon-Subduing Court stood beside her.

Lee Hyun flew up and landed on the deck, and Lu Hongyan introduced him to her fellow disciples.

“This is Junior Brother Li Dongsi from the Lotus Court. He’ll be participating with us this time.”

Several of them greeted him warmly, and Lee Hyun returned each greeting in turn with his palms pressed together.

A moment later, the formation inscriptions on the flying boat began to glow brightly.

Hummm―

The plaza slowly receded into the distance.

Chapter 82

On the second day after their departure.

Lee Hyun set down his teacup in the flying boat's tearoom.

At one side of the tearoom, a burly man sat silently drinking tea.

Across from Lee Hyun sat Yuanjing, a monk of the Concentration and Wisdom Court. He was a senior brother with narrow eyes and a faint smile that always lingered at the corners of his lips.

Between them floated a bronze bell about two finger joints long.

"I'm ready."

Yuanjing spoke.

Lee Hyun drew his divine sense into a fine point.

The divine sense infused with vow power condensed into the shape of a needle. The moment its tip pointed toward the bronze bell, Yuanjing's divine sense surrounding the bell shifted ever so slightly.

The Spirit-Jolting Needle shot forward.

A thin outer layer of the divine sense enveloping the bronze bell peeled away. The Spirit-Jolting Needle pierced the thin membrane, but as the membrane gave way and curled around it, the needle was pulled off course.

Lee Hyun withdrew the Spirit-Jolting Needle after it veered past the bell.

"...Missed again."

"Still, that was close."

Yuanjing smiled and raised his teacup.

The bronze bell was a training magic tool that rang whenever divine sense touched its interior.

At first, Yuanjing had simply been ringing the bell by himself with his divine sense.

It had looked like nothing special, but on closer inspection, Lee Hyun saw that the divine sense surrounding the bell was constantly changing shape.

When Lee Hyun showed interest, Yuanjing had invited him to try it together.

"Fascinating. How do you predict where I'll strike...?"

"Predict? Junior Brother, you told me where you were going to strike."

"I did?"

"The tip was pointing this way from the moment you formed the needle."

Yuanjing pointed to one side of the bronze bell.

Lee Hyun thought for a moment, then nodded.

'I see.'

He could maintain the shape of the Spirit-Jolting Needle, but he was still unskilled at concealing the signs of its formation or changing its direction just before releasing it.

Against an opponent watching him, that was as good as giving them all the time they needed to prepare.

'Of course, if I really wanted to, I could force my way through...'

Lee Hyun's divine sense was also far stronger than that of cultivators at the same realm. Unlike spiritual power, however, there was no clear numerical standard by which to measure it, so he had been unable to include it in his handmade status window.

Even just now, while forming the Spirit-Jolting Needle, he could have poured far more divine sense into it, even if the same was not true of vow power.

But if he did that, Senior Brother Yuanjing would notice his abnormal strength.

Besides, Lee Hyun liked practicing this way. There was much he could learn from Senior Brother Yuanjing about controlling divine sense.

"May I try again?"

"Of course."

With Yuanjing's help, Lee Hyun continued practicing for one ke (about 15 minutes).

Yuanjing deliberately repeated the same movements, and thanks to that, Lee Hyun began to get a feel for how he should train the Spirit-Jolting Needle.

'I'm already learning something before we've even reached the Dao symposium. I'm glad I came.'

Lee Hyun brought his palms together.

"Thank you for helping me."

"What need is there for thanks between fellow disciples? Still, Junior Brother Li, you're quite skilled at condensing divine sense."

"I suppose it's because I use divine sense so often while practicing alchemy."

"Come to think of it, you're from the Lotus Court, aren't you? Perhaps I should learn a little about fire control myself..."

The burly man who had been silently drinking tea laughed.

"If you say that to the Elders of the Lotus Court, they'll have you preparing medicinal ingredients for the next ten years."

It was Zhang Taishan, a disciple of the Vajra Court. His hair was tied back, and he was so broad across the shoulders and arms that their contours showed even beneath his loose robe.

A teacup was wedged between his thick fingers. The cup looked so tiny in his hand that, from a distance, it seemed as though he were pinching a small lid between his fingertips.

When Zhang Taishan set down his cup, black prayer beads slipped out from beneath his sleeve.

Thud.

The moment one bead touched the table, round ripples spread across the surface of the tea.

When Lee Hyun's gaze fell on the prayer beads, Zhang Taishan smiled.

"Would you like to hold them?"

He sent the prayer beads flying over, and Lee Hyun reached out to catch them. Not only were they remarkably heavy, but fierce Metal-attribute spiritual power was condensed within them.

"Are these for training?"

"Indeed."

Lee Hyun returned the prayer beads while studying Zhang Taishan's arm.

A faint golden sheen flowed beneath the skin of his thick forearm.

The energy had been invisible while he sat still, but when he retrieved the prayer beads, it moved along his wrist and elbow.

Once the energy was drawn back in, Zhang Taishan's arm returned to an ordinary flesh tone.

'That must be another kind of golden body modeled after the Leakless Golden Body...'

Zhang Taishan looked at Lee Hyun.

"For some reason, Junior Brother Li, you strike me as strong."

"Surely not."

"How about a spar once we arrive?"

"I think I'd lose."

"Liar."

A voice came from the entrance to the tearoom.

It was Lu Hongyan.

She looked over the three of them before taking an empty seat.

"Junior Brother Li is probably the strongest one here, isn't he?"

Lee Hyun picked up the teapot.

"Senior Sister Lu, someone might misunderstand if they heard you. Would you like some tea?"

"Changing the subject, are we?"

...

The flying boat continued northeast with barely any shaking.

By day, rivers and mountain ranges passed beneath the clouds. At night, lamps and formation inscriptions softly illuminated the hull.

The disciples cultivated in their own cabins, but from time to time they came outside to socialize.

Even those who had spent decades at Baoguang Temple rarely had an opportunity to mingle with fellow disciples from so many different courts.

On the sixth day after their departure.

Lee Hyun was refining the shape of the Spirit-Jolting Needle inside his cabin when he sensed a commotion outside.

When he opened the door, Senior Brother Mingyun of the Lotus Court was passing through the corridor.

"Looks like we've arrived."

The two went up to the deck together.

The first thing Lee Hyun saw was a long chain of mountain peaks.

A vast basin spread out beneath them, and at its center stood an enormous immortal city gleaming white in the sunlight. Tall towers and halls stretched endlessly within the walls, while small boats traveled along the waterways that cut between them.

The cities known as immortal cities in this world were truly immense. Even when Lee Hyun thought back to the cities he had seen in Korea in his previous life, he could not think of anything that offered a proper comparison.

The waterways that had looked like thin lines from afar were, up close, twice as wide as the Han River in Seoul had been in his previous life. More than a hundred carriages were traveling abreast across the stone bridge spanning them. The watchtowers flanking the city gates rose high enough to look down upon all but the grandest halls.

Everything that made up the city was built on such a different scale from the cities of his previous life that it was difficult to grasp its full size at a glance.

A blue lake lay to the north of the city, and villas and cultivation grounds rose in tiers along the slopes beside the shore.

Lee Hyun's gaze, however, soon turned toward the sky.

Flying boats.

Flying boats hung everywhere in the sky.

There were long, slender vessels wrapped in clouds, as well as strangely shaped ships that traveled with enormous bronze rings revolving around their hulls.

In the distance, a flying boat approached that looked as though it were carrying an entire sprawling pavilion.

Dozens of banners fluttered above its tiered railings, their shadows sweeping across the clouds below.

Lee Hyun moved closer to the railing.

'There really are a lot of flying boats.'

Those aboard the other vessels were probably thinking the same thing when they saw Baoguang Temple's flying boat, emblazoned with the image of a lion walking upon clouds.

Flying boats dispatched by great sects from every region, along with smaller flight magic tools ferrying guests, filled the skies.

Yet all those vessels moved in an orderly fashion.

Tall towers had been erected atop each peak outside the city. Whenever the crystal pillars atop those towers lit up, paths of light appeared in the air.

The flying boats followed those paths, slowing down before descending toward the broad mooring grounds on different peaks.

Mingyun braced a hand against the railing and leaned out slightly.

"Look at that."

"Which part?"

"The pillars between the peaks. They're connected to the formation inscriptions in the city walls."

Excited, Mingyun, who was skilled in formations, began looking back and forth between the pillars and the walls as he analyzed their structure.

While Lee Hyun listened quietly, the voice of a Golden Core Elder came from behind them.

"That is Huiyun Immortal City."

The disciples turned to see an elderly monk in Buddhist robes stepping onto the deck.

"It is jointly administered by Taiyue Sect and Qingxiao Palace of Jing Kingdom. It lies along the route between the territories of the two sects, so cultivators pass through in great numbers even in ordinary times."

Lee Hyun looked around.

Flying boats were descending even beyond the distant mountain ridges.

The disciples participating in the Dao symposium were not the only ones coming here.

Merchants who had come to sell goods, cultivators wishing to exchange their arts, and people coming to meet members of other sects were all converging on the city.

Hummm―

A small boat appeared in front of Baoguang Temple's flying boat.

Two cultivators dressed in blue stood upon it and respectfully offered their greetings.

"Greetings, Seniors of Baoguang Temple. We have come from Qingxiao Palace to escort you."

After the Elder returned the greeting, the silver boat slowly turned around.

Baoguang Temple's flying boat followed behind it.

...

On the way down toward the mooring ground, they passed alongside another flying boat.

Dozens of male and female cultivators stood on the deck of the pale jade vessel.

Lee Hyun naturally began observing them.

Three sword sheaths were strapped diagonally across the back of a sharp-eyed young man. A female cultivator with her hair tied high had her hands exposed beyond her sleeves, and dark droplets of water rolled between her fingers.

A man leaning against the rear railing had his eyes closed.

He was merely standing there, yet his aura seemed unusually deep and steady.

Lu Hongyan spoke quietly.

"Most of them are at higher cultivation levels than us."

She was right.

Most of the people Lee Hyun noticed were at late Foundation Establishment, and some appeared close to Great Perfection.

The disciples on the opposite flying boat were also examining those on Baoguang Temple's deck.

At that moment, a door on the upper level of the other flying boat opened. When a white-haired old man stepped out, the surrounding disciples naturally moved aside.

The old man exchanged greetings with Baoguang Temple's Elder.

Neither Golden Core Elder displayed any particular pressure, yet the presence of the two old men made the imposing auras of the Foundation Establishment cultivators who had filled the decks moments before seem to vanish without a trace.

...

The residence assigned to Baoguang Temple was a villa in the northern part of the immortal city.

Several pavilions stood within a low wall, with a small pond and pavilion in the center.

The disciples were divided into small groups and assigned buildings. Lee Hyun ended up staying in the same building as Mingyun.

Each room was equipped with a simple defensive formation.

After putting away their luggage, everyone gathered again in the front courtyard.

A steward from the Guest Reception Hall handed each of them a jade token and a thin jade slip.

"Do not lose your jade tokens. You will need them to pass through the villa's restrictions, and they will also serve as proof of identity for those participating in the sparring matches."

Lee Hyun hung the jade token at his waist and pressed the jade slip to his forehead.

The first thing that appeared was a simple map of Huiyun Immortal City.

It marked the locations of the cultivator market, auction houses, the villas housing the various sects, and the training ground where the sparring matches would be held.

After that came the schedule for the Dao symposium.

'There are still ten days until the opening.'

The official events were scheduled to continue for roughly a month from opening day.

The spaces between the sparring matches were packed with the times and locations of various other events.

There were alchemy lectures, artifact-refining demonstrations, magic tool appraisals, joint formation demonstrations, and exchange gatherings for spirit plants and spirit beasts. Technique symposiums were also being held, where the various sects would share their experiences with techniques and cultivation.

A disciple from the Vajra Court standing nearby asked,

"Will we be able to attend all of these and still compete in the sparring matches?"

The steward smiled.

"Check the time of your own match first, then choose whichever other events you wish to attend. You don't need to go to all of them."

"How many people are participating in the sparring matches?"

"The rosters submitted by the various sects already contain more than five hundred names. We won't know the final number until registration is complete."

Several disciples let out quiet exclamations.

More than five hundred.

And they were not just any Foundation Establishment cultivators gathered together at random.

They were disciples whose abilities had been recognized by their sects and who had been chosen to represent them.

Once the cultivators accompanying them and those who had come to attend the lectures were included, the number of people gathering in the immortal city would be far greater.

The prizes for the sparring matches also caught Lee Hyun's eye.

Three exceptional supreme-grade magic tools listed in Yunzhou Artifact Appraisal had apparently been prepared as prizes.

The Elder looked over the disciples and said,
