"Until the opening, you need only complete your registration and make whatever preparations you require. You may interact with people from other sects or browse the cultivator market if you wish."

The disciples' expressions brightened.

"However, wherever you go, make sure at least one fellow disciple knows your destination. If you engage in a private sparring match, use one of the designated training grounds."

"Yes."

The Elder paused for a moment before adding,

"Do not create needless grudges. Someone you befriend here may one day be able to help you, so give some thought to building good relationships as well."

...

After they dispersed.

Lu Hongyan prepared to go out with several disciples from the Demon-Subduing Court.

"Junior Brother Li, want to come with us?"

"I'm going to look around the cultivator market first. There are a few things I need."

"Really? Then let's go around together later."

Lee Hyun told Mingyun, who was standing in the villa's rear courtyard, where he was going, then left the villa alone.

...

The main streets of the immortal city were broad, but they certainly did not feel empty.

Cultivators in all manner of clothing traveled up and down the streets, and people streamed through the covered corridors stretching between the buildings.

Large signs advertising the Dao symposium hung outside the shops on both sides of the street.

Many temporary stores had also opened specifically for the symposium.

Some displayed spirit plants from various regions, while others kept spirit insects suspended within small restrictions.

A circle of spectators had gathered in front of a shop demonstrating a new magic tool.

The sound of music drifted from the windows of upper-story pavilions, while the cultivators passing below carried jade slips or small boxes in their hands.

Lee Hyun walked slowly as he looked around.

There was an enormous amount of merchandise.

'This must be the largest cultivator market I've ever visited.'

Goods that would normally require traveling between major cultivator markets in several different nations were all gathered on a single street.

Plenty of things caught his eye, but he already knew what he intended to buy today.

Magic tools.

He had the Sinking Moon Sword, the Six-Leaf Shield, and the Three-Molt Silkworm Robe worn beneath his outer robe. All three were excellent exceptional supreme-grade magic tools, but that also meant they were famous.

The Sinking Moon Sword ranked eighth in the Nanming Hundred Artifacts Register.

Because of its light-retraction property, the blade itself was difficult to see, and someone unfamiliar with the magic tools of the Nanming Twelve-Sect Alliance might fail to recognize it.

But artifact refiners and appraisers from various nations had gathered here.

If even one person recognized it, word could spread.

The Six-Leaf Shield was listed in Yunzhou Artifact Appraisal, making it even more conspicuous.

'This isn't the same as sparring a few times inside the temple...'

At Baoguang Temple, the only people who had seen his magic tools up close were his acquaintances from the Lotus Court and the fellow disciples who had gone on missions with him.

Even if they recognized his exceptional supreme-grade magic tools, they had no reason to go around telling outsiders about them.

But matters were different in sparring matches watched by cultivators from across the Nine Kingdoms of Yunzhou.

The Three-Molt Silkworm Robe was less of a concern because he wore it as an undergarment.

Unless he took an attack powerful enough to force it to shed a spirit molt, there was almost no chance anyone would see it from the outside.

'It would be better to prepare a separate sword and shield.'

With any magic tool at all, he could easily win a sparring match against a Foundation Establishment cultivator. The outcome depended entirely on how much Lee Hyun chose to reveal, so for now, he only needed magic tools that could stand in for his exceptional supreme-grade ones.

Lee Hyun stopped walking and counted the spirit stones in his storage pouch.

A staggering 6,400 mid-grade spirit stones!

In the past, when he had accumulated 4,000 spirit stones, he had bought the Three-Molt Silkworm Robe. Soon afterward, however, he had recovered most of its purchase price through the spirit stones and proceeds from the magic tools taken from the four cultivators who had attacked him.

A little over twenty years ago, he had received 1,200 mid-grade spirit stones for the Scale-Armored Sea Ape's demon core, and another 400 for its scales, tendons, skeleton, and other materials. That alone had brought in 1,600 mid-grade spirit stones.

There was also the money he had earned over the decades by taking on refining and alchemy work and selling spirit plants. Even after accounting for cultivation pills and other supplies, along with the expenses of maintaining his spirit field and Bonefuzz, his spare funds had increased by another 900 or so.

After tallying all his income and expenses, he was left with 6,400 spirit stones.

Moreover, the spirit plants growing in his spirit field were worth far more than that, so he could simply buy a few ordinary magic tools to use without worrying about them.

...

A shop specializing in magic tools stood a little way off the main street.

Four swords lay on the table.

The middle-aged cultivator who owned the shop pointed to one of them.

"If you intend to pour a large amount of spiritual power into it, this Azure Steel Sword would be the better choice."

"May I test it?"

"Of course."

The owner led him to a small training ground in the rear.

Lee Hyun sent the Azure Steel Sword floating into the air, infused it with a little spiritual power, and moved it around several times.

'Not bad. Perfect for something I can use without worrying about it.'

The owner explained,

"Even among supreme-grade magic tools, its blade is quite durable."

"How much?"

"One hundred and eighty mid-grade spirit stones."

Lee Hyun nodded.

"I'd also like to see defensive magic tools."

The owner soon brought out several.

Lee Hyun chose the Threefold Shield, which consisted of three shield plates.

Unlike the Six-Leaf Shield, it could not disperse the force received by one plate across the others. Still, Lee Hyun was already accustomed to using multiple shield plates floating independently around his body.

'This one will be easy to use too.'

"This is one hundred and ninety."

The last item he selected was a magic tool called the Mountain-Suppressing Seal. It was a square seal with a yellowish hue, about the size of a fist when resting in his palm.

When infused with enough spiritual power, it could expand to a maximum of ten zhang (about 33 m) and was well suited to smashing down from above.

Other than that, it possessed no particular features.

The owner priced it at 130 mid-grade spirit stones.

After examining the restrictions in all three magic tools, Lee Hyun took out 500 mid-grade spirit stones and paid.

...

By the time he returned to the villa, the sky had already grown dark.

Once inside his room, Lee Hyun took out the Azure Steel Sword, Threefold Shield, and Mountain-Suppressing Seal and began bonding the three magic tools through their restrictions.

...

Three days later.

The training ground in the villa's rear courtyard.

Three round shields, the Azure Steel Sword, and the Mountain-Suppressing Seal slowly revolved around Lee Hyun.

'This should be enough for basic use.'

Just then.

"Junior Brother Li, are you here?"

Mingyun's voice came from nearby.

"Yes."

"Good. Junior Sister Lu is looking for you."

"What is it?"

"She said we're going to meet fellow Daoists from Qingxiao Palace and Jinding Sect. I've agreed to go as well. Would you like to come?"

"Certainly."

Lee Hyun put away the magic tools.

...

The lakeshore in the northern part of the immortal city.

Small waterside pavilions stood at intervals along a long covered walkway extending over the water.

Liuxia Waterside Pavilion.

Beneath a signboard written in an elegant, old-fashioned handwriting, Qi Refining attendants welcomed the guests.

Lotus leaves floated between the pavilions, and beautiful fish of every color swam beneath them. When the breeze from the lake passed through the covered walkway, the small bells hanging from the pillars rang with a clear sound.

Seven people had come from Baoguang Temple. Along with Lee Hyun, Mingyun, Yuanjing, and Zhang Taishan were Lu Hongyan and two other disciples from the Demon-Subduing Court.

Lee Hyun followed behind his fellow disciples while looking over the lake.

Guests were also seated in the waterside pavilions across the walkway.

They could see one another, but no voices carried between them. Formations around each pavilion blocked the sound.

An attendant guided the group farther inside.

Eight cultivators had already gathered in the largest pavilion at the very end. Four were disciples of Qingxiao Palace, and the other four were disciples of Jinding Sect from Xuan Kingdom.

A round-faced cultivator with a short beard was the first to rise.

"Venerable Yuanjing, it has been a long time."

"Fellow Daoist Lin, have you been well?"

It was Lin Jinghua of Qingxiao Palace in Jing Kingdom. He and Senior Brother Yuanjing had apparently become acquainted at an exchange gathering in Xuan Kingdom several years ago.

Beside him sat a female cultivator in a dark blue robe. Her hair was neatly tied back, and thin silver thimbles covered two fingers of her right hand.

Yin Cailing of Jinding Sect in Xuan Kingdom.

When she was introduced as someone skilled in artifact-refining arts, Mingyun was the first to strike up a conversation with her. The others also exchanged their sects and names with the people seated nearby.

Once all fifteen had taken their places around the large round table, the previously quiet pavilion quickly grew lively.

Lin Jinghua nodded to the attendant.

Before long, the dishes began arriving one after another.

Clear broth was poured over thin slices of spirit fish. Beside it were bowls of spirit rice and a plate of tender spirit-vegetable shoots.

When the attendant lifted a small lid, gentle steam rose along with a fresh fragrance.

Lu Hongyan picked up her chopsticks.

"How did you find this place?"

"Disciples of our palace often bring fellow Daoists from other lands here. There are many guests today, so I reserved a larger pavilion."

Lin Jinghua smiled and picked up the wine flask.

Yuanjing lightly brought his palms together.

"I'll have tea."

"Of course."

Spirit wine was poured for those who drank, while those who did not were served pale spirit tea.

Lee Hyun took a spoonful of the broth.

A clear, refreshing flavor spread through his mouth.

When he swallowed, warmth spread through his stomach, and gentle spiritual qi seeped into his meridians before slowly dispersing.

'Delicious!'

Lin Jinghua raised his cup.

"Thanks to the Dao symposium, we have the chance to sit together with fellow Daoists from many different nations. I hope we can meet often while you're staying here."

The cups lightly clinked together.

...

The conversation began with the sparring matches.

They talked about who had seen disciples from which sects, and what kinds of techniques this year's competitors were known to use.

The brackets had not even been announced yet, but several cultivators' names had already come up repeatedly.

Lu Hongyan said,

"I saw him too. The cultivator with three sword sheaths on his back, right?"

"That's the one. I've heard he's extremely strong."

A Jinding Sect disciple seated nearby added to the conversation.

Lin Jinghua looked at Yin Cailing.

"Fellow Daoist Yin, do you know which magic tools will be offered as prizes?"

"I don't know what they are either. But even if I win an exceptional supreme-grade magic tool, I plan to sell it and use the money for travel expenses."

Lee Hyun asked,

"Is there somewhere you're planning to go?"

"I'm thinking of traveling to the Qianyuan Empire."

Those sitting nearby turned toward her.

Mingyun raised an eyebrow.

"The empire to the east?"

"Yes."

The Qianyuan Empire.

A Tier-5 cultivation nation said to lie in the distant lands east of Yunzhou.

It was supposedly an empire guarded by Spirit Transformation cultivators.

That, however, was about all Lee Hyun knew of it.

Yin Cailing said,

"One of the Elders of my sect traveled there to study artifact-refining arts before returning. Since then, the number of refining methods taught within our sect has increased considerably. According to the Elder, the Nine Kingdoms of Yunzhou are nothing but the countryside compared to the cultivation world of Qianyuan."

Yin Cailing paused briefly before continuing.

"I believe people need to venture into a wider world if they want to grow. The Qianyuan Empire is classified as a single Tier-5 cultivation nation, but its overall scale is beyond comparison with the Nine Kingdoms of Yunzhou."

Lee Hyun nodded.

Considering that Tier-4 cultivation nations did not even regard regions containing only Golden Core sects as proper cultivation worlds, a Tier-5 cultivation nation was likely on an entirely different level from a Tier-4 one.

Lin Jinghua spoke.

"Isn't the Qianyuan Empire far away?"

"It is. Even after traveling east through Heng Kingdom and leaving Yunzhou behind, you still pass through several cultivation nations. There are Tier-4 cultivation nations there as well, ruled by Nascent Soul sects."

"And after that comes a desert, from what I've heard."

At Yuanjing's words, Yin Cailing nodded.

"You have to cross the Duanmai Sand Sea. Even after crossing it, you've only reached the empire's western frontier."

The Duanmai Sand Sea was a vast desert where spirit veins appeared only in scattered, broken stretches.

Where small spirit veins remained, there were oases and settlements, and merchant caravans crossed the desert by traveling between those outposts.

The problem was the distance between them.

"Keeping a flying boat in the air consumes spirit stones, and cultivators need to rest as well. If you take the wrong route, you might go days without being able to properly replenish your spiritual qi."

Yin Cailing emptied the wine left in her cup.

"I haven't seen it myself either. I've only read the records left by people who made the journey."

...

Another round of dishes was served.

Perhaps because the Qianyuan Empire had come up, the conversation spread to other distant lands.

"In the north, there is a place where the very landscape moves."

One of the Qingxiao Palace disciples brought it up. He said he had traveled the northern trade routes before.

Someone asked,

"You mean the Liutian Plateau?"

"Yes. I've been as far as its southern reaches. The mountain belonging to the sect we were supposed to deliver our goods to arrived late, so we had to wait nearly a month."

Lu Hongyan asked,

"The mountain arrived?"

"Yes. The mountains really do move."

The Qingxiao Palace disciple opened his palm and slowly moved it through the air.

"The mountains float through the air and wander across the plateau. Some contain spirit veins. Great sects occupy the larger mountains, while cultivation clans sometimes live on the smaller ones."

Mingyun spoke.

"I'd like to see it for myself one day."

"If you ever go, a map alone won't be enough."

The Qingxiao Palace disciple smiled.

"You need to know where each mountain will pass at different times. Most follow roughly fixed routes, but they can still be delayed, as happened with the mountain I was waiting for."

Lu Hongyan asked,

"What's beyond that plateau?"

The Qingxiao Palace disciple shook his head.

"I've never heard any stories about what lies beyond it."

Lu Hongyan said,

"It's similar in the west. Even our sect has almost no records from people who traveled farther west beyond the Cangmang Forest."

Lin Jinghua nodded.

"I've heard there are many demon beasts in that region."

"They say that deeper inside are territories belonging to Tier-4 demon beasts, the equivalent of Nascent Soul cultivators."

One of the Jinding Sect disciples joined in.

"Our sect also has records left by a Nascent Soul Elder who traveled there. They say it is extremely dangerous because you have to cross the territories of several demon beasts."

Someone said,

"I suppose every good spirit vein already has an owner, no matter where you go. Even if that owner isn't of the human race."

Lin Jinghua replied,

"Indeed. I've even heard that in the Nanming region, they force the spirit veins they seize to yield more than they normally would."

Lee Hyun stopped halfway through raising his cup and looked at Lin Jinghua.

"Force them to yield more?"

"I heard there's a method that shortens the lifespan of a spirit vein in exchange for making it produce higher-grade spiritual qi than normal for a time."

Mingyun also turned toward Lin Jinghua.

"Who did you hear that from?"

"A merchant who travels the Nanming Sea. It's one of the theories people have long put forward to explain how the Nanming Twelve-Sect Alliance was able to expand its power while advancing north."

Someone asked,

"What utter fools. Do they not think of future generations? Once the spirit vein declines, what are the disciples left behind supposed to do?"

Lin Jinghua replied,

"Someone whose lifespan will run out unless they break through now might see things differently. Of course, it has yet to be confirmed whether such a method truly exists."

Author's Note:

Map as of Chapter 81 (Spoiler Warning)

Some readers have been asking about the geography and the balance of power between the different factions, so I brought a simple map to give you a rough idea of how things are laid out.

As you can see, the borders on the map are drawn in neat, angular shapes. This is because it is only a simplified diagram meant to make the relative locations easier to understand.

In the actual world of the story, the borders and coastlines are much more complex and irregular.

The scale and distances are not exact either, so I would appreciate it if you could treat this as a general reference only.

If there is ever a discrepancy between the map and the descriptions in the main chapter, the main chapter should be considered canon.

Thank you, as always, for reading and following the story. I hope you enjoy it!

Chapter 83

Mingyun looked puzzled.

“If it is only a matter of temporarily gathering the surrounding spiritual qi, a Qi-Gathering Formation can do that as well. But making the spirit vein itself produce higher-grade spiritual qi is truly difficult to believe... I have read quite a few books on earth veins while studying formations, yet I have never heard of such a method. How did the Nanming Twelve-Sect Alliance obtain such an unfathomable inheritance?”

“I haven’t seen it with my own eyes either.”

Lin Jinghua set down his wine cup.

“Whatever the case, it is true that the Nanming Twelve-Sect Alliance once pushed north and greatly expanded its influence... so the rumor does not sound entirely groundless. Perhaps they thought they could simply seize better lands before the spirit veins were exhausted. That is more or less how demonic cultivators behave. They would hardly care what happened to the cultivators who came after them.”

Lu Hongyan frowned.

“Could it have been some sort of blood sacrifice? They say demonic cultivators treat mortals like livestock.”

“Methods like that certainly exist.”

Yin Cailing replied.

“But gathering mortal essence blood and strengthening a spirit vein enough for Foundation Establishment cultivators and above to use are two different matters. If something like that were common, surely we would have heard more concrete accounts from merchants who trade with Nanming.”

Zhang Taishan nodded.

“Exactly. There are dark arts that use mortal essence blood or souls, but that does not mean such things are useful cultivation resources for every demonic cultivator. A mortal soul, for example, is different from the primordial spirit of a cultivator formed after being tempered by spiritual qi. Even if mortal souls are used as material for a soul banner, far more of them would be needed to achieve the same power. If the process strains one’s Dao heart, piles up karma, and even brings enforcement cultivators down on one’s trail, it would hardly be worth the trouble for most cultivators.”

A Qingxiao Palace cultivator spoke up.

“Besides, children with spiritual roots are born among mortals, and those children later become disciples of the sects, do they not? Even setting aside matters of Dao heart and karma, demonic sects also need a steady supply of new disciples to serve them, just as we do. Qi Refining demonic cultivators are valuable manpower. If they want a steady supply of that manpower, it is actually better for the mundane world to prosper.”

Lee Hyun recalled the mortal county seats he had passed through in Kun Kingdom.

Even after they had fallen within the Nanming Twelve-Sect Alliance’s sphere of influence, people still tilled their fields, conducted business, and returned home at sunset. Lands ruled by demonic cultivators were not necessarily littered with corpses everywhere.

After thinking for a moment, he asked,

“When fellow Daoists call the Nanming Twelve-Sect Alliance part of the demonic path, which do you weigh more heavily, their cultivation arts or their conduct?”

Lin Jinghua looked at him.

“What do you mean?”

“Even demonic sects must have people who grow spirit plants and make pills. Conversely, being a disciple of an orthodox sect does not mean one never covets another person’s possessions. I was simply wondering whether the label comes from the cultivation art one practices or from what one actually does.”

Lin Jinghua scratched his chin.

Yuanjing smiled faintly.

“The term is indeed used in several different senses.”

“How do you see it, Senior Brother?”

“Some call inheritances that manipulate devilish qi part of the demonic path, while others use the term for cultivators who commit wicked deeds.”

He cupped his teacup in both hands.

“For one thing, devilish qi itself truly exists. I have even heard of inheritances that transform heaven-and-earth spiritual qi into devilish qi. Of course, even in such cases, demonic sects do not all use the same kind of energy. I hear their inheritances differ from sect to sect.”

“Then should those who handle yin qi, corpse qi, toxic qi, and the like also be considered demonic cultivators?”

“It is not that simple. Even if they take in the same kind of energy, what ultimately accumulates within their bodies differs depending on the cultivation art used to refine it.”

Yuanjing paused before adding,

“There are also stories that those who cultivate devilish qi and ascend become connected to the Devil Realm rather than the immortal realm. I do not know how much truth there is to that, but if those stories are accurate, then devilish qi cannot merely be some sinister and evil energy. It may instead have a fundamental nature of its own, existing across multiple planes.”

Lin Jinghua spoke.

“That may be so if one classifies them by the energy they use. But when people call the Nanming Twelve-Sect Alliance part of the demonic path, they do not usually consider matters that deeply. Frankly, I do not particularly care whether they truly use devilish qi or some other kind of true qi. We simply classify them as demonic cultivators...”

Yin Cailing turned her teacup with the hand wearing a silver thimble.

“Indeed. Perhaps the standards by which we divide the orthodox path from the demonic path are not all that fair. In truth, it is difficult to judge a person solely by the cultivation art they practice. Nor can everyone from an orthodox sect be trusted.”

Lee Hyun drank his spirit tea.

He himself could produce Profound Yin White Bone True Qi. From his perspective, it was simply a kind of true qi well suited to manipulating bones, with no apparent distinction between good and evil.

‘I wonder if Profound Yin White Bone True Qi counts as the devilish qi Senior Brother Yuanjing described. The Nanming Twelve-Sect Alliance must have plenty of other inheritances as well....’

Then he remembered that the Two Heavens Society secretly drew spiritual qi from other people’s spirit veins, and Lee Hyun felt slightly sheepish.

‘Hmm... At least the Two Heavens Society doesn’t damage the spirit veins themselves....’

...

As the drinking gathering stretched on, people began chatting among themselves in smaller groups.

They discussed which family in Jing Kingdom had the best spirit wine, which exceptional supreme-grade magic tools might be offered as prizes, and even which sect had owned the largest flying boat they had seen on the journey here.

Mingyun and Yin Cailing began drawing formation inscriptions with spiritual power across the table as they discussed where artifact refining and formations intersected. Zhang Taishan got into an argument with a Jinding Sect disciple over whether they should arm-wrestle, while someone nearby egged them on to place bets.

Some conversed through voice transmission.

A sudden question occurred to Lee Hyun, and he sent Lu Hongyan a voice transmission.

[Senior Sister Lu. Do you happen to know anything about dual cultivation arts practiced together by Dao companions?]

[Planning to try one with Shulin?]

[...I thought it might help with cultivation.]

Lu Hongyan laughed.

[You’re looking for a Dharma teaching that helps both people cultivate, rather than one that just drains one person’s vital essence, right?]

[Yes.]

[I have heard that such Dharma teachings exist. But they need to be compatible with the cultivation arts practiced by both people, so finding one probably won’t be easy. I wonder if Baoguang Temple has an inheritance like that... Since we’re already attending the Yunzhou Dao Symposium, it might not be a bad idea to look around the places that trade inheritances.]

She picked up the teapot and refilled Lee Hyun’s cup.

[Shulin takes her own cultivation seriously too, so give it some serious thought together.]

The next afternoon.

Lee Hyun told Mingyun where he was going, then left the detached residence alone.

He first stopped by a bookstore on the main street, where a travelogue about the Liutian Plateau caught his eye. It contained illustrations of several floating mountains, along with observations recorded by a cultivator who had accompanied merchant caravans traveling through the region.

After flipping through a few pages, he paid for the book.

‘Mountains floating through the sky... If I dug a tunnel into one, I suppose the tunnel would be flying too.’

Lee Hyun also asked the Qi Refining cultivator who owned the bookstore about dual cultivation arts.

The owner handed him a jade slip containing summaries of various Dharma teachings. It only briefly described their effects and cultivation requirements, but for Lee Hyun, who did not yet know what he should be looking for, that was actually ideal.

Lee Hyun bought the jade slip as well and left the bookstore.

After walking along the main street for some time, the scents mingling in the air gradually changed.

The bitter fragrance of dried medicinal herbs, the acrid smoke of charcoal heating pill furnaces, and a sweet medicinal fragrance drifting from somewhere, as though a pill furnace had just been opened.

Before long, a plaza came into view.

‘This place...’

Alchemy platforms stood at regular intervals across the spacious plaza, which had been opened for cultivators to exchange their skills. Tables displaying pills and medicinal ingredients surrounded them, while alchemists inspected one another’s wares and conversed.

Wooden plaques at the entrance listed the demonstrations and times for each spot.

Lee Hyun slowed his steps.

Flame threads were moving atop one of the alchemy platforms.

His gaze froze when a flame thread with almost no visible light crossed beside another that burned brightly.

‘Is that...?’

A male cultivator at the mid Foundation Establishment stage sat before the pill furnace. The emblem of the Taixuan Sect was embroidered on his sleeve.

As the man moved his fingers, the flames circling the edge of the pill furnace folded inward. Two strands wrapped around the medicinal liquid while the remaining flame threads supported it from below.

‘The Flame-Threading Art?’

Lee Hyun moved closer to the alchemy platform.

The order in which the flames were withdrawn and the way the flame threads were gathered and rotated were not exactly the same, but the foundation was unmistakably the technique he knew!

A short while later, the male cultivator finished Refining, and the clear medicinal liquid was transferred onto a jade dish. When a middle-aged cultivator standing nearby placed it beside another medicinal liquid that had been Refined earlier, the onlookers moved closer to compare the two.

Lee Hyun waited until the others had finished asking their questions before speaking.

“Your method of controlling the flames is impressive. Is it an inheritance of the Taixuan Sect?”

“It is. It is the fire-control art of our sect’s Yanxia lineage.”

The Yanxia lineage!

Lee Hyun repeated the words silently.

An ancient pine tree came to mind, along with the flat stone beneath it.

Tan Yunsheng had sat there with medicinal stains on his fingers.

Tao Wenqian had poured tea for the Junior Brother who had just arrived.

His fellow disciples had shared their thoughts over a pill split apart on the stone table.

Seeing that Lee Hyun could not take his eyes off the alchemy platform, the middle-aged cultivator pointed to a wooden plaque beside it.

“If you are interested in fire control, you should apply for our lineage’s lecture. On the third day of the symposium, True Lord Xiaoying will personally offer instruction.”

Lee Hyun turned his head.

“...True Lord Xiaoying?”

“Yes. It will be held at the Alchemy Court in the eastern district. Applications to attend are not accepted here, so you will need to visit the symposium administration office.”

The guide jade slip he handed over contained the lecture’s location, time, and the procedures required to attend.

「Lecture on the alchemy and fire control of the Tier-3 True Essence Pill.」

The True Essence Pill was a cultivation pill widely used by Golden Core cultivators to build magical power.

Lee Hyun read the lecturer’s name.

「Taixuan Sect, Yanxia lineage, True Lord Chen Xiaoying.」

‘...!’

Even after lowering the jade slip, he could not speak for some time.

When the Danxiao Sect had scattered, Chen Xiaoying had followed Tan Yunsheng to the Taixuan Sect.

And now that same Chen Xiaoying had become a Nascent Soul great cultivator revered throughout the Nine Kingdoms of Yunzhou!

The days when they had taken the Special Selection for Skilled Practitioners together felt like the distant past.

“Fellow Daoist, are you surprised?”

The middle-aged cultivator smiled as though he were accustomed to that reaction.

“Everyone makes that face. It is rare for the True Lord to give a public lecture.”

“...Thank you. I will be sure to attend.”

Lee Hyun saluted him and stepped away from the alchemy platform.

After leaving the plaza, he read the guide jade slip once more.

For a moment, he wondered if it could be someone else with the same name, but considering the mention of the Taixuan Sect’s Yanxia lineage, it had to be the person he knew.

‘Incredible! She reached the Nascent Soul realm...’

Chen Xiaoying had distinguished herself from a young age as a dual spiritual root cultivator.

Yet even that did not guarantee reaching the Nascent Soul realm. There were plenty of single spiritual root geniuses who ended their lives without ever reaching Nascent Soul, or even the Golden Core realm.

A cultivator’s life was that unpredictable, yet Senior Sister Chen, who had lost her sect and departed for a foreign land, had ultimately made it through that narrow path.

‘I’m glad she’s doing well, but... I can’t exactly go visit her.’

Lee Hyun put away the guide jade slip.

...

There was a line of cultivators at the administration office waiting to apply for lectures.

When Lee Hyun’s turn came, he presented his Baoguang Temple identity token.

“I would like to attend True Lord Xiaoying’s alchemy lecture.”

A short while later, the steward handed him a small attendance token engraved with a seat number.

“Bring this with you on the day of the lecture. Entry will be restricted once the lecture begins. During the alchemy demonstration, do not carelessly extend your divine sense into the pill furnace. If a Nascent Soul True Lord becomes angry, we cannot take responsibility, so please be careful.”

“Understood.”

...

Over the remaining few days, Lee Hyun continued practicing with his newly purchased magic tools to familiarize himself with them and completed registration for the sparring matches alongside his fellow disciples.

The day the Yunzhou Dao Symposium opened.

The central training ground of Huiyun Immortal City.

Perhaps because it had been built with cultivators’ sparring matches in mind, its scale was enormous.

Dozens of tiers of seating rose like steps around a vast circular arena constructed from white stone. Platforms bearing the flags of various sects had been placed among the stands.

Baoguang Temple’s section was on the eastern side.

Beneath a banner embroidered with a lion treading upon clouds, Lee Hyun sat among his fellow disciples and looked around.

He could not see a single empty seat.

There were disciples participating in the sparring matches and the Elders leading them, cultivators who had come for lectures, members of merchant caravans, and rogue cultivators who had traveled from all across Jing Kingdom simply to watch.

The lower stands were already packed with people, yet even that was not enough. Others watched from the rooftops of pavilions outside the training ground or from flight magic tools suspended in the air.

Mingyun exclaimed in admiration.

“That arena itself is a single formation plate.”

Lee Hyun had already sensed it as well.

Thousands of formation inscriptions intertwined beneath the surface of the white stone. Eight pillars standing around the arena were connected to those inscriptions, binding the entire arena within one enormous restriction.

‘No matter how wildly Foundation Establishment cultivators fight, the aftermath won’t reach the stands.’

When noon arrived, the commotion in the stands gradually died down.

People appeared on the highest platform to the north of the training ground.

At the front stood Golden Core Elders of the Taiyue Sect and Qingxiao Palace. Several separate seats of honor had been prepared behind them.

The moment the occupants of those seats appeared, the air seemed to grow heavy.

None of them had released their aura or displayed their might. They had merely taken their seats, yet even the faint whispers remaining in the stands ebbed away like a receding tide.

Nascent Soul.

They were the great cultivators who upheld the great sects of the Nine Kingdoms of Yunzhou.

Lee Hyun steadied his breathing and examined the seats of honor one by one.

An old man with long white hair, a middle-aged Daoist sitting with his eyes closed, a sword cultivator with a sword at his waist.

There were only a few of them, yet that alone was enough to overwhelm the surroundings.

And at the end of the row sat a female cultivator in a pale blue enchanted robe. A clear aura flowed faintly through the patterns along its hem, making the garment look extraordinarily expensive.

A jade hairpin adorned her neatly tied-up hair.

Her face looked to be around thirty. Even without elaborate makeup, she naturally drew the eye.

Lee Hyun recognized her at once.

It really was Chen Xiaoying!

He quickly looked away. Staring at a Nascent Soul cultivator for too long would be discourteous.

A Nascent Soul cultivator from the Taiyue Sect rose from his seat.

“Fellow Daoists of the Nine Kingdoms of Yunzhou.”

His calm voice rang clearly through every corner of the vast training ground, as though he were speaking right beside each listener. Faced with such an astonishing method, the crowd fell silent.

The opening address was not long.

He welcomed the cultivators of the Nine Kingdoms of Yunzhou who had gathered again after sixty years and expressed his hope that they would exchange insights into the Dao and learn from one another. He also urged them to compete in the sparring matches without leaving grudges behind.

“With this, I declare the Yunzhou Dao Symposium open.”

At those words, the eight pillars surrounding the arena shone simultaneously.

Wooooom―

A vast screen of light spread through the air above the arena, and in its center appeared enormous images of three magic tools.

The stands erupted into murmurs.

They were exceptional supreme-grade magic tools listed in the Yunzhou Artifact Appraisal. Beneath each magic tool, its name and ranking appeared in golden characters, and exclamations and assessments burst out from all around.

The first thing to catch the eye was an iron awl a little over one chi (about 33 cm) long.

Its body was dark gold, and three spiral grooves converged toward its sharp tip. Each time it slowly rotated, a small point of light gathered at the tip and flashed sharply.

「Aura-Piercing Awl. Ranked 37th in the Yunzhou Artifact Appraisal.」

The voice of the Golden Core Elder introducing the magic tool rang out.

“This magic tool concentrates spiritual power at a single point on the tip, making it exceptionally effective at piercing body-protecting spirit light and defensive restrictions. After a fully charged strike, it must accumulate spiritual power again, but the force of that initial attack is so tremendous that it scarcely seems possible for a mere magic tool. For that reason, it is highly regarded in the Yunzhou Artifact Appraisal.”

Lu Hongyan uncrossed her arms.

“I heard that thing once pierced a low-grade defensive magic treasure.”

The second item looked like a piece of folded silk.

However, when the object in the image unfolded, it revealed itself to be a net woven from fine silver threads. Tiny ice crystals glimmered whenever the mesh spread open, and blue beads hung around its edges.

「Profound Ice Net. Ranked 68th in the Yunzhou Artifact Appraisal.」

“When fully deployed, it can cover more than ten zhang (over 33 m). If it wraps around a body or magic tool, a deep chill seeps in and slows its movements.”

Mingyun nodded.

“That would be useful for capturing demon beasts.”

Several disciples of the Life-Release Court leaned forward as well.

The final item was a pair of shoes made from dark blue leather.

Wing-shaped designs were embroidered on either side of the ankles, while patterns of flowing wind along the soles repeatedly brightened faintly and faded.

「Whirlwind Shoes. Ranked 112th in the Yunzhou Artifact Appraisal.」

“When wearing this magic tool, one can burst across a short distance at great speed, whether on the ground or in the air, and can easily change direction even while moving rapidly.”

Lee Hyun’s gaze lingered on the final magic tool.

‘A magic tool that boosts speed... I do want that one a little.’

The Aura-Piercing Awl, which held the highest ranking, drew the most exclamations, but quite a few cultivators were unable to take their eyes off the other two magic tools as well.

The Golden Core Elder continued.

“One will be awarded to each of the final top three. The champion will choose first, the runner-up will choose next, and the third-place finisher will receive the remaining magic tool.”

The murmuring in the stands grew louder.

Lu Hongyan leaned toward Lee Hyun.

“Which one are you going to choose, Junior Brother Li?”

“Do I really need to think about it when I probably won’t win one?”

“That’s too much. No sense of romance at all... You’re giving me such a halfhearted answer because I’m not Shulin, aren’t you? You could at least think about it in advance. Wait, are you trying to tell me something? Are you saying Junior Brother Li might win a prize, but I definitely won’t, so I shouldn’t bother thinking about it?”

“.......”

As soon as the opening ceremony ended, the drawing for the sparring-match groups began.

A Golden Core Elder of Qingxiao Palace flew above the arena and suspended a large formation plate in the air.

“All participants in the sparring matches, take out your jade tokens.”

Hundreds of jade tokens rose above palms throughout the stands.

Lee Hyun also took out the jade token he had received at the detached residence.

As the formation plate began to rotate, hundreds of fine beams of light shot outward and flew toward the jade tokens scattered throughout the stands. One beam descended onto the token in Lee Hyun’s palm as well.

Characters appeared on its surface.

「Group 47.

First sparring match: Hour of the Horse (approximately 11 a.m.–1 p.m.) on the fifth day of the symposium.」

‘Fortunately, it doesn’t overlap with Chen Xiaoying’s lecture.’

The Elder’s voice rang out again.

“Five hundred and forty-three participants completed final registration. They have been assigned to sixty-four groups of eight or nine. Each participant will face every other opponent in their group once, and the top two from each group will advance to the main tournament. A total of one hundred and twenty-eight competitors will qualify.”

Cultivators all around could be seen studying their jade tokens.

“The preliminary round will run from the fourth through the twelfth day of the symposium. Check your jade token for the names of the others in your group, the time of each sparring match, and the rules for determining rankings in the event of a tie.”

...

The morning of the third day of the symposium.

Cultivators had been streaming toward the Alchemy Court in the eastern part of the immortal city since early morning.

Attendance tokens were checked at the entrance, while disciples of the Taixuan Sect guided people to their seats in the inner corridor.

Lee Hyun followed the corridor inside and looked ahead.

A circular stone platform rose from the center of a broad courtyard.

A large bronze pill furnace sat atop it, and formation inscriptions on the ground extended from beneath the furnace to four pillars surrounding the platform.

The seating rose in tiers around the stone platform, designed so that the person in front would not block the view no matter where one sat.

There was no roof above the platform.

As Lee Hyun took his seat, he examined the restriction running between the pillars. It was a formation meant to prevent heat and the aftermath of medicinal strength from reaching the audience. Its sides appeared sealed while the top had been left open.

‘Does an alchemy demonstration really need a formation this elaborate?’

The Golden Core cultivators in the front row all sat upright with formidable bearings, their gazes fixed on the stone platform.

They were Elders who had brought disciples from various sects. Among them was an Elder of the Lotus Court whom Lee Hyun recognized from Baoguang Temple.

Foundation Establishment alchemists filled the seats farther back. Even those who had been exchanging greetings moments earlier fell silent when a bell rang.

A short while later, the door behind the stone platform opened.

Two Golden Core cultivators of the Taixuan Sect emerged first and stepped aside to the left and right. A female cultivator walked out between them.

It was Chen Xiaoying.

Seeing her from much closer than during the opening ceremony made it even clearer. The focused look in her eyes as she examined the pill furnace and medicinal ingredients one by one overlapped with the image Lee Hyun remembered from the old Yanxia Peak.

When the Golden Core Elders rose from their seats, all the cultivators behind them stood as well.

“We greet True Lord Xiaoying!”

Hundreds of powerful voices filled the courtyard.

Chen Xiaoying lightly returned the greeting.

“You have all come a long way. Please, sit.”

She stood before the pill furnace.

She displayed no oppressive aura and stirred no magical power. Even so, the courtyard was so quiet that scarcely even the rustle of clothing could be heard.

Alchemists from many different kingdoms waited for her to speak.

When Chen Xiaoying raised a hand, several jade trays beside her slowly floated into the air.

“Today, I will demonstrate the fire control and Pill Condensation of the True Essence Pill. Most of the medicinal ingredients have already been Refined, so we will begin by completing the remaining Refining and proceed from there into Harmonizing.”

The trays held medicinal liquids wrapped in preservation restrictions, along with several medicinal ingredients that had not yet been prepared.

“The True Essence Pill is one I have made regularly since my early Golden Core days, when I used it for my own cultivation.”

Chen Xiaoying opened the lid of the pill furnace.

“The more familiar an alchemist becomes with a pill recipe, the easier it is to fall into routine, neglect further study, and rely only on a sequence already ingrained in one’s hands. Today, I hope this will be an opportunity to consider how far we alchemists can go when we break free of that inertia and continue forward.”

A tiny spark appeared at her fingertip.

Whoosh.

The spark split apart, and slender flames spread over the pill furnace, tracing circular paths at different heights.

‘The Flame-Threading Art!’

Lee Hyun opened his eyes wide, determined not to miss a single movement.

...

For a while, he was able to follow the flow.

He could tell which flame loosened the medicinal ingredients and which caught the medicinal potency as it began to disperse. The patterns woven by the flame threads were complicated, but the underlying principles were ones Lee Hyun himself had honed over many years.

Chen Xiaoying brought two Refined medicinal liquids closer together.

One was pale yellow, while the other was clear blue.

When the edges of the two liquids touched, a tiny bubble formed within the blue liquid.

A single flame thread pierced into the blue medicinal liquid. As the bubble swelled, the flames wrapped around the outside weakened until scarcely any light remained visible.

Pop.

The bubble burst.

The medicinal strength that seemed ready to scatter with the force of the rupture was caught within the flames. The yellow medicinal liquid then seeped into that spot in a thin stream, and the two colors blended smoothly.

An elderly Golden Core cultivator in the front row leaned forward slightly in surprise.

As more medicinal liquid was added, the flow of the flames grew increasingly complex.

At some point, Lee Hyun could no longer anticipate the next manipulation. Despite his extraordinary mastery of the Flame-Threading Art, he could not understand why the medicinal liquid was divided or why the fire control changed at particular moments.

More and more people in the front row began leaning forward.

Around the time one shichen (about two hours) had passed.

The medicinal strength mingling above the pill furnace divided into six portions.

The flames surrounding each portion rotated in circles, and the once-fluid medicinal liquids gradually began to take shape.

The cultivators in the courtyard held their breaths.

A short while later, five pills that had taken shape first descended toward the lower part of the pill furnace.

Only one remained above.

The flame threads surrounding it grew thinner.

Thinner still.

Even with Lee Hyun’s eyes, despite having cultivated the Flame-Threading Art to Perfection, it became difficult to distinguish the boundary between the firelight and the medicinal strength.

Then a breeze swept through the courtyard.

‘A breeze? No, this is...’

Goosebumps rose along Lee Hyun’s arms.

Every tassel hanging in the corridor tilted in the same direction.

Toward the pill furnace.

The surrounding spiritual qi was moving.

As though responding to the tiny pill atop the stone platform, the scattered spiritual qi was gathering of its own accord.

A very quiet voice escaped from somewhere in the front row.

“Surely....”

Lee Hyun raised his head as well.

A single black speck had appeared in the clear sky.

It spread rapidly.

Water qi in the air gathered together as spiritual qi coiled around it, forming a mass of dark clouds several zhang wide above the pill furnace.

It was not large enough to cover the entire courtyard, yet the shadow beneath it was unnaturally dark.

Sunlight formed a golden rim around the edges of the clouds, while slender streaks of violet light silently flickered through their pitch-black depths.

At that moment, several cultivators in the front rows jolted in shock and began murmuring.

“Impossible...”

“It’s a pill tribulation!”

Chapter 84

Lee Hyun was surprised as well.

'Is that really a pill tribulation?'

He had read about pill tribulations while working as an alchemist.

Generally, pills were divided into grades according to the major realm of the cultivators who used them, and within each grade they were further divided into low, mid, high, and supreme grades.

It was said that some supreme-grade pills, once they surpassed a certain threshold, would resonate with the energies of heaven and earth and summon a small tribulation cloud.

Supreme-grade pills that reached that level were separately known as Dao pills!

It was his first time witnessing the actual alchemy process of a Dao pill.

When Chen Xiaoying triggered the pill tribulation, several Golden Core Elders moved.

Soon, the formation inscriptions around the stone platform lit up, and the blue barrier stretched between the viewing stands and the alchemy platform grew thicker. The top remained open.

'I see. They accounted for the possibility of a pill tribulation from the very beginning. Impressive.'

Crackle.

A thin streak of light flashed beneath the cloud.

Someone behind him sucked in a breath.

Chen Xiaoying kept her eyes fixed on the pill without even looking up.

The flame threads slowly revolved around the pill. Each time the flames passed over it, tiny points of light gathered on its surface and vanished.

The purple light within the dark cloud converged in one place.

The wind in the courtyard died.

Flash!

His vision turned white.

The instant a bolt of purple lightning pierced down through the air, Chen Xiaoying's fingers were already moving.

The flame threads surrounding the pill instantly spread apart.

Lee Hyun's eyes widened.

Chen Xiaoying was not blocking the lightning. She was guiding it!

The pill swallowed the lightning.

Where there should have been a tiny bead, a fist-sized orb of light bloomed instead. Purple afterglows stretched in every direction, whirling between the flame threads.

A sharp peal of thunder erupted a moment later.

Rumble!

Then the formation barrier rippled.

Lee Hyun gathered spiritual power in his eyes and tried to see inside the orb of light.

He could faintly make out the outline of the pill.

Dazzling medicinal strength leaked through fine cracks on its surface.

Chen Xiaoying supported the outer shell of the pill as it threatened to split, constantly altering the flames in response to the violent changes occurring within.

Only then did Lee Hyun begin to understand.

Destroying such a small bolt of lightning would probably not be difficult for a Nascent Soul cultivator.

But she was trying to make the pill withstand the lightning without collapsing and ultimately absorb even that energy into itself.

The orb of light shuddered.

The medicinal fragrance intensified, then abruptly vanished.

As the leaking medicinal strength curled back inward, the purple light circled once around the pill's surface before sinking deep inside.

Hum―

A round pill rose above the pill furnace.

The cracks that had covered it moments ago were gone, and in their place a single silvery-purple marking had appeared.

The marking continued around the pill. Unlike the ordinary pill markings Lee Hyun had seen before, the surrounding spiritual qi moved ever so slowly along that fine line.

'That marking is...'

The dark clouds in the sky began to disperse.

Starting from the black edges, they scattered as though melting in the sunlight, and even the last remaining purple glow soon vanished.

The courtyard brightened once more.

Someone let out a long breath.

Only then did Lee Hyun realize he had been holding his breath as well.

A Golden Core cultivator in the front row cupped his hands.

"Congratulations on completing a one-mark Dao pill, True Lord."

Several people paid their respects to Chen Xiaoying, and she gave a slight nod in return.

She placed the pill on a transparent jade tray. She also took out the remaining five pills that had been undergoing warm nurturing below and placed them on another dish one by one.

They too were all high-grade or supreme-grade True Essence Pills.

Chen Xiaoying raised the jade tray.

"This is the tribulation marking that forms after a pill survives a pill tribulation. It differs from ordinary pill markings, which appear as medicinal strength gathers."

The silvery-purple line glimmered faintly beneath the sunlight.

"With Dao pills, the more tribulation markings there are, the greater the degree of completion. A one-mark Dao pill is the most I can show you, but somewhere in the cultivation realm, there must be those capable of refining two-mark or three-mark Dao pills."

She looked down at the pill for a moment.

"Which means there is still much left to study."

Though Chen Xiaoying spoke calmly, everyone present understood.

Even a one-mark Dao pill was an extraordinary feat, not an achievement anyone could dare take lightly.

A mere pill could summon a tribulation cloud and draw down a lightning tribulation. If that was not the art of an Immortal, then what was?

A Golden Core cultivator in the front row asked cautiously.

"True Lord, can you also refine other pills into Dao pills?"

Chen Xiaoying shook her head.

"So far, I have only achieved results at this level with True Essence Pills."

'I see....'

Apparently, reaching a high realm did not mean one could master every pill recipe to its absolute limit.

She had said earlier that she had been steadily refining True Essence Pills since her early Golden Core days. It seemed those long years of study had finally borne fruit in the single pill before them.

It had been over eight hundred years since they had taken the Special Selection for Skilled Practitioners together, so Chen Xiaoying must have been around that age as well. But judging by her current appearance, as though she had taken a Youth-Preserving Pill, there was no way to tell when she had formed her golden core or when she had entered the Nascent Soul realm.

'If she occasionally made and used True Essence Pills like this even back in her Golden Core days... she must have cut down the time needed for cultivation considerably.'

While Lee Hyun was lost in thought, the Tier-3 alchemists in the Golden Core realm seated in the front row had already begun eagerly competing to ask questions like well-behaved fledglings, and Chen Xiaoying answered them one by one.

Why she had lowered the fire control before adding more medicinal liquid, what to watch for at the instant the medicinal liquid was divided just before Pill Condensation, and how to finish the alchemy when it seemed the pill would fail to survive the pill tribulation.

The Golden Core cultivators' questions kept coming, so the Foundation Establishment cultivators did not even dare waste True Lord Xiaoying's time with foolish questions.

Lee Hyun carefully recorded every question and answer he heard in a jade slip.

He did not leave out even the parts he could not understand yet. Perhaps they would make sense when he read them again later.

When she finished answering the last question, Chen Xiaoying prepared to leave, and all the cultivators rose together to pay their respects.

Lee Hyun also put away the jade slip and pressed his palms together.

'Thank you for the lesson, Senior Sister Chen.'

The fourth day of the symposium.

The preliminaries began in the sparring arenas around the martial platform.

The sparring arenas lined the broad road, and in front of each hung a list of groups and that day's matchups.

After checking when their turns would come, the cultivators either sat in nearby viewing stands or headed toward other sparring arenas.

When the clang of metal rang out from one side, flames on the opposite side dyed a barrier red.

After a sparring match ended, steward cultivators entered the arena to inspect the floor and formation inscriptions. As soon as they came down, the next participants went up.

Lee Hyun sat in the viewing stands with Mingyun and Yuanjing.

Below them, Lu Hongyan's long spear was thrusting viciously toward the chest of the opposing cultivator.

Hum!

The lapels of his gray enchanted robe puffed out as circular patterns rotated, causing the spearhead to slide aside at an angle.

At the same time, two flying blades shot from his sleeves like venomous snakes.

Lu Hongyan twisted her body, and the two flying blades swept past her chest and shoulder. When one suddenly changed course and aimed for her back, the vajra above Lu Hongyan's head burst with golden ripples.

Boom!

The flying blade was knocked helplessly away. Lu Hongyan did not miss that momentary opening.

She kicked off the ground and shortened her grip on the spear shaft, making her opponent recoil in alarm.

The patterns on the enchanted robe rotated again.

But this time, the palm force struck before the spear did.

Thud!

A golden palm burst from Lu Hongyan's left hand and smashed into the enchanted robe's protective barrier, denting it inward.

Immediately after, the six metal rings on the long spear howled fiercely.

Clatter―

Before the body-protecting spirit light could recover, the sharp spearhead pierced through the gap and stopped a handspan from her opponent's shoulder.

The referee raised a hand.

"Enough."

Lu Hongyan withdrew her spear.

The cultivator across from her took a moment to steady his breathing, then cupped his hands.

"I concede."

"It was a good sparring match."

As the two came down, the steward cultivators who had been waiting entered the sparring arena.

Mingyun nodded.

"Junior Sister Lu truly strikes quickly."

Yuanjing responded.

"She read her opponent's protective enchanted robe well. Once it blocked an attack, there was a brief opening before the patterns came around again."

A short while later, Lu Hongyan came up to the viewing stands.

As soon as she sat in an empty seat, she opened a palm-sized booklet, pulled out a short wooden brush tucked inside the cover, and began writing something.

Eventually, she closed the booklet and looked at Lee Hyun.

"Junior Brother, your match is tomorrow at the Hour of the Horse (approximately 11 a.m.–1 p.m.)?"

"Yes."

"I'll be free after one match in the morning. I'll come watch."

...

Before the next sparring match began, the four of them came down from the viewing stands and stopped in front of a pavilion across the road. The rewards were written on a wooden board hanging on the wall.

Below three exceptional supreme-grade magic tools, it stated that each of the 128 cultivators who advanced to the main tournament would receive thirty mid-grade spirit stones. Those who reached the round of 32 could choose one item from a separate set of rewards or take spirit stones instead.

Lu Hongyan said,

"So it isn't just the top three who get anything? Now that's more like it."

Lee Hyun's gaze lingered briefly on the Whirlwind Shoes.

He did like them.

But to obtain them, he would have to place among the top three out of several hundred Foundation Establishment cultivators gathered from the Nine Kingdoms of Yunzhou.

'There's no need to draw that much attention just for one exceptional supreme-grade magic tool.'

Lee Hyun had only come intending to enjoy himself as though he were on an outing.

He could spar a few more times in the main tournament, then bow out at an appropriate moment.

The fifth day of the symposium, Hour of the Horse.

The sparring arena assigned to Group 47.

After presenting his jade token and having his identity verified, Lee Hyun stepped onto the stone platform.

Across from him, a male cultivator from Qingxiao Palace was straightening his sleeves.

He was at Foundation Establishment Stage 8 and wore a metal ring on each side of his waist. The surfaces of the rings were densely carved with diagonal grooves.

He cupped his hands.

"Han Jingxiu of Qingxiao Palace."

"Li Dongsi of Baoguang Temple. I look forward to our match."

The referee outside the sparring arena looked at them both.

"Begin!"

Han Jingxiu moved first.

The two rings released from his waist crossed in midair, then split left and right with a low rush of wind.

Whoosh!

Two shield plates rose in front of Lee Hyun.

Clang!

The ring flying in from the right smashed against the edge of one shield plate. Almost simultaneously, the ring on the opposite side dipped low near the ground before surging toward his thigh.

Lee Hyun knocked it aside with the third shield plate.

Meanwhile, the Azure Steel Sword flew toward Han Jingxiu.

But Han Jingxiu was already retreating. Dust swept out in a long trail beneath his feet as his body slid diagonally away.

The Azure Steel Sword cut through empty air.

'Not bad! My acting skills...'

He had planned to take it easy, but his opponent was no incompetent either.

The trajectory of the incoming Azure Steel Sword was trembling ever so slightly.

Everywhere the rings passed, taut currents of air overlapped, weaving an invisible net of wind across the entire sparring platform.

'Interesting.'

Han Jingxiu rode the spring of the currents he had created, gliding around like a ghost.

Whenever Lee Hyun thrust with his sword, Han Jingxiu slipped aside with the wind, and whenever Lee Hyun raised a shield plate, a ring riding the air current slipped in from his blind spot.

Swoooosh!

At Han Jingxiu's gesture, the paired rings shot above his head and began spinning violently, pouring down condensed wind blades like a torrential rain.

Lee Hyun layered the three shield plates together into a wall.

Boom-boom-boom!

At the instant the fierce wind pressure hammered the shield plates and obscured his vision, Lee Hyun compressed his divine sense into a thin point and sharpened the Spirit-Jolting Needle.

Han Jingxiu's eyes narrowed at the sharp presence of divine sense.

The moment he instinctively sprang backward and tried to recall one of the rings,

Rumble―

A huge shadow descended over the sparring platform.

It was the Mountain-Suppressing Seal.

The heavy seal, expanded to two zhang (about 6.6 m) in size, dropped as though it meant to crush the entire space above Han Jingxiu's head.

"Ugh!"

Han Jingxiu panicked and overlapped both rings above his head. A compressed gale shot upward from within the narrowed rings and smashed against the corner of the Mountain-Suppressing Seal.

Boom!

The seal tilted sideways and crashed to the ground.

Boom!

The stone platform shuddered as fragments of rock flew. Han Jingxiu barely escaped its shadow and tried to breathe a sigh of relief.

But at the very instant the trajectories of the paired rings opened up from knocking away the Mountain-Suppressing Seal,

Clang!

The two shield plates that had moved to the outer edge snapped together in midair like scissors.

One of the returning rings was caught between them and pinned so tightly it could not budge.

"...?!"

Han Jingxiu's face went pale.

The moment one ring was trapped, the net of air currents tightening around the sparring platform collapsed in an instant.

Having lost the spring of the wind, Han Jingxiu staggered.

The circling Azure Steel Sword shot into that opening like lightning.

Fwoosh!

Before he could raise the remaining ring, the sword tip pierced into the body-protecting spirit light at Han Jingxiu's side and stopped.

At the same time, the Mountain-Suppressing Seal that had fallen to the ground rose again and aimed at the crown of his head.

"Enough."

The referee's voice rang out.

Han Jingxiu looked back and forth between the Mountain-Suppressing Seal above his head and the sword halted near his side.

After pressing his lips together for a moment, he slowly relaxed his hands.

"I concede."

Lee Hyun recalled the sword and seal, then cupped his hands.

"It was a good sparring match."

...

Below the viewing stands, Lu Hongyan raised a hand.

Yuanjing and Mingyun were beside her as well.

"Well done."

As Lee Hyun approached, Lu Hongyan gestured with her eyes toward his storage pouch.

"That seal... you bought it recently, right? Why does everything look so good when Junior Brother Li uses it?"

Lee Hyun let out a quiet laugh.

Yuanjing said,

"A shame about the Spirit-Jolting Needle."

"Yes. It isn't easy to conceal the signs of forming it."

"That fellow was also a cultivator with keen divine sense. It could not be helped."

Lee Hyun nodded.

Mingyun looked down at his jade token.

"My turn is at the Hour of the Goat (approximately 1–3 p.m.). Shall we get something to eat before then? We came all this way, so it would feel rather wasteful to make do with Hunger-Warding Pills, wouldn't it?"

Lu Hongyan nodded.

"Sounds good."

The four of them headed for a roadside restaurant.

The preliminaries continued after that.

Lee Hyun fought his remaining opponents one after another.

There were cultivators who commanded spirit beasts, cultivators who scattered several talismans around the narrow sparring arena and then herded their opponents through them, and some who handled a single magic tool with great skill, while others alternated between magic tools with different properties.

As he fought them, Lee Hyun gradually grew more accustomed to the Azure Steel Sword, the Threefold Shield, and the Mountain-Suppressing Seal.

...

And so the twelfth day of the symposium arrived.

When Lee Hyun came down from the stone platform after his final sparring match, a steward checked his jade token.

"You won all seven matches. You placed first in Group 47."

"Thank you."

"Tomorrow morning, report to the front of the martial platform to receive your main-tournament jade token and reward. The main-tournament matchups will also be decided there."

Lee Hyun took back the jade token.

He had advanced to the round of 128.

Lu Hongyan waved at him from a distance.

She had also placed second in her group and advanced to the main tournament. Mingyun, on the other hand, had lost his final sparring match and narrowly ended in third place.

"Senior Brother almost had him at the end too."

At Lu Hongyan's words, Mingyun shook his head.

"I still have much to improve. Now I can simply relax and enjoy watching."

Just then.

A low, drawn-out bell rang in the distance.

Lee Hyun raised his head.

Flying boats had appeared in the sky southeast of the immortal city.

The largest was a great vessel with a dark gray hull and black sails. Two somewhat smaller flying boats followed on either side.

Dark metal plates overlapped beneath the tall, sharply pointed prow, while flags bearing different symbols hung between the masts.

Flying boats had continued arriving even after the Dao symposium opened, so there was nothing strange about seeing new ones.

Yet this time, something felt off.

Lu Hongyan slowed her steps.

"That ship...."

A small silver flying boat approached the three vessels from the front.

It was a guide boat from Qingxiao Palace.

As the crystal pillars atop the peaks lit up one after another, a path of light opened in the air. The three flying boats slowed and followed the path toward the northern part of the immortal city.

Mingyun narrowed his eyes.

At that moment, a familiar voice came from behind them.

"Fellow Daoists of Baoguang Temple."

It was Lin Jinghua of Qingxiao Palace.

He seemed to have noticed Lee Hyun's group while walking with two fellow disciples.

Yuanjing pressed his palms together.

"Fellow Daoist Lin. Where did those flying boats come from?"

Lin Jinghua looked up at the sky.

"They are envoys from the Nanming Twelve-Sect Alliance."

'Hm?'

Lu Hongyan asked,

"Did Nanming send people to the Dao symposium too?"

"They said they had matters to discuss with the Seniors from Heng Kingdom."

"Heng Kingdom?"

Lin Jinghua nodded.

"It is because of Qingyan Island."

It was a name Lee Hyun had never heard before.

When he asked, Lin Jinghua pointed toward the southeast of the immortal city.

"It is an island in the sea east of Kun Kingdom. It is also not difficult to send ships there from southern Heng Kingdom. In the past, passing ships only stopped there briefly, but recently, a spirit-stone mine was apparently discovered."

"A spirit-stone mine...."

"They say it mostly produces mid-grade spirit stones. The deposit is extensive, and I heard they have even found a small amount of high-grade spirit stones deeper down."

Mingyun exhaled.

"No wonder both sides covet it."

"Haiming Sect of Heng Kingdom claims they were the first to find the vein and had already begun digging tunnels, while the sects on the Nanming side that govern Kun Kingdom apparently insist the island originally belonged to their territory."

Lin Jinghua briefly glanced around before continuing.

"I heard both sides have sent people there and are locked in a tense standoff. Since so many Seniors have gathered here in Jing Kingdom, they probably intend to settle the matter here. I was told the visit itself had been coordinated several days in advance."

Lu Hongyan looked up at the sky again.

"Then why did they bring so many disciples?"

As the flying boats drew closer, the people on deck became easier to see.

There was a man carrying a coffin on his back.

Beside a young man with several spirit-insect pouches around his waist stood a female cultivator holding a long sword case. Farther back, two cultivators were moving a cage covered in black cloth.

Their clothing varied, but the realms of those who stood out were mostly similar.

Late Foundation Establishment.

There were easily more than a hundred of them.

They too were looking down, taking in the crowded streets, the flags announcing the Dao symposium, and the lights of techniques rising from the sparring arenas.

Then the upper-deck door of the largest flying boat opened.

A silver-haired old woman stepped out first.

Behind her came a middle-aged cultivator in a black crown and an extremely gaunt old man, while the last to appear was a man in a long white robe.

Lin Jinghua lowered his voice.

"The old woman in front seems to be from Heishui Sect. I do not know the others."

The old woman stood before the railing and turned her head toward the training ground.

In that instant, it felt as though someone had laid a palm on the crown of Lee Hyun's head and was slowly pressing down.

The voices in the street abruptly ceased.

Clatter.

A Qi Refining clerk at a roadside stall dropped a tray. The sound rang out unusually loudly, but no one turned to look. None of them could.

Lu Hongyan's hand unconsciously gripped the spear strapped across her back. Mingyun pressed his lips together and held his breath, while one of the Qingxiao Palace disciples behind Lin Jinghua turned deathly pale.

'Nascent Soul...!'

Lee Hyun immediately withdrew his divine sense.

A massive divine sense swept over the cultivators in the street one after another. It passed Yuanjing, then Lu Hongyan...

And reached Lee Hyun.

A chill ran down his spine.

He had spent more than two thousand years refining his Aura-Concealing Art and Spirit-Concealing Art. But he had never tested whether they would work before the eyes of a Nascent Soul cultivator.

Fortunately, the divine sense passed over him in an instant. It lingered no longer than it had on his fellow disciples.

'...She doesn't seem particularly interested in me.'

Only then did the other three standing at the railing enter his awareness. From each of them flowed an aura whose depth he could not fathom.

Four Nascent Soul cultivators!

At that moment, a clear bell rang once from a peak in the north of the immortal city.

Dooong―

The pressure that had settled over the street split apart.

A calm voice came from the air.

"Our guests have traveled a long way, yet you seem to be taking an excessive interest in the children."

A smile appeared at the corners of the old woman's mouth.

"Hoho. I simply could not help myself when I saw so many promising talents."

The immense divine sense withdrew.

Only then did the people begin breathing again.

Lu Hongyan released her spear and rubbed her palm against the hem of her robe.

...

The flying boats descended onto a high mooring platform in the north.

Cultivators from Taiyue Sect and Qingxiao Palace were already waiting there.

Even from the road Lee Hyun's group was walking along, they could see the long stone steps leading to the mooring platform and the pavilion above.

When the Nascent Soul cultivators from Nanming disembarked, those waiting before the pavilion went forward to greet them.

At the very front stood the white-haired elder from Taiyue Sect who had delivered the opening address, and beside him was a female cultivator in a pale blue enchanted robe.

It was Chen Xiaoying.

Unlike when she had been taking questions before the pill furnace, there was no trace of a smile on her lips.

While the two sides exchanged formal greetings, Nanming's disciples also began disembarking from the flying boats.

The procession stretched on and on.

The Nascent Soul cultivators went somewhere else, while Nanming's disciples were guided toward another corridor.

Morning of the thirteenth day of the symposium.

The cultivators who had advanced to the main tournament gathered in front of the martial platform.

Lee Hyun lined up with his fellow disciples from Baoguang Temple.

The stewards were checking the roster and handing out main-tournament jade tokens and spirit stones. However, there was no drawing box for determining the matchups.

Instead, several seats had been arranged atop the martial platform.

A short while later, the elderly Nascent Soul cultivator from Taiyue Sect appeared.

Cultivators from Qingxiao Palace and Haiming Sect came up behind him, while across from them sat the Nascent Soul cultivators from Nanming whom they had seen yesterday.

The front courtyard fell silent.

The elderly Taiyue Sect cultivator began to speak.

"Before we determine the main-tournament matchups, there is something I must tell you."

Lee Hyun put away his jade token.

"Negotiations concerning Qingyan Island were concluded during the night. Both sides have agreed to entrust one side with the rights to administer the island and operate the mine for the next hundred years."

The old cultivator's gaze swept over the disciples.

"Which side receives those rights will be decided by a contest between the disciples of both sides."

Heads rose here and there.

"Yunzhou and Nanming will each send sixty-four disciples to fight one-on-one matches. The side with more victories will gain the rights. If the results are tied thirty-two to thirty-two, each side will send one additional representative for a final match."

The silver-haired old woman from Nanming leisurely lifted her teacup.

The elderly Taiyue Sect cultivator continued.

"Yunzhou intends to choose its participants from among the main-tournament entrants gathered here."

The atmosphere in the courtyard changed.

Hands that had been checking jade tokens a moment earlier went still.

Lee Hyun looked toward where the Nascent Soul cultivators were seated.

The Haiming Sect cultivator was studying the disciples with a rigid expression, while the Nascent Soul cultivators from Nanming showed little reaction.

The old cultivator said,

"The standoff between both sides on Qingyan Island has already consumed no small amount of spirit stones and manpower. But old fellows like us cannot personally make a move and risk destroying the island and mine along with each other, can we?"

He smiled faintly.

"Since we are asking this of you, we have prepared suitable compensation. Participation will be rewarded with three hundred mid-grade spirit stones. If you win, you may either receive another three hundred or choose one item from a separate set of rewards."

The eyes of several disciples changed.

Three hundred mid-grade spirit stones was enough to buy a fine magic tool and still have plenty left over.

Victory would double that amount.

"The main tournament of the existing sparring matches will continue after these contests conclude. The Dao symposium's rewards will also remain unchanged, so there is no need to worry about that."

The old cultivator paused briefly, then added,

"However, these matches will differ from the sparring matches held thus far. Neither side will hold the other responsible for any casualties that occur during the contest."

The courtyard fell silent.

Someone slowly lowered the jade token they had been holding.

"...A life-and-death duel?"

A cultivator in the front row asked.

"You may admit defeat and withdraw. But you will have to make that judgment yourself. There will be no referee inside to intervene and stop an attack."

Lu Hongyan's eyes narrowed.

Lee Hyun also waited for the old cultivator's next words.

"A screening restriction will be deployed over the martial platform. Once a match begins, those outside will be unable to see inside or inspect it with divine sense."

Murmurs arose.

This time, the old woman from Nanming spoke.

"When disciples are fighting for their lives, would they hold back their sect's secret teachings? We cannot have those arts displayed openly for all to see."

Her gaze turned across the platform.

"Surely Yunzhou thinks the same?"

The elderly Taiyue Sect cultivator nodded calmly.

"The same conditions will apply to both sides. The restriction will also be jointly inspected and guarded by both sides."

He took a small jade token from his sleeve.

"If you break this, it will be treated as an admission of defeat and the screening restriction will be released. Any attack after that point will be treated as harming someone after the sparring match has ended."

The jade token slowly rotated above his palm.

Lee Hyun felt it was little more than a token gesture meant to reassure the Foundation Establishment cultivators.

Even battles between Foundation Establishment cultivators were exceedingly fast and brutal.

There was almost no chance to hold out long enough to break the jade token and wait for the restriction to release.

The old cultivator looked over the disciples.

"We have already requested the cooperation of the Elders of each sect. The roster will be finalized before sunset today, and the matches will begin tomorrow."

His gaze paused briefly.

"I have heard that Yunzhou's finest young talents are gathered here. Surely finding sixty-four among you will not be difficult."

...

After leaving the martial platform, Baoguang Temple's disciples gathered around Huijing, the Elder leading them.

The old monk lowered the jade slip in his hand.

"They have asked our temple to provide three participants."

Lu Hongyan asked,

"Was this all decided overnight?"

"Yes. It seems they originally intended to discuss the island's boundaries and mining terms, but the Nanming side proposed settling the matter through contests between the disciples."

Yuanjing looked toward where Nanming's disciples had gathered.

"They may have planned this from the start."

Huijing did not deny it.

"Haiming Sect accepted after the terms were adjusted. They also separately settled terms for supplying spirit stones to the sects that help with this matter."

The old monk looked at the disciples.
