"Anyone willing to participate should tell me. But do not decide based on the reward alone. They too will have brought disciples selected from their respective sects."

A brief silence followed.

'What a troublesome development.'

A Nascent Soul cultivator had personally encouraged participation, and Baoguang Temple had been allotted spots as well.

Even so, Lee Hyun had no reason to volunteer first. He was an alchemist of the Lotus Court, while the Demon-Subduing Court and Vajra Court had disciples far more interested in sparring.

Lu Hongyan spoke.

"Where can we see the rewards?"

Huijing pointed toward the pavilion beside them.

"They have been prepared inside. Some items require you to check how they are cultivated or the conditions for using them, so if anything catches your eye, ask the steward about it."

Lu Hongyan moved first.

Lee Hyun followed his fellow disciples into the pavilion.

...

Inside the pavilion, jade caskets, bottles, and various magic tools were arranged in rows.

Several potted spirit plants sat inside glass cases protected by restrictions.

Wooden boards listing the items hung on the walls, and beneath them stewards handed out jade slips containing detailed explanations.

Most of the rewards had been supplied by Haiming Sect, so many were spirit materials from the sea. There were also refined materials made from demon-beast carapaces and pearls, as well as ores suitable for water-element magic tools.

Lu Hongyan stopped before the section listing materials that could be used to improve her spear and vajra.

Yuanjing carefully examined a small jade bottle.

Lee Hyun read down the list of items one by one until his gaze stopped on the section for spirit plants.

「Heaven-Origin Divine Tree. One sapling.」

'Heaven-Origin Divine Tree?'

A brief description was written beneath it.

「A rare spirit tree whose fruit nurtures Heaven-Origin Qi. Cultivation records and observation records of mature trees included.」

Lee Hyun requested a jade slip from the steward beside him.

When he sent in his divine sense, images of the spirit tree's overall form, leaves, and roots appeared one after another.

The leaves were small and thick, and round fruits hung from the tips of the branches. Shallow grooves ringed the surfaces of the fruits.

Lee Hyun's eyes widened as he read the explanation that followed.

The Heaven-Origin Divine Tree grew by absorbing heaven-and-earth spiritual qi, but only after an extremely long time would it bear small fruits at the tips of its branches.

While hanging from the branches, the fruits nurtured a unique energy within themselves.

It was called Heaven-Origin Qi.

According to the records, dust did not accumulate around fruits imbued with Heaven-Origin Qi.

If water was poured toward them, it split apart before touching the fruit, and if a small stone was brought close, it was pushed away as though blocked by something invisible.

'This is... repulsive force, isn't it? Could I use this to create Heaven-Origin Force, the opposite of Earth-Origin Force?'

Chapter 85

Lee Hyun returned to the beginning of the jade slip.

There was no cultivation formula for converting Heaven-Origin Qi into Heaven-Origin Force.

It contained only records examining the energy within the fruit, the spirit tree's growth process, and the soil conditions and concentration of spiritual qi required for cultivation.

'Hmm... Still, if I can at least obtain the energy itself, I might be able to get a feel for it.'

The situation was different from when he had created Earth-Origin Force.

Back then, while looking through formation texts, he had discovered that the method used to generate Earth-Origin Force in a Tier 2 Grand Flight-Suppressing Formation was an application of the Foundation Establishment Section of the Primordial One-Qi Art. Afterward, he had applied the mnemonic formula for Materialization, which he found in materials on the Tier 1 Flight-Suppressing Formation, to his Primordial True Qi.

Its principle was to first use Return to Unity to revert postcelestial Five-Element spiritual qi to the state of primordial unity, then imitate the transformation described by the Five Precelestial Stages in which form acquired substance and condensed. For Lee Hyun, who already used Primordial True Qi, even the Return to Unity process was unnecessary.

In other words, what he had found back then was not some form of energy like Earth-Origin Qi, but the method for generating Earth-Origin Force itself.

What he had found this time, however, was not a method for refining heaven-and-earth spiritual qi into Heaven-Origin Force, but merely clues about Heaven-Origin Qi. There was still a missing link before he could make that power his own.

If he could only use Heaven-Origin Force by consuming Heaven-Origin Qi obtained from the fruit, it would be of limited use. He could hardly expect the tree to produce an abundance of fruit.

For Lee Hyun to use Heaven-Origin Force in actual combat, he needed a mnemonic formula that could transform Primordial True Qi into Heaven-Origin Force. Only then could he turn his vast spiritual power directly into Heaven-Origin Force.

Even with Earth-Origin Force, a cultivator without as much spiritual power as Lee Hyun would find it difficult to produce an attractive force strong enough to pull in another cultivator of the same realm.

'Could the Nascent Soul Section or Spirit Transformation Section of the Primordial One-Qi Art contain a related mnemonic formula?'

But he had no way of knowing whether any of them could actually produce Heaven-Origin Force.

He could understand how Earth-Origin Force arose through Return to Unity and Materialization based on the theory of the Five Precelestial Stages. It was analogous to mass generating gravity.

But what, exactly, was repulsive force?

'Wait. It said the fruit of the Heaven-Origin Divine Tree already repels matter. Then doesn't that mean the Heaven-Origin Qi inside the fruit is actually producing repulsive force? If I examine its structure closely enough, I might find a clue to creating Heaven-Origin Force. Either way, I should get this divine tree.'

If he could gain the power to repel in addition to the power to attract, there would be plenty of ways to use them.

Slightly excited by the thought that he might eventually wield Heaven-and-Earth-Origin Force beyond mere Earth-Origin Force, Lee Hyun lowered the jade slip.

“Where did you obtain this tree?”

The steward turned his head toward the glass case.

“It was brought in by a merchant group that trades with the Qianyuan Empire. Our sect purchased it along with other spirit materials.”

The Qianyuan Empire was the Tier 5 cultivation nation Yin Cailing had told him about not long ago.

'Hm? “Qianyuan” in the empire’s name and “Heaven-Origin” in the divine tree’s name are both written 乾元. Are they related somehow?'

The jade slip did not explain the origin of the name.

Lee Hyun examined the records again.

It said that when grown in a suitable environment, the tree would bear its first fruit at around a medicine age of one thousand years. Even after the fruit appeared, however, it would take some additional time for enough Heaven-Origin Qi to accumulate within it.

Fortunately, once it began bearing fruit, the tree's medicine age would continue to affect the fruit's grade, just as with the Stone Honey Peach.

When Lee Hyun removed the jade slip from his forehead, the steward added,

“To be frank... if it were me, I would choose something else. It takes an extremely long time... and I have yet to hear of anyone in Yunzhou obtaining fruit from this divine tree. Even the specimens that came into our sect haven't been cultivated long enough to bear fruit. More importantly, even if one obtains Heaven-Origin Qi, very little is known about what it can actually be used for. At least, not in Yunzhou.”

Lee Hyun nodded, but his eyes remained fixed on the glass case.

The sapling was not even two chi (about 66 cm) tall.

Lee Hyun read through the cultivation conditions once more.

A lack of heaven-and-earth spiritual qi would not harm the tree, but it would slow its growth.

'Unlike the Ringless Divine Tree, it probably won't simply accumulate age at the full rate. Will it grow at one-third the normal rate, like other spirit plants? If I have to wait three thousand years instead of one thousand...'

Even so, it did not matter all that much if the tree took a long time to bear fruit.

'If I really need to, I can install a Qi-Gathering Formation in Tunnel No. 3. As long as I raise the spiritual qi concentration around the Heaven-Origin Divine Tree, I can afford the spirit stones it would consume. With some research, I should even be able to set up a Tier 2 Qi-Gathering Formation myself...'

Lee Hyun asked again,

“Is there no way to purchase this with spirit stones right now?”

“It has been offered as a reward for these matches, so it is not for sale here.”

“I see.”

...

Lu Hongyan, who had been waiting outside the hall, spoke when she saw Lee Hyun.

“There was a material in there that would be useful for refining my spear. It's normally quite difficult to obtain.”

“Senior Sister, are you planning to participate?”

“No.”

Lu Hongyan's hand touched the small booklet at her waist.

“I told you about the problem with my vow before, didn't I? How it makes me want to take part in fights too often. But if I fight Foundation Establishment cultivators selected by the Nanming Twelve-Sect Alliance, there's a real chance I could die. If my opponent pulls out a talisman treasure or something... This is exactly the kind of time when I shouldn't participate.”

Lee Hyun nodded.

“That is wise.”

“Then why were you in there for so long, Junior Brother?”

After a brief silence, Lee Hyun answered.

“I intend to participate.”

Lu Hongyan's expression changed.

“...Even after everything I just said?”

“Yes. There's something I truly want to obtain.”

“I know you're strong. But this is a life-and-death duel. If you die, how am I supposed to face Shulin?”

“I'll make sure that doesn't happen.”

...

Huijing was preparing to return to the detached residence.

When Lee Hyun told him that he intended to participate, the old monk lowered the jade slip in his hand.

“You intend to enter?”

“Yes.”

“Just because they asked our temple to provide three participants doesn't mean I intend to fill every place by force.”

“This is my own decision.”

“Then I'll put your name on the list.”

...

Baoguang Temple's three participants were decided.

Yuanshi of the Vajra Court.

Liu Jingdao of the Demon-Subduing Court.

Li Dongsi of the Lotus Court.

Yuanshi was a monk with a broad forehead and thick eyebrows. Liu Jingdao was a middle-aged cultivator with a scar beside one eye and a long sword sheath hanging from his waist.

Huijing took the three of them back to the reward hall.

When Lee Hyun chose the Heaven-Origin Divine Tree, the steward wrote his name on a wooden token. Fortunately, no one else had selected it.

“If you win, you will receive the sapling together with its cultivation records.”

“Will I still receive it even if Yunzhou loses the overall contest?”

“Of course. Rewards for individual victories are separate.”

...

That evening.

The rosters for both sides were finalized.

Under the joint supervision of Nascent Soul cultivators from Taiyue Sect and Nanming, the names floating above two formation plates were paired off one by one.

Lee Hyun's match was seventeenth.

His opponent was Yan Bai of the Yin Bird Sect.

Beside his name, his realm was listed as Foundation Establishment Stage 9.

'The Yin Bird Sect....'

It was the sect to which the Haigu Island branch belonged.

After the matchups were confirmed, they were given instructions regarding the entry procedure.

A Qingxiao Palace steward said,

“Leave inheritance jade slips and any items unnecessary for combat with your respective sects. You may not touch the possessions of anyone who surrenders and withdraws. Corpses will be retrieved by their original sects. Attacking after a match has ended is strictly forbidden.”

...

After returning to the detached residence, Lee Hyun sorted through his belongings.

The possibility of him losing was almost nonexistent anyway, so the storage pouch he left with Huijing contained only things that posed no risk of exposing his identity, such as a few jade slips from Baoguang Temple.

This way, even if Martial Uncle Huijing secretly opened the storage pouch, he would have no reason to suspect Li Dongsi's identity.

The fourteenth day of the Dao symposium.

People had gathered at the training ground from early morning.

The atmosphere was different from the sparring matches held up until the previous day.

People were still discussing the matchups and predicting winners, but the participants and those close to them all wore solemn expressions.

Restrictions had been set up around the broad martial platform at the center, while Golden Core cultivators from Yunzhou and Nanming stood facing one another outside it.

Lee Hyun sat in the stands with his fellow disciples.

The Nascent Soul cultivators were seated on a raised platform to the north.

A short while later, the first participants stepped onto the stone platform.

'Han Jingxiu of Qingxiao Palace?'

He had fought Lee Hyun in the preliminaries, placed second in their group, and advanced to the main tournament. Apparently, he had also entered this special contest.

Opposite him stood a Nanming cultivator in a brown robe. Several layers of cords were tied around the ends of his sleeves, and two spirit-insect pouches hung from his waist.

A moment later, the formation inscriptions lit up.

Hummm–

A black curtain rose around the stone platform, quickly obscuring the interior completely.

Beside him, Senior Brother Yuanjing's eyes briefly glowed blue before he shook his head.

“I truly can't see anything.”

...

Only the faint movements of those waiting remained in the stands.

Not even sound escaped from within the curtain.

The people who had been appraising the participants' magic tools moments earlier gradually fell silent.

Before long, the curtain lightened and opened.

Han Jingxiu stood alone.

The ring in his left hand was half-shattered, and his right sleeve had been torn away below the shoulder. Black spots were spreading across his exposed arm.

The Nanming cultivator lay collapsed at the edge of the stone platform, surrounded by the corpses of tiny insects.

“Qingxiao Palace, Han Jingxiu wins.”

...

The matches continued.

When the restriction was lifted once more, the first thing revealed was a foot clad in a black boot.

It belonged to a Nanming cultivator.

Dark red blood dripped one drop at a time from the short axe in his right hand.

Opposite him, a Yunzhou cultivator lay collapsed.

He was the young man whose unusually ornate golden enchanted robe had drawn attention when he entered. Now the chest of that robe had been torn open by a deep gash.

Two Golden Core cultivators below the stone platform climbed up at the same time.

One examined the fallen young man while the other briefly declared the victor.

A section of the stands erupted into commotion. His fellow disciples, dressed in similar golden enchanted robes, murmured among themselves in disbelief.

In the third match, both participants walked off the platform.

One had both ends of his sleeves burned away, while the other had a long wound across his forehead. The injured cultivator handed a shattered jade token to the supervising steward and admitted defeat.

When the curtain lifted after the fourth match, the floor was littered with shattered magic tools.

Even the victorious Yunzhou cultivator suddenly doubled over and vomited blood.

The fighting continued. Each time a match ended, the supervising cultivators cleaned the platform and inspected the formation inscriptions.

Even the places where corpses had lain were quickly wiped clean.

The spectators, who had initially watched as though enjoying a spectacle, gradually grew solemn or grim.

Every participant was an exceptional talent recognized even within a great sect.

Yet each time the curtain darkened and brightened again, cultivators of such caliber emerged maimed. It inevitably left the impression that even Foundation Establishment cultivators were little more than expendable pawns to the great sects.

Each time the spectators witnessed another miserable outcome, they were reminded that such a fate could just as easily befall them.

The spectacle unfolding on the martial platform was both merciless and riveting.

The matches were also decided quickly enough that even normally dispassionate cultivators could not tear their eyes away.

After roughly eight matches, the wooden scoreboard at the center read Yunzhou 3, Nanming 5.

...

The matches that followed also produced some unexpected results.

A Yunzhou cultivator whom Lu Hongyan had singled out as strong was defeated.

He was the man who had stood with his eyes closed, leaning against the railing of a jade-colored flying boat on the day they entered the immortal city.

Lee Hyun also remembered his deep, steady aura.

When the curtain lifted, the man lay at the edge of the stone platform. Broken magic tools were scattered around him, and one leg was bent at an unnatural angle.

The victorious Nanming cultivator's hand was also trembling violently. The last charred fragment of a talisman fell from his fingertips.

A mark remained on the stone floor as though some enormous bladed weapon had smashed down upon it.

“A talisman treasure...”

...

By the end of the sixteenth match, Yunzhou had won six times and Nanming ten.

Senior Brother Yuanshi of Baoguang Temple's Vajra Court was staring up at the wooden board displaying the names of the next participants. Senior Brother Liu Jingdao of the Demon-Subduing Court had yet to remove his hand from the sword resting across his knees.

Martial Uncle Huijing looked at Lee Hyun.

“It's your turn.”

As Lee Hyun rose, Lu Hongyan lightly caught his sleeve, then let go.

“You have to come back alive.”

“Yes.”

Lee Hyun descended the stone steps.

Below the stone platform, the supervising steward checked his jade token.

“Li Dongsi of Baoguang Temple.”

“Correct.”

On the opposite side, another steward was checking the identity of the Nanming cultivator.

Lee Hyun looked at him.

It was the man who had stood on the deck when Nanming's flying boats arrived, a coffin strapped to his back.

He was tall, with dark circles beneath his eyes, but the flow of his qi and blood was deep and stable.

The man studied Lee Hyun in return.

His gaze swept over the storage pouch at Lee Hyun's waist, then over his wrist and down to his feet, before a sneer appeared at the corner of his mouth.

Soon, the two stepped onto the stone platform.

“Yan Bai.”

“Li Dongsi.”

“......”

Yan Bai shifted his shoulder, releasing the coffin from his back and letting it drop onto the stone platform.

Thud.

The coffin was large enough to hold a person.

Its surface was engraved with a pattern resembling a bird feeding on a corpse, and black nails had been driven into all four corners of the lid.

Lee Hyun examined the markings on the coffin.

Corpse qi was leaking all the way through to the outside, and from within came the faint sound of something scratching.

Yan Bai placed a finger on the coffin.

A voice came from outside the stone platform.

“Ready.”

Hummm–

Black curtains rose on every side.

The stands vanished from sight. The place where Lu Hongyan sat, along with the Nascent Soul cultivators, soon disappeared as well.

Once the restriction closed, all sound from outside was cut off.

A beat later, one of the formation inscriptions on the floor turned red, and Yan Bai moved first.

Boom!

The coffin lid flew upward, and a hideous figure burst out from beneath it.

Its desiccated face had no lips. Both arms hung nearly to its knees, and several layers of cloth were wrapped around its chest and abdomen.

As it planted a foot, its toes gouged marks into the surface of the stone platform.

Whoosh!

A long arm tore through the air.

One of the Six-Leaf Shield's blue-green shield plates rose in front of Lee Hyun.

Screech!

Its nails scraped across the shield plate, sending a long spray of sparks through the air.

The corpse puppet immediately thrust out its other arm.

Lee Hyun shifted sideways and raised his palm.

A golden palm imprint flew toward the corpse puppet's chest.

Demon-Subduing Seal.

Just before the palm imprint struck, a shrill cry burst from the corpse puppet's mouth, and red smoke billowed from between the layers of cloth wrapped around its chest.

The golden palm imprint plunged into the smoke, but rather than dispersing, the smoke wrapped itself around the palm imprint instead.

Yan Bai curled his fingers, and the golden light trapped within the smoke split into several tiny points.

'Hm?'

Boom!

The red smoke exploded.

Three shield plates were driven backward, and the corpse puppet's claws shot out from the smoke toward Lee Hyun's throat.

Almost simultaneously, a flying blade shot from Yan Bai's sleeve.

Lee Hyun's feet slid across the ground.

A fourth shield plate knocked away the flying blade, while the corpse puppet's claws swept past Lee Hyun's cheek as he twisted aside.

'A technique that can swallow the Demon-Subduing Seal... Interesting.'

It seemed to be something prepared in advance specifically to counter Baoguang Temple's techniques.

The corpse puppet spread both arms and charged again.

The flying blade used the recoil from striking the shield plate to dart backward before flying low toward Lee Hyun's legs.

Meanwhile, a small bone token floated up from Yan Bai's hand.

Even while attacking, his movements as he positioned a defensive magic tool in front of himself were smooth and practiced.

At that moment, Lee Hyun suddenly withdrew his Buddha-Light True Qi.

'Enough time has passed. No one outside should find it strange if I finish this now.'

Click, click.

The six blue-green shield plates interlocked at different heights.

The corpse puppet's hand struck the shield again.

Boom!

The six shield plates distributed the impact between them. Rather than being pushed back, they knocked the corpse puppet's arm outward instead.

Startled, Yan Bai changed his hand seal, and dense corpse qi surged from the corpse puppet's body.

With a sharp crack from its joints, the arm that had been knocked away bent back at an unnatural angle.

Just as Yan Bai reached into his storage pouch for something, the sword in Lee Hyun's hand moved like lightning.

Flash!

Sword light engulfed the corpse puppet's neck and shoulder. Its head fell away, and its body crashed to the floor.

Yan Bai recoiled in shock and immediately retreated.

'Dammit, there's something wrong with this bastard!'

The instant he reached out to shatter his jade token, a razor-sharp wave of divine sense surged toward him.

Yan Bai hurriedly raised a barrier with his own divine sense. But the absurdly powerful divine sense smashed straight through it.

His mind went completely blank.

When his briefly severed consciousness returned, Lee Hyun was already standing before him.

'Wh...en?'

Yan Bai realized that foreign true qi was blocking his meridians at multiple points. Lee Hyun had even sealed his acupoints while he was unconscious, leaving him unable to move so much as a finger.

Even his jade token for surrender was now in his opponent's hand.

The face of the bastard called Li Dongsi showed none of the tension one would expect from someone who had supposedly just fought a desperate battle.

“It would be a little troublesome if it looked as though I'd cut you in two with a single sword strike... I hope you'll understand.”

Lee Hyun took an old Black Scale Inner Armor from his storage pouch, lifted one of the immobilized corpse puppet's hands, and ruthlessly drove its claws into the armor.

Thunk, thunk.

Ragged holes appeared in the inner armor.

Next, he threw one plate of the Threefold Shield onto the floor, picked up the flying blade Yan Bai had used, and slashed a long split across its surface.

He put away the Six-Leaf Shield and left the split shield plate somewhere clearly visible.

Then, using the sharp tips of the corpse puppet's claws, he roughly tore the sleeve and shoulder of his outer robe.

When he put the punctured inner armor on beneath the robe, its damaged scales showed through the torn fabric.

Watching the entire process, Yan Bai felt a chill run down his spine.

'Monster.......'

As the truth dawned on him, Yan Bai's eyes became bloodshot and filled with terror.

The man before him was not merely another Foundation Establishment cultivator like himself. He was a terrifying existence on an entirely different level.

From the very beginning, all this man had wanted was to fabricate the traces of a desperate battle to deceive those outside. Yan Bai had never posed the slightest threat to him!

'Why would someone like this...... I have to tell the others......!'

With all his strength, he tried to send his spiritual power toward the jade token in his opponent's hand, but his blocked meridians refused to respond at all.

“I can't leave a witness alive. Farewell.”

At those words, Yan Bai was seized by overwhelming terror. Yet before he even realized what had happened, a huge gash had already opened from his side to his chest.

Shhk!

Lee Hyun withdrew the Azure Steel Sword.

Yan Bai's knees buckled, and he collapsed.

Thud.

Lee Hyun carefully examined his opponent and confirmed that even his primordial spirit had been extinguished.

He then shattered Yan Bai's jade token in his hand, and the curtains surrounding them began to dissolve.

The sounds from outside gradually returned.

Someone let out a low exclamation.

Two Golden Core cultivators climbed onto the stone platform and examined Yan Bai's corpse and Lee Hyun.

“Baoguang Temple, Li Dongsi wins.”

“Well done!”

His fellow disciples from Baoguang Temple were waving at him.

...

Lu Hongyan quickly looked Lee Hyun over from his face to his hands and clothes.

“Are you hurt anywhere?”

“No.”

She let out a breath.

Zhang Taishan also came over and patted Lee Hyun on the shoulder.

“So he was a cultivator who controlled a corpse puppet. That must have made him a difficult opponent.”

“I was fortunate.”

Martial Uncle Huijing approached.

“Your complexion looks fine. Still, corpse poison may have entered your body, so circulate your qi and check yourself carefully.”

...

While the other matches continued, Lee Hyun left the stands and headed for the reward hall.

The hall was nearly empty. Most of the cultivators had gathered at the training ground.

When Lee Hyun presented the jade token confirming his victory, the steward examined it, rose from his seat, and walked over to the glass case.

As his palm touched the restriction, the transparent wall faded, and the flowerpot within slowly floated out.

“Here is the Heaven-Origin Divine Tree you reserved. These are the cultivation records and the observation records for the mature tree as well.”

...

After putting everything into his storage pouch and leaving the hall, Lee Hyun heard a murmur of voices coming from the training ground.

By the time he returned to the stands, another curtain was lifting from the martial platform.

The score showed Yunzhou 10, Nanming 14. Several cultivators sighed.

“Those Nanming bastards are every bit as formidable as expected.”

“We chose our people based on sparring matches rather than life-and-death duels. Of course there's going to be a difference....”

...

It was Yuanshi's turn, representing Baoguang Temple's Vajra Court.

As the monk slowly rose from his seat, Zhang Taishan approached and gave his shoulders a firm squeeze.

“Senior Brother, make sure you win.”

Yuanshi nodded, pressed his palms together in salute to Huijing, and descended the stone steps.

His opponent was a cultivator from Dongming Sect.

The man was short and narrow-shouldered. Every time he walked, something beneath the back of his neck slowly writhed, causing the collar of his enchanted robe to shift slightly with the movement.

The two briefly exchanged greetings before the curtain rose.

A short while later, the curtain dissolved.

Yuanshi was kneeling in the middle of the stone platform, both hands braced against the floor.

Almost nothing remained of the front of his monk's robe, and fine black specks were densely embedded across his exposed chest and shoulders.

The golden radiance flowing over his skin was broken in several places.

Opposite him, the Dongming Sect cultivator lay collapsed.

Dark red liquid slowly spread beneath his body.

All around him lay broken, slender fragments resembling insect legs.

“Senior Brother Yuanshi!”

As Zhang Taishan moved toward the stone steps, Martial Uncle Huijing hurried down as well.

While the Golden Core cultivators confirmed the outcome, blood poured from Yuanshi's mouth.

Huijing placed a palm against his back.

Hummm–

A gentle golden radiance enveloped Yuanshi's body.

“Do not move.”

With his other hand, the old monk took out a jade bottle.

When Yuanshi barely managed to open his mouth, Huijing placed a pill inside.

As Huijing touched Yuanshi's shoulder and chest in turn, several black specks were forced out through his skin.

They were fragments as thin as needles.

As they writhed in midair, a tiny flame appeared between Huijing's fingers.

Sizzle.

The smoke dispersed.

...

Yuanshi was moved to a small hall behind the stone platform that had been prepared for treating injuries.

While Huijing examined him inside, Lee Hyun and Zhang Taishan waited outside the door.

A short while later, the old monk emerged.

“His life is not in danger. His internal injuries are fairly serious, but with proper rest, he'll recover.”

...

By the time the sun began sinking toward the west, it was Senior Brother Liu Jingdao's turn, representing the Demon-Subduing Court.

His opponent was a female cultivator carrying a long sword case in her arms.

She was the woman who had stood on the deck beside the young man wearing several spirit-insect pouches when Nanming's flying boats arrived. Apparently, she belonged to the Heishui Sect.

The woman set her sword case upright at one side of the stone platform and brought her hands together.

Liu Jingdao also drew a broad sword from the sheath at his waist.

The blade was unusually thick, like the spine of a saber, and dark blue patterns ran along it.

A long, slender sword slid out of the female cultivator's sword case.

The curtain rose.

A short while later, it vanished.

Both of them were still standing.

Liu Jingdao's right arm hung limply at his side, while his left hand held the fragments of a shattered jade token.

The female cultivator was sheathing her sword.

As the slender blade slid back into its case, the dark blue-black energy lingering in the air was drawn in along with it.

The supervising steward declared Nanming the winner.

Liu Jingdao's sword had been broken into two pieces.

...

Lu Hongyan waited below the stone steps.

“Senior Brother.”

“I lost.”

Lu Hongyan looked at his right arm.

“Are you badly hurt?”

“I think some of my meridians were damaged.”

Liu Jingdao swallowed a pill and steadied his breathing for a moment before looking back toward the martial platform.

The Heishui Sect woman had already returned to her fellow disciples.

“She was surprisingly restrained. To think she spared my life...”

“Was she that strong?”

At Lu Hongyan's question, Liu Jingdao nodded.

“Her sword intent was far stronger than I could have imagined. Frankly, I'm shaken... I had no idea how vast the world truly was.”

...

The score continued to change.

By the end of the fortieth match, Yunzhou had 18 points and Nanming 22...

Then the female cultivator Lee Hyun had seen playing with a droplet of water aboard a jade-colored flying boat when he first came to Huiyun Immortal City also appeared.

She belonged to Qingheng Sect of the Jin Kingdom, one of the Nine Kingdoms of Yunzhou.

The Nanming cultivator opposite her had a thick iron ring floating in the air.

Soon, the curtain closed.

...

When they came back into view, the iron ring lay on the floor, severed in several places.

The Nanming cultivator was kneeling on one knee with a hand raised. The shattered jade token in his palm was losing its light.

A tiny droplet of water rolled between the Qingheng Sect woman's fingers.

Lee Hyun looked at the severed iron ring. The cut surfaces were remarkably smooth.

'Did she cut it with that droplet? Interesting.'

...

By the end of the forty-eighth match, Yunzhou had won twenty-three times and Nanming twenty-five.

As the gap narrowed, voices gradually began to rise in the stands again.

Someone spread out the list of remaining participants and pointed to one of the names.

“They still have that cultivator left.”

“Don't we still have Zheng Yubai of Qingheng Sect?”

...

Before long, the sixty-fourth match had ended.

Yunzhou, 32 points.

Nanming, 32 points.

The stands stirred.

The Nascent Soul cultivators of Yunzhou and Nanming conferred briefly. At last, a Golden Core steward stepped forward and announced that, as agreed beforehand, each side would send out one representative for a tiebreaker.

A short while later, the representatives from both sides were chosen. After separately confirming the willingness of both participants, the steward spoke again.

“With the consent of the sects and participants on both sides, this final match will be conducted with the battle inside visible to everyone!”

The stands erupted!

Yunzhou's final representative was Zheng Yubai of Qingheng Sect in the Jin Kingdom. The young man with three sword sheaths strapped to his back, who had already won an earlier match, was rising from his seat.

Beside Lee Hyun, Lu Hongyan spoke excitedly.

“We'll finally get to see it! We'll see how a heaven's prodigy counted among the strongest at this Dao symposium actually fights!”

Yuanjing nodded.

Lee Hyun asked,

“Is he really that strong?”

Chapter 86

“I heard he has a wind-and-lightning dual spiritual root.”

Lu Hongyan said as she watched Zheng Yubai descend toward the martial platform.

“Wind and lightning...? He has a dual spiritual root, yet both of its attributes are mutated spiritual roots?”

“Yeah. It’s an incredibly rare aptitude. Even rarer than a single spiritual root. On top of that, he’s a Foundation Establishment Great Perfection cultivator who has brought the Qingheng Sect’s sword art to Major Attainment. I hear he has almost no equal within the same realm.”

Lee Hyun looked at Zheng Yubai’s back.

The three scabbards differed slightly in length and width. The one on the right was long and slender, while the one on the left was shorter and thicker. The scabbard in the middle was made of faded wood.

Mingyun spoke.

“Does having two mutated spiritual-root attributes make cultivation faster?”

Martial Uncle Huijing shook his head.

“No. In terms of cultivation speed alone, he is no different from any other cultivator with a dual spiritual root. And no matter how rare one’s aptitude may be, without a suitable inheritance, one might even end up worse off than an ordinary dual-spiritual-root cultivator.”

“Then the Qingheng Sect must have an inheritance suited to him.”

“Most likely. But as far as I know, that young man isn’t famous solely because of his spiritual roots.”

The old monk’s gaze lingered briefly on the weathered scabbard in the middle.

At that moment, someone on Nanming’s side also rose to his feet.

It was the young man who had been sitting beside the female cultivator holding the long sword case in the stands.

He wore a black enchanted robe bearing the emblem of the Heishui Sect and had no particularly distinctive features apart from his tied-up hair. A single long sword hung at his waist.

As he descended toward the martial platform, his name could be heard here and there.

“Situ Tian.”

“His opponent in the last match didn’t make it out alive, did he?”

“When the barrier came down, the defensive magic tool had melted. I wonder what kind of technique he used....”

At the foot of the stone steps, Situ Tian presented his jade token to the steward.

A short while later, the two men stepped onto the stone platform.

“Qingheng Sect, Zheng Yubai.”

“Heishui Sect, Situ Tian.”

They exchanged brief introductions.

Zheng Yubai raised a hand, and a blue sword slid free from the scabbard on his right.

Yuanjing exclaimed in admiration.

“That’s the Flying Wind Sword, ranked twenty-first in the Yunzhou Artifact Appraisal. Could all three swords on his back be exceptional supreme-grade magic tools?”

A thin groove ran along the center of the blade. Within it, faint currents of air trembled as though wind were flowing through the channel.

Across from him, Situ Tian drew his sword as well.

Shing.

The blade was a deep gray. Even under the light, its edge did not gleam, and winding patterns covered its surface like traces left behind after water had dried.

Seeing it, Lu Hongyan asked,

“Senior Brother Yuanjing, is that one famous too?”

Yuanjing answered.

“I’ve heard that Nanming has the Nanming Hundred Artifacts Register, which ranks exceptional supreme-grade magic tools much like the Yunzhou Artifact Appraisal does, but I don’t know much about it... Still, judging by its appearance, that’s clearly an exceptionally fine sword.”

While Zheng Yubai and Situ Tian took their positions, the Golden Core cultivators outside the martial platform checked their respective formation plates.

Hummmm―

A barrier rose between the eight pillars.

This time, the inside was perfectly visible. Not only could they see the two cultivators atop the stone platform, but even the smallest marks left on its surface stood out clearly.

The Golden Core steward looked from one man to the other.

“Begin!”

Zheng Yubai’s sword vanished.

Swoosh!

The next instant, blue light flashed in front of Situ Tian’s throat.

Clang!

The gray sword rose at an angle and knocked it aside.

A gust exploded from the point where the two swords collided. Situ Tian’s robes streamed backward, but he did not retreat.

The Flying Wind Sword, having been knocked away, changed direction in midair.

Once, twice, and on the third attack, the dust on the ground split apart to either side before the sword had even arrived.

Situ Tian twisted his body, and a sharp sword wind brushed past his shoulder. His descending gray sword knocked away the pursuing blade once more.

Clang! Claang!

Each time the swords collided, blue light scattered in a different direction.

The dispersed sword light swept around the edge of the stone platform before gathering once more behind Situ Tian.

‘Interesting.’

Lee Hyun’s gaze swept over the ground.

Thin currents of air lingered wherever Zheng Yubai’s sword had passed. The sword following behind would ride those currents, either accelerating or abruptly changing direction.

There were similarities to the technique Han Jingxiu of Qingxiao Palace had used to create air currents with his rings.

But Zheng Yubai’s sword path was far sharper.

Sword wind remained even where the blade had already passed. At times, it was difficult to distinguish from actual sword qi, making it hard for Situ Tian to judge what needed to be blocked and what could safely be ignored.

Then it happened.

As the space around Situ Tian gradually filled with blue light, blue-black energy spread across his gray sword.

Ssssss.

In the clash that followed, astonishingly, there was no sound of metal!

It sounded like a red-hot lump of iron being plunged into mud, dull and strangely wet.

When the sword light surrounding the Flying Wind Sword’s edge touched the gray blade, it dimmed and was drawn into the blue-black energy.

Zheng Yubai’s fingers moved, and the Flying Wind Sword immediately pulled back.

But a strand of dark energy remained inside the groove along the blade. Only after the wind spun fiercely within it did the energy finally break away.

Lu Hongyan narrowed her eyes.

“Martial Uncle, what is that?”

Huijing spoke quietly.

“The Heishui Sect’s Spirit-Eroding Demonic Sword Art. I heard it was an inheritance of the Way of the Sword passed down from antiquity. It certainly lives up to its reputation.”

Meanwhile, Situ Tian stepped forward and swept his gray sword once through the air.

Blue-black light spread outward like a fan, severing the air currents Zheng Yubai had left behind in several places. Deprived of the paths of wind, his sword lost much of its ferocity.

Situ Tian did not miss the opportunity. His body seemed to stretch into a blur as he surged forward at tremendous speed, thrusting his sword toward Zheng Yubai’s chest!

Claaang!

The Flying Wind Sword hurriedly blocked it.

Zheng Yubai retreated.

One step.

Then another.

The blue-black energy gathered around the gray sword stretched out in a long trail. Every time it brushed against the Flying Wind Sword, its sword light melted away.

Situ Tian pressed his opponent harder and faster, closing the distance between them with every exchange.

He knocked Zheng Yubai’s sword away, then launched another attack before the blade could regain its momentum.

Dark traces spread beneath Situ Tian’s feet as he took control of the center of the martial platform.

‘What an unusual inheritance...’

Lee Hyun observed the movements of the two cultivators.

Zheng Yubai attempted to restore the currents of wind, but Situ Tian continuously severed them while leaving more and more of his own traces across the martial platform.

Judging by the movement of his sword qi, Situ Tian seemed adept at gradually taking control of the battlefield, almost as though he were encroaching upon it.

Then the scabbard on Zheng Yubai’s left opened.

Crackle!

White lightning leapt from the mouth of the scabbard.

A sword roughly three fingers wide shot out and met the descending gray blade head-on.

Booom―

Blue-black energy scattered in every direction, and Situ Tian’s feet slid backward.

He lowered his sword tip toward the ground, and the scattered energy began gathering again. But Zheng Yubai’s two swords moved first.

The Flying Wind Sword swept low, while the sword wreathed in lightning rose upward.

A violent gust erupted between them, and brilliant white lightning exploded within it!

Rumble!

The cultivators in the stands all leaned forward at once.

Sword light curved along the gale and wrapped around Situ Tian, while bolts of lightning struck repeatedly through the gaps.

The air inside the barrier seemed to burn in an instant, filling the arena with an acrid smell. Even the stone platform trembled in tiny vibrations as though an earthquake had struck.

The blue-black energy Situ Tian had left beneath his feet began to boil away and disappear.

Situ Tian’s sword immediately accelerated.

Sword light spread from the gray blade and layered itself before him again and again. The successive bolts of lightning crashed into that curtain of sword light, tearing at it without mercy!

“He’s suppressing the devilish qi with lightning!”

At Zhang Taishan’s exclamation, Yuanjing gave a brief shake of his head.

“No. He hasn’t broken through. Unless it is legendary lightning like Supreme Wood Divine Lightning, which has an overwhelming advantage against devilish qi, merely wielding lightning won’t be enough to defeat one of Nanming’s heaven’s prodigies so easily.”

Lee Hyun had the same thought.

Long ago, when he had gotten into a dispute with Shi Zhenheng of the Azure Cloud Sect’s External Affairs Hall, the man had unleashed lightning using a magic tool called the Wind-Thunder Umbrella, yet Lee Hyun had easily cut through it with the Profound Gate Sword.

‘That cultivator must have faced lightning arts before too.’

He was a heaven’s prodigy selected and sent here by the Heishui Sect. There was no way an inheritance that collapsed the moment it encountered lightning could have brought him this far.

In the end, a cultivator’s own ability mattered more than elemental compatibility.

The fiercer Zheng Yubai’s lightning became, the more tenaciously the blue-black devilish qi rising from Situ Tian’s gray blade clung to it and swallowed it.

Crack! Craaack!

Inside the barrier, Situ Tian’s bloodshot eyes flashed.

He raised the gray sword, and the curtain of sword light curled inward. The winding patterns along the blade lit up one after another as the blue-black energy compressed into a thin layer along its edge.

The instant Zheng Yubai’s lightning sword plunged downward, Situ Tian also burst forward with no less momentum, as though the pent-up recoil within him had suddenly exploded.

Boom!

White and blue-black light erupted simultaneously from the point of impact.

Some of the lightning scorched Situ Tian’s sleeve and sent smoke curling upward, but he did not withdraw his sword.

Instead, black stains spread across the surface of the lightning sword.

Zheng Yubai hurriedly recalled it, and the lightning coiled around the blade crackled violently, blasting the stains away.

At that moment, Situ Tian kicked off the ground.

Thud!

His blue-black afterimage stretched long behind him as he shot forward.

Swoooosh!

Rather than swinging his sword at the Flying Wind Sword stabbing toward his flank, Situ Tian angled the flat of his blade and deflected it with a glancing blow.

Booom!

The deflected sword tip tore across his waist and scattered fresh blood, but Situ Tian’s advance did not slow by even half a handspan. He turned the recoil from deflecting the sword into forward momentum and surged directly in front of Zheng Yubai!

Slash!

The gray blade swept upward, staining Zheng Yubai’s left sleeve with blood.

Zheng Yubai retreated and crossed his two swords.

Lightning erupted, and a gale shoved Situ Tian backward.

Only then did the distance between them widen.

...

Blood ran down Zheng Yubai’s left arm.

He flexed his fingers once.

The swords of wind and lightning still circled around him, but their spirit light had dimmed compared to before. Controlling wind and lightning together clearly consumed no small amount of spiritual power.

Situ Tian’s breathing had also grown slightly ragged.

The arm exposed beneath his burned sleeve bore scorch marks from the lightning, and blood continued to seep from the wound at his waist.

Yet the energy wrapped around his gray sword had not diminished. It was still impossible to tell who held the advantage.

Situ Tian raised his sword and pointed it at Zheng Yubai.

Zheng Yubai reached behind him.

At last, he grasped the final sword that everyone in the stands had been wondering about!

A faint sound came from the faded wooden scabbard.

Shhk.

Murmurs of confusion spread throughout the stands.

‘A wooden sword...?’

Old-fashioned wood grain ran along the blade, and the handle had been polished smooth, perhaps from years of being gripped during training.

Unlike the first two swords, it gave off neither a noticeable glow nor even the slightest trace of spiritual power.

Mingyun furrowed his brow.

“Is that a magic tool too?”

Even Martial Uncle Huijing did not answer.

Situ Tian also narrowed his eyes in puzzlement at the wooden sword.

But there was no reason to give Zheng Yubai time when he had no idea what sort of trick his opponent might have prepared with it.

Blue-black energy swept across the ground as Situ Tian shot forward once more.

The first two swords Zheng Yubai had drawn moved simultaneously.

The Flying Wind Sword crossed to Situ Tian’s right, while the lightning sword swept across his left.

As the wind and lightning generated by the two swords interlocked around Situ Tian, a circular ring of light appeared atop the stone platform.

Situ Tian twisted his sword.

With a sudden flash, terrifying sword light erupted outward!

The circle of wind and lightning shattered instantly and scattered in all directions. Riding that momentum, Situ Tian burst through the opening.

Zheng Yubai stood before him, gripping the wooden sword in both hands.

Its tip was angled slightly downward, and blood flowing from his injured left arm had soaked the hilt.

As Lee Hyun watched, he suddenly noticed something strange.

‘His divine sense....’

The divine sense controlling the first two swords had grown thinner.

The divine sense withdrawn from them was beginning to gather in front of the wooden sword.

Zheng Yubai raised his head.

The two other swords circled back to either side of him and turned their tips forward in unison.

Blue and white light stretched out from their points.

Situ Tian raised his gray sword, and blue-black energy extended several times the length of the blade.

A single slash from where he stood looked as though it could cleave Zheng Yubai’s upper body in two.

Then Zheng Yubai raised the wooden sword.

At that instant, Lee Hyun’s eyes widened.

Between the wind and lightning, he saw the thin, translucent outline of a sword.

What surprised him was not some extraordinary quantity of spiritual power within it.

Like when forming the Spirit-Jolting Needle, divine sense had been condensed into something thin and solid, taking the shape of a sword. Yet within it flowed another energy that could not be explained by spiritual power and divine sense alone.

It felt strangely familiar....

‘Vow power?’

Lee Hyun unconsciously held his breath.

The tip of the wooden sword pointed toward Situ Tian.

Crack!

A hole opened directly through the center of the long stream of blue-black sword qi.

The cultivators in the stands felt an oppressive force descend, as though the entire martial platform had frozen solid.

Situ Tian’s eyes widened. The instant he pulled his sword back in front of himself, an ear-piercing crack rang out.

Astonishingly, Zheng Yubai’s wooden sword had done nothing more than remain pointed into the air!

All three swords were still in their original positions, yet Situ Tian’s gray blade bent violently in midair.

Situ Tian’s body-protecting spirit light swelled, and dark light burst from between his brows to protect his primordial spirit, but his right shoulder was jerked backward.

Splurt!

Blood sprayed in a long arc.

Situ Tian staggered back.

He nearly lost his grip on the gray sword, but barely managed to hold onto the hilt.

At the same time, Zheng Yubai dropped to one knee.

Crack.

A faint sound came from the wooden sword in his hand.

A fracture was spreading from the tip toward the hilt.

The stands fell silent.

Situ Tian forced himself upright, but the hand holding his gray sword trembled uncontrollably.

The only visible wound left by the strike was on his shoulder, but his sea of consciousness and meridians appeared to have been shaken as well.

By contrast, the Flying Wind Sword beside Zheng Yubai wavered but rose into the air again. The lightning sword also floated up, beginning to release a faint glow of lightning.

Situ Tian looked at Zheng Yubai and the two swords before him, then raised his left hand, which held his jade token.

Crack.

He crushed the jade token!

As the barrier dissolved, two Golden Core cultivators who had been watching from outside immediately stepped onto the stone platform.

“Qingheng Sect, Zheng Yubai, victorious!”

A brief silence followed.

Then cheers erupted from the stands!

“He won!”

“Yunzhou won!”

The final scores appeared on the wooden board in the center.

Yunzhou, 33 points.

Nanming, 32 points.

Lu Hongyan sprang to her feet.

Zhang Taishan slammed a fist against his own knee.

“He broke through it!”

Yuanjing could not take his eyes off the stone platform.

At some point, the prayer beads between his fingers had stopped moving.

Huijing spoke quietly.

“So that is the Mind Sword. Its reputation is well deserved.”

Lee Hyun turned toward the old monk.

“The Mind Sword?”

“It is a legendary level of sword attainment spoken of in the mundane world. That young man is famous because he learned what was considered the strongest inheritance of the martial path passed down through Yunzhou’s mundane world. They say one of his family’s ancestors even went beyond what the mundane world calls the Profound Realm.”

Huijing looked toward Zheng Yubai.

“I heard he had studied martial learning from the mundane world alongside his cultivation since childhood, but I never expected him to combine it with the Qingheng Sect’s sword art like that.”

On the stone platform, a Golden Core cultivator from the Qingheng Sect was taking the wooden sword from Zheng Yubai’s hand. He did not seem particularly concerned about the wooden sword itself.

It was nearly broken in half, and no matter how one looked at it, it seemed to be made from ordinary wood rather than being a magic tool.

After swallowing a pill handed to him by the Elder, Zheng Yubai put away his remaining two swords.

On the opposite side, Situ Tian was being supported by a fellow disciple.

The cloth wrapped over his shoulder wound was rapidly soaking through.

...

The cultivators nearby began excitedly discussing the final strike.

Some claimed it was simply the combined power of wind and lightning. Others insisted that the wooden sword itself must have been a special treasure. Still others grew excited at the thought that the Qingheng Sect had revealed some hidden sword art.

The scene from moments earlier replayed again and again in Lee Hyun’s mind.

The divine sense and spiritual power gathered in the wooden sword, along with that unfamiliar yet familiar energy flowing among them.

‘It was similar to creating Buddha-Light True Qi.’

He remembered when he had first learned the Buddha-Light Heart Art.

Only after adding the vow power gained through keeping his vow had the true qi of Baoguang Temple displayed its distinctive properties.

The Spirit-Jolting Needle was the same.

Simply gathering his divine sense into a thin point was not enough. Only by imbuing it with vow power could he produce the strength described in the cultivation formula.

‘Can the same thing... be done with a sword?’

Once he assumed that Zheng Yubai’s final strike had contained spiritual power, divine sense, and vow power together, things he had previously understood as separate began connecting in his mind.

‘Could what sword cultivators call sword intent be....’

Wang Shulin’s voice surfaced in his memory.

She had said that the conviction gained from keeping a vow was refined through a cultivation formula and transformed into vow power.

Then could those who spent years tempering their hearts toward the sword obtain a similar kind of power?

Even if the method differed from the vows of the Buddhist tradition, its foundation would still lie in the primordial spirit.

‘Is that why some sword cultivators become so obsessed with their swords?’

They refuse to abandon an intent once embraced, repeat the same sword path for decades, and preserve that conviction through countless battles.

If that process produced a change similar to cultivating vow power....

Lee Hyun felt a spark of excitement.

‘Then is the unyielding heart of a sword cultivator essentially similar to a vow? If so, could that be the reason sword cultivators speak of One Sword Breaks Ten Thousand Arts...?’

Cultivators who practiced inheritances of the Way of the Sword commonly believed that a sword could break ten thousand arts, and to some extent, they actually made that belief a reality.

Lee Hyun had always found that difficult to understand. Everything in the world had its strengths and weaknesses, so why should inheritances of the Way of the Sword alone be so overwhelmingly powerful?

It seemed unreasonable.

But if vow power were involved, that changed everything.

Vow power was that sort of force to begin with!

It was, in a sense, a power that defied logic, something that could be called the power of wishes or belief.

Incense-offering qi was the clearest example. The prayers of countless mortals gathered together and became part of Baoguang Temple’s strength through the same principle.

If sword intent, the force that made One Sword Breaks Ten Thousand Arts possible, truly worked as he suspected, through a vow that imposed a restriction upon oneself...

‘I see! One Sword Breaks Ten Thousand Arts might be a kind of self-fulfilling prophecy. By believing that the sword can break ten thousand arts, a sword cultivator strengthens their own vow power, then refines that vow power into sword intent and uses it to break those ten thousand arts! Until they suffer defeat, the cycle can keep reinforcing itself! Maybe that’s why powerful sword cultivators are so often portrayed as stubborn fanatics or madmen.’

This differed from the usual cultivation methods of cultivators who pursued straightforward increases in strength. It was more like altering the nature of one’s power within the same major realm by pushing it heavily in a single direction.

‘When a sword cultivator’s spirit breaks and their Dao regresses, is it because their vow has collapsed?’

Fragments of knowledge he had gathered across many different fields, the Sutra of Refining Intent into Vow, the Spirit-Jolting Needle, the martial path of the mundane world, his research into spiritual power, and various other arts and skills, began converging as Lee Hyun approached a new insight.

‘Even the Mind Sword shouldn’t let someone exceed the limits of the power they’ve actually cultivated. And its release speed was only comparable to the Spirit-Jolting Needle, not anything like the speed of light. If someone trusted that one strike enough to challenge a Golden Core cultivator, they’d be in for a rude awakening.’

Lee Hyun’s thoughts continued branching outward in explosive succession.

‘Should vow power be classified as a fourth category? But considering how cultivators of earlier generations emphasized the three components of essence, qi and spirit, vow power should probably fall under spirit. Could I imbue my Great Unity Heavenly Dipper Sword Qi with vow power too? Still, I don’t want to burden myself with a restriction that makes me weaker whenever my resolve falters... I want to create a flexible sword intent. Is there a way to use the Mind Sword without establishing a vow? There must be sword cultivators who have pursued that path....’

As all those concepts flashed through his mind, he felt as though something were hovering just beyond his grasp. Lee Hyun could not even tell whether he had understood something or overlooked something crucial.

For a moment, the countless obscure phrases he had read in the past seemed to take on different meanings.

Where the heart goes, the sword follows.

If you cannot trust your sword, its point will waver.

He had always assumed they were merely sayings emphasizing the proper mindset of one who cultivated.

Of course, not all of them could be referring to actual techniques.

But some of them....

“Junior Brother Li?”

At Yuanjing’s voice, Lee Hyun turned his head.

“Yes.”

“What have you been drawing with your finger all this time?”

Lee Hyun looked down at his hand.

He had been tracing sword paths over his knee.

“That final sword fascinated me.”

“As it did me.”

Yuanjing looked back toward the stone platform.

“To think divine sense could be condensed into a sword like that. I thought I had practiced the spirit-refining method for quite some time, but seeing the methods of another sect reminds me how much there still is to learn.”

Lee Hyun hesitated for a moment before asking,

“Senior Brother, did you sense anything like vow power within it?”

Yuanjing looked back at him.

“You saw it too, Junior Brother?”

“I’m not certain.”

“Neither am I. But it did remind me of several cultivation formulas from our temple.”

He slowly rolled the prayer beads between his fingers.

“Even with the same vow power, its applications differ depending on what one cultivates and how. Whether what was contained in that sword was something of that nature or an entirely different power... we would have to seek his guidance directly to know for certain.”

Lee Hyun nodded.

...

North of the training ground stood a high platform.

The Nascent Soul cultivator from the Haiming Sect wore a satisfied expression.

Patterns of magical power appeared above the jade slip placed before him.

While the Nascent Soul cultivators from both sides confirmed its contents, the injured were carried away below and the martial platform was cleared.

The silver-haired old woman from Nanming gazed for some time in the direction Zheng Yubai had departed.

“‘The mountains of Yun have not yet grown old, and the younger generation is formidable’... Yunzhou’s mountains and rivers still stand vigorous, and its younger generation truly is formidable.”

The white-haired old cultivator from the Taiyue Sect replied,

“We merely had fortune on our side. Had the outcome of just one match been reversed, we would be saying the same thing about you.”

“Winning that one match is itself a matter of skill. Today, Yunzhou had the better of us.”

The old woman set down her teacup and looked at the Haiming Sect cultivator.

“We will abide by the agreement. The disciples of our alliance on Qingyan Island will withdraw within the stipulated period.”

“I trust in your word, fellow Daoist.”

“Hoho. I made the promise before all these people. I do have my reputation to uphold.”

When she rose from her seat, the other Nascent Soul cultivators from Nanming stood one after another.

As they exchanged courtesies, there was no particular hostility in their manner.

Watching from a distance, Lu Hongyan murmured softly,

“They settled that more cleanly than I expected.”

Huijing said,

“They came here in the first place because they wished to avoid a battle between Nascent Soul cultivators. They failed to obtain what they wanted, but this is still far from the worst possible outcome.”

The old monk looked toward the treatment hall.

“Let us take Yuanshi and return as well.”

...

When Yuanshi emerged after receiving treatment, his face was pale, but fortunately, he could walk on his own.

Zhang Taishan moved to his side.

“Senior Brother, shall I give you a hand?”

“I’m fine.”

Liu Jingdao also joined the group.

His right arm remained tucked inside his sleeve while he used his left hand to adjust his storage pouch.

Lu Hongyan asked,

“Senior Brother, did you see the final match too?”

“I did.”

Liu Jingdao gave a bitter smile.

“The female sword cultivator I fought gave me a similar feeling to that Situ Tian. Yet Zheng Yubai even managed to defeat him. I still have a long way to go.”

...

By the time they returned to the guest compound, the sun had already set.

Once inside his room, Lee Hyun first sealed the room behind its restriction.

Chapter 87

Lee Hyun sat on the edge of the bed with the Azure Steel Sword resting across his knees.

When he closed his eyes, Zheng Yubai's final sword strike came to mind.

He recalled the momentum that had surged forward before the sword even moved, and the spiritual power and divine sense that had followed, converging into one.

And mingled with them had been something that resembled vow power.

‘Should I try it too?’

Lee Hyun slowly ran his finger along the blade.

He invoked the Great Unity Heavenly Dipper Sword Art, and the sword qi he had honed countless times took shape.

He awakened the mind seal within his primordial spirit, drew out a thread of the gently stirring vow power, and infused it into the sword qi.

Crackle.

The tip of the sword qi quivered.

Lee Hyun immediately added his divine sense. He held the two energies together as they threatened to scatter, channeling them along the circulation pattern of the sword art.

This time, the sword qi extended a little farther.

But that was all.

Its surface rippled violently before breaking apart into slender fragments of light.

Lee Hyun looked down at the sword.

‘So I can't just throw things together and expect it to work?’

He tried several more times, but the results were much the same. Only the point at which the sword qi grew unstable or lost cohesion changed slightly with each attempt.

At the very least, adjusting the amounts of vow power and divine sense did not seem enough to solve the problem. Unlike Lee Hyun's sword, Zheng Yubai's blade had carried his intent with it as he executed that move.

‘Even with Buddha-Light True Qi, vow power only blended naturally into true qi when I followed the circulation pattern of the Buddha-Light Heart Art. I also referred to the cultivation formula and mnemonic formula when condensing the Spirit-Jolting Needle.’

All of those things had been possible only because of the research and experience accumulated by previous generations.

‘I've only just begun to grasp the broad principles of the Mind Sword. It would be stranger if I could use it right away.’

No matter how long he had practiced with a sword, the answer to a question he had never considered would not simply come to him on its own.

Zheng Yubai must have had his own wealth of experience to draw on.

He must have spent years honing something through faith in his sword and the intent he entrusted to it.

‘Could that be connected to sword intent?’

Lee Hyun once again formed sword qi at his fingertip.

‘The kind of sword I want...’

He had no intention of following a Way of the Sword in which a single retreat could shatter his conviction and even shake his Dao.

If his opponent was too strong, he would avoid them. He would block what he could, deflect what he could, and, when necessary, cut through whatever stood in his way.

‘Easy enough to say, but...’

If thinking up a convincing phrase were enough to develop sword intent, the sword cultivators of the world would have no reason to work so hard for it.

...

After roughly one shichen (about two hours), Lee Hyun put away the Azure Steel Sword.

‘Perhaps someday I'll obtain an inheritance that teaches how to wield a sword and vow power together. For now, I'd be better off honing the methods I already know.’

He took two jade slips from his storage pouch. One held the cultivation records for the Heaven-Origin Divine Tree, while the other held the observation records for the mature tree.

Then he took out the flowerpot as well.

The young Heaven-Origin Divine Tree stood quietly in its small pot. Even when he examined its leaves up close, he could sense no trace of the strange force that repelled nearby objects.

‘A thousand years, huh.’

...

The next morning.

With the Yunzhou Dao Symposium’s main tournament set to resume, the matchups were announced.

Lee Hyun's first opponent was a Foundation Establishment Great Perfection cultivator from the Taiyue Sect.

After confirming his name on the matchup list, he went straight to Martial Uncle Huijing.

“I would like to withdraw from the main tournament.”

Huijing looked up.

“Are you feeling unwell?”

“No, nothing of the sort. However, my magic tools were damaged, and I have already obtained what I wanted. I would rather not push myself any further.”

Lee Hyun had decided to exercise restraint, knowing that he had already drawn considerable attention. Attracting Senior Sister Chen Xiaoying's notice would be particularly troublesome.

He had disguised his face during his time as Li Dongsan, and his current appearance was different again. But he could not be certain that he had changed every habit in his swordplay or the way he performed techniques.

For a start, he was calling himself Li Dongsi. She might think nothing of the name, but after a few encounters at close quarters, might she not be reminded of Li Dongsan?

Lee Hyun had even imagined claiming that he was actually Li Dongsan's successor if Chen Xiaoying came looking for him.

Fortunately, Chen Xiaoying had not sought him out.

There were plenty of people in the world and no shortage of similar names, so there was nothing strange about her not growing suspicious.

Withdrawing from the main tournament now would allow the attention Li Dongsi had been steadily attracting through the clashes with Nanming to die down again.

Many had been injured fighting Nanming, and Lee Hyun had deliberately displayed his damaged Black Scale Inner Armor and Threefold Shield before everyone. There would be nothing strange about his withdrawal.

It was a pity to miss out on an exceptional supreme-grade magic tool like the Whirlwind Shoes, but winning one would mean several more sparring matches. He had no way of knowing how much of his strength he would have to reveal in the process. If he truly needed one, he could look for a similar magic tool to buy with spirit stones later.

Obtaining the Heaven-Origin Divine Tree was enough.

Martial Uncle Huijing nodded.

“Very well. I'll let the organizers know. Knowing when to step forward is important, but so is knowing when to stop.”

“Thank you.”

When Lee Hyun left the room, Lu Hongyan happened to be approaching from the other end of the corridor.

After hearing his explanation, she nodded.

“Good choice. After fighting Nanming like that, the strange ones are the guys climbing back onto the sparring stage.”

“I wish you success as well, Senior Sister Lu.”

...

The sparring matches resumed.

More than a hundred cultivators who had qualified for the main tournament were still in Huiyun Immortal City, and people's attention soon shifted to the new sparring matches.

Trade within the city continued unabated as the main tournament progressed.

In fact, as the Dao symposium drew to a close, more cultivators began trying to sell off their goods or obtain whatever they still needed.

The Baoguang Temple group planned to remain for a while longer.

Yuanshi was able to walk, but his complexion was still poor, and Liu Jingdao's right arm still needed time to heal.

...

“This is the dual cultivation art you requested, Inspector.”

At the back of a small shop selling medicinal ingredients.

Several masked cultivators sat in an underground stone chamber there.

With trading at the gathering in full swing, a jade slip was placed before Lee Hyun, who wore a cicada mask.

“Of the cultivation arts our members found, this one has the most verified accounts of use in Yunzhou. It also includes an account from a cultivator who practiced it with a Dao companion.”

Lee Hyun picked up the jade slip.

It was something he had asked them to track down.

Dual cultivation arts themselves were not rare.

Some focused heavily on one partner taking the other's vital essence, while others promised rapid progress but carried a high risk of conflicting with the practitioner's original cultivation art.

What he wanted was a cultivation art that two people could practice together over the long term without putting undue strain on either of them.

Finding something that met those requirements and checking the experiences of people who had actually practiced it had taken time.

“We've separated the main text from the annotations. We've also marked the passages that agree across multiple editions, as well as the sections added separately by practitioners.”

“Good work.”

Lee Hyun handed over the agreed payment and put away the jade slip. Then he briefly glanced at the cultivator guarding the entrance to the stone chamber.

When Lee Hyun had arrived earlier, that cultivator had not stepped aside merely upon seeing the cicada mask. Only after checking the restriction on Lee Hyun's jade token and comparing it against the letter of introduction sent in advance had he shown him inside.

Lee Hyun approved of that attitude.

Never trust someone based on a mask or title alone!

It was a rule he had emphasized many times.

The older an organization grew, the more easily familiarity led people to skip procedures. Then, if even one member was captured or impersonated, everyone connected to them could be exposed at once.

The Two Heavens Society limited how many contacts any one member could know.

Members could pass on commissions as needed, but they would not necessarily know who ultimately received them.

A higher-level gathering had to confirm the appointment of anyone entrusted to oversee meetings, as well as the approval of new channels of contact. This prevented local leaders from expanding their authority at will, without concentrating information on every member's identity and movements in one place.

It made many things cumbersome, but it was also what had allowed the Two Heavens Society to survive for so long.

...

After returning to the detached residence, Lee Hyun took out the jade slip.

《Yin-Yang Origin-Harmonizing Method》

It was a dual cultivation art that had been passed down in Yunzhou for many years.

The members had also checked its main text against editions obtained from other cultivator markets. Most of the differences were in annotations adding precautions for its practice.

There were detailed explanations of the adjustments needed when Dao companions with different types of spiritual power practiced together. In Lee Hyun's case, his Primordial True Qi had no particular attribute, making the practice relatively safe for both him and his partner.

Lee Hyun examined the jade slip's contents.

「When yin and yang first unite, long-preserved primordial yang and primordial yin are released. The vital essence transferred to one's partner at this time does not immediately disperse, but remains mingled with the partner's own vital essence. If traces of primordial yang and primordial yin remain unrefined, the cultivation art may be especially effective when first practiced. An error at this stage can cause true qi to flow backward, so proceed calmly...」

...

The rest of the Yunzhou Dao Symposium proceeded without incident.

No one from Baoguang Temple finished high enough in the rankings to receive an exceptional supreme-grade magic tool.

The temple was not particularly disappointed. It had sent fewer competitors than the other great sects in the first place, and had not chosen only its very best disciples.

The journey back to Baoguang Temple went smoothly.

With their business in Huiyun Immortal City concluded, the group boarded a flying boat and reached the Mountain Gate six days later.

Between the ten-day wait before the opening, the event itself lasting a little over a month, and the round trip by flying boat, nearly two months had passed since they had left the Mountain Gate.

As soon as Lee Hyun disembarked and finished saying goodbye to his fellow disciples, he flew straight to Wang Shulin's residence, filled with anticipation.

...

Wang Shulin happened to be at home, and the moment she sensed Lee Hyun's presence, she rushed outside, unable to hide her delight.

She came straight over, glanced around, then nestled into his arms and spoke.

“Ahh... I feel alive again!”

The two went inside. Several sheets of paper lay spread across the table, each covered with the names and quantities of medicinal ingredients.

When Lee Hyun noticed them, Wang Shulin began chattering away about everything that had happened while he was gone. Most of it was about her struggles to learn the correct blend of medicinal ingredients for the Golden Core Condensing Pill.

Once she finished, Lee Hyun took a jade slip from his storage pouch.

“I brought something back too.”

“What is it?”

She accepted the jade slip without giving it much thought and pressed it to her forehead. A moment later, she looked up with an embarrassed expression.

“Did you go to the Dao symposium just to get this?”

“I came across it by chance. I thought it might help with cultivation.”

...

They first practiced the Yin-Yang Origin-Harmonizing Method that night.

Then, near dawn.

The two sat facing each other, circulating their qi.

Since it was their first time practicing the cultivation art, Lee Hyun limited the exchange to small amounts of energy. Wang Shulin likewise followed the sequence in the jade slip, slowly completing one qi circulation cycle after another.

After several qi circulation cycles, Lee Hyun sensed something unfamiliar stirring within him.

It was a very fine thread of energy.

Normally concealed within his own vital essence, it slowly became distinguishable as it resonated with Wang Shulin's energy.

It was calm and gentle.

There was more to it than the presence of yin qi.

It had the distinctive quality said to linger only after the first exchange of vital essence that had never before been released.

It matched what he had read in the jade slip's annotations.

‘This is....’

Lee Hyun traced the energy with his divine sense. It was the lingering primordial yin that had passed from Wang Shulin into his body and had not yet been fully refined.

‘So I was Shulin's first too. And to think she'd claimed she was the experienced one and acted like she knew everything...’

Lee Hyun opened his eyes to find Wang Shulin looking at him. Her expression suggested that she, too, had realized something.

When their eyes met, Wang Shulin's gaze flicked to the side.

“What!”

“Nothing.”

“Stop grinning and concentrate.”

“Okay.”

He closed his eyes again.

A short while later, he felt a faint tremor through their joined hands.

This time, it was not from embarrassment.

“Junior Brother.”

Wang Shulin's tone had changed slightly.

“Send a little less energy.”

Lee Hyun immediately withdrew the true qi he had been sending her.

Yet the changes within her body did not subside. Pure energy continued to be released with each of Wang Shulin's qi circulation cycles.

It was not new energy entering from outside, but something that had already been mixed into her vital essence.

Lee Hyun realized that as well.

‘Could this be because of my primordial yang?’

The lingering primordial yin he had received had helped him considerably.

But the lingering primordial yang being released within Wang Shulin was far more substantial.

Wang Shulin immediately slowed her qi circulation.

Rather than trying to turn all the released energy into spiritual power at once, she assimilated it a little at a time, never exceeding what she could handle.

Lee Hyun matched his rhythm to her breathing.

The room fell silent.

As time passed, Wang Shulin's energy gave one powerful surge, then gradually settled within her. Lee Hyun waited without speaking for her to finish circulating her qi.

It was a long while before Wang Shulin finally let out a slow breath.

A faint flush remained on her cheeks.

“Junior Brother Li, just how much vitality do you have? I just broke through!”

‘Huh?’

Lee Hyun examined her now-stable energy again.

Wang Shulin had been at Foundation Establishment Stage 7 just the day before, yet she was already at Stage 8!

The pure energy she had just refined, added to the true essence she had accumulated over the years since reaching Stage 7, had pushed her past the final barrier.

They had only practiced the cultivation art once.

‘Is this the power of two thousand years...’

Wang Shulin stared at him.

“Junior Brother, what on earth have you been eating during your cultivation?”

Lee Hyun hedged.

“I think my constitution might have something to do with it. I didn't expect the effect to be this strong either.”

The look in Wang Shulin's eyes changed. After experiencing such a boost to her cultivation firsthand, she could not afford to dwell on embarrassment. She was, after all, a cultivator pursuing the Great Dao!

“Let's do it again!”

“......You need to stabilize your realm first.”

Fifteen days later.

The restrictions surrounding Wang Shulin's residence rippled faintly.

The spiritual qi gathering inside the room briefly grew denser before settling within her.

Lee Hyun sat opposite her and waited quietly as her breathing gradually grew steady.

A little later, she opened her eyes.

She looked down at her hands, checked her dantian once more, and finally looked at Lee Hyun.

“...I've reached late Stage 8! Are you sure this isn't a demonic cultivation art?”
