Wang Shulin sounded more bewildered than delighted.

She circulated her qi again and realized she had refined almost all the primordial yang lingering within her vital essence. She was not yet fully accustomed to controlling her increased true qi, but there were no impurities in her energy, nor any signs of strain on her meridians.

A smile gradually spread across her face.

“Junior Brother, you're a walking tonic! Let's cultivate every day from now on!”

“You've already used up almost all the vital essence I gave you the first time. I'm not complaining, but...”

“You never know!”

Wang Shulin spent a while examining her strengthened energy, then suddenly looked at him.

“Why haven't you broken through, Junior Brother?”

“It helped me too.”

He was not just saying that.

Refining Wang Shulin's primordial yin had further stabilized the spiritual power in his lower dantian, which had only just reached Stage 7. It had also supplied a good deal of the energy he would otherwise have needed to build up through cultivation, and improved his balance of yin and yang.

Lee Hyun, however, had stored the energy he received evenly throughout his Primordial Body. Even his lower dantian had only recently reached Stage 7, so it would have been difficult to advance another full Stage on the energy he had gained this time alone.

Most importantly, they had transferred very different amounts of vital essence during their first exchange. Wang Shulin had received an especially large amount of his primordial yang.

...

Within a few days, the two realized that the Yin-Yang Origin-Harmonizing Method was no longer as effective as it had been at first. Once they had sufficiently refined the primordial yang and primordial yin lingering in their vital essence, only the cultivation art's usual, gentle effects remained.

Even so, they grew closer. Senior Sister Wang still became embarrassed whenever they talked about the cultivation art, but when it was time to practice together, she enjoyed it even more than Lee Hyun did.

Three months later.

Lee Hyun left the Mountain Gate.

He had finished his duties at the Lotus Court and had some time to spare before his next Refining session.

He also brought the Heaven-Origin Divine Tree. He had been tending it at his residence, watering it with the Spirit Rain Art, but now he intended to plant it in the tunnel.

Along the way, he stopped at several cultivator markets to obtain materials for repairs to the tunnel and its formations.

Once he had gathered everything he needed, he disappeared beneath the ground in a secluded spot.

...

Several days later, at Tunnel No. 3.

He passed through the thick bedrock, and the familiar cavern came into view.

Before Lee Hyun had even landed on the floor, a golden ball of fur darted out of a nearby passage.

Squeak!

A second followed, then a third.

Wingbeats sounded from all directions as fuzzbees swarmed onto Lee Hyun, clinging to him as though delighted to see him.

“Have you all been well?”

Squeak, squeak!

The cavern became even noisier when he opened his spirit-insect pouch.

The little fellows quickly mingled, then scattered off to their usual spots.

Lee Hyun began by checking the cavern and spirit fields in turn, filling the water tanks with the Spirit Rain Art and inspecting the irrigation pipes.

In several spirit fields, he cleared away wilted leaves and thinned out patches of overcrowded seedlings.

A few fuzzbees followed him around, pouncing whenever a small spirit insect appeared in the soil he turned over.

‘No problems here.’

He no longer worried as much as he once had, but returning to the tunnel and finding everything in order still filled him with a quiet sense of contentment.

...

For the Heaven-Origin Divine Tree, he chose a spot a short distance from the spirit field he used as an orchard.

The new plot would be Spirit Field No. 3-9.

He would be able to expand the surrounding area as the tree grew.

Lee Hyun first examined the grain of the bedrock, then cleared away as much earth and stone as he needed.

He used the excavated stone to reinforce the inside of the passage and piled the soil separately. Across the floor of the new space, he spread the spirit soil he had brought, mixing it little by little with the existing earth.

When he cast the Soil-Turning Art, the clods crumbled into fine, loose soil.

A Bonefuzz puppet standing at one side of the cavern turned its head.

Lee Hyun pointed toward the remaining pile of stones.

“Move those over there.”

Two Bonefuzz puppets began carrying the stones.

Fuzzbees circled around them, seemingly checking for anything edible whenever the soil was turned over.

But most of the newly excavated area had been solid bedrock.

Before long, the little fellows lost interest and flew off to other spirit fields.

Lee Hyun ran a bamboo irrigation pipe from the existing water tank and dug a shallow channel to drain off excess water.

Once he had finished preparing the ground, he took out the flowerpot.

The sapling stood less than two chi (about 66 cm) tall.

Looking down at it, he found it a little funny that he had even fought a life-and-death duel just to obtain something so small.

‘Anyone else seeing this probably wouldn't understand, but...’

He tapped the rim of the flowerpot with his finger.

Tap.

A thin crack appeared in the clay pot.

As he removed the pot a piece at a time, the roots and soil within were exposed. Lee Hyun supported the root ball with spiritual power to keep the root tips from breaking, then lowered it intact into the hole he had dug.

After filling in the surrounding soil and lightly packing it down, he cast the Spirit Rain Art.

Patter, patter.

Clear droplets fell onto the leaves and soil, and the Heaven-Origin Divine Tree's thick leaves stirred slightly.

Lee Hyun crouched before the tree and cast the Aura-Reading Art. He could see energy flowing from its roots through its trunk and into its leaves.

The tree slowly drew spiritual qi from the soil.

Life force gathered within it before spreading back out through the branches.

Yet he could not tell where Heaven-Origin Qi was being produced. To observe the changes described in the records firsthand, it seemed he would still have to wait for the tree to bear fruit.

Just then.

One of the leaves moved ever so slightly.

Lee Hyun's gaze shifted toward it.

A golden fuzzbee was clinging to the underside of the leaf. The little fellow had been feeling along its veins with its slender forelegs, but when its eyes met Lee Hyun's, it raised its head.

Squeak?

“Keep this little fellow safe from spirit insects too. You're all heavy, so try not to hang off it if you can help it.”

The fuzzbee checked the edge of the leaf once more, then took flight.

Apparently, it had found nothing.

Lee Hyun tidied the soil around the tree again, then carved the spirit field number, the tree's name, and the planting date into a small stone plaque and set it in the ground beside the tree.

Next, he prepared to install a formation around the new spirit field.

He took out the formation devices and formation plate for a Tier 1 Qi-Gathering Formation he had made for practice when he first began studying formations.

He wanted to give the Heaven-Origin Divine Tree a slightly better growing environment.

The Tier 1 Qi-Gathering Formation consumed low-grade spirit stones, but it only needed to cover a small space containing a single sapling, so the cost was manageable.

After calculating the formation plate's consumption rate, Lee Hyun estimated that ten low-grade spirit stones could keep it running for roughly a year at its current strength.

At that rate, even a hundred years of operation would cost only the equivalent of ten mid-grade spirit stones, which was no burden at all for Lee Hyun.

‘Should I switch to a better Qi-Gathering Formation once the tree grows?’

He began to consider studying the Tier 2 Qi-Gathering Formation as well.

When he had first begun learning Tier 2 formations, Lee Hyun had devoted most of his efforts to the Spirit-Concealing Formation, which could be adapted to the terrain to conceal Tunnel No. 3.

The designs for the Spirit-Concealing Formation's formation plate and formation devices had been included in the jade slip he obtained from the Danxiao Sect.

He could now call himself a Tier 2 formation master, but the Spirit-Concealing Formation was essentially the only Tier 2 formation he had completed by crafting its formation devices and formation plate himself. With other formations, his knowledge extended only to basic theory and recognizing formation inscriptions, so he would have to study the Qi-Gathering Formation separately before he could build one.

Fortunately, there were plenty of people he could ask at the Lotus Court. Senior Brother Mingyun would be delighted to answer questions about formations.

Once Lee Hyun finished setting up the Tier 1 Qi-Gathering Formation and activated it, the formation devices and the formation inscriptions carved into the floor glowed faintly, and the surrounding spiritual qi slowly began to gather.

He watched for a while, then left the tree and headed out of the cavern.

‘It's been a while. I should check on the Spirit-Concealing Formation too.’

Chapter 88

The formation devices of the Spirit-Concealing Formation were embedded throughout the bedrock surrounding Tunnel No. 3.

Lee Hyun used the Earth Escape Art to move through the bedrock, inspecting each formation device in turn.

Most of the formation inscriptions on their surfaces were intact. In a few places, however, changes in the flow of spiritual qi and the earth vein had weakened the Spirit-Concealing Formation's effects.

The weakening was nowhere near enough to expose the tunnel. After all, he had dug it beneath barren land no one had any reason to visit, even before the Spirit-Concealing Formation was in place.

With the Spirit-Concealing Formation in place, imperfect though it was, discovery was even less likely.

Still, since he had noticed the problem, he decided to fix it.

He moved from place to place, repeating a series of adjustments: pressing his palm against the rock walls to cast the Soil-Turning Art, using the Soil-Softening Art on the stone, and so on.

Once the repairs were finished, the Spirit-Concealing Formation blended seamlessly with the surrounding earth vein, concealing Tunnel No. 3 even more effectively.

Lee Hyun also replaced the dimming mid-grade spirit stones in the formation plate with fresh ones.

...

He went up to the surface and checked the surrounding energy.

The lower slopes of the mountain were quiet.

The spiritual qi was thin, and there was not the slightest hint of anything beneath the ground.

Standing directly above Tunnel No. 3, he sent his divine sense straight down, but it fell far short of reaching eighteen li (about 7.1 km) underground.

Lee Hyun's divine sense could extend at most a few li through open air, but beneath the ground, he struggled to detect anything after only a hundred zhang (about 330 m).

He estimated that even a great cultivator at late Nascent Soul would have almost no chance of detecting Tunnel No. 3 while flying overhead unless they probed straight down from directly above it.

Satisfied, Lee Hyun descended into Tunnel No. 3 again and stopped by Spirit Field No. 3-9.

The young Heaven-Origin Divine Tree seemed to be growing well despite the change in its surroundings.

Squeak!

A fuzzbee landed on his shoulder. He had not noticed it following him.

Lee Hyun examined the energy flowing through the little fellow's body.

Having spent so long catching and eating spirit insects in Lee Hyun's tunnels, the fuzzbees were noticeably stronger than when he had first brought them there. Compared with Lee Hyun, whose entire body was at the Foundation Establishment level, however, they were still just tiny insects.

The Bonefuzz puppets silently hauling stones at one side of the cavern were also pitifully weak in combat compared with him.

'Should I try to make these fellows stronger?'

With some effort, he could acquire better spirit insects to feed them, mix spirit medicine into their food, and replace the Bonefuzz puppets' bones with superior materials.

'But......'

Why had he raised the fuzzbees in the first place?

These fellows caught spirit insects for him, making his life easier.

If he had to run around finding spirit insects and preparing special food just to make them stronger, that would defeat the whole purpose.

As Lee Hyun grew stronger, he might eventually need to build his tunnels near a better spirit vein anyway.

By then, the spirit insects found nearby would naturally be of a higher tier, so the fuzzbees could advance without him going out of his way.

The same went for the Bonefuzz puppets.

Someday, when he needed to produce Golden Core Condensing Pills in large quantities from demon cores, he would naturally acquire the bones of Tier 3 demon beasts as well. It would not be too late to research improvements then.

'In the end, my own strength matters most. The fuzzbees and Bonefuzz puppets are here to help me. There's no reason to let them take up all my time.'

Squeak?

"Just keep catching spirit insects like you always have."

Splat!

For the first time in ages, the fuzzbee responded by taking a dump instead of squeaking.

On the day Lee Hyun returned to Baoguang Temple, Lotus Court was unusually noisy.

"Late Stage 8!?"

Martial Uncle Huijue's voice carried over the wall.

A young monk sweeping the corridor spotted Lee Hyun and spoke quietly.

"Elder Huijue has finished his cultivation and come out. Ever since he saw Senior Wang... he has been like that."

He had emerged from a brief period of secluded cultivation to find that his disciple, who had long been stuck at Foundation Establishment Stage 7, was now at late Stage 8. His surprise was understandable.

'...Maybe I should have come back a little later.'

...

When Lee Hyun entered the alchemy chamber, it was Huitan who was waiting for him.

The old monk beckoned without a word, led him into a small study farther inside, and even activated the restriction on the door.

Before Lee Hyun could ask what was wrong, Huitan leaned in as though he were about to grab him by the collar and whispered.

"You brat! Just how much of your vital essence did that fellow Wang Shulin suck out of you to advance so far? Is there any marrow left in your bones!?"

"......."

"...You're perfectly fine?"

"Yes."

"Why are you perfectly fine?"

"?"

Huitan pressed a hand to his forehead.

“Do you know what that damn monk Huijue came to tell me first thing this morning? ‘Your disciple was just the spark she needed, Senior Brother.’ That’s what he said! What in the world happened?”

Lee Hyun answered without batting an eye.

"Senior Sister Wang is exceptionally gifted, and it seems the pills she took have only now taken full effect."

"Only now taken full effect? Have you forgotten that I'm a Tier 3 alchemist?"

"Please don't worry too much. I'm perfectly healthy."

...

A few days later.

Lee Hyun visited Senior Brother Mingyun's residence.

"A Tier 2 Qi-Gathering Formation?"

Mingyun's eyes lit up.

"Yes. I'd like to work out the arrangement of the formation inscriptions myself, but there are quite a few points where I'm stuck."

"To think you'd take an interest in formations! Where are you having trouble?"

Lee Hyun took out the diagram of the Qi-Gathering Formation he had devised. Mingyun studied it for a long while, then praised him and launched enthusiastically into an explanation.

The explanation went on for more than one shichen (two hours). Though the endless talk was wearing him out, Lee Hyun listened attentively. Mingyun even fetched a jade slip from his shelves.

"I compiled these notes when I was young and studying the Qi-Gathering Formation. I compared several versions of the formation diagram and even recorded the changes I made after setting them up myself."

"Are you sure you should be sharing something so valuable with me?"

"Fate has brought it to a Junior Brother with an interest in formations, that's all."

After copying the contents of the jade slip, Lee Hyun returned it and took a jade bottle from his robes.

"These are three Tier 2 Spirit-Calming Pills, all mid grade. They'll help with cultivation of the primordial spirit."

"These are... quite valuable, aren't they?"

"Then fate has brought these to you, Senior Brother."

"Hoho, I think I'm the one getting the better deal here."

Thirty years passed.

Despite his other pursuits, Lee Hyun studied the contents of Mingyun's jade slip whenever he had the chance, until he could craft the formation plates and formation devices for a Tier 2 Qi-Gathering Formation.

However, a Tier 2 Qi-Gathering Formation consumed too many spirit stones for him to install one around the Heaven-Origin Divine Tree in Tunnel No. 3 right away.

During that time, Lu Hongyan reached Foundation Establishment Great Perfection and attempted Core Formation using one of Baoguang Temple's Golden Core Condensing Pills.

But she failed to form a golden core.

Her true essence surged backward, rupturing her meridians. She had tried not to push herself too hard, but Core Formation left her no chance to retreat.

During Lu Hongyan's Buddhist cremation ceremony, Wang Shulin, Lee Hyun, and their fellow disciples were overcome with grief at her tragic death.

...

Then, one night.

In a pavilion on the peak east of Lotus Court.

Wang Shulin leaned against the railing, her brush moving over a painting board, while Lee Hyun lay beside her reading a popular novel.

"Junior Brother. Lately, I can't seem to find anything new to paint."

"You've been painting for decades. That's bound to happen. What did you paint today?"

Wang Shulin turned the board around to show him.

She had painted a moth of some sort clinging to one of the pavilion's pillars.

"Wasn't it the chipped corner of a teacup saucer yesterday? Your subjects keep getting smaller."

"Exactly."

Wang Shulin set down her brush.

She gazed silently down the mountain for a while before speaking again.

"There is something I haven't painted yet."

"What?"

"Our child's face."

Lee Hyun's heart gave a sudden jolt.

Not because he disliked the idea. He was simply startled.

Lee Hyun closed his book.

Wang Shulin kept gazing down the mountain without looking at him.

"I've got about thirty years left until Foundation Establishment Great Perfection."

"I know."

"After that comes Golden Core..."

Her voice was calm.

"You saw what happened to Senior Sister Lu. They say plenty of cultivators fail to form a golden core even after taking a Golden Core Condensing Pill. Some die on the spot."

"Shulin."

"Let me finish."

Only then did Wang Shulin turn to him.

"If I fail, I'll be gone. Just like that."

Her expression was serious.

"That's why I want to leave something in this world to show that we were together, Junior Brother."

Lee Hyun could not say anything.

"And even if I succeed in Core Formation, there's another problem. They say that once a golden core forms, it takes over the internal organs' role in the body's metabolism, changing how the body functions. That makes it much harder for Golden Core cultivators to have children."

Wang Shulin took a breath before continuing.

"Let's get married. Let's leave the mountain and have children."

The night breeze swept beneath the pavilion.

Lee Hyun looked at her face.

In his past life, Lee Hyun had never even considered marriage. The same had been true after coming to this world.

For more than two thousand years, he had tried not to grow too close to anyone. Once he grew attached, he would inevitably have to watch them pass away before him.

So he had always kept his distance.

But...

"All right."

Wang Shulin's eyes widened.

"...Really?"

"Yes."

"Don't you need to think about it? We'd be leaving the mountain for decades."

"I thought about it."

"When?"

"Just now."

Wang Shulin burst out laughing. As she laughed, she wiped at the corners of her eyes with the back of her hand.

...

A few days later, the two stood side by side before Huijue and Huitan.

Both old monks wore grave expressions, but Huijue soon spoke.

"Hohoho! Senior Brother, what did this old monk tell you? Didn't I say it was an immortal affinity?"

"Hmph......."

Huitan looked not at Lee Hyun, but at Wang Shulin.

"...Take good care of him. This fellow may seem a little clueless, but deep down, there's something of an old man about him."

"I know, Senior Martial Uncle."

Baoguang Temple regularly dispatched cultivators to mortal kingdoms throughout Xu Kingdom.

It stationed a resident cultivator in each kingdom to deal with demon beasts that might descend from the mountains or bandit cultivators targeting the royal family, and provided them with lodgings and a suitable cultivation environment.

This was a longstanding practice not only at Baoguang Temple, but at the Danxiao Sect and countless other great sects as well.

Wang Shulin and Lee Hyun decided to make use of that system.

She chose Xianghe Kingdom, a mortal kingdom in northeastern Xu Kingdom.

"Xianghe Kingdom? Do you have some connection there?"

Wang Shulin shrugged at Lee Hyun's question.

"It's where my family lives."

"Your family?"

"The royal family there is my family. The Wang royal clan."

Lee Hyun stared at her for a moment.

"...You were a princess?"

"A princess? That was more than eighty years ago."

"Still..."

Lee Hyun gave an exaggerated sigh.

"Oh dear. So I've gone and seduced someone so highborn."

"I'm the one who seduced you, remember?"

Wang Shulin shot him a look.

"The current King is my older brother's grandson. He's never even seen me. Besides, that's just my status in the mundane world. Though it does come in handy at times like this."

...

Xianghe Kingdom was only a small kingdom within Xu Kingdom, but to mortals, it was an enormous country.

Such was the sheer size of this world.

The royal capital stood beside a river an astonishing hundred li wide.

The population numbered in the hundreds of millions as well. Though the dynasty was mortal, its royal family's power seemed almost boundless to ordinary people.

But when Baoguang Temple's flying boat descended onto the square before the royal palace, even the mighty royal family of Xianghe Kingdom had no choice but to throw open every gate.

At the front stood a middle-aged King in golden dragon robes. Behind him stretched an endless line of the queen, princes, royal kin, and civil and military officials.

They all prostrated themselves at once.

"Greetings, Great-Aunt!"

"...Great-Aunt?"

Lee Hyun echoed the title under his breath, and Wang Shulin's ears turned red.

The King raised his head and looked at Wang Shulin's face, his eyes reddening.

"Your eyes are exactly as they appear in the portrait. I have known your likeness since childhood."

"There's a portrait of me?"

"Yes. I was told that after you entered the immortal sect, Great-Aunt, the King at the time summoned a court painter to make it. For generations, our royal family has prayed for your success on the immortal path."

For a moment, Wang Shulin was at a loss for words.

Since leaving for Baoguang Temple after her dual spiritual root was discovered in childhood, she had never once returned home. News of her parents' deaths, and of her older brother's ascension to the throne and later passing, had all reached her while she remained within the Mountain Gate.

Yet through all those long years, the people here had never forgotten her.

Wang Shulin helped the King to his feet.

"Rise."

...

The King provided a luxurious detached palace north of the royal capital for Wang Shulin, who was approaching Foundation Establishment Great Perfection, and her Dao companion, Lee Hyun.

A branch temple of Baoguang Temple stood nearby, along with a storehouse for the medicinal ingredients offered by the royal family and the surrounding districts. In many ways, it was a convenient place for the two of them to live.

An old plum tree stood in the garden, and a small mountain rose behind the grounds.

The detached palace had not originally been intended to house a resident cultivator, so it had no Tier 2 Qi-Gathering Formation.

Since they had chosen it as their home as husband and wife, Lee Hyun installed the Qi-Gathering Formation himself.

He used formation plates and formation devices of his own making, while Baoguang Temple supplied the mid-grade spirit stones needed to power the formation as part of the allowance for resident cultivators.

Once the formation was activated, the spiritual qi within the detached palace grew denser. It could not match the conditions at Baoguang Temple, but it was sufficient for Foundation Establishment cultivators to cultivate.

...

The two held their wedding according to Xianghe Kingdom's customs.

The royal family wanted a grand celebration, but Wang Shulin firmly refused. In the end, they held a modest ceremony attended only by the King and queen and a few of their royal kin.

The following spring, their first child was born.

Lee Hyun took the baby into his arms and stood motionless for a long while.

She was so small and fragile that he was terrified the slightest mistake might hurt her.

...

Before he knew it, ten years had passed.

By then, their third child had been born.

Their eldest was Li Hua, their second Li Dan, and their youngest Li Mo.

The children grew up healthy and strong.

Li Hua took after her mother and loved painting. At five years old, she nearly made the palace attendants faint by drawing an enormous dragon in charcoal across the detached palace's wall.

Li Dan took everything apart: water clocks, wagon wheels, even a formation plate Lee Hyun had hidden away.

Li Mo, whose name suggested silence, was anything but quiet.

Lee Hyun and Wang Shulin cultivated within the detached palace's Qi-Gathering Formation and, as resident cultivators, dealt with the Tier 1 demon beasts that occasionally appeared near Xianghe Kingdom.

Lee Hyun sometimes visited nearby cultivator markets to handle matters for the Two Heavens Society, but he spent most of his remaining time with the children.

He carved wooden figurines for them: knights in armor, horned demon kings, and figures resembling robots he had seen in his past life.

"Dad, what's this?"

"Hmm... a robot?"

"What's a robot?"

"...A person made of metal."

"Why does a person made of metal look like this?"

"I don't really remember either."

...

One day, when their eldest daughter, Li Hua, was a little over ten, she stared at Lee Hyun's true face and asked a question.

"Dad, why don't you get old?"

Before Lee Hyun could answer, Wang Shulin spoke.

"Because he took a Youth-Preserving Pill."

"What's a Youth-Preserving Pill?"

"A medicine that keeps your face from aging."

"Did you take one too, Mom?"

"I did. Your dad gave me one."

Li Hua tilted her head.

"Then give me one too."

"It would be dangerous for you. You're not a cultivator."

"That's not fair."

Wang Shulin laughed and stroked her daughter's hair.

...

A few years later, when their youngest was five or six, they performed the last of the children's spiritual root tests.

As they had with their first two children, Wang Shulin and Lee Hyun placed the spiritual-root testing orb in their youngest child's palm.

Once again, the orb gave off no light.

None of the three had spiritual roots.

Children born to two cultivators were far more likely to possess spiritual roots than children born to mortal parents. Still, it was common for them to be born without spiritual roots, so there was nothing particularly unusual about it.

Wang Shulin put away the orb and remained silent for a while.

"Disappointed?"

"...A little."

Lee Hyun picked up their youngest. The child tugged at his hair and giggled.

"I think it's a good thing."

"Why?"

"The cultivation world is dangerous. It isn't such a bad thing if the children never have to walk that path. They can live ordinary, happy lives."

Wang Shulin looked at him and smiled.

"That's true."

Twenty years had now passed since the birth of their youngest.

That year, Wang Shulin reached Foundation Establishment Great Perfection.

In preparation for Core Formation, she obtained a Golden Core Condensing Pill.

It was not from Baoguang Temple.

She had bought it at an auction within the Nine Kingdoms of Yunzhou. It had been refined using a Tier 3 spirit plant rather than a Tier 3 demon core, making it a proper Golden Core Condensing Pill that would not hinder her later advancement to Nascent Soul.

Lee Hyun had intended to help in his own way, but she had acquired one herself before he had the chance.

...

Wang Shulin returned to Baoguang Temple to attempt Core Formation and entered a secure secluded cultivation chamber above a Tier 3 spirit vein.

Lee Hyun sat in the corridor outside the secluded cultivation chamber and waited for forty-nine full days.

At dawn on the forty-ninth day, the restriction around the secluded cultivation chamber rippled violently.

A golden glow spread across the sky above Lotus Court.

A short while later, the door opened and Wang Shulin stepped out.

The energy emanating from her body was fundamentally different from that of a Foundation Establishment cultivator.

Golden Core!

The moment Wang Shulin saw Lee Hyun, she ran over and threw herself into his arms.

"I did it."

"I know."

"I really did it!"

"I know."

Lee Hyun held her tightly.

...

Now that Wang Shulin had succeeded in Core Formation, Baoguang Temple granted her a peak and a residence of her own.

She became an Elder of Lotus Court.

As she absorbed spiritual qi from a Tier 3 spirit vein in the cultivation chamber reserved for Elders, channeling energy through her newly stabilized golden core became much easier.

Once the celebrations were over, Wang Shulin found herself facing a dilemma.

If she hoped to reach the Nascent Soul realm in the future, she would be better off staying at the main temple to cultivate.

Fortunately, she no longer had any reason to remain in Xianghe Kingdom.

Their three children were already grown, had families of their own, and were living well under the royal family's protection.

The real problem was Lee Hyun.

"My lifespan has increased by several hundred years. But you... why haven't you advanced to a higher realm?"

Lee Hyun knew the time had come.

In a place protected by a screening formation, he told her that he had a special constitution and could live at least as long as a Golden Core cultivator.

"You're not lying, are you?"

"No."

Wang Shulin let out a long breath.

"Then that's all right."

Then her eyes suddenly widened.

"Wait, what are we going to do? If you spend hundreds of years at Foundation Establishment without aging or dying... how do we explain that to the sect?"

Lee Hyun grinned.

"I'll just join again."

"What?"

"Li Dongsi will grow old, leave the mountain to enjoy his retirement, and die. Then I'll enter Baoguang Temple under another name and become a disciple of Elder Wang Shulin of Lotus Court."

Wang Shulin laughed.

"I'll be your Master?"

"Don't like the idea?"

"No, I love it! That sounds fun!"

Her eyes sparkled.

"Then you'll have to call me Master."

"...All right."

"And you'll have to speak respectfully to me."

"Only in front of other people."

"I'll give you assignments, too."

"Well......"

Time passed, indifferent to them all.

Lee Hyun and Wang Shulin's children grew old.

The two visited Xianghe Kingdom whenever they could. On every visit, there were more wrinkles on their children's faces and more grandchildren to meet.

Their children's families had become prominent clans at Xianghe Kingdom's royal court.

Li Dan's grandson headed the royal workshop, improving waterwheels and wagons, while Li Mo's daughter became the King's consort. Li Hua's paintings hung in the corridors of the royal palace.

...

One autumn.

The two visited their eldest daughter, Li Hua.

Li Hua's hair had turned white, and her back was bent. Her brush hand trembled slightly.

She was sitting on the veranda, looking out over the garden. When she saw the two of them at the entrance, her face lit up with a smile.

"Father, Mother."

Lee Hyun stopped where he stood.

Li Hua's smile was exactly as he remembered it from her childhood.

It was the same smile she had worn while proudly showing off the dragon she had drawn in charcoal on the detached palace's wall.

But eighty years had left their mark on that face.

Lee Hyun had watched countless people in this world grow old and pass away.

It had hurt a little every time, but he had been able to bear it.

They had not been his children.

But now...

"You haven't changed at all, Father."

Li Hua smiled as she spoke.

Lee Hyun could not answer.

Beside him, Wang Shulin broke down first.

She ran to her daughter and burst into tears. None of the dignity of a Golden Core cultivator remained. She was simply a mother weeping as she held her elderly daughter.

"Mom, why are you crying?"

Li Hua patted her mother's back with a trembling hand.

"Don't cry. I've had a good life. I really have."

Before long, Li Dan and Li Mo arrived as well, having heard the news.

Li Dan walked with a cane, while Li Mo was supported by a grandson.

The three elderly siblings gathered around their parents, who looked far younger than any of them, and comforted them.

"Father, Mother. We really have been happy."

"I still have the wooden carving you made me, Father."

...

Li Hua passed away the following year.

Li Dan followed a few years later, and Li Mo the year after that.

Each time one of their children passed away, Wang Shulin went down to Xianghe Kingdom to attend the funeral.

And each time she came back, she took out one of the portraits she had painted of her children and gazed at it.

...

Li Dongsi was nearing the maximum lifespan of a Foundation Establishment cultivator.

He stepped down from his duties at Lotus Court, saying he wished to spend his remaining years outside the Mountain Gate.

A few years later, word came that he had passed away in a distant land.

Several more years passed, and Wang Shulin brought back a Foundation Establishment cultivator as her disciple, claiming she had met him during her travels.

He went through the necessary admission checks, but no one was inclined to make things difficult for a disciple a Golden Core Elder had personally vouched for.

The steward of the Guest Reception Hall responsible for his admission looked over the register.

"You're fortunate to have Elder Wang Shulin's recommendation. Elder Wang doesn't have any direct disciples yet. And she's exceptionally beautiful, too."

Chapter 89

Lee Hyun became a disciple of Lotus Court once again.

After the initiation ceremony ended, he knelt outside Elder Wang Shulin’s residence.

“I pay my respects, Master.”

Wang Shulin spoke from inside, her voice solemn.

“Come in.”

When he opened the door and stepped inside, he found Wang Shulin seated primly at a table.

For a while, she struggled to keep her expression stern, but the corners of her mouth kept creeping upward.

“Come closer.”

As Lee Hyun approached, she could no longer keep a straight face.

“Pfft!”

“...”

...

The years continued to pass.

Familiar peaks passed to new masters, and the names of people he had known for years were entered into the Scripture Pavilion’s records. New disciples simply took it for granted that Wang Shulin was an Elder.

Then one day, Master Huitan reached the end of his lifespan as a Golden Core cultivator and passed away in meditation.

He had never managed to cross the threshold into Nascent Soul, but the old monk’s face was serene.

On the day of the Buddhist cremation ceremony, Lee Hyun stood among the disciples of Lotus Court as Wang Shulin’s direct disciple.

Master Huitan had been a good man.

Several decades later, Elder Huijue followed him in death.

...

After nearly two hundred years under his new identity, Lee Hyun left Baoguang Temple once again.

Wang Shulin’s first direct disciple was said to have died after spending his final years elsewhere.

A few years later, she accepted another Foundation Establishment cultivator, one with a different face and name.

Her second direct disciple was also Lee Hyun.

...

The years continued to pass.

Wang Shulin devoted herself to her Golden Core cultivation, and Lee Hyun did not neglect his own.

But bringing every part of his body to the Great Perfection stage of Foundation Establishment would still take time. He had no intention of merely forming a golden core in his lower dantian and stopping there, so he could not rush.

Lee Hyun supported Wang Shulin’s efforts to reach Nascent Soul. Little by little, he sold the Tier 3 Bone-Rot Flowers, Purple Poison Orchids, and Yin Soul Grass grown in the tunnel’s spirit fields through the Two Heavens Society, then used the spirit stones to buy pills for Golden Core cultivation.

He could not sell much. Bringing too many Tier 3 spirit herbs to market at once would draw attention, so he could offer only a few plants every few decades.

He also occasionally used alchemy to produce Tier 2 Bone-Forging Powder, Poison-Warding Pills, Spirit-Calming Pills, Origin-Opening Pills, Profundity-Penetrating Pills, and other medicines for sale.

Whenever Lee Hyun brought home pills such as Tier 3 True Essence Pills without consulting her first, Wang Shulin felt guilty.

“These are expensive.”

“They didn’t cost much.”

Nearly five hundred years had passed since their wedding day.

Wang Shulin had reached the Great Perfection stage of Golden Core.

But she had little time left.

A Golden Core cultivator’s lifespan was finite, and without reaching Nascent Soul, there was no escaping that end.

She entered secluded cultivation one last time.

...

Lee Hyun waited outside the secluded cultivation chamber.

He had waited just like this when she formed her golden core long ago. She had succeeded then.

Lee Hyun thought of Senior Sister Chen Xiaoying. She, too, was a dual-root cultivator, and she had become a Nascent Soul cultivator.

‘Shulin can do it too.’

...

The restrictions on the secluded cultivation chamber trembled on the seventy-first night.

Lee Hyun immediately rose to his feet.

The energy inside the chamber swelled. Her Golden Core magical power converged at a single point, sending out violent pulses as though trying to shatter something.

Shattering the Core to Form the Nascent Soul!

It was the process of breaking the golden core and nurturing a nascent soul within it.

For a long time, the pulses swelled, ebbed, then swelled again.

And then, all at once.

Nothing.

The pulses stopped.

A short while later, the restrictions were lifted from within.

Lee Hyun threw open the door and rushed inside.

Wang Shulin sat in the lotus position.

Blood trickled from the corner of her mouth, and he could sense a deep crack in the golden core within her dantian.

She opened her eyes and looked at Lee Hyun, then smiled weakly.

“...It didn’t work.”

...

Wang Shulin had chosen to stop midway through forming her nascent soul.

Had she pressed on, her golden core would have shattered on the spot. At the last moment, she had withdrawn her magical power, barely managing to hold her fractured golden core together.

The price was that she now had little more than a year left to live.

“Don’t be too sad. This path was never open to most cultivators in the first place.”

Wang Shulin spoke as Lee Hyun brought her back to her residence and examined the damage to her golden core.

“It wasn’t easy getting this far, either. I tried my best... It just didn’t work out this time.”

“Don’t talk. Save your strength.”

“What’s the point? I only have a year anyway.”

She took his hand.

“I really have had a happy life.”

...

Wang Shulin said she wanted to spend her final days in Xianghe Kingdom.

“Our children are there.”

Their children had passed away long ago, but their bloodline had continued from one generation to the next.

When word came that their distant ancestor was returning, the royal family of Xianghe Kingdom once again threw open every gate of the palace.

This time, those prostrating themselves before her included many with the surname Li as well as Wang.

They were the descendants of Li Hua, Li Dan, and Li Mo.

Wang Shulin greeted them one by one. She asked their names, which ancestor they descended from, and how many generations removed they were. She studied each face for a long time.

“This child looks like Dan.”

“This one has Hua’s eyes.”

“Mo... somehow managed to leave behind nothing but noisy descendants.”

...

Wang Shulin visited the burial grounds where their children lay.

They were well tended.

The inscriptions on the gravestones had been recarved several times, and collapsed sections of the stone walls had been repaired. The descendant responsible for the ancestral rites carefully explained what had been repaired and when.

Wang Shulin thanked them.

After she sent the others away, she and Lee Hyun were left alone.

She ran a hand over their eldest child’s gravestone.

Then she stood before their second child’s grave, and finally their youngest’s.

“Here would be good.”

Lee Hyun looked at her.

Wang Shulin pointed to an empty spot on one side of the burial grounds.

“I want to be with the children.”

“...”

...

As winter deepened, Wang Shulin spent more and more time in bed.

Her face was still youthful.

Her appearance, preserved by the Youth-Preserving Pill, was slow to change. But even a little movement left her short of breath, and her wrist would go weak if she held a brush for too long.

Lee Hyun placed a small table beside her bed.

During those final months, she painted every day.

Even now, her vow remained unbroken.

...

One morning.

Wang Shulin called Lee Hyun to her side.

“Hold my hand.”

He sat beside the bed.

Wang Shulin’s hand felt light in his.

She lay with her eyes closed for a long while before speaking quietly.

“I’ve had a good life, haven’t I?”

“You have.”

“I have, haven’t I?”

She smiled.

“I’m glad I asked you to marry me.”

Lee Hyun opened his mouth, then closed it again.

Wang Shulin tugged gently on his hand.

“Our children were lovely, too.”

“They were.”

“And I loved our life together.”

Lee Hyun lowered his head.

She touched his cheek.

“I do wish I could stay with you a little longer, though.”

He held her hand against his face.

Wang Shulin paused to catch her breath, then continued.

“I couldn’t form a nascent soul... and there’s nothing we can do about that now. If it were so easy, why would there be so many old Golden Core cultivators in the world?”

“Shulin.”

“Yes?”

Lee Hyun did not know what to say.

He could not tell her that he would find another pill or look for some other way. He had already spent so long doing just that.

Wang Shulin gazed at him in silence.

“Don’t spend too long alone after I’m gone. Meet new people, too.”

Lee Hyun’s grip tightened.

“Read novels. Eat good food. And laugh when something’s funny.”

Lee Hyun did not answer.

She pointed a finger toward the drawing board and brush beside the bed.

“I want you to have those.”

“But they’re yours.”

“Exactly. They’re mine, so I’m giving them to you.”

Her voice grew softer and softer.

“Try painting when you’re bored.”

“....”

She closed her eyes for a moment, then opened them again.

“You have such a lovely smile.”

Lee Hyun tried to smile.

He could not quite manage it.

Wang Shulin stroked his cheek once more.

“I love you.”

She slowly closed her eyes.

She was buried in the ancestral burial grounds of the royal family of Xianghe Kingdom, in the spot she had chosen beside their children.

Lee Hyun could not let himself sob aloud.

Throughout the funeral, he remained quiet, as though he were no more than Wang Shulin’s disciple. He acknowledged the descendants’ greetings, received the mourners, and watched as earth covered her coffin.

Even after the funeral ended, he stayed in Xianghe Kingdom for a while.

He built a hut at the foot of the mountain, within sight of her grave, and lived there.

During the day, he sat endlessly beside her grave.

At night, he drank.

A cultivator’s body was not easily intoxicated by mortal wine. Lee Hyun tried drinking with his spiritual power deliberately suppressed, yet even then, he found it hard to get drunk.

...

Spring arrived.

The caretaker weeded the burial grounds.

Summer brought heavy rains. Lee Hyun widened the drainage channel behind her grave a little.

In autumn, fallen leaves piled up. He cleared them away by hand.

Then one day, Lee Hyun left the hut without a word.

Tunnel No. 3.

Lee Hyun lay down on the floor of a stone chamber in one corner of the cavern.

And he did not get up.

He did not go out to the spirit fields. He did not open any of his popular novels.

He simply lay curled on his side like a child in its mother’s womb, staring at the dark wall until he drifted off to sleep.

When he was desperately thirsty, he drank water. When he could no longer bear his hunger, he swallowed a Hunger-Warding Pill. He often forgot even to do that.

The drawing board and brush she had left him were still in his storage pouch, but he could not bring himself to take them out.

...

A year passed.

The last spirit stone in Spirit Field No. 3-9’s Qi-Gathering Formation went dark. The formation stopped working, but Lee Hyun did not notice.

Two years passed.

Squeak! Squeak-squeak!

The fuzzbees flew into the stone chamber.

These were not their usual cheerful cries, but sharp, urgent squeaks. The little fellows circled above Lee Hyun’s head, then bit down on the hem of his clothes and tugged.

Lee Hyun waved them away irritably.

Squeak-squeak-squeak-squeak!

The fuzzbees would not give up. Nor was it just one or two of them. Every fuzzbee in the tunnel had gathered, swarming over his body and squeaking noisily.

Eventually, Lee Hyun sat up.

When he went out to the spirit fields, he found the reservoir nearly dry. The water pipes were empty, the soil had begun to crack, and the leaves of some of the weaker spirit herbs were starting to wilt.

Lee Hyun stared at the scene for a long time.

Then he raised a hand.

Patter-patter-patter―

Rain conjured by the Spirit Rain Art poured into the reservoir.

Lee Hyun stood there, one hand raised and his mind blank, until the reservoir was full.

Even after it filled, the rain continued for a long time.

Water kept spilling over the brim, and the drainage channels carried it away as though nothing had changed.

The fuzzbees hovered around Lee Hyun as though worried about him.

Lee Hyun returned to the stone chamber and lay down again.

After that, he dragged himself up whenever the fuzzbees came swarming in. Once he had refilled the reservoir or cleared a blocked water pipe, he went straight back and lay down.

...

Twenty years passed.

Lee Hyun’s body had wasted away.

The spiritual power of his Primordial Body remained abundant, but his flesh told a different story. Barely sustained by the occasional Hunger-Warding Pill, his body had grown so thin that his bones stood out beneath his skin.

One day, he picked a lotus seed from the pond.

He shelled it and put it in his mouth.

He could not taste a thing.

The next day, he picked a Stone Honey Peach. Again, he could taste nothing.

The day after that, he ate two lotus seeds.

Little by little, Lee Hyun began eating again.

Eventually, he went aboveground to gather nuts and fruit on the mountain. Its colors had changed with the seasons. Lee Hyun looked on without interest.

Some of his strength returned, but he still had no desire to do anything.

...

Forty years passed.

One day, Lee Hyun went to a mortal county seat for the first time in ages and stopped in front of a bookstore.

Stacks of popular novels were on display.

He recognized none of the titles. Tastes had changed over the past forty years.

Lee Hyun picked up a book and paid for it without giving it much thought. Back in the tunnel, he opened it.

It took him a month to finish. Once, he would have read that much in a single shichen (about two hours).

After that, Lee Hyun occasionally went to the county seat to buy popular novels. Most were not very good. Very occasionally, he found a decent one.

...

Sixty years passed.

The book Lee Hyun brought back that day was titled 《The Teahouse Beneath the Thousand-Year Pine》.

Its cover showed an old pine tree and a small teahouse beneath it.

The protagonist was an old rogue cultivator who had lost his Dao.

In his youth, he had been a genius who dreamed of reaching Nascent Soul. But a failed breakthrough to the next realm had brought even his hard-earned cultivation level crashing down. By the time he left the cultivation world and returned to the mundane world, his entire family had passed away.

He opened a teahouse beneath an old pine along a mountain road.

All sorts of guests came to the teahouse.

A young sword cultivator on his way to a secret realm stopped for tea. He promised to stop by again on his way back, but never returned.

An old mortal searching for his daughter came by. Several years later, he returned holding his daughter’s hand.

A demonic cultivator on the run took shelter there. The owner served him tea, too.

But fewer and fewer guests returned.

Lee Hyun read the book slowly.

Whenever a guest left, he closed the book and lay there for a long time before opening it again.

The final chapter of the final volume.

The teahouse owner was now so old that he might close his eyes for the last time at any moment. There were no guests that day, either.

He washed the teacups, fetched water, and set it to heat over the brazier.

As he waited for the water to boil, he thought.

He had thought he was spending his life waiting for those who had left.

The guests who never returned, the family who had gone before him.

He had believed he was keeping the teahouse open for their sake.

But he had been wrong.

He had not been waiting only for those who would never return.

He had also been boiling water for someone new who might arrive that day.

And he enjoyed those moments spent brewing tea with that water and drinking it.

Hssss―

The water over the brazier began to boil.

The old man added the tea leaves.

The book ended there.

Lee Hyun lay with the book open on his chest.

...

Seventy years passed.

Lee Hyun took the drawing board and brush out of his storage pouch.

Even after taking them out, he left them untouched for a whole month.

Then one day, he painted his first picture.

It was a fuzzbee.

It was a mess. The wings were crooked, and the body looked more like a potato than a ball of fluff. If Wang Shulin had seen it, she would have doubled over laughing.

Squeak?

The fuzzbee that had been his model looked at the painting and tilted its head.

“...Doesn’t it look like you?”

Squeak!

The fuzzbee fired a pellet of dung at the painting, punching a hole through it.

“You’re an honest one, aren’t you?”

The next day, he painted a lotus seed. The day after that, a Stone Honey Peach. The next day, Bonefuzz’s bones.

Each day, he painted one thing he had never painted before.

At first, there was plenty to paint. Everything in the tunnel was a new subject.

After about a month, he seemed to have painted most of the obvious, easy subjects. Lee Hyun began searching every corner of the tunnel. The grain of the rock walls, droplets of water clinging to the reservoir, a single strand of fur shed by a fuzzbee.

Then he opened the stone door to Spirit Field No. 3-9.

And stopped in his tracks.

The Heaven-Origin Divine Tree stood before him.

When he first planted it, it had been a sapling less than two chi (about 66 cm) tall. Over the centuries he had lived with Wang Shulin, it had flourished, and by the time she passed away, it was already tall enough to touch the cavern ceiling.

That tree had stood alone for seventy years.

The Qi-Gathering Formation had stopped working long ago. Throughout the years of Lee Hyun’s neglect, the tree must have had nowhere near enough spiritual qi.

Yet the tree had not died.

Its leaves had grown thicker, and its branches had spread sideways along the rocky ceiling. Its roots had thickened too, gripping the soil of the spirit field firmly.

It was growing slowly, very slowly, but growing all the same.

Lee Hyun stood before the tree for a long time.

Then he took spirit stones from his storage pouch and fitted them into the Qi-Gathering Formation.

As the formation plate lit up again, spiritual qi slowly resumed its flow toward the tree.

That day, he painted the Heaven-Origin Divine Tree.

...

Eighty years passed.

For the first time in many years, Lee Hyun appeared at one of the Two Heavens Society’s contact points.

The members there nearly jumped out of their skins when the figure in the badger mask appeared. Some had thought he was dead.

“Society Head, where have you been all this time...?”

“I took a little break.”

...

Ninety years passed.

More than seven thousand sheets of paper lay stacked beneath the drawing board.

By painting one thing each day, just as she had, Lee Hyun had come to understand something.

There were still so many things in the world he had never painted.

The moss on the reservoir today was different from yesterday’s. A fuzzbee had brought back a spirit insect in its mouth today, a little guy he had never seen before.

...

It was the hundredth year since Lee Hyun had shut himself away in the tunnel like a broken man.

That morning, he poured water into a pot and lit a fire beneath it.

Hssss―

The water began to boil.

Lee Hyun squatted in front of the pot.

He could find a little enjoyment even in watching the bubbles rise.

Lee Hyun took a handful of noodles from his storage pouch. They were ordinary wheat noodles from the mundane world, which he had bought in the county seat a couple of days earlier.

He added the noodles to the boiling water.

...

The noodles tasted good.

The flavor was nothing special.

A little salt, a little spice, a few dried mountain greens.

Even so, they tasted good.

That alone made it a pretty good day.

After eating the noodles, he felt oddly full and drowsy, despite being a Foundation Establishment cultivator.

Lee Hyun rolled onto his left side.

And he soon fell asleep, just like a mortal in the mundane world.

...

He seemed to have had a warm, nostalgic dream.

He thought someone might have been laughing beside him.

He opened his eyes.

Lee Hyun took stock of his feelings.

He no longer felt despondent.

He slowly rose to his feet and stretched.

Then he tried to smile.

The smile came naturally now.

And so Lee Hyun let go of his grief and found his strength again.

Chapter 90

With his spirits restored, Lee Hyun first took out the stone tablet.

It was a flat piece of stone with slightly worn corners.

He wiped away the dust with his hand, revealing the characters he had carved into it long ago.

【Age: 2,208】

【Realm: Foundation Establishment Stage 7 (lower dantian), Foundation Establishment Stage 4 (rest of the body)】

“...I haven’t updated this in ages.”

The record dated back to when he had advanced his lower dantian to late Foundation Establishment at Baoguang Temple.

It would have been convenient if the numbers changed on their own.

Unfortunately, his handmade status screen had no such function.

Lee Hyun closed his eyes and slowly circulated his qi according to the Primordial One-Qi Art.

After several qi circulation cycles, a gentle warmth spread throughout his body.

He examined his body from within, then began updating the stone tablet.

【Age: 2,840】

【Realm: Foundation Establishment Stage 8 (entire body)】

【Spiritual Power: 7,460 → 18,100】

【Constitution: Primordial Body, Foundation Establishment Stage 8】

【Cultivation Art: Primordial One-Qi Art (Foundation Establishment Section)】

‘These numbers have gotten ridiculous...’

In terms of total spiritual power alone, he probably surpassed most Golden Core cultivators.

The figures on the stone tablet were estimates of his current reserves, calculated using the same scale he had always used. There was still room to accumulate more even within Stage 8, and he would need ever greater amounts of spiritual power as he progressed toward Stage 9 and Great Perfection.

Although he had spent the past hundred years living without much motivation, he had made tremendous progress while living with Wang Shulin. Her successive breakthroughs must have spurred him on at the time.

Rather than focusing on further advancing his lower dantian, which was already ahead, he had worked to bring his cultivation level into balance throughout his body.

Had he cultivated alone, moving between tunnels where spiritual qi was sparse and the Two Heavens Society’s vein seats, he would have struggled to reach this point in the same amount of time.

Throughout his time with Wang Shulin, he had continually obtained and taken pills for his own cultivation, shared her access to a Tier 3 spirit vein, and practiced a dual cultivation art with her. Those advantages had made his progress possible.

Lee Hyun next examined his primordial spirit.

The vow power that arose as he practiced the Sutra of Refining Intent into Vow was purer and more potent than before.

In this cultivation art, a mind seal was formed when the ability to establish and sustain an intent became ingrained in the primordial spirit through visualization and spirit refinement. That tempered will provided a foundation for cultivating vow power without being bound to any particular vow.

His primordial spirit and divine sense, both honed through long cultivation, had also grown stronger.

‘I see. Is it because I’ve experienced life’s joys and sorrows and finally found it in myself to start living again...?’

Wang Shulin’s face suddenly came to mind. His heart ached, but the vow power he had summoned did not waver.

He no longer needed to shut out his grief or force his mind to remain still. He could hold to his intent even as emotions rose and fell.

He could now control more vow power with greater precision and less effort.

...

Updating his handmade status screen made Lee Hyun think he ought to review the techniques he had learned as well.

He took jade slips from his storage pouch and laid them out on the table.

Some were old, while others had been acquired during the latter part of his stay at Baoguang Temple. A few included brief explanations left by Wang Shulin.

Spiritual qi and cultivation pills were not all he had gained during his centuries at Baoguang Temple.

He had used his accumulated merit to study inheritances and, as Wang Shulin’s direct disciple, had also received Dharma teachings from her in person. Two in particular had appealed to him.

《Sumeru Mountain-Suppressing Seal》, 《Vajra Wisdom Sword Scripture》

The former was a much more demanding seal art than the Demon-Subduing Seal.

The technique did more than create a giant palm imprint and slam it down. The spiritual power forming the seal interlocked in layers, concentrating force at the point of impact and suppressing the target’s movement.

It required considerable vow power and precise control, and consumed so much spiritual power that an ordinary Foundation Establishment cultivator could scarcely hope to execute it properly.

Lee Hyun, however, was already well practiced in condensing Buddha-Light True Qi with the Demon-Subduing Seal. Through the Condensed-Essence Grasping Hand, he had also learned to control spiritual power shaped into a hand with great precision. Since the Sumeru Mountain-Suppressing Seal layered power within a fixed palm imprint, he could draw on the foundations he had built through both inheritances.

He formed a hand seal with one hand, and a deep golden palm appeared in the air.

Fine golden lines overlapped across its palm and fingers. The energy condensed within the small palm imprint was far denser than that of his previous Demon-Subduing Seal, enough to make the surrounding air feel heavy.

Lee Hyun glanced around Tunnel No. 3, then released the hand seal.

‘Using this in here would be a disaster.’

There was no need to wreck the tunnel on his first day back in action.

Next, he tried the Spirit-Jolting Needle Method.

As he gathered a strand of divine sense, vow power seeped into it.

The needle, slender and firmly condensed, rose above his head before circling behind his back. It then split into several strands and merged back into one.

Its movement was smooth and unimpeded. Even with more vow power and divine sense infused into it than before, the needle held its form.

Rather than launching it, Lee Hyun dissolved it and drew its power back into his primordial spirit.

‘Not bad.’

Lee Hyun then slipped into the cavern wall and began traveling through the ore veins around the tunnel. He slowed where different minerals were intricately intertwined, but nothing blocked his way. After making a full circuit, he returned to the tunnel passage.

It was the Metal Escape Art.

‘I’m not as proficient with it as I am with the Earth Escape Art, but I’ve reached Minor Attainment....’

...

The Vajra Wisdom Sword Scripture was a Way of the Sword inheritance from the Buddhist tradition. It refined the intent carried by a sword, combining divine sense and vow power with sword qi.

Its foundational Dharma teachings trained the practitioner to form a clear image of a sword in the mind and gather intent and divine sense into that image. The Sword Condensation Section that followed explained how to infuse that refined power into actual sword qi and condense them into a single whole.

What he found especially appealing was that it could complement the sword qi and sword light he had learned from the Great Unity Heavenly Dipper Sword Canon. The vow power and divine sense carried within the sword qi would pressure an opponent together, allowing it to do more than cut flesh. It could also disrupt the opponent’s control over their primordial spirit.

He would not need to abandon this foundation even after reaching Golden Core and learning the Great Unity Earthly Fiend Sword Canon. He could still infuse his intent into stronger sword qi.

For now, however, he had only reached Minor Attainment in the foundational Dharma teachings. He was accustomed to forming the image of a sword in his mind, but when practicing the Sword Condensation Section, his vow power and sword qi still refused to merge properly.

Among his other inheritances from Baoguang Temple, the most profound remained the Sumeru Visualization Scripture.

When he visualized the All-Hearing Heavenly King, even the tiny patterns on the parasol and pagoda appeared distinctly in his mind. He could maintain the visualization while using other techniques without difficulty.

Yet giving the form he projected outside his body any real force would require magical power that had undergone the qualitative transformation of the Golden Core realm. The technique helped temper his primordial spirit, but he still could not use the Dharma manifestation to attack an enemy or defend himself.

...

He continued updating the stone tablet.

【Techniques (Minor Attainment): Vajra Wisdom Sword Scripture, Sumeru Visualization Scripture (All-Hearing Heavenly King manifestation), Sumeru Mountain-Suppressing Seal, Metal Escape Art...】

【Techniques (Major Attainment): Sutra of Refining Intent into Vow...】

【Techniques (Perfection): Great Unity Heavenly Dipper Sword Art, Spirit-Refining Essentials, Spirit-Jolting Needle Method...】

【Crafts (Tier 2): spirit-plant cultivation, alchemy, insect control, puppet crafting, formation, artifact refining】

His proficiency varied so much from one craft to another that classifying all of them as Tier 2 was a stretch. Yet neither Tier 1 nor Tier 3 quite fit either.

These specialized disciplines, also known as the Hundred Cultivation Crafts, encompassed an enormous variety of subjects and methods even within the same tier.

For example, even a Tier 3 alchemist could fail to refine an unfamiliar Tier 2 pill. Conversely, a Tier 1 artifact refiner with modest overall attainments might, after a lifetime working with the same materials and restrictions, refine a supreme-grade magic tool for Foundation Establishment cultivators to an astonishing standard.

Of course, the latter would still need something to compensate for their shortcomings, such as a Tier 2 spirit beast capable of controlling flames.

Lee Hyun considered spirit-plant cultivation and alchemy his only real strengths. In the other fields, he still had far too much to learn.

But listing all six fields like this did have one advantage: it made him feel good!

For the first time in ages, he propped up the stone tablet and admired it, savoring his sense of accomplishment.

...

Lee Hyun turned his attention to the water tanks next.

He had kept them filled, but he now realized how long he had left Tunnel No. 3 almost entirely unattended.

When he drained a tank, he found fine roots and silt matted together in the bottom corners, along with dry leaves that had washed in from somewhere.

“What a mess...”

Lee Hyun lifted the debris from the bottom with spiritual power and used the Cleansing Art to remove everything clinging to the walls. He replaced the cracked bamboo pipes with new ones and adjusted the slope wherever water tended to pool.

The fuzzbees swarmed over to watch whenever he drained a tank, and peered inside each pipe he lifted out. Whenever a small spirit insect emerged from a pile of soil, several of them pounced at once.

The fellows seemed delighted by the thorough cleaning of Tunnel No. 3. Pretending to help Lee Hyun, they sent the Bonefuzzes creaking about the place.

The sight prompted Lee Hyun to inspect the Bonefuzzes as well once he had finished cleaning.

He dismantled nearly fifty Bonefuzzes one by one, replacing every worn or damaged part. He also replaced their spirit stones with fresh ones before reassembling them.

...

After the maintenance was done, Lee Hyun took out broad, shallow stone bowls, gathered clear water with the Spirit Rain Art, and mixed in plenty of Hundred-Flower Honey.

As the sweet fragrance spread, the buzzing of wings suddenly grew louder.

“You’ve worked hard all this time. Let’s have a special treat.”

The snack would make the fuzzbees happy, but it would do nothing to further their growth as spirit insects.

Lee Hyun watched them crowd around the bowls for a while.

There were old fuzzbees in the tunnel that had been alive since he first brought them there, as well as younger fellows born afterward. But because their bodies renewed themselves with every molt, it was hard to tell from their appearance how long any of them had lived.

Without these fellows, he might have let his spirit fields go to ruin. They acted as though they took pride in protecting the countless plants in the fields, and whenever the water tanks ran dry, they came to get Lee Hyun up and moving.

“Thank you.”

...

Sorting out his records for the spirit fields took longer than cleaning the water tanks.

He had been planting young spirit herbs in the gaps left whenever he removed older ones to sell off or use in alchemy, until each spirit field had become a confusing jumble.

Lee Hyun compared the entries in his old cultivation records with the spirit herbs themselves, one by one.

Perhaps because he had neglected them for a time, or perhaps because of Tunnel No. 3’s environment, the rate at which the older spirit plants accumulated medicine age had been steadily slowing.

He examined the veins in their leaves and the color of their stems, probing around their roots with his divine sense. Then he rested a finger against the stem of an old Bone-Rot Flower.

‘About nine hundred years.’

At the growth rate recorded in his old ledger, its medicine age should have exceeded 920 years. Yet its actual medicinal strength was a little less than expected.

If its medicine age could exceed a thousand years and its medicinal potency grow to rival that of a Tier 4 spirit plant, its value would rise even further. Whether simply giving it enough time would suffice was something he would have to investigate.

‘The spiritual qi drawn in by the Earth Vein Flowers doesn’t seem quite enough. I may need to apply the principles of a Tier 1 Qi-Gathering Formation to improve the way spiritual qi circulates through the entire tunnel.’

Lee Hyun recalled the buildings he had seen in his past life. Engineers on Earth designed all manner of circulation systems for large buildings. Such installations circulated air and water, supplied electricity....

But he had no background knowledge in that field.

That was all right. He could simply start researching it now.

‘What if I sent each spirit field as much spiritual qi as it needed, the way a central air-conditioning system sends air throughout a building?’

He could not conjure spiritual qi out of nothing, and running a Qi-Gathering Formation consumed spirit stones.

Still, if he could keep energy from accumulating in one area or leaking away needlessly, the same number of spirit stones might provide a better environment.

Drawing in large amounts of spiritual qi from outside, however, might reveal the traces he had hidden with the Spirit-Concealing Formation.

‘It would be hard to make this work in Tunnel No. 3... I should keep it in mind for when I build Tunnel No. 4.’

...

The older Yin Water Lotuses and Stone Honey Peach trees had medicine ages of around 870 years.

Lee Hyun picked the ripe Stone Honey Peaches and carefully placed all but one in jade caskets.

After putting the jade caskets into his storage pouch, he bit into the peach he had set aside.

Crunch.

Sweet juice and a refreshing coolness flooded his mouth.

...

He paused briefly before the Ringless Divine Tree.

He took out the old ledger to check. It seemed the tree had sprouted around 1,400 years ago.

“Didn’t it say dark blue lightning markings appear after two thousand years, and it starts emitting Profound Nether Frost Lightning after five thousand?”

Lee Hyun looked at the tree and laughed despite himself.

“You’re even slower than I am.”

Concentrating spiritual qi around this tree with a Qi-Gathering Formation would do no good. A reference guide he had read long ago stated that forcing its growth with dense spiritual qi would only stunt it instead.

Only the passage of time could nurture the Ringless Divine Tree. That made this barren tunnel unexpectedly well suited to growing it.

Lee Hyun checked the moisture beneath the tree, then simply adjusted the water channels so the water pooled near its roots could drain away slowly.

He closed the ledger and moved on to Spirit Field No. 3-9.

The Heaven-Origin Divine Tree’s branches stretched along the rocky ceiling. Spirit Field No. 3-9 was simply too cramped for it.

He widened the cavern a little and thinned out only the small branches that were pressing against one another and hampering growth.

He also adjusted the existing Tier 1 Qi-Gathering Formation to cover the expanded root system.

‘Keeping it running at this strength will cost about twenty low-grade spirit stones a year. Still, that works out to twenty mid-grade spirit stones every hundred years, so it’s hardly a burden.’

He had planted it more than six hundred years ago, yet there were still no flower buds at the branch tips.

...

A few days later.

Lee Hyun was sorting through some ten thousand drawings.

As he laid two drawings of the same crack in a rock face side by side, a passage from the Vajra Wisdom Sword Scripture suddenly came to mind.

「Let intent precede the sword tip, yet do not let the sword tip stray from that intent.」

When he first read it, he had thought it was merely stating the obvious.

Wasn’t it simply a matter of deciding where to cut and then cutting there?

Yet whenever he practiced the Sword Condensation Section, his vow power had failed to permeate his sword qi evenly.

Without thinking, Lee Hyun traced a line in the drawing with his finger. The motion resembled the gestures he had made while contemplating Zheng Yubai’s demonstration of the Mind Sword.

‘Huh...?’

Lee Hyun picked up the Sinking Moon Sword.

He formed a clear image of a single thrust in his mind, then guided his spiritual power, divine sense, and vow power together, following that intent.

Sword qi gathered at the tip, and his vow power and divine sense condensed together along the slender blade.

He moved his wrist, and the sword tip advanced, piercing a narrow hole in a stone slab he had set up for practice.

He immediately withdrew the sword qi and picked up the stone slab to examine it.

The vow power had held together even at the moment the sword qi struck the stone.

‘This is....’

He raised his sword again.

This time, the condensed power came apart. He paused to recall the sensation, then repeated the thrust. Only on the third attempt did energy similar to what he had felt before gather at the sword tip.

He lowered his sword and let out a long breath.

‘To think the drawings would help...’

Of course, what had helped him most was the Vajra Wisdom Sword Scripture, along with the growth of his primordial spirit and mind seal.

Just as the martial path inheritance passed down through Zheng Yubai’s family had provided the basis for his Mind Sword, the Vajra Wisdom Sword Scripture could serve as Lee Hyun’s foundation.

Fifteen days later, Xianghe Kingdom.

Lee Hyun walked along the lower slopes of a mountain, keeping out of sight.

The stone steps leading to the burial grounds had been replaced.

The gravestones were well tended, and an incense burner that seemed to have been replaced recently stood in front of Wang Shulin’s grave.

He briefly visited the children’s graves as well.

The longing had not faded, but memories of the times they had laughed together now came to him before the grief.

He ran a hand over the gravestones, then left without lingering long.

...

A few days later, at a cultivator market in eastern Xu Kingdom.

A small shop selling medicinal ingredients.

When Lee Hyun entered wearing his Badger mask, the member inside struggled to conceal their surprise as they asked,

“Are you looking for any particular medicinal ingredients?”

Lee Hyun held out a jade token instead of answering. Only after checking its restrictions did the member bow deeply.

“Greetings, Society Head.”

“Is the person in charge here?”

“They are in the back.”

Lee Hyun descended into the underground stone chamber.

A cultivator wearing a Goose mask rose from their seat.

“I’ve been in charge of this place for thirteen years.”

“And your predecessor?”

“They reached the end of their lifespan.”

Lee Hyun nodded.

Jade slips were already laid out on the table.

“Some of the newer members have asked whether the Society Head actually exists.”

Lee Hyun answered while reading the jade slips.

“I heard much the same thing twenty years ago.”

“Some have asked whether the name Badger is passed from one person to the next....”

“What does it matter? The person behind the Goose mask keeps changing too. What’s the latest on the Nanming Twelve-Sect Alliance?”

Lee Hyun asked a few more questions, then settled the trading matters that had been on hold for so long.

Once he had checked the payments for the goods he had entrusted to them and listed the medicinal ingredients and pills he planned to sell from now on, the voice behind the Goose mask brightened.

“Will you be supplying Foundation Establishment Pills and Tier 2 Spirit-Calming Pills again as well?”

“There won’t be many.”

“There are people waiting for them.”

Lee Hyun left a few trade requests with them, then checked the news from the outside world as well.

The reports covered changes in kingdoms and sects, developments involving spirit veins and cultivator markets, and the activities of well-known cultivators.

There were records concerning Baoguang Temple too, but fortunately, nothing in the reports struck him as an immediate threat.

The Nanming Twelve-Sect Alliance had not expanded its territory in quite some time. He could not tell whether it had given up on expansion, whether the Nine Kingdoms of Yunzhou were too powerful, or whether there was some other reason.

Twenty years later.

An uninhabited valley a short distance from Xu Kingdom’s southern coast.

Lee Hyun sat before a pill furnace, his fingers moving.

Fine flame threads wove in and out of the pill furnace. With Refining complete, the medicinal liquids swirled at different speeds, gradually mingling through gaps opened by the flames.

Essence-Cultivating Pill.

Of the cultivation pills Baoguang Temple passed down for late Foundation Establishment, it was among those with the greatest medicinal strength. The Refining process was more demanding than for the Essence-Augmenting Pill, Dew-Condensing Pill, or Jade Marrow Pill. Its medicinal strength was so intense that even late Foundation Establishment cultivators needed ample time to refine and absorb it after taking the pill.

Lee Hyun had been making these pills since his days at Baoguang Temple. Since resuming cultivation, he had been refining his own supply while exploring how much further he could improve their quality using the same pill recipe.

Raising his entire body’s realm by a single Stage required far too many pills. If he could increase the medicinal strength each pill provided, he could save both materials and time.

In the process, he had reread the old jade slip recording Chen Xiaoying’s demonstration countless times.

Before, he had not understood why she chose those exact moments to adjust her fire control or divide the medicinal liquid. But as he gained experience through repeated failures in his own alchemy, he gradually came to understand her reasons.

In several recent attempts, spiritual qi had even begun gathering around pills refined to supreme grade.

That was why he had left the tunnel for this attempt.

On the off chance that the phenomenon he had witnessed long ago occurred again, he did not want to face it underground, with his spirit fields nearby.

...

The medicinal strength within the pill furnace separated into several clusters.

The pills that took shape first descended toward the bottom. Lee Hyun kept only the one with the smoothest internal flow near the top.

Instead of rushing to form the next hand seals, he watched how the medicinal strength responded. Outwardly, the flow seemed even, but one current inside had yet to align with the rest.

When a single flame thread touched that spot, the knot of energy loosened a little.

Lee Hyun immediately shifted the flame to one side, opening a path for the loosened medicinal strength to flow through.

The medicinal strength made a full circuit, then settled into its proper place.

At that moment, the light seeping from the pill’s surface receded inward.

Lee Hyun’s fingers slowed almost to a stop.

A wind stirred in the valley.

The surrounding spiritual qi was moving toward the pill furnace. It was not being drawn in by a formation. The scattered energy gathered as though responding to the flow within that single tiny pill.

Lee Hyun slowly lifted his head.

A black speck formed in the clear sky.

‘Huh? It actually worked?’

The speck expanded as it drew in water qi, soon becoming a small cloud a little over one zhang (about 3.3 m) across.

Lightning flickered beneath it.

Crackle.

Chapter 91

Crackle.

Purple lightning flickered beneath the cloud.

Lee Hyun opened the lid of the pill furnace.

A pill slowly rose from within. Spiritual qi swirled over its round surface, while slender flame threads coiled around it.

‘A pill tribulation really is coming....’

The corners of his mouth lifted slightly.
