It was a valuable mineral used as a primary material for refining or repairing magic treasures.

False Badger seemed to have been saving it for a long time, either to repair his Golden Light Pagoda or to forge a new magic treasure.

Lee Hyun sealed the spirit material back inside the box and put it in his storage pouch.

...

He set the jade slips from the spoils to one side.

They contained a mixture of cultivation methods, techniques, instructions for using artifacts, and transaction records.

As far as he could tell from a quick look, none of it was particularly valuable.

Lee Hyun set aside only the records on the Golden Light Pagoda and Mother-Child Rings, then sorted and stored the rest.

Then he examined the gold-threaded Badger mask again.

The bridge of the nose and the muzzle were finely shaped, and the inside was even lined with soft leather for a snug, comfortable fit.

‘Isn’t this nice...? I’ll wear this one from now on.’

...

Finally, he examined the magic treasures.

False Badger’s Golden Light Pagoda had shrunk to fit in his palm. It was hard to believe this was the same treasure that had grown nearly to the ceiling at Qingshi Ridge and unleashed beams of light.

The pagoda’s exterior bore marks where the Sinking Moon Sword’s sword qi had grazed it.

Lee Hyun rubbed the spot with a fingertip.

The marks were very shallow.

‘It’s sturdy.’

When he cautiously extended his divine sense into it, he sensed a complex web of restrictions within. Most importantly, the energy its previous owner had imparted through prolonged nurturing had seeped deep into the treasure.

The real problem, however, was how to use the magic treasure.

The restrictions in a magic treasure were designed for a Golden Core cultivator’s magical power. Lee Hyun would have to investigate further to see whether a large quantity of Foundation Establishment spiritual power alone would be enough to operate it fully.

Nor would it be easy for him to turn the spirit materials into other artifacts better suited to his needs.

Melting down and refining Tier 3 spirit materials such as Golden-Thread Cold Iron, or completed magic treasures, required the core flame of a Golden Core cultivator or a Tier 3 flame.

Here, too, the quality of magical power mattered. He would struggle with Foundation Establishment spiritual power alone, no matter how much he used.

Lee Hyun chose not to push it and withdrew his divine sense for now.

He then took out the Azure Thunder Mother-Child Rings he had collected and examined them as well.

Eight smaller rings overlapped a single large one. Despite being knocked away by Lee Hyun’s sword qi, they showed almost no visible damage.

The stele-shaped defensive magic treasure, on the other hand, had a crack near its base.

Apparently, he had pressed down too hard with the Sumeru Mountain-Suppressing Seal.

‘That’s a shame.’

He had not had the luxury of holding back for the sake of his spoils, so it could not be helped.

Lee Hyun sealed the Golden Light Pagoda and Azure Thunder Mother-Child Rings separately and put them in his storage pouch, then packed away the damaged treasures on their own.

Even the fragments of the shattered red mirror and the cracked stele would retain some value as spirit materials.

...

After putting away the spirit stones and miscellaneous spoils, Lee Hyun thought back to the cultivation plan he had recently made, which included producing Essence-Cultivating Pills through alchemy.

That plan left him with an annual shortfall of just under four hundred mid-grade spirit stones.

Even after deducting the spirit stones he had returned to the members at Qingshi Ridge and given to the bereaved families, today’s haul alone would cover that shortfall for decades.

Of course, repairing his sword and shield and acquiring other artifacts would cost money too.

Still, he would not have to dig up and sell his older spirit herbs for some time.

‘And their medicine age will keep increasing in the meantime.’

...

Ten days later, at Tunnel No. 3.

Lee Hyun was examining the Sinking Moon Sword.

The hairline cracks in the blade were not deep. The problem was that the tip was slightly chipped.

Lee Hyun first used his divine sense to examine the points where the hairline cracks met the blade’s restrictions.

Fortunately, the core restrictions were undamaged.

When he bought the Sinking Moon Sword, he had been told it contained Tier 2 Thick Earth Refined Metal, which made scratches and fine cracks easy to repair. Perhaps it could be repaired.

But a clumsy repair attempt could ruin the properties of a sword listed in the Nanming Hundred Artifacts Register, and there would be no undoing that damage.

The Six-Leaf Shield, in particular, seemed far too badly damaged for him to repair himself.

With his limited knowledge of the artifact-refining art, he was reluctant to work on either one. Lee Hyun decided to visit cultivator markets in search of a skilled artifact refiner.

At the same time.

A cultivator market in northern Jing Kingdom.

A cultivator wearing a Black Wolf mask set down a jade slip.

Opposite him stood a Foundation Establishment cultivator in a Crow mask.

“Crane and Badger are both dead?”

“That is what the reports say.”

“Tell me what you know for certain.”

Crow offered him another jade slip.

“The hall at Qingshi Ridge collapsed. The warehouse was empty, and those who handled communications had relocated.”

“Who took the goods?”

“It appears they were distributed to the parties involved in the transactions.”

Black Wolf’s hand went still.

“They returned them?”

“Yes. It was not looting. It seems they identified the owners of the goods and the amounts owed, then settled the accounts through the existing contact network. We have only been able to verify some of the transactions, though...”

“Who do they say did it?”

“Inspector Cicada.”

Black Wolf was silent for a moment.

He had heard of Inspector Cicada before. The man supposedly answered directly to the former society head, traveling from region to region to trade and occasionally inspect the bases.

“He did it alone?”

“No one else was named in the message.”

Black Wolf tapped a finger against the table.

‘Impossible... Crane and False Badger were Golden Core cultivators... Is Inspector Cicada really that strong? Could Society Head Badger from all those years ago still be alive? If the same man has survived all this time... he would have to be at least a Nascent Soul cultivator!?’

Of course, the position of society head could have been passed down from one successor to the next. But he had never personally confirmed the former society head’s death.

Suddenly, he found himself afraid of the Two Heavens Society.

Chapter 94

Black Wolf stared down at the jade slip for a long while.

Crane and False Badger were anything but weak. Even Black Wolf would have struggled to emerge unscathed from a fight against both at once.

Yet after killing those two, their attacker had even sorted through the goods and ledgers in the warehouse?

This had been no hurried strike followed by a retreat. The attacker had stayed there for quite some time after the fighting was over.

‘Did the possibility of a trap not concern them? Or the chance that another senior elder might arrive? If a Nascent Soul cultivator is behind this...’

A sense of dread crept over Black Wolf.

‘Could that cultivator already be close by...?’

- Nothing in this world happens by chance, and by the time the danger becomes clear, it is already too late.

It was the iron rule Black Wolf had lived by while enduring the hardships of a rogue cultivator’s life and rising from nothing to the Golden Core realm.

Across from Black Wolf, Crow asked cautiously.

“Should I send word for the remaining senior elders to gather here?”

Black Wolf’s eyes narrowed briefly before he spoke, his voice as calm as ever.

“Yes. Tell the senior elder in Heng Kingdom and the one in northern Jing Kingdom to come here. You are to keep watch for anyone coming from Qingshi Ridge.”

“Yes, grand elder!”

Black Wolf immediately opened his storage pouch once Crow had left.

...

The next day, Black Wolf’s residence was deathly quiet.

After spending the night watching the outskirts, Crow returned to find the secret warehouse’s stone door standing wide open. The sight left them speechless.

The warehouse was empty.

Black Wolf’s personal collection was gone, along with the goods entrusted to the outpost by members and every spirit stone the Council of Senior Elders had amassed through tolls.

Only ash and fragments of shattered jade slips remained on the shelves that had held the ledgers.

A single jade casket, however, sat alone on a table farther inside.

It held the members’ primordial-spirit imprints.

Ten days later.

A small contact outpost in western Xuan Kingdom.

Settlement records lay before Lee Hyun, who wore the Cicada mask.

Across from him sat a cultivator wearing the Otter mask.

Until recently, that person had been Toad.

“Word has arrived from Jing Kingdom. Black Wolf reportedly took everything and fled, including the members’ entrusted goods and spirit stones.”

“Cunning bastard.”

“Black Wolf even abandoned Crow, who served directly under him. Crow passed on all the outpost locations and transaction details they knew to us, then disappeared.”

“What about the imprints of the Jing Kingdom members?”

“The entire jade casket was left behind. Crow handed that over as well.”

“Bring it here. Once I’ve checked the imprints, I’ll remove them.”

Otter bowed his head.

“And the remaining senior elders?”

“The senior elder in Heng Kingdom also took the goods and fled. The other senior elder in northern Jing Kingdom left their residence, and no one has heard from them since.”

...

Once the senior elders fled, the outposts that had sided with them rushed to contact the inspector.

Two Golden Core senior elders had died at Qingshi Ridge following a visit from the inspector, Cicada. Then the grand elder and the remaining senior elders had disappeared as well. It was clear whose rules they should follow.

After checking the contents of the jade casket against the binding method, Lee Hyun removed the remaining primordial-spirit imprints.

He also had records of the stolen goods and proof of the transactions collected. After returning the property recovered at Qingshi Ridge to its owners, he ordered that some of the remaining spirit stones be used to compensate those who had suffered losses.

That would not cover every loss, and Lee Hyun could not pay for everything himself.

Nor could he scour several countries for the senior elders who had fled.

He did not even know what Black Wolf looked like, and both the Sinking Moon Sword and Six-Leaf Shield were damaged.

He recorded the Council of Senior Elders’ abuses and all verified descriptions of its members, then ordered new contact channels and outposts established to replace those known to the fugitives.

He also investigated the backgrounds of the two dead Golden Core cultivators. Cross-checking the letters and transaction records from their storage pouches against information from other outposts revealed that both were rogue cultivators currently unaffiliated with any great sect. Nothing suggested that a sect had been involved behind the scenes.

...

A few days later, reports began arriving from the other outposts as well.

Trade resumed first in the places that had suffered the least damage, and medicinal ingredients whose supply had been blocked by the Council of Senior Elders began arriving again.

The ingredients for Essence-Cultivating Pills also became easier to obtain than before.

‘Now I can get back to my own work.’

The next day.

Lee Hyun laid out the notes on operating the Golden Light Pagoda and Azure Thunder Mother-Child Rings, then tested both magic treasures.

When he poured Primordial True Qi into them, the Golden Light Pagoda’s surface brightened and the Azure Thunder Mother-Child Rings rose into the air. But that was as far as he got.

Whenever he tried to activate the core restrictions according to the notes, the flow of spiritual power was blocked. Pouring in more made no difference.

‘It seems only a Golden Core cultivator’s magical power will work. In that case...’

There was no reason to keep spoils he could not even use yet.

Still, he was reluctant to sell them in Yunzhou. Cultivators who had known the dead men might recognize their magic treasures.

‘What about selling them in the south?’

The Two Heavens Society had outposts in Kun Kingdom as well.

Kun Kingdom lay within the Nanming Twelve-Sect Alliance’s territory and had little contact with Yunzhou. There was much less chance of anyone knowing who the magic treasures had belonged to.

Lee Hyun submitted a request to arrange a sale.

...

After returning to Tunnel No. 3, he retrieved a jade casket he had stored deep inside.

He released the seal, revealing a small incense burner and a brush lying side by side.

Lotus-petal patterns encircled the incense burner’s body. A faint aura lingered on its lid, the result of years of nurturing.

Beside it lay a magic treasure shaped like a painting brush, called the Cloud-Mist Brush. Its shaft was carved from clear jade, and silver hairs from a spirit beast were neatly bound at the tip.

Wang Shulin had acquired these magic treasures after reaching the Golden Core realm. Following her death, Lee Hyun had collected them along with her storage pouch.

They were in an entirely different class from the ordinary drawing board and brush she had given him before leaving, when she had encouraged him to try painting.

He had tried using these treasures before, only to encounter the same limitation.

Lee Hyun lightly ran his fingertips along the incense burner’s rim and the smooth shaft of the Cloud-Mist Brush.

He could still picture her vividly, painting in the air with incense burning beside her.

He lingered for a while, then returned the incense burner and brush to the jade casket.

He had no wish to sell these treasures. Nor did he intend to erase the traces she had left behind and bond them to himself, or melt them down to make something else.

Three months later, on the western coast of Kun Kingdom.

Luochao Market stood on a black basalt headland jutting into the sea.

The place had an entirely different atmosphere from the cultivator markets of Yunzhou.

At the docks, corpse puppets wrapped tightly in cloth carried cargo. Nearby, a cultivator haggled while feeding spirit insects to a centipede that had crawled out of their sleeve. The stalls displayed dried venomous insects, gu insect eggs, and venom sacs from sea beasts.

Wearing the Lion mask, Lee Hyun entered a dried-seafood shop tucked away in an alley.

An elderly cultivator wearing the Seahorse mask managed the Kun Kingdom outpost.

“So you’re Lion, the inspector who brought the goods from Yunzhou.”

“Where is the buyer?”

“The buyer is already here and wishes to inspect the goods personally before naming a price.”

A female cultivator sat in the underground stone chamber.

Her hair was tied in a high bun, and a sword case as tall as she was stood beside the table. She was not even wearing a mask.

And she was a Golden Core cultivator!

Lee Hyun placed the Golden Light Pagoda, Azure Thunder Mother-Child Rings, a cracked stone stele, and mirror fragments on the table. Her gaze lingered briefly on the shallow marks left by sword qi on the Golden Light Pagoda’s exterior.

“The previous owner’s aura is still strong inside.”

“The owner is gone.”

“I’ll give you one hundred and twenty high-grade spirit stones for the two intact ones.”

“One hundred and sixty.”

“A Foundation Establishment cultivator brings in a Golden Core cultivator’s magic treasures and has the nerve to ask for more?”

As the woman released a wave of razor-sharp pressure, the elderly cultivator in the Seahorse mask quietly edged toward the wall.

Lee Hyun did not answer. He simply extended his divine sense.

The pressure bearing down on him parted to either side as though it had struck an invisible wall. The woman’s eyes narrowed.

‘Tch... The Aura-Concealing Art? I’ve never seen a guy conceal his realm this thoroughly.’

She withdrew her pressure.

“Very well. One hundred and sixty. But the broken mirror and stele fragments must be included.”

“Agreed.”

She took two jade caskets from her sleeve and opened them. Both were packed with high-grade spirit stones.

Lee Hyun accepted the spirit stones and handed over the goods.

...

Before leaving the cultivator market, he also sold the materials from the Silver-Eyed Sea Eagle through Seahorse.

He kept only a few wing bones for his bone puppet research, selling the sealed demon core, claws, beak, and other materials to a merchant house that dealt in demon beast materials.

The intact early Tier 3 demon core fetched 1,300 mid-grade spirit stones. The remaining materials brought in another 320 after the brokerage fee was deducted.

With the accounts settled, Lee Hyun put the spirit stones in his storage pouch and headed north.

Fifteen days later, in Hua Kingdom, north of Xu Kingdom.

Hua Kingdom, one of the Nine Kingdoms of Yunzhou, was home to the Myriad Artifacts Sect, a great sect renowned for its artifact-refining art.

As artifact refiners from the Myriad Artifacts Sect opened workshops nearby or founded cultivation clans, knowledge of the artifact-refining art spread throughout the country.

Qianlu Mountain was a gathering place for these artifact refiners. The cultivator market at its foot was so large that some called it Qianlu Immortal City.

On his way to Qianlu Market, Lee Hyun looked up.

A massive flying boat floated overhead, though he could not tell which sect it belonged to.

Its hull was more than one hundred zhang (about 330 m) long, with passenger cabins arranged across three levels below deck. At the bow sat an enormous bronze crane puppet with folded wings, scanning the wind and clouds ahead with beams of light from its eyes. Human-sized puppets even checked passengers’ jade tokens and carried their luggage.

As he traveled, taking in the sights, Qianlu Mountain soon came into view.

It was an immense mountain with dozens of linked peaks. Chimneys crowded every summit, their smoke forming a red band across the sky.

Earth fire drawn from deep underground shone red through the mountain’s fissures. The whole mountain brightened and dimmed as though it were breathing.

The sky was crowded too.

Palm-sized bird puppets flew in flocks with letters in their beaks. A giant beetle puppet laden with ore descended toward a warehouse halfway up the mountain, its six pairs of wings buzzing.

Higher up, a cultivator who had been testing an unfamiliar disc-shaped magic tool was spiraling downward, trailing smoke.

...

The cultivator market rose in terraces along Qianlu Mountain’s southern slopes.

The lowest level was devoted to trading raw ore and spirit materials. Cart-sized lumps of ore lay piled beside the road, and appraisers scanned them with divine sense while calling out prices. Higher levels offered more processed components, restriction plates, puppet joints, and spirit silk used to weave the sails of flying boats.

Above those streets lay the workshop district.

The ringing of hammers was incessant. Furnace heat spilled into the streets from every building, while flashes from the engraving of restrictions shone through gaps around the doors.

The larger shops even accepted commissions from Golden Core cultivators, while smaller workshops handled only magic tool repairs or the refining of particular components.

Lee Hyun first visited a large shop.

The artisan examined the Sinking Moon Sword and spoke politely.

“We can repair it. However, we have a backlog of commissions from Golden Core Seniors, so it will be about two years before we can begin.”

Lee Hyun put the sword away.

After obtaining estimates from several other workshops, he found that repairing the Sinking Moon Sword alone would cost between 400 and 800 mid-grade spirit stones.

One workshop proposed cutting away the shattered tip and attaching a new one made from a different material. Another examined the Six-Leaf Shield as well and claimed it would perform better if they replaced its entire set of restrictions with newly engraved ones.

Lee Hyun had no wish to spend so many spirit stones on repairs that would change the items’ properties. He only needed them until he reached the Golden Core realm, so he wanted them restored to their familiar original condition.

He visited more workshops before finding a small shop tucked away in an alley.

The owner’s name was Murong Ke.

The elderly cultivator had reached late Foundation Establishment and was well regarded for skill in the artifact-refining art, though somewhat prickly in temperament.

“If you’re in a hurry, go elsewhere.”

Lee Hyun set down the sword case.

“Look it over first and tell me whether it can be repaired.”

Murong Ke took out the Sinking Moon Sword and examined it at length.

Only after inspecting the tip, studying the hairline cracks along the blade, and tracing the restrictions within did Murong Ke speak.

“A fine sword. Is it from the south?”

“How can you tell?”

The Sinking Moon Sword had disappeared from the Nanming Hundred Artifacts Register long ago. To earn a place in Yunzhou Artifact Appraisal or the Nanming Hundred Artifacts Register, a magic tool had to distinguish itself regularly in the hands of Foundation Establishment cultivators. But Lee Hyun often disappeared for centuries at a time, so the exceptional supreme-grade magic tools in his possession had inevitably slipped out of the rankings.

Murong Ke’s words interrupted his thoughts.

“Southern artifact refiners tend to apply Moon Shadow Stone powder in a thin layer like this. The Light-Retracting Restriction is done in their style too. What’s the sword called?”

“The Sinking Moon Sword.”

“Never heard of it.”

The elderly cultivator held the sword at an angle.

“This looks like damage from a clash with a magic treasure... but this section was blown out from within. What in the world did you do to this sword?”

“....”

Murong Ke set the sword down.

“I can repair it. The core restriction is intact, and the Thick Earth Refined Metal has retained its properties. But I’ll need to add more material and reshape the shattered tip.”

Lee Hyun then took out the Six-Leaf Shield.

The elderly cultivator’s eyebrows rose.

“This too?”

“I’d like both repaired.”

Murong Ke laid out the six shield plates one by one.

“A shield made up of six plates... A lot of work went into this. Each shield plate needs its own restrictions, and they all have to work together. Few artifact refiners make them this way these days.”

The two plates that had taken the attacks head-on had broken edges, while the remaining four had fine cracks and were slightly warped.

“Two will have to be remade. The rest can be salvaged. But the restrictions distribute the force across the whole set, so I’ll have to adjust all six to match the new shield plates.”

Murong Ke wrote out an estimate.

Repairs to the Sinking Moon Sword would cost 450, and the Six-Leaf Shield another 550. The total came to 1,000 mid-grade spirit stones.

It was expensive.

It would have been an enormous burden for an ordinary Foundation Establishment cultivator, but not for Lee Hyun.

‘The spirit stones from selling the Silver-Eyed Sea Eagle alone will cover it, with some to spare.’

“How long will it take?”

“Fifteen days. It may take longer if the materials turn out to be in poor condition.”

“Very well.”

Lee Hyun also took out the Golden-Thread Cold Iron and showed it to Murong Ke.

“I was wondering... Could adding a Tier 3 spirit material like this make a Foundation Establishment cultivator’s exceptional supreme-grade magic tool more durable?”

Murong Ke examined the spirit material, then shook their head.

“Simply mixing it in won’t make the sword better. Altering the blade’s properties too much could destroy the qualities that make it effective.”

“I see.”

“The same goes for the Six-Leaf Shield. It would be a different matter if you planned to redesign it, but using this for the current repairs would be a waste.”

Murong Ke tapped the Golden-Thread Cold Iron with a finger.

“Besides, my furnace can’t melt it. I’d have to borrow Tier 3 earth fire from one of the workshops higher up. I’ve never worked with this material before, either.”

Lee Hyun put the Golden-Thread Cold Iron away.

...

He watched as much of the repair work as Murong Ke permitted.

He paid another 100 mid-grade spirit stones for permission to observe, and 50 more for a jade slip setting out the essential formula for the repairs.

The essential formula covered how to heat sections containing Thick Earth Refined Metal, how to check the flow through the restrictions after sealing fine cracks, and more. Lee Hyun had only reached Novice proficiency in Tier 2 artifact-refining art, so there was much for him to learn.

Even when striking the same spot, Murong Ke subtly varied the hammer’s angle and the force of each blow. Lee Hyun watched intently, determined not to miss those differences.

...

The repairs were finished after fifteen days.

The Sinking Moon Sword’s tip was as smooth as when Lee Hyun had first seen it, and all six plates of the Six-Leaf Shield fit together perfectly.

On his way back, he paid 300 mid-grade spirit stones at a workshop on a lower level for six yellow flying swords of supreme grade.

He felt he lacked options for fighting at long range.

In a pinch, he could also use them to unleash the Great Unity Wisdom Sword, which he had yet to master. With six of them, damaging one would be less of a concern.

One month later.

A deserted mountain valley in southern Xu Kingdom.

Lee Hyun established an alchemy site far from the coast. He checked for signs of powerful demon beasts nearby and set warning restrictions at the valley’s entrance.

He had no wish to be ambushed at his pill furnace again, as he had been by the Silver-Eyed Sea Eagle.

Before long, a small dark cloud gathered above his head.

Crackle.

A bolt of lightning struck.

Boom!

Purple light spread across the pill’s surface.

At that instant, a strand of concentrated medicinal strength inside the pill suddenly surged.

Crack.

The pill split.

Silver-purple light seeped through the crack, then quickly faded.

Lee Hyun stared at the pill, now broken in two.

When he had made his first Dao pill, he had thought he only needed a little more practice.

Yet even reproducing the same fire control and hand movements had failed to yield the same result.

He placed the fragments of the failed pill on a jade plate and examined them with divine sense.

‘It’s incredibly sensitive...’

...

After that, Lee Hyun began examining the medicinal liquid more carefully once the Refining stage was complete.

Just before Pill Condensation, he identified pockets where the medicinal strength had not blended evenly and recorded which areas solidified first.

He guided the flame threads of the Flame-Threading Art more slowly than before, adjusting the flames whenever the flow inside the pill changed.

Sometimes he widened the gap through which the tribulation lightning could enter. At other times, he delayed closing it.

Making Dao pills remained difficult, but he was gradually improving.

...

Ten years later.

He was now producing Dao pills in two out of every ten furnace batches.

Compared with the mere three or four Dao pills he had managed to make during the first few years, it was a tremendous improvement.

Lee Hyun was delighted.

...

Another hundred years passed.

After returning from an alchemy session, Lee Hyun spread his jade slips across the table and reviewed his recent alchemy records one by one.

「Most recent 100 furnace batches.

Essence-Cultivating Dao Pills: 52.」

“Over fifty percent!”

After that, Lee Hyun’s life settled into a regular routine.

Forty-eight furnace batches a year.

Circumstances sometimes forced him to cut back on alchemy or concentrate it into shorter periods, but averaged over the years, it came to roughly that amount.

He produced a little over twenty Dao pills a year, or nearly thirty in a good year.

He consumed about sixty ordinary Essence-Cultivating Pills each year and sold the rest.

The plan he had first drawn up was now his everyday routine.

He rotated among several alchemy sites, never lingering where tribulation lightning had appeared.

He also bought medicinal ingredients and sold pills through separate outposts.

His surplus Essence-Cultivating Pills reached different regions in small quantities, so there was never a sudden flood of stock in any one place.

The members of the Two Heavens Society welcomed the steady stream of good deals.

For rogue cultivators, a reliable supply of Essence-Cultivating Pills for cultivation was reason enough to remain in the trade network.

Every ten years or so, he sold a few of the older spirit herbs from his spirit field to cover any shortfall in spirit stones.

...

Whenever turbid qi accumulated in his body, he stopped taking pills for a while and let his body recover, eating Yin Water Lotus seeds and Stone Honey Peaches as he continued his qi circulation cycles.

He inspected the spirit field every day as well.

He replaced leaking irrigation pipes and transplanted spirit herbs that had grown too close together. He replaced Bonefuzz’s worn joints and cleared the passages the fuzzbees had blocked.

After cultivation, he read novels or painted.

He practiced techniques steadily and kept up his sword training.

On days when his sword condensation faltered, he practiced with less power, learning to withdraw it before it could damage the blade.

Whenever the Sinking Moon Sword developed a small nick, he repaired it himself using the methods he had learned from Murong Ke.

...

After a long absence, Lee Hyun returned to Qianlu Market to have the Sinking Moon Sword inspected.

The skies above Qianlu Mountain were still crowded, and the workshop’s signboard was unchanged.

But Murong Ke was not the one who greeted him inside.

The elderly cultivator had died several decades earlier, having reached the end of their lifespan. A disciple now ran the workshop.

...

The people wearing the Two Heavens Society’s masks changed one by one as well.

When the person behind the Goose mask grew old, someone else took their place.

One year, Lee Hyun stopped hearing from Toad, who had survived Qingshi Ridge and switched to the Otter mask. When he looked into it, he learned that Toad had handed his duties to a successor and left to spend his remaining years in retirement.

The Council of Senior Elders incident became an old story told to new members.

Other members reached the Golden Core realm, but none proclaimed themselves senior elders and tried to seize control of the trade network.

...

And so Lee Hyun cultivated, practiced alchemy, ate, and rested.

Faces came and went, and the streets of the cultivator markets changed.

Some pills grew more expensive, while some medicinal ingredients became cheaper.

His success rate in producing Dao pills varied from year to year as well.

Still, time moved steadily on...

Three hundred and thirty years after Lee Hyun had begun studying the Essence-Cultivating Dao Pill in earnest.

A stone chamber in Tunnel No. 3.

Lee Hyun sat in lotus position.

Spiritual power circulated throughout his body along the pathways prescribed by the Primordial One-Qi Art.

It flowed through his limbs and internal organs, his sinews, bones, and skin.

He continued the qi circulation cycles slowly, keeping the energy from concentrating too heavily in any one place.

Countless times, he had directed medicinal strength into the areas that had long lagged slightly behind, refining them until they reached the same level as the rest of his body.

It happened as the medicinal strength of a single Essence-Cultivating Dao Pill completed a full circuit.

Hummm–

A vibration spread from deep inside his body to every limb and bone.

As the medicinal strength seeped into the last areas still lagging behind, all the energy in his body resonated as one!

Whoooosh–

The dark stone chamber was instantly flooded with light.

An auspicious glow rose like mist from Lee Hyun’s entire body, gently enveloping him in a rounded cocoon as he sat in lotus position.

The clear radiance flowed through his skin, sinews, and bones as though celebrating his achievement.

Dust drifted up from the stone floor with the light, then settled again.

How much time had passed?

The light filling the chamber gradually sank back into Lee Hyun’s body.

For an instant, his skin shimmered with light. Then it returned to normal.

His entire body had reached Foundation Establishment Great Perfection!

As Lee Hyun slowly opened his eyes, a clear gleam flashed in their depths.

“Finally!”

He looked down at his hands and flexed his fingers.

With even the slightest movement, he could feel the energy filling his entire body.

After examining the state of his body for a while, he took out the stone tablet, erased the old inscriptions, and carved new ones.

【Age: 3,191 years】

【Realm: Foundation Establishment Great Perfection (whole body)】

【Spiritual Power: 18,100 → 24,500】

【Constitution: Primordial Body, Foundation Establishment Great Perfection】

【Cultivation Art: Primordial One-Qi Art (Foundation Establishment Section)】

Lee Hyun withdrew his hand after engraving the final character.

It had taken so many long years.

Through patient, tireless cultivation, he had finally laid the foundation for the Leakless Golden Body.

Had he chosen to advance just his lower dantian first, he would have reached another realm long ago. But Lee Hyun had refused to compromise, and at last, he had made it this far!

Chapter 95

Lee Hyun looked down at the stone tablet he used as a homemade status screen, then activated the Yang Metal Art at his fingertip and revised the inscriptions on the lower half as well.

His realm was not the only thing that had advanced over the long years.

【Techniques (Major Attainment): Vajra Wisdom Sword Scripture (Sword Condensation Section), Sumeru Visualization Scripture (All-Hearing Heavenly King manifestation), Sumeru Mountain-Suppressing Seal, Metal Escape Art...】

【Techniques (Perfection): Sutra of Refining Intent into Vow...】

‘Can I really say I’ve reached Major Attainment in the Wisdom Sword Scripture and the Visualization Scripture too...?’

Fortunately, he was the only one writing or reading it, so there was no harm in getting it wrong.

Lee Hyun casually extended a hand. The Sinking Moon Sword slipped out of his storage pouch and rose into the air, its silver-gray blade exposed.

The spiritual power filling every part of his body flowed smoothly into the blade. He added his divine sense, then his vow power.

In the past, whenever he forced those powers into the blade, the process had felt dangerously precarious.

Now, guided by the image of the sword he had formed in his mind, his spiritual power, divine sense, and vow power circulated in unison, as though they had always been a single current.

Hummmm―

A mysterious light gathered at the sword’s tip.

Instead of firing it, Lee Hyun slowly steadied his breathing and drew the power back in.

Not a single scratch marred the blade.

“Phew... Good.”

Lee Hyun put away the Sinking Moon Sword, readjusted his lotus position, and activated the Sumeru Visualization Scripture.

The air behind him rippled, and brilliant golden light blossomed.

It took the form of the All-Hearing Heavenly King, holding a parasol in his left hand and supporting an intricately crafted pagoda with his right. Thanks to the greater depth of his visualization, every detail was vividly lifelike, from the close-set scales of the armor and the patterns on the flowing celestial robes to the majesty in the king’s fierce gaze.

As he steadied his primordial spirit while maintaining the All-Hearing Heavenly King manifestation, his mind cleared as though washed clean with cold, pure water.

Yet a small pebble Lee Hyun flicked toward the Heavenly King manifestation passed straight through without the slightest resistance.

Tap.

Lee Hyun clicked his tongue as he watched the pebble strike the stone chamber floor and roll away.

His visualization had reached Major Attainment, but the inheritance required the magical power of a Golden Core cultivator. Without it, the Dharma manifestation had no real power.

‘Still beyond my reach. But I’m almost there!’

Lee Hyun dispersed the golden Heavenly King manifestation and flopped onto his back on the stone chamber floor.

‘Maybe I’ll rest for a little while...?’

He took out a pulp novel and began reading.

...

Ten days later.

After lazing about for a bit, Lee Hyun finally got up and laid a bundle of jade slips on the stone table.

They contained the Golden Core section of 《Primordial One-Qi Art》 he had obtained during his days in the Danxiao Sect, the annotations to 《Arhat Golden Body》 he had copied from Baoguang Temple’s Scripture Pavilion, and the Golden Core Condensing Pill recipes and records on the refining of demon markings he had studied countless times in the Inner Alchemy Chamber.

He had read and reread these texts whenever he had a spare moment over the centuries. Yet now that every part of his body had reached the absolute limit of Foundation Establishment Great Perfection, each passage carried an entirely different weight.

Embracing Unity and Returning to the Elixir!

It gathered all the energy within the body into one and condensed the entire body at once.

As always, the problem was resources.

Even a simple calculation put the minimum at fifty Golden Core Condensing Pills. Some medicinal strength might also dissipate or be consumed as he raised the true essence throughout his entire body in perfect unison.

If he entered secluded cultivation with exactly fifty Golden Core Condensing Pills and ran short of medicinal strength, he might fail to form the Leakless Golden Body and end up as ‘just a young man with a big golden core.’

The shock of seeing all his efforts come to nothing might well send him into qi deviation.

He would feel much safer starting with seventy or eighty pills on hand.

‘I transmigrated, but I don’t even have the usual status screen or regression ability. All I’ve got is a body that doesn’t age... I can’t afford to fail.’

Lee Hyun stroked his chin.

‘A furnace batch of Golden Core Condensing Pills takes an entire, intact Tier 3 demon core. It isn’t like ordinary cultivation pills, where a single furnace batch yields three or four pills. And if I account for demon cores getting damaged during a hunt, or an alchemy failure ruining the ingredients...’

Lee Hyun went blank.

“...Doesn’t that mean I’ll have to kill more of them than a typical great sect has Golden Core Elders?”

Whether in the Nine Kingdoms of Yunzhou or the Nanming Twelve-Sect Alliance, a sect might have as few as twenty Golden Core cultivators. Even a special case like Baoguang Temple, which could produce Golden Core Condensing Pills with relative ease, had only a little over a hundred at most.

However dim-witted the beasts might be, each Tier 3 demon beast was a match for a Golden Core cultivator. He would have to kill the equivalent of all the Golden Core cultivators in two or three great sects, all by himself.

Of course, sect Elders and wild demon beasts were different. He would not be fighting cultivators who could contact one another and rush to each other’s aid. He could hunt the beasts scattered across the land one at a time.

Unfortunately, the fact that they were ‘scattered’ presented another problem.

The Tier 3 demon beasts Lee Hyun had killed so far, such as the Scale-Armored Sea Ape and the Silver-Eyed Sea Eagle, had all happened to come to him first.

Now the situation was reversed. He would have to scour the world himself in search of prey.

‘This won’t be over in a year or two. I’ll have to allow a few decades... Wait, a few decades? Maybe that isn’t so long...’

Medicinal strength did fade over time, but a few decades would not seriously diminish the quality of properly sealed demon cores or refined Golden Core Condensing Pills.

First, however, there was something he needed to confirm.

Could he make a Golden Core Condensing Pill entirely on his own, from start to finish?

He had assisted with the Refining stage countless times at Baoguang Temple and spent a long time watching the Elders perform alchemy. He had plenty of pill recipes and records, too.

But he had never completed the entire process alone.

‘Let’s make one first.’

Lee Hyun took out a blank jade slip and began listing the materials he needed.

Half a month later, at Qianlu Market in the Hua Kingdom.

The enormous cultivator market still sweltered in the heat, the air thick with the smell of molten metal.

Lee Hyun passed along a road busy with ore-laden carts and headed farther up the mountain.

Long ago, Murong Ke had told him that the workshops higher up rented out access to Tier 3 earth fire.

A Foundation Establishment cultivator needed Tier 3 earth fire to melt a Tier 3 demon core reliably.

Once he actually went looking, however, he discovered that it was not simply a matter of paying spirit stones and using a burner whenever he pleased.

The first workshop he visited had no burner available for the next two years. The second did not rent its facilities to outside cultivators.

At the third, he was able to inspect an unused facility, but this time Lee Hyun was the one who shook his head and left.

Six auxiliary burners surrounded a central main furnace, all sharing a single earth-fire vein. Whenever an artifact refiner in the neighboring room worked the bellows hard to melt materials for a magic treasure, the heat from the burner on this side fluctuated ever so slightly.

Such a minor change in heat would hardly matter during the preliminary refining of spirit materials. When refining a Golden Core Condensing Pill, however, even a momentary fluctuation could reduce expensive ingredients to ash.

...

It was the tenth day of trudging up and down Qianlu Mountain’s slopes.

At last, Lee Hyun found a stone chamber that met his requirements in a workshop called Huoyun Pavilion, situated against a relatively secluded cliff on the mountain’s northern slope.

A wave of dry heat rushed out as the stone door opened.

Unlike the other workshops, which were lined with hammers, anvils, and other equipment for refining magic treasures, the chamber was surprisingly empty. It measured roughly five or six zhang (about 16–20 m) on each side. Formation restrictions for handling heat and toxic fumes were engraved on the walls, and a single burner with a thick red copper rim sat alone in the center of the floor.

Steward Zhang, the mid Foundation Establishment cultivator showing him around, stroked his beard as he explained.

“This was originally a refining room for melting Tier 3 spirit materials separately and removing their impurities before the main work of crafting a magic treasure. These days, so many workshops rent out their facilities that things have been quiet here...”

Lee Hyun swept his divine sense over the arrangement of formation inscriptions on the floor.

Along each branch of the earth-fire vein beneath the burner, he found interlocking formations designed to shut off the fire qi and maintain constant pressure.

Steward Zhang channeled spiritual power into a jade token, and the closed burner opened by about half a cun (about 1.7 cm).

Red light spilled out, and the temperature in the stone chamber rapidly rose. Lee Hyun carefully studied the movement of the flames.

“This should do.”

“What sort of material do you intend to work with?”

“I’ll be using it for alchemy.”

“Alchemy?”

The steward glanced around the empty stone chamber, puzzled.

“As you can see, this is an artifact-refining workshop. We have no pill furnaces here.”

“I’ll procure the pill furnace myself. I only need to rent the burner and the room.”

The rental fee was five mid-grade spirit stones per day.

He also had to put down a deposit of one hundred mid-grade spirit stones against any damage to the burner. In addition, his reservation could be pushed back if Huoyun Pavilion received an urgent refining commission of its own.

Since he only needed to rent the room while performing alchemy, the price was hardly burdensome. He was grateful enough just to have sole use of Tier 3 earth fire of this quality.

...

Next came the pill furnace.

The Tier 2 pill furnace that had served Lee Hyun so well when refining Essence-Cultivating Dao Pills could not withstand the heat of Tier 3 earth fire.

He visited shops that sold pill furnaces, explaining his requirements.

The elderly proprietor of the fifth shop, Guyun Hall, listened to everything he needed before silently heading down into the underground storeroom.

A while later, he returned with a dark indigo three-legged furnace that stood as high as an adult man’s waist.

Various patterns were engraved on its surface, and an octagonal bronze base was attached beneath its three short legs.

“This is called the Demon-Suppressing Three-Legged Furnace. Although it is a low-grade magic treasure, it was designed for use by Foundation Establishment cultivators.”

The proprietor tapped the broad metal plate beneath the pill furnace.

“Fit spirit stones into these slots and place it over an earth-fire burner. The restrictions that draw in and contain the fire qi run on spirit stones and earth fire, so controlling it requires little spiritual power. Of course, it cannot make up for a lack of skill....”

Lee Hyun examined the pill furnace for a long while.

“How much?”

“Twelve thousand mid-grade spirit stones. Pay in high-grade spirit stones, and I’ll lower the price to one hundred and fifteen.”

...

The next day.

The Demon-Suppressing Three-Legged Furnace stood in the center of the stone chamber Lee Hyun had rented from Huoyun Pavilion.

He channeled Tier 3 earth fire into it and refined several kinds of Tier 2 pills as a test.

Controlling the chamber’s formation and the pill furnace’s restrictions simultaneously required delicate adjustments, but his wealth of experience allowed him to handle both with practiced ease.

As he sent Clear Yang Purifying Fire streaming in every direction with the Flame-Threading Art, Lee Hyun looked less like a Foundation Establishment cultivator than a seasoned Tier 3 alchemist.

After a full day of testing, he was certain he could refine Golden Core Condensing Pills in this environment.

“Now, shall I go find the ingredients?”

Lee Hyun bought a generous supply of top-quality jade caskets for carrying demon cores and bundles of Tier 2 high-grade Spirit-Sealing Talismans before descending Qianlu Mountain.

From there, he traveled more than a hundred thousand li (about 39,200 km) south, visiting cultivator markets large and small throughout southern Xu Kingdom and southwestern Xuan Kingdom, then along Kun Kingdom’s western coast.

The coastal cultivator markets had far more merchant groups dealing in demon-beast byproducts and far more veteran hunter cultivators than those inland.

Changing his identity and appearance along the way, Lee Hyun bought illustrated guides to marine demon beasts. He also gathered rumors from the gatherers who traveled among the reefs and uninhabited islands of the outer sea, asking which waters had seen high-tier demon beasts in recent decades.

He even paid a premium for five sea charts marking places where Tier 3 demon beasts had been sighted.

...

Lee Hyun continued roaming the coast.

The walls of one sea cave bore enormous claw marks, while bones from fish as large as houses lay scattered across the floor. Yet they crumbled at the lightest nudge of his foot.

Occasionally, he found more recent traces among the rugged reefs.

Fragments of formation flags and charred magic tools were lodged haphazardly among collapsed rocks. On the beach, the enormous remains of a demon beast lay half-buried in the sand.

Naturally, its chest and skull, where the demon core might have been, had already been cleanly cut open and emptied.

‘I’ve got competition... Back when I didn’t need Tier 3 demon beasts, they came right to me. Now that I’m actually looking, they’re nowhere to be found. Should I try the Cangmang Forest along the coast?’

But he had heard that powerful forces of the demon race lurked within the Cangmang Forest, so he needed to be cautious. He might also end up clashing with Baoguang Temple’s monks over a Tier 3 demon beast hunt.

For now, he focused on the coasts of Yunzhou and Nanming controlled by the human race, roaming the surrounding seas and islands.

On stormy days, he would dig a small temporary tunnel beneath the cliffs of an uninhabited island and spend several days resting inside, brewing tea. Once the sea calmed, he would resume searching beyond the shipping routes.

After several months of wandering, Lee Hyun grew fed up and visited a cultivator market in Kun Kingdom.

He returned to a shop where he had bought a map marking the locations of Tier 3 demon beasts. The proprietor had charged extra, claiming it reflected recent sightings, but Lee Hyun’s investigations had revealed that the information was decades old.

When Lee Hyun confronted him, the demonic cultivator who owned the shop snorted.

“Idiot. Use that head of yours. If someone had confirmed that a Tier 3 demon beast was nesting somewhere, do you think I’d sell that information to a Foundation Establishment cultivator like you? It would have gone to Golden Core Seniors or a great sect for a handsome price long ago!”

“Oh, really?”

A short while later, the demonic cultivator spoke with newfound respect, both eyes swollen and blackened.

“We have received a recent sighting report. However, we have not confirmed whether it really was a Tier 3 demon beast, or whether it is still there.”

“Oh, really?”

...

Several days later.

Following his new information, Lee Hyun was crossing the tidal flats of an island away from the shipping routes.

Half of an enormous blue-green carapace was wedged between wave-battered rocks.

Its thickness and residual demon power alone told him that it had belonged to a Tier 2 aquatic demon beast with formidable defenses. Yet the center of the iron-hard shell had been crushed inward as though something had bitten it, and the broken edge bore deep, unmistakable tooth marks as large as a human torso.

Lee Hyun crouched down, turned the carapace over, and examined its underside.

Torn pieces of viscera and red flesh still clung to it, not yet washed away by the seawater. They gave off the fishy stench of flesh that had only begun to rot.

‘A Tier 3 demon beast’s kill!’

...

That night, in a shadowed crevice halfway up the rocky island.

Using the Earth Escape Art to conceal his presence as though he were part of the rock, Lee Hyun quietly watched the blue-black water before him.

Before long, the calm surface began to swell.

The first things to rise above the water, without so much as a bubble, were two yellow eyes the size of cartwheels.

An elongated snout lined with interlocking, sawlike teeth followed, then a thirty-zhang body covered in thick, pitch-black scales.

It was a savage predator of the sea, a Tier 3 Iron-Armored Crocodile!

Grrrrrr―

The enormous crocodile planted its forefeet on the coastal rocks and hauled itself ashore. A single sweep of its tail, thicker than a house, ground the solid rock to sand.

A smile appeared on Lee Hyun’s lips as he watched from the shadows.

Faint blue-black demonic light glimmered between its scales, and several bone spines rose along its back.

It matched the records kept in the library of Baoguang Temple’s Inner Alchemy Chamber. More importantly, he was already familiar with the Iron-Armored Crocodile’s demon core, having handled one himself while assisting with the Refining stage.

Pale moonlight filtered through the clouds and illuminated the dark strait.

Dark-red blood dripping from beneath its jaws, the Iron-Armored Crocodile climbed over a rocky ledge and headed toward a broad, flat slab as though following a familiar routine.

Moving sluggishly, it lowered its thick belly onto the middle of the rock.

Just as its enormous jaw settled on its forefeet and its eyelids drooped halfway shut,

a streak of shadow swept toward it.

Warned by the keen instincts of a wild demon beast, the Iron-Armored Crocodile’s yellow eyes snapped open. But Lee Hyun’s left hand had already formed a brilliant golden Dharma seal and thrust it into the air.

Humm―

An enormous golden palm imprint manifested overhead.

It was the Sumeru Mountain-Suppressing Seal at Major Attainment!

As he poured tremendous amounts of spiritual power into it without restraint, the golden palm imprint grew so distinct that it seemed almost solid.

The ten-zhang palm, brimming with terrifying power, struck down like lightning at the Iron-Armored Crocodile’s back and neck!

BOOOOM―

With a deafening crash, the slab beneath the Iron-Armored Crocodile, dozens of zhang across, caved in.

GRAAAARGH!

The Iron-Armored Crocodile roared in agony and thrashed its massive body. Every scale on its body rose at once as blue-black demonic light surged forth, pushing fiercely upward against the Sumeru Mountain-Suppressing Seal pinning its back.

At the same time, its steel-like tail tore through the air toward Lee Hyun.

WHOOOOSH!

But Lee Hyun had already flattened himself against the ground with the Reclining Escape Art. Skittering across the rock, he slipped around to the Iron-Armored Crocodile’s flank, beyond the reach of its tail.

The Iron-Armored Crocodile shuddered at the revolting way the little human bastard scuttled about like a sea roach. It whipped its head around and opened its jaws as wide as they would go.

Demon power swirled deep in its throat, then a high-pressure jet of water exploded toward Lee Hyun’s face.

ROOOAR!

The black torrent narrowly grazed his shoulder, scraping violently against his body-protecting spirit light before punching through the jagged cliff behind him.

Lee Hyun slipped into the rock where he stood and burst out elsewhere.

Meanwhile, the Iron-Armored Crocodile finally managed to throw off the palm imprint pinning its back. It pushed off the shattered ground with all four bleeding feet and desperately turned toward an underwater cave beneath the seaside cliff.

The bedrock beneath its forefeet shattered. Just as its enormous body was about to slide toward the water, terror filled its yellow eyes.

A yellow flying sword had appeared directly in front of it, shining brilliantly and radiating lethal sword intent!

Great Unity Wisdom Sword, Third Form: Heavenly Dipper Vertical Slash!

The Iron-Armored Crocodile hastily opened its jaws, but just before its demon power could erupt, the power enveloping the flying sword shot forward like lightning.

Sword intent raced ahead of the blade, piercing the Iron-Armored Crocodile’s primordial spirit and freezing its consciousness for an instant.

Shhk!

Sword light split through its snout and drove straight into the brain within its skull.

THUD!

The Iron-Armored Crocodile’s enormous body went rigid.

The powerful claws scraping against the ground lost their strength and slipped. Its tail gave one final convulsion, shattering a rocky ledge before falling limp.

“Phew... That was a clean kill.”

Lee Hyun recalled the yellow flying sword and examined it. There was no damage. Unlike the Sinking Moon Sword, it was merely a supreme-grade magic tool, not an exceptional supreme-grade magic tool, yet it had withstood the technique. Seeing it hold up brought home just what it meant to have reached Major Attainment in the Sword Condensation Section of the Vajra Wisdom Sword Scripture.

...

Only the quiet sound of the night waves drifted over the shattered slab.

Lee Hyun planted a few simple formation flags around the area for concealment and warning, then crouched beside the Iron-Armored Crocodile’s corpse.

Sharp sword qi carefully cut along the seams of its tough belly hide.

He used the Qi Sphere Barrier to keep the spilling blood and fishy stench at bay, then opened up the body. A sphere brimming with dense demon power floated up from beneath the heart.

It was a Tier 3 demon core the size of an adult’s fist.

Lee Hyun took it in hand and sent his divine sense inside.

Because he had cut through the brain in a single strike, the intricate, weblike structure of the demon power condensed within the core remained perfectly intact, without even a hairline crack.

He placed the demon core in a jade casket he had prepared beforehand and affixed a Tier 2 Spirit-Sealing Talisman.

Then, using the Condensed-Essence Grasping Hand and Heavenly Dipper Sword Qi, he carefully harvested the Iron-Armored Crocodile’s thick scaled hide, teeth, and the sturdy bones that had survived a direct hit from the Sumeru Mountain-Suppressing Seal without breaking. He packed everything into his storage pouch.

He had spent no fewer than one hundred and fifteen high-grade spirit stones on the Demon-Suppressing Three-Legged Furnace. Selling the byproducts would at least help cover the chamber rental and the supplementary medicinal ingredients for the Golden Core Condensing Pill.

As the eastern horizon began to brighten, Lee Hyun erased the lingering traces of his aura, retrieved his formation flags, and rose into the air before disappearing.

...

Lee Hyun headed north toward the Xu and Hua Kingdoms, selling the byproducts at several cultivator markets along the way. Apart from a few high-grade intact bones he kept for bone puppet research, he sold most of the hide, teeth, and other materials for three hundred and fifty mid-grade spirit stones.

He then consulted the Golden Core Condensing Pill recipe that used an Iron-Armored Crocodile’s core, which he had copied at Baoguang Temple, and bought all the necessary supplementary medicinal ingredients.

...

One month after hunting the Tier 3 Iron-Armored Crocodile, inside a stone chamber at Huoyun Pavilion.

Lee Hyun had completed the Refining stage for the demon core. Keeping the essence of demon power under control as it spun furiously at the center of the pill furnace, he deftly manipulated the Clear Yang Purifying Fire and earth fire for several shichen (about two hours each).

Finally, he picked up the jade bottle beside him.

Shhhh―

A stream of special medicinal liquid poured into the pill furnace. Guided by the Flame-Threading Art, it gently enveloped the whirling essence at the center like a soft cotton quilt.

Ssssss―

As the medicinal liquid seeped into the essence, the violently surging demon power began to subside.

Lee Hyun closed the pill furnace’s lid and, a moment later, formed the intricate Pill-Condensing Seal with his hands.

Humm―

The instant the pill furnace trembled, he swiftly lifted the lid. Dazzling radiance burst through the gap, lighting up the entire stone chamber!

The light vanished as though being drawn back inside, and a Golden Core Condensing Pill floated up, pale blue light shimmering over its golden pill markings.

“It worked! Hahaha!”

Confidence surged through Lee Hyun. He had mastered the entire process himself, from hunting a Tier 3 demon beast to refining a Golden Core Condensing Pill!

Taking part in a few stages was nothing like doing it all himself, from hunting down the beast that supplied the raw material to refining the finished pill.

He immediately activated the Aura-Reading Art and extended his divine sense, carrying out a thorough pill inspection on his first creation.

The structure of the condensed demon power had been preserved, but every trace of the Iron-Armored Crocodile’s distinctive properties and toxicity had been purified away.

Because of the Iron-Armored Crocodile’s realm, the pill’s medicinal strength was only on par with a mid-grade Golden Core Condensing Pill. Yet it contained almost no extraneous qi, perhaps because he had taken such care at every stage, knowing he would be consuming it himself.

He could confidently call it a fine pill.

‘For a first attempt, this is a tremendous success!’

Lee Hyun felt that almost no uncertainties remained on his path to the Leakless Golden Body. All he had to do now was repeat the process, from hunting to alchemy.

About ten years later.

On the deck of a medium-sized flying boat crossing a remote reef archipelago in the outer sea west of Kun Kingdom.

Five cultivators from Haigu Island, a branch of the Yin Bird Sect of the Nanming Twelve-Sect Alliance, gazed down at the sea with sour expressions.

The Yin Bird Sect had been relatively late to expand north and had once had no branches in Kun Kingdom. Recently, however, it had extended its reach to several islands in the outer sea southwest of Kun Kingdom.

As a branch of the Yin Bird Sect, Haigu Island had taken part in that expansion.

Four of the five cultivators aboard the flying boat were seasoned hunters whose cultivation ranged from late Foundation Establishment to Great Perfection. The one-eyed old man at their head was an Elder at early Golden Core.

“Dammit, we’ve been scouring the outer sea for four months now! How have we not caught so much as a glimpse of a Tier 3 demon beast!”

The Elder vented his frustration.

He had reached Golden Core through a stroke of extraordinary luck, but he still carried little weight on Haigu Island.

He had somehow secured an Elder position and an inheritance, but he had not been provided with the materials to craft his own magic treasure.

In the end, he had brought his Juniors out to hunt for them himself.

The elites of the Nanming Twelve-Sect Alliance had a firm grip on the resources of the southern seas. Despite the danger, he had been forced to come all the way here, close to the Nine Kingdoms of Yunzhou.

Yet for some reason, every place known to harbor Tier 3 demon beasts held nothing but traces of their presence.

Unlike Lee Hyun, ordinary cultivators could not afford to waste four months. The Elder and the Juniors accompanying him were growing anxious.

Chapter 96

“We’re heading back.”

At the one-eyed Elder’s words, the four cultivators standing aboard the flying boat looked up.

“Are we returning to Haigu Island?”

“No. We’re going to the cultivator market. I need to buy some Tier 3 bone material.”

“Anything on the market will be expensive.”

“What choice do we have?”

Riding the wind, the flying boat turned east toward the coast.

...

Two days later, at a cultivator market on the western coast of Kun Kingdom.

The one-eyed Elder sat at a table in the back of a shop dealing in bone material, facing a young man in a plain gray robe. The young man was a rogue cultivator whose aura placed him at the Great Perfection stage of Foundation Establishment.

Three thick vertebrae and two leg bones with a bluish sheen lay on the table. The formidable demon power lingering over their surfaces made it obvious that they had come from Tier 3 demon beasts. Beside them, the shopkeeper smiled as he cautiously watched the Elder’s reaction.

“As luck would have it, this guest has brought in some rare goods. They’re much like what you were looking for, aren’t they, Elder?”

Rather than answer, the Elder picked up a vertebra and examined its cross-section, then sent his divine sense through it to inspect the structure around the marrow. The bone was in excellent condition.

The energy within the skeleton had remained undisturbed at the moment of the demon beast’s death, and the demon power inside had been fully preserved when the carcass was taken apart. Even if he had hunted the beast himself, he would have struggled to extract the bones in better condition.

“How much?”

“Five hundred sixty mid-grade spirit stones for all five.”

It was not cheap, but considering how much he had spent operating the flying boat over the past four fruitless months, perhaps he would have been better off paying a premium from the start. The thought only soured the Elder’s mood.

“The end of this leg bone is slightly damaged. Five hundred thirty.”

“That part would be cut away during refining anyway, so I haven’t charged for it. I can lower the price to five hundred fifty.”

The Elder’s heart suddenly lurched as he picked up the other leg bone in the midst of their bargaining.

His divine sense swept along the inside of the bone and caught on a tiny groove at the joint. The thin membrane covering the bone was still intact, though it would surely have been scraped away if whoever had butchered the beast had tried to remove even a little more flesh.

Without showing any sign of surprise, the Elder turned the bone to examine the cut beneath the joint. Normally, the cut would be made at the end of the joint, but this bone had been severed about half a cun (about 1.7 cm) below it. A short section of bone had been left in place like a plug, keeping the demon power flowing through the marrow from leaking out.

‘This is...!’

Examining the bones from the different demon beasts, he found the same distinctive details in all of them: the direction in which the tendons had been severed, the places where the bone membrane had been preserved, and even the angles of the cuts that sealed in the energy.

This was Haigu Island’s method!

Each inheritance concerned with bone material had its own preparation methods, but the differences were so slight that most cultivators could hardly tell them apart.

But they could not fool a Golden Core Elder who had spent his entire life working with bones on Haigu Island.

‘Did he prepare these himself? Or is he reselling goods smuggled out of Haigu Island...’

The Elder composed himself and set down the bone.

“Let’s make it five hundred forty. The quality is good. We should do business again.”

“Agreed.”

The disguised Lee Hyun nodded readily, accepted the spirit stones, and put them into his storage pouch. Even after deducting the shop’s brokerage fee, it was a respectable price.

Once the one-eyed old man, who had inspected the goods so meticulously, left the shop with his Juniors, Lee Hyun also rose from his seat.

...

The one-eyed Elder stopped at a street corner about two alleys away from the shop.

“You two stay behind and see where that man goes. Whatever you do, don’t get too close.”

“Was there something wrong with the bone material?”

“The goods are impeccable. I won’t even need to prepare them any further myself. Did nothing strike you about those bones?”

The Juniors fell silent, clearly at a loss. The Elder clicked his tongue.

Had the man been an ordinary Foundation Establishment rogue cultivator, the Elder could simply have seized him by the scruff of the neck. But he had offered no fewer than five pieces of Tier 3 bone material, which even Golden Core cultivators struggled to obtain. And the divine sense that had brushed against the Elder’s during the exchange had been strangely calm.

If another expert was backing the man, or Haigu Island’s inheritance had leaked to outsiders, the matter would be difficult for someone with his limited standing to handle alone.

“Perfected Yan is still staying at the cultivator market, isn’t he?”

“Yes. He’s aboard the flying boat at the eastern pier.”

Yan Wuzhen belonged to the Yin Bird Sect’s main sect.

A late Golden Core great cultivator, he had recently been traveling up and down Kun Kingdom’s coast on orders from the main sect.

Had the Elder approached him empty-handed after a failed hunt, he would only have invited ridicule. A matter involving their sect’s inheritance was another story.

...

A short while later, in a cabin aboard the flying boat docked at the eastern pier.

Yan Wuzhen ran his hand over the bone material on the table, then lightly flicked one of the vertebrae with a finger. A clear yet eerie note resonated through the cabin.

“It’s a little old-fashioned, but... there’s no mistaking our method. Who is that guy?”

“He appeared to be at the Great Perfection stage of Foundation Establishment, but he was unusually composed. I suspect he either deals in goods smuggled out of Haigu Island or has someone else behind him.”

The gap in strength between the one-eyed cultivator and Yan Wuzhen was so vast that, despite being a fellow Golden Core cultivator, he did not dare speak to him casually.

“So you brought this to me because our inheritance is at stake and you couldn’t afford to take it lightly. Is that it?”

Yan Wuzhen rose with a faint smirk.

“There’s no need to cause a disturbance in the cultivator market. Once the bastard leaves, we’ll follow him.”

That afternoon, Lee Hyun left the cultivator market and headed north along the coast. After crossing several mountain ridges, he quietly slowed his pace.

He could sense someone following him at a steady distance.

‘Is it the group from the shop?’

Lee Hyun sped up to test them. Even after he crossed two ridges in a single burst, the presence behind him had not fallen back at all. When he slowed again, his pursuers did the same, maintaining their distance.

‘They won’t be easy to shake. Should I hide underground?’

Lee Hyun considered it briefly, then shook his head.

He had yet to gather all the Tier 3 demon cores he needed for the Golden Core Condensing Pill.

He would still need to travel between this coast and the open sea. Not knowing why he was being followed would make his future movements here troublesome.

Better to confront his pursuers and deal with the problem at its source.

If his pursuer was a Nascent Soul cultivator, even the Earth Escape Art would not let him escape easily. Otherwise, he could simply slip underground if things went wrong.

Rather than continue inland, Lee Hyun turned out to sea and headed for a barren rocky island far from the shipping routes. The uninhabited island was covered in cliffs and rocky peaks scoured by fierce sea winds, with a dry valley at its center that seawater could not reach.

Landing in the middle of the valley, Lee Hyun lightly probed the earth vein beneath his feet. Beneath the thick bedrock, he found no unusual mineral veins or traces of formations that might interfere with an escape art. If necessary, the bedrock would provide him with a way out.

He turned and looked up. Before long, a medium-sized flying boat parted the clouds above the island. On its deck stood the one-eyed old man and four Foundation Establishment cultivators he had seen earlier, along with a middle-aged man in blue robes.

Lee Hyun’s eyes narrowed at the sight of the middle-aged man. The magical power radiating from him felt as deep and heavy as the sea itself.

‘Late Golden Core...’

As Lee Hyun extended his divine sense in every direction and confirmed that no one else lay in ambush, the blue-robed cultivator descended from the flying boat and stood at the valley entrance.

“You waited for us instead of running?”

“You kept following me, so I thought I’d hear what business you had with me.”

Lee Hyun turned his gaze toward the one-eyed old man.

“Was there a problem with the bone material I sold earlier?”

“The goods were excellent.”

Answering in the old man’s place, the blue-robed cultivator stepped forward and flicked his sleeve. One of the vertebrae from their earlier transaction floated into the air.

“I am Yan Wuzhen of the Yin Bird Sect. This bone was prepared exactly as our secret teachings on Haigu Island prescribe. Tell me who supplied you with these goods, or where you learned that method.”

‘Ah... so that’s what this is about.’

Lee Hyun gave a brief inward sigh as he looked at the floating bone.

“I merely sold my own goods for a fair price. Am I also obliged to explain where they came from?”

“If you won’t talk, I’ll have to pry the answer out of you myself.”

A black feather fan inscribed with silver patterns appeared in Yan Wuzhen’s hand. The moment he opened it halfway, the valley’s temperature plummeted as yin qi spread, cold enough to bite into the flesh.

At the same time, the four Foundation Establishment cultivators leaped from the flying boat, scattered along the ridges surrounding the valley, and planted gray formation flags. The one-eyed old man also descended and concealed his presence in the shadow of a boulder near the valley entrance.

Hummmm–

Ash-gray mist surged along the ridges, instantly preventing sound and fluctuations of spiritual power from passing into or out of the valley. Watching calmly as the concealment formation closed around him, Lee Hyun asked a question.

“You expect me to open my primordial spirit and submit to soul searching? And what will you do if it damages my primordial spirit?”

“That depends on how well you behave. Resist, and I’ll shatter your limbs before dragging your primordial spirit out myself!”

Before he had finished speaking, Yan Wuzhen’s fan slashed through the air.

Ruuumble!

The magical power of a late Golden Core great cultivator erupted, warping the air throughout the sky above the valley.

The Nine Nether Yin Wind burst from the fan and instantly formed the talons of a monstrous, house-sized bird, shrieking as they reached for Lee Hyun’s head and both shoulders.

Primordial True Qi surged from Lee Hyun’s entire body like a tidal wave.

Humm! Hummmm!

Fifty gleaming Spirit Light Shields sprang into being in the blink of an eye.

But the instant the black talons, condensed from late Golden Core magical power, struck them, the thirty-odd shields at the front shattered at once!

Baaang!

Lee Hyun did not so much as blink as the shields broke. He angled the remaining dozen or so Spirit Light Shields to deflect the talons to the side. At the same time, he activated the Reclining Escape Art, his feet sliding into the ground.

BOOOOM!

The bedrock where he had stood caved in several zhang (about 3.3 m each) deep, sending stone fragments spraying upward like torrential rain.

Lee Hyun slid out through the dust cloud, firing one fireball after another from the fingertips of both hands, each compressed until it burned almost white-hot.

‘A mere basic technique!’

Yan Wuzhen snorted, thickening his body-protecting magical light. Ignoring the first fireball, he started to swing his fan again.

Then he sensed the density of spiritual power packed into the fireball just before his face, and his expression changed abruptly.

Boom-boom-boom-boooom–

A chain of explosions turned the entire valley into a blazing sea of crimson fire. There was nothing unusual about the flames produced by the Fireball Art, but the amount of spiritual power crammed into them defied common sense.

His body-protecting magical light buckled inward at once, and Yan Wuzhen was driven far back.

He hurriedly swung his black fan, raising a wall of yin wind that tore through the oncoming firestorm. At that instant, beyond the flames, Lee Hyun’s newly drawn Sinking Moon Sword traced a silver-gray arc.

Whoooosh!

Great Unity Heavenly Dipper Sword Qi split into dozens of strands and surged through the gaps between the exploding fireballs. With the flames disrupting both vision and divine sense, two fireballs circled around and struck Yan Wuzhen in the flank, followed so closely by sword light that he had no chance to recover.

Several streaks seemed to miss him entirely, slipping past Yan Wuzhen and vanishing into the shadows of the valley walls.

Under the relentless succession of attacks, a blue jade token shot up from Yan Wuzhen’s waist.

Humm–

Bang! Screeeech!

Fireballs and sword qi battered the rippling blue screen of light projected by the jade token, sending violent waves across its surface.

Every trace of the easy smile vanished from Yan Wuzhen’s face.

‘Is this bastard really a Foundation Establishment cultivator? Just what is he?!’

Lee Hyun formed hand seals faster than the eye could follow. From the speed at which he created Spirit Light Shields to the timing of his interlocking fireballs and sword qi, everything about his technique was extraordinary.

Most staggering of all was the absurd amount of spiritual power at his disposal.

‘Trading attacks at a distance like this will get me nowhere.’

Yan Wuzhen slapped the pouch at his waist with his left hand.

Ruuumble–

Pitch-black yin qi shot skyward in a towering column, and two enormous skeletal monsters appeared at once in the middle of the valley.

One was a twenty-zhang-long White Bone Flood-Dragon Puppet, carved from the intact skeleton of a Tier 3 sea beast. The other was a Six-Armed White Bone Demon, twice a man’s height and covered in formation inscriptions. Each of its six arms held a bone saber with a chilling blue sheen!

And that was not all.

Yan Wuzhen formed a hand seal with his left hand. Ghastly pale flames erupted at once from his palm and the mouths of the two bone puppets.

Fwoooosh–

White Bone Yin Fire, capable of melting even bone with ease, rode the fan’s Nine Nether Yin Wind throughout the valley. The Spirit Light Shields constantly forming around Lee Hyun hissed like snowflakes falling into boiling water and melted away in an instant.

Trying to counter White Bone Yin Fire fueled by late Golden Core magical power with a basic defensive technique was costing Lee Hyun far too much spiritual power.

Whoooosh!

The Six-Armed White Bone Demon kicked off the ground and shot through a gap in the melting Spirit Light Shields, appearing right before Lee Hyun faster than the eye could follow.

Wreathed in White Bone Yin Fire, its six bone sabers slashed toward Lee Hyun’s neck, chest, dantian, and limbs in a crisscrossing barrage.

Behind it, the White Bone Flood-Dragon Puppet smashed its massive tail into the ground, raising a tidal wave of stone fragments. Overhead, Yan Wuzhen swept his black fan downward, unleashing a Great Wind Blade dozens of zhang long to cut off Lee Hyun’s retreat!

Clatter!

The Six-Leaf Shield’s six plates interlocked and spun like gears, meeting Yan Wuzhen’s descending black Great Wind Blade at an angle.

BOOOOM–

An ear-splitting explosion rang out as the Great Wind Blade’s shockwave sheared through the middle of the rocky peak behind the valley, bringing it crashing down.

Lee Hyun lowered his body and rode the tremendous shockwave. Rather than evade the Six-Armed White Bone Demon’s six sabers already upon him, he slipped half a step forward.

Fwoooosh!

Clear Yang Purifying Fire streamed from his fingertips and split into countless threads of flame, burning directly against the frigid energy of the White Bone Yin Fire.

He conjured the golden hand of the Sumeru Mountain-Suppressing Seal with his left while executing the precise footwork of the martial path.

Clang! Clang-clang!

Guided by the sword principles of a grandmaster of the martial path, the Sinking Moon Sword in his right hand changed direction three times in an instant, deflecting the first four bone sabers at uncanny angles.

As the deflected sabers struck the Six-Armed White Bone Demon’s other arms and tangled its attacks, Lee Hyun twisted his left hand as though wrenching the air apart.

Whooom–

The Sumeru Mountain-Suppressing Seal seized the Six-Armed White Bone Demon by the nape and hurled it directly into the path of the White Bone Flood-Dragon Puppet’s massive tail as it swept toward him.

At the same time, an explosive surge of Earth-Origin Force pulled at the White Bone Flood-Dragon Puppet’s body!

Crrrunch!

The White Bone Flood-Dragon Puppet’s tail struck the Six-Armed White Bone Demon head-on with a deafening crash.

Just as a startled Yan Wuzhen tried to bring the two puppets under control with his divine sense, Lee Hyun burst up through the dust, another golden palm imprint forming in his left hand.

BOOOOM–
