Yan Baishou frowned. The three jade gui tablets circling Nie Xingya had all gone dim.

[We know nothing about that guy's origins. If we press this any further, we'll truly be staking our lives on it.]

It was now the two of them against three great demons. Nie Xingya had a point.

When Yan Baishou lowered his bloodstained hand, the silver liquid scattered across the sea and between the reefs stretched into fine threads and streamed into his sleeve.

Seeing this, Tan Yue bared his fangs and sent the seawater beneath his feet surging upward.

“And where do you think you're going?”

But before he could throw himself forward, Master Hu stopped him with a glance toward the crater.

“Tan Yue. Let them go.”

Tan Yue looked between Yan Baishou and Nie Xingya before dispersing the waves beneath his feet with a displeased expression. Driving away Nascent Soul cultivators was one thing. Taking their lives was another. Who knew what tricks those scheming old monsters of the human race might hide in secret arts they were willing to stake their lives on?

A moment later, the two human cultivators turned into streaks of light and swept through the sky side by side.

Only long after the two trails of light had vanished beyond the horizon did Lee Hyun finally let out an inward sigh of relief.

...

Lee Hyun lightly clenched his fist and reconsidered what had just happened.

‘Was that just the residual force erupting?’

It had been similar to opening the lid of a pill furnace immediately after completing a Golden Core Condensing Pill. The instant the energy throughout his body had condensed, the lingering force that had yet to settle had erupted all at once through his fist. It certainly felt different from clenching his fist now.

Even if his total magical power was fifty times that of an ordinary early Golden Core cultivator, and even if he had obtained the Leakless Golden Body, he could not underestimate Nascent Soul cultivators based solely on what had just happened.

‘Stay humble. Don't let my guard down.’

If his opponent had not approached because he wanted Lee Hyun's corpse intact, but had instead bombarded him with techniques from a distance or used a secret art targeting his primordial spirit, there was no telling whether the outcome would have been the same.

Just then, two people descended from the rim of the crater.

One was an elderly scholar with white, pointed ears. The other was a massive man nearly nine chi (about 3 m) tall.

They were even more intimidating up close.

Back when Lee Hyun had been at Foundation Establishment Great Perfection, he would have struggled even to meet the eyes of experts like these.

Master Hu took a pair of green jade spectacles from his sleeve and put them on. Beside him stood Tan Yue, faint hexagonal armor plates still visible around his thick neck. Lee Hyun immediately bowed to them both.

“Thank you both for coming to my aid.”

“How is your body?”

Master Hu's gaze swept over Lee Hyun's shoulders and chest.

A look of admiration entered his eyes as he studied the golden demon markings flowing beneath Lee Hyun's skin. The qi and blood visible on the surface were terrifyingly vigorous.

Strangely, however, the demon power within him was difficult to perceive clearly. Perhaps because the golden boundary running through his skin and flesh enveloped the fluctuations within, it was difficult to distinguish where his demon power arose and where it gathered.

‘What a strange bloodline.’

“I have no trouble moving.”

“Well, of course you don't! Not after sending a Nascent Soul cultivator of the human race flying like that. Did you see the look on that bastard's face?”

As Tan Yue laughed heartily, Lee Hyun pulled a fresh long robe from his storage pouch, shook off the charred remnants of his clothing, and put it on. He took care not to put too much strength into his fingertips as he tied the sash.

When he looked toward the bottom of the crater, he spotted jade caskets scattered among the wreckage.

‘...! I need to hide those, fast.’

He had no idea how they would react if they discovered what ingredients had gone into the Golden Core Condensing Pill. Lee Hyun swept his sleeve, and the jade caskets, half-burned Spirit-Sealing Talismans, and fragments of magic tools were instantly drawn into his storage pouch.

Master Hu spoke.

“Do you have a name?”

“My name is Li Dongwu.”

He had come up with the name without much thought.

After abandoning the identity of Li Dongsi at Baoguang Temple, he had used an entirely different surname and given name. After all, it would be suspicious if Li Dongwu and Li Dongliu appeared one after another at the same Lotus Court.

So this was the first time he had ever used the name Li Dongwu.

“Li Dongwu... What clan are you descended from?”

Here it comes!

Lee Hyun chose his words carefully.

“I lived alone for a long time in the lands of the human race. There was no one who could tell me anything about my roots.”

Master Hu exchanged a glance with Tan Yue.

To think a Junior with such an extraordinary body did not even know his own bloodline.

Still, such cases were not particularly rare among the descendants of clans scattered beyond Cangmang Forest.

If their parents died early, or disappeared while leaving behind young who had yet to awaken their intelligence, they could spend thousands of years in the wilderness without ever learning who their ancestors were.

“Then have you cultivated alone all this time?”

“For the most part.”

“Can you read the writing of the human race as well?”

“Yes. I have no trouble reading or writing it.”

“Oh! Then you must have read cultivation manuals and technique manuals of the human race as well?”

Master Hu visibly brightened as he asked, and Lee Hyun nodded.

“Yes.”

“That is welcome news!”

Tan Yue laughed beside them.

“You've finally found a Junior you can actually talk to, Master.”

Master Hu nodded with a satisfied expression.

As Lee Hyun listened to them, he quietly activated the Spirit-Concealing Art and Aura-Concealing Art. His outward presence faded, but fierce demonic qi continued to seep from his chest, back, arms, and legs beneath his long robe.

‘Damn... Can't I conceal this aura?’

When refining the Golden Core Condensing Pill, he had thoroughly removed the demon beasts' impure qi and toxins. But he had been unable to eliminate the structure of the concentrated demon power used to condense his true essence.

For an ordinary cultivator, the demon markings would have remained on the golden core inside the dantian. In Lee Hyun's case, they spread through the flesh of his entire body and along the core shell running through his skin, each giving off its own presence.

When Lee Hyun tried to sink the demon markings deeper beneath his skin, golden patterns flared across the nape of his neck before stopping.

Tan Yue saw it and stepped closer.

“Whoa, don't rush.”

“What do you mean...?”

“Your newly transformed body is overflowing with energy. If you try to force it down right away, you could damage your bloodline.”

Master Hu nodded as well.

“You need to be careful until the energy settles completely. For now, let us head to Cangmang Forest.”

“Am I allowed to enter Cangmang Forest?”

“We can hardly remain here. Those two from earlier might return with more old monsters of the human race.”

“I have another place where I was staying....”

“If you have belongings to collect, you can always return for them later.”

Tan Yue picked up the conversation.

“What would become of my reputation if word got around that I left a Junior who had just completed his human-form transformation alone at sea in this state? Come, let's go. I'll take you as far as the coast.”

Before Lee Hyun could say anything else, Tan Yue threw himself into the sea.

Splash!

A massive shadow swelled beneath the blue waves. A moment later, the island-like carapace of the Dark-Armored Sea Turtle's true body pushed above the surface.

“Climb aboard!”

Lee Hyun considered it for a moment.

On one side, a Nascent Soul-level sea turtle was offering him its back. On the other, a Nascent Soul-level fox was waiting for him.

Anyone could see that they were sincerely trying to look after their Junior.

Without their intervention, he might have died before completing Core Formation. Besides, returning to the lands of the human race while radiating this much demonic qi was hardly a good option.

He had already put Tunnel No. 3 in order before leaving, so nothing disastrous should happen even if he could not return for about three years.

Lee Hyun slowly bowed his head.

“Then I'll accept your hospitality for a while.”

“Good choice.”

...

The enormous carapace cut through the sea.

Master Hu placed a small table on top of it, took out a tea set, and deftly measured out tea leaves as he spoke.

“This is something called spirit tea that I obtained from the storage pouch of a Golden Core cultivator of the human race. Any civilized being ought to drink tea! It is important to calm both body and mind after a human-form transformation, so have a cup.”

“Thank you.”

The moment Lee Hyun accepted the teacup, there was a faint crack, and a hairline fracture appeared where his fingers touched it. Master Hu stared at it for a moment before taking out another cup.

“It's fine. When I first completed my human-form transformation, I broke things every time I tried to pick them up.”

After concentrating carefully, Lee Hyun managed to hold the second cup without incident.

He drank, and a faint fragrance lingered as the tea passed down his throat.

Master Hu looked pleased to see Lee Hyun drinking tea quite naturally, much like a human.

“If you lived in the lands of the human race, I suppose you know little about Cangmang Forest.”

“Yes.”

“What the human race knows of Cangmang Forest is mostly limited to its eastern outskirts. Its true size is beyond imagination. Its lands stretch more than a million li (about 392,000 km) to the west and north.”

‘A million li!?’

“Is all of it forest?”

“There are forests, but there are also lakes vast as seas, and swamps where the poison mist never clears throughout the entire year. There are volcanoes, plateaus, and mountain ranges covered in ice as well.”

Master Hu took a sip of tea and continued.

“Various clans and great demons divide those mountains and waters among themselves and rule them. That is the region we call the Cangmang Demon Realm. The place we're heading to now is only its southeastern corner.”

“Does each clan have its own territory?”

“Indeed. Even within the same forest, one cannot simply settle wherever one pleases. Think of how the human race recognizes ownership of Mountain Gates and spirit veins.”

“Then is it truly all right for an outsider like me to enter?”

“Who would stop a guest I am bringing with me? If you decide to settle there, you can formally notify your neighbors then.”

Master Hu smiled and added,

“There are more than ten Tier-4 fellow practitioners who regularly come and go around Lulin Pavilion. If you include those we exchange letters with from across Cangmang Forest, there are more than a hundred. You will have many people to greet in the future.”

‘More than a hundred?’

Lee Hyun struggled to keep his expression unchanged.

More than a hundred Nascent Soul-level beings? As far as he knew, even gathering every Nascent Soul cultivator in the Nine Kingdoms of Yunzhou would only amount to roughly half that number.

And Master Hu was not finished.

“Deeper within the forest, there are even Demon Lords who have reached Tier 5.”

“......Tier 5? Don't tell me...”

“It corresponds to what the human race calls the Spirit Transformation realm.”

Master Hu nodded as though it were nothing remarkable.

“They rarely leave their own residences, but having lived for so long, they know a great deal. One of them may even be able to tell us something about your bloodline.”

Lee Hyun felt the back of his neck go cold.

Just what kind of being was a Spirit Transformation cultivator?

He had heard that such experts existed in the distant Qianyuan Empire. But at least within the Nine Kingdoms of Yunzhou, it was a realm whose very existence was uncertain.

It was already enough to send cold sweat down his back knowing he was deceiving members of the demon race at the Nascent Soul level. And now he was supposed to stand before a Spirit Transformation expert and ask them to examine his body?

“If the opportunity ever arises someday.......”

Lee Hyun trailed off. Master Hu looked startled when he noticed golden patterns emerging across the back of Lee Hyun's hand.

‘Could it be...?’

The moment he mentioned Tier-5 Demon Lords, the young man's gaze hardened, the veins on the back of his hand bulged, and the energy of his bloodline began to surge...

‘Just hearing that there are stronger opponents has already made him eager for a fight?’

Master Hu remembered the sight of Lee Hyun sending Yan Baishou flying. It was said that some of the mighty bloodlines from ancient times were unusually fond of battle.

Even if they understood proper conduct in their heads, the demonic nature ingrained in their bodies did not always obey. If this Junior was one of those types... bringing him before a Demon Lord would inevitably lead to trouble!

Master Hu hurriedly sent a mental intent toward Tan Yue. Laughter came from beneath the carapace.

“Hoho! There is no need to greet a Demon Lord right away, is there? Junior, once we reach the coast, would you care for a little exercise with me?”

“Pardon?”

“We've almost reached the coast anyway. There's a nice flat rock over there.”

‘...?’

A short while later, the three stepped onto land.

“The rules are simple.”

Having returned to human form, Tan Yue dropped onto a flat rock.

“We brace our feet against each other, clasp hands, and pull. Whoever's backside leaves the ground loses. No other divine abilities. Let us compete using only the strength of our bodies.”

Master Hu chimed in.

“Fellow Daoist Tan has a sturdy body, so there is nothing to worry about.”

Lee Hyun looked from one to the other.

‘Only physical strength?’

If they were not using techniques or magical power and were competing purely through physical strength, this was a good opportunity to see just how much his body had changed. He slowly sat across from Tan Yue, pressed the soles of his feet against the other man's, and clasped right hands. Tan Yue's grip felt like an enormous pair of iron pincers.

“Then let us begin.”

Lee Hyun gradually put strength into their clasped hands.

Crack!

Tan Yue's shoulder was pulled forward, and the smile vanished from his face.

‘Huh?’

Tan Yue hurriedly tensed the muscles in his lower back.

Hummm!

This time, Lee Hyun's upper body tilted slightly forward.

‘Damn!’

Lee Hyun gritted his teeth.

As expected of a Nascent Soul-level demon beast!

Tan Yue's grip tightened further.

‘So he's saying it's fine to use this much strength?’

Lee Hyun planted his feet firmly and drew out a little more power. Golden light spread from his wrist toward his elbow, and intricate demon markings appeared between the folds of his robe collar.

Tan Yue's eyes widened.

‘What kind of brute is this?’

The Junior was pulling as though he intended to rip Tan Yue's hand clean off. If Tan Yue had been an ordinary member of the demon race, his body would already have been torn apart!

If he got dragged across the rock after being the Senior who had offered to help the Junior loosen up, he would never live it down.

Tan Yue's neck thickened, armor-plate patterns appeared across both shoulders, and a harsh cracking sound came from the rock beneath him.

Lee Hyun swallowed a curse.

The giant in front of him had said this was only a quick warm-up, yet now he was baring his fangs as though he might swallow Lee Hyun whole.

Hummmmmm―

The spiritual qi along the shore slowly converged toward the two of them.

Golden skin and dark blue-black armor plates gleamed with contrasting lusters as they faced off. Their clasped hands remained perfectly motionless at a single point in midair. Instead, the rock beneath them began to split.

Craaack!

Master Hu's expression turned serious as he watched through his jade spectacles. At first, it had looked like harmless bonding between the two, but the atmosphere was becoming increasingly dangerous. Tan Yue was renowned for his raw strength, yet this Junior who had only just completed his human-form transformation was not budging in the slightest!

Meanwhile, the cracks in the rock deepened.

Cr-r-rack!

Tan Yue gritted his teeth inwardly.

‘Why won't this crazy bastard of a Junior stop?’

Lee Hyun was thinking the same thing.

‘How long is this damn turtle planning to keep going?!’

Their arms and shoulders had gone rigid from resisting each other's strength. If either one suddenly relaxed, the other would go tumbling backward.

At that moment, Master Hu thrust a hand between them.

“Enough! He only just came through a heavenly tribulation! Fellow Daoist Tan, you said you wanted to look after our Junior. What are you doing?”

Tan Yue spoke with obvious relief.

“R-Right. I got a little carried away.”

“Both of you, ease off slowly.”

Lee Hyun nodded as though he had been waiting for those very words.

“Yes, Senior.”

Their clasped hands separated, and silence hung between them for a moment. Then Tan Yue was the first to burst into hearty laughter.

“Now that's strength! Excellent strength!”

He discreetly hid his throbbing right hand behind his back.

...

Tan Yue decided to part ways with them at the coast.

“I need to spend a little longer looking around the southern islands. I still have to finish investigating the waters where demon beasts have disappeared.”

Master Hu nodded.

“I'll leave it to you.”

Tan Yue turned to Lee Hyun.

“Master Hu knows far more about Cangmang Forest than I do, so listen to him. Next time we meet, let's have another contest.”

“I won't forget what you did for me today.”

“Hoho! What a courteous Junior.”

Once the Dark-Armored Sea Turtle disappeared beneath the water, Master Hu, who remained on the coast, spread his sleeve and wrapped them both in a soft glow for the flight.

“Let us go.”

...

Enormous trees with thick roots sunk deep into the seawater stretched endlessly along the coast.

Dark blue-black stone pillars stood between them. Characters carved into their surfaces glimmered faintly.

They were prohibition markers declaring the territory of the demon race of Cangmang Forest.

At the entrances to waterways winding between the tree roots, members of the demon race stood guard with crude spears.

As soon as Master Hu descended in a glow of light, they immediately bowed in greeting.

“Greetings, Master Hu!”

“He is my guest. He will be accompanying me to Lulin Pavilion, so bear that in mind.”

The guards turned their attention to Lee Hyun.

At first, they seemed to wonder whether Master Hu had brought someone from the human race. But the moment they sensed the ferocious demonic qi pouring from Lee Hyun, they immediately bowed their heads.

“Greetings, Senior!”

Lee Hyun nodded.

Once they passed beyond the prohibition markers, the sea wind subsided and the smell of damp earth and grass grew thick.

After following the waterways for a while, they began to see lights among giant trees rising dozens to hundreds of zhang (roughly 100 m to over a kilometer).

Houses sat atop branches so thick that several people holding hands could not have encircled them, and vine bridges stretched from tree to tree.

High overhead, enormous birds lowered bundles tied to their legs, while broad-backed demon beasts moved through the waterways below carrying loads of cargo.

On the ground, beside a huge beast laden with baggage, a small weasel standing on two legs scrutinized a wooden tablet and appeared to be arguing over something.

The sounds of wood being struck, beasts crying out, and voices chattering blended together from somewhere nearby.

Master Hu spoke beside him.

“This is where those traveling to and from the coast stop for a while. Lulin Pavilion is a little farther in.”

...

A little farther in turned out to mean something very different from what Lee Hyun had expected.

They had already crossed several mountain ranges since leaving the coastal settlement, yet Master Hu continued flying without stopping.

Whenever the forest seemed about to end, a lake vast enough to reach the horizon would appear. Once they crossed the water, dark blue-black trees would once again stretch all the way to the horizon.

At one point, enormous caves had been carved in rows across cliffs beside a lake. Rather than flying straight over them, Master Hu made a wide detour.

“That mountain belongs to another fellow practitioner.”

For a long time after that, they did not see so much as a single house. Occasionally, an enormous presence stirred among the trees, but once it sensed Master Hu's passing radiance, it quietly withdrew into the distance.

Only after resting for a night and setting out again did an unusually tall tree finally rise above the endless Cangmang Forest. Something appeared to rest among its branches, but it was still too far away to make out clearly.

“That is Lulin Pavilion. Before we go there, let us first see where you will be staying.”

Master Hu changed course, and a low mountain range appeared amid the dense forest.

One of the peaks contained a hollowed basin on its inner side. A small lake lay at the bottom of the basin surrounded by forest, with gentle slopes and rocky cliffs rising behind it.

Master Hu pointed toward it.

“How would you like to stay on that mountain?”

Lee Hyun felt the dense spiritual qi flowing from the mountainside. Far richer than in the surrounding area, it gathered inside the basin before slowly seeping into the trees, water, and soil.

“Could this be... a Tier-3 spirit vein?”

Master Hu looked slightly apologetic.

“It isn't really sufficient for a Tier-4 fellow practitioner to live on. Unfortunately, all the other Tier-4 spirit veins in this area already have owners.”

Lee Hyun stared blankly at Master Hu.

What was he talking about? This was a Tier-3 spirit vein!

“Are you saying I may stay on that mountain?”

“If you like it.”

“Which part of the mountain...?”

“The mountain isn't particularly large. Why would there be any need to divide it?”

Master Hu gave him a puzzled look.

“Lulin Pavilion keeps several guest mountains vacant for fellow practitioners who come from afar. This one is under my care, so there is no need to seek anyone else's permission.”

“Was there no clan living here originally?”

“No. It is also a little removed from the residences of the other fellow practitioners, so it should be quiet enough for you to settle your energy.”

“Is there anything I would need to do in exchange for using this place?”

“Now that we are neighbors, there may naturally be times when we help one another. But who would assign work to someone who has only just come through a tribulation? Consolidate your realm first.”

Lee Hyun looked at the mountain again and thought of the Heaven-Origin Divine Tree in his tunnel.

What if he transplanted it here?

He gave the area a quick examination with the Ground-Sense Art. The water vein beneath the basin was not particularly deep, and beneath it lay a thick layer of bedrock. If he built a house above ground and then dug down beneath it to construct Tunnel No. 4...

“Do you not like it?”

Master Hu asked. Lee Hyun immediately raised his head.

“No. This place is more than enough.”

“Truly?”

“Yes.”

“Then it seems I chose well. If the spiritual qi becomes insufficient later, you can look for another place.”

Master Hu was inwardly relieved. A Junior with such a formidable body was satisfied with a Tier-3 spirit vein, so he did not seem difficult to please. Master Hu took a small jade token from his robes and handed it to Lee Hyun.

“Carry this for the time being. It is my identification token, so you should have no trouble traveling around this area. Lulin Pavilion will prepare a separate identification token for you.”

“I'm indebted to you.”

“I'll stop by Lulin Pavilion and report what happened. You should rest and examine your body first. I'll return tomorrow morning.”

After Master Hu disappeared to the north, Lee Hyun remained where he was for a while, looking around at the beautiful scenery.

‘Should I live here...?’

If he returned to the lands of the human race, the powerful demonic qi pouring from his body would be a problem. It would not be easy for him to remain in the cultivation world of the human race for the time being.

This place had its dangers as well, but at least the members of the demon race he had met so far were far friendlier than the old monsters of the human race who had tried to capture him. More importantly, there was a Tier-3 spirit vein right in front of him.

Lee Hyun looked up at the mountain once more and decided to stay here for the time being.

That night, Lee Hyun dug a small temporary cave beneath a rocky cliff and installed a warning formation. He slowly examined his newly acquired body, and before he knew it, it was light outside.

...

The next morning, Lee Hyun followed Master Hu, who had returned as promised, to Lulin Pavilion.

Lulin Pavilion had been built both inside and around an enormous tree. Wooden walkways spiraled up its trunk, which rose hundreds of zhang into the air.

A pavilion rested wherever the branches divided, so from a distance it looked as though a single tree were supporting an entire small sect.

Lee Hyun stood below, looking up.

‘Is that tree a spirit tree too? How many spirit stones would it be worth?’

Completely unaware of his Junior's wicked thoughts, the good-natured Master Hu led the way up the stairs.

Inside the pavilion, which smelled of old wood, every wall carved into the trunk was lined with books, jade slips, stone tablets, and scrolls made from beast hides. Their sizes and shapes varied so widely that some sections looked more like warehouses stacked with spirit materials than bookshelves.

A small monkey carried two stone slabs across the branches, while beneath it, a long-bodied white weasel sorted wooden tablets.

Clack-clack.

A small member of the demon race flicking abacus beads at a table farther inside looked up. It was a squirrel with round ears and a long tail, perched on a tall stool.

“You've returned?”

“I've brought a new fellow practitioner. I intend to let him stay at the vacant Qingshi Mountain, so update the records.”

Apparently, Qingshi Mountain was the name of the mountain where Lee Hyun would be staying.

“What name and realm should I record?”

“Li Dongwu. Early Tier 4.”

The paw working the abacus stopped. The squirrel climbed down from its stool, brought its forepaws together, and bowed.

“Greetings, Senior.”

“Ah, yes.”

Lee Hyun responded calmly.

“Which clan should I register you under?”

“He is a fellow practitioner who cultivated alone. He will be staying here for the time being, and I will vouch for him.”

“Understood.”

The squirrel pulled over a wooden tablet and began carving characters unlike the writing of the human race, their slender strokes intertwined like bird tracks.

Master Hu explained.

“It is the Bird-Track Script. The symbols used by each clan differ somewhat, but records that need to be read by several clans generally use this script.”

As Lee Hyun studied the shape of the characters, Master Hu pointed toward the shelves farther inside.

“Most records over there concern the boundaries of territories, waterways, and places where medicinal herbs or minerals can be found. There are also records about ancient bloodlines and human-form transformation. Each clan contributed a little, and over time it accumulated into all of that.”

“You keep records from different clans together in one place?”

“We make copies of whatever they don't mind sharing. Few fellow practitioners are generous enough to bring their secret teachings here.”

A short while later, the squirrel held out a green jade token.

The front was carved with characters Lee Hyun could not read, while the reverse bore a simple emblem depicting a mountain and a tree.

“This token identifies you as a guest of Lulin Pavilion. It also records that you are staying at Qingshi Mountain.”

Master Hu took back his own identification token and added,

“When entering a place ruled by another mountain lord, show them this token and state your business. Do not gather spirit treasures without permission or harm clan members or demon beasts under their protection, or you may cause a dispute.”

“Understood.”

...

Master Hu's study was located in the upper reaches of Lulin Pavilion.

A thick branch stretched diagonally past the window, with a row of small birds perched on it basking in the sunlight.

The room was neatly arranged.

Books from the human race filled one wall, while scrolls depicting the forms and patterns of various beasts hung along another.

Lee Hyun spoke.

“Is there a way to contain this energy?”

“Every bloodline differs, so I don't know what will suit you.”

Master Hu took out a small jade slip.

“This is a basic Qi-Regulating Method used by the demon race. Read it first, and do not force yourself to follow any part that does not suit you.”

“I still can't read the Bird-Track Script.......”

“I added explanations in the writing of the human race. I made it so that I could compare it with cultivation arts of the human race while studying.”

Lee Hyun accepted the jade slip.

When he lightly sent his divine sense into it, methods for gathering and releasing qi and blood around a demon core appeared in his mind.

‘Damn... Even the demon race centers its qi circulation around a demon core in the dantian?’

He had no separate golden core or demon core to serve as a center.

“Do you have any older methods? Perhaps a way to regulate energy throughout the body's flesh and blood rather than gathering it into one place....”

“It seems that Qi-Regulating Method does not suit you well.”

“Yes.”

Rather than answering immediately, Master Hu went to another shelf. A short while later, he returned with a thin booklet.

When he turned the pages, faint lines ran across an illustration of an enormous beast curled in on itself.

“This is an illustration that accompanied an ancient Record of Transformation.”

The look in Lee Hyun's eyes changed.

“Has the complete cultivation formula for this survived as well?”

“Among the clans that preserve ancient inheritances, some possess related methods or martial learning. But Lulin Pavilion only has records and annotations such as these. To see the main text, you would need permission from its owner.”

Master Hu slid the booklet toward Lee Hyun.

“Start with this. If you find any clues that suit your body, I will look into which clan's records we should seek next.”

Lee Hyun accepted the booklet.

“Thank you. But... are you sure it is all right to help someone you've only just met this much?”

Master Hu studied him for a moment.

“You seem to think I'm making a terrible bargain here. Cangmang Forest has many powerful fellow practitioners, but only a few I can truly reason with.”

Master Hu pointed through the branches outside the window toward the many mountain peaks beyond.

“Those who maintain Lulin Pavilion with me each have their own clans and territories. Normally, we exchange records and help procure whatever the others need. But once disputes begin over the boundaries of spirit veins or the ownership of spirit treasures, even they become reluctant to listen to me.”

“Master, are you the one who mediates between them?”

“If a matter can be settled by talking it through, then that is what should be done. But sometimes I need a powerful fellow practitioner willing to lend weight to my words. All the better if that person favors no particular clan.”

Master Hu rested a hand on the booklet.

“You reached human-form transformation alone, and you can read the books of the human race. Is it really such a terrible bargain to give one vacant guest mountain and a few copied books to a Junior who matched Tan Yue in strength and came away perfectly unharmed?”

Only then did Lee Hyun begin to understand Master Hu's goodwill.

“Of course, I am not asking you to do anything immediately. Recover first and live here for a while to see whether the place suits you. If you lend me a hand once or twice when I run into trouble in the future, I will be grateful.”

“If it is something within my ability, I will help.”

Master Hu nodded.

Chapter 100

Lee Hyun gathered some additional information before leaving Lulin Pavilion.

He asked in turn about the residences and trading posts of the demon race near Qingshi Mountain, then about the rare spirit treasures found in Cangmang Forest. Master Hu patiently explained everything without the slightest sign of annoyance.

He explained that the various clans and factions occasionally held markets for major trades, but everyday necessities could also be found in nearby settlements.

“Does the demon race use spirit stones as well?”

“Of course. Though compared to the human race, we don't tend to carry as many.”

“What about pills?”

“They're useful for barter, provided their quality and effects can be judged. But many are made by alchemists of the human race, so they aren't necessarily useful to the demon race. Constitutions can differ from clan to clan as well.”

Lee Hyun asked several more questions.

Could he obtain seeds and young saplings of spirit trees? Were there craftsmen who worked with high-grade spirit materials? Was it common to exchange ancient inheritances?

Master Hu looked a little more pleased with each question.

This Junior certainly had an inquisitive mind.

He had said he lived alone in the lands of the human race, yet he seemed to have taken an interest in much more than simply tempering his body.

“Surely you aren't thinking of growing plants?”

“I might, depending on the circumstances.”

Master Hu was stunned. He was actually thinking of growing plants? Li Dongwu was more cultured than he could ever have imagined.

Master Hu took a jade slip from a small box beneath the bookshelf and held it out.

“This shows the territories of the mountain lords near Lulin Pavilion.”

When Lee Hyun sent his divine sense into it, mountain ranges, lakes, and distant residences unfolded before him one after another. Qingshi Mountain was marked as a tiny dot on one side of the map.

Lee Hyun found the coast they had departed from at the edge of the map. They had traveled through that enormous forest for so long, yet even the full area shown on the map covered only the southeastern corner of Cangmang Forest.

‘So we're barely past the entrance.’

Master Hu said,

“Don't pass directly over another fellow practitioner's residence without good reason. At first, you'd be better off following the established routes.”

“What about traveling underground? I imagine some clans dig burrows and live beneath the earth.”

Master Hu nodded.

“Of course they do. But traveling underground doesn't make it any less of an intrusion into someone else's territory. If anything, approaching an underground spirit vein or nest may provoke an even stronger reaction.”

“I see.”

Cultivators of the human race found it troublesome to travel deep underground, but there was no guarantee the same held true for the demon race of Cangmang Forest.

‘I can't assume I'll be safe here just because I dig deep. Perhaps this isn't a suitable place for Tunnel No. 4 after all...’

Only after committing the map's borders and travel routes to memory did he collect the diagrams from the ancient Record of Transformation and rise from his seat.

“Thank you for all your help.”

Master Hu saw him off.

After returning to Qingshi Mountain, Lee Hyun used the Aura-Reading Art and Ground-Sense Art to survey the entire mountain.

He checked where water collected and drained away, the thickness of the bedrock layers, and the directions in which the fractures ran.

The mountain streams flowed through the lake in the basin before draining outward. Behind the lake rose a long, blue-tinged cliff face, through which the main current of the spirit vein ran.

When Lee Hyun placed his palm against the rock, he felt spiritual qi flowing from beyond the bedrock. It was different from energy forcibly gathered by a Qi-Gathering Formation. This current flowed without interruption, formed over long ages by the interplay of mountain and water, earth and trees.

‘A Tier-3 spirit vein....’

For a long while, he could not bring himself to take his hand away. How much trouble had he once gone to just to set up a vein seat that secretly tapped someone else's spirit vein? He had spent long years cautiously drawing off only a little spiritual qi to avoid discovery, frequently shifting the positions of his formation flags.

Yet now he had been given an entire mountain, complete with a Tier-3 spirit vein, right from the start. It really did pay to grow stronger!

...

Before sunset, a small cave abode had been carved into the cliff some distance from the temporary cave he had dug the previous day. Its layout was simple: a room for receiving guests, an empty cultivation chamber, and a storeroom dug only a short way into the rock.

Lee Hyun leveled the floor and brought in a table and stools carved from the cliff rock.

He set up a Tier-2 Spirit-Concealing Formation and a basic alarm formation around the cave abode. They were better than nothing, but they fell far short of what his current strength called for.

‘I should get some better formations eventually.’

After hanging Lulin Pavilion's identification token somewhere clearly visible from outside, Lee Hyun closed the cultivation chamber door and looked down at the floor.

Swish.

His body sank beneath the floor.

...

Lee Hyun made a small temporary stone chamber between the layers of bedrock and sat in the lotus position.

First, he examined the Qi-Regulating Method he had received from Master Hu once more. For half a shichen (about one hour), he compared several passages and tried circulating a little energy himself, but as expected, the method did not suit his body.

He set down the jade slip containing the Qi-Regulating Method and pressed to his forehead the one containing the complete Golden Core Section of the 《Primordial One-Qi Art》.

Rereading the passages on the Primordial Body was a different experience now that he had completed the Leakless Golden Body.

In the past, he had merely memorized the mnemonic formulas and understood the diagrams. Now he could clearly feel which currents within his body those passages described.

Lee Hyun slowly steadied his breathing. For now, gaining full control of his new body mattered more than further increasing his magical power. The problem was that the demon markings began to show across his skin whenever he drew on even a little energy.

‘If only I could at least reduce the demonic qi leaking out....’

According to the experimental records of the Baoguang Temple monks, refining the demon markings themselves would take many years. But that did not necessarily mean he had to spend all those years radiating such menacing demonic qi. Surely there was some way to dampen that aura?

Lee Hyun gradually circulated energy from his toes to the crown of his head.

After a long while, he took a flat stone tablet from his storage pouch. He rubbed away the old writing and engraved new information with his fingertip.

【Age: 3,207 years】

【Realm: Golden Core Stage 1】

【Magical Power: 24,500 → 50,000】

【Constitution: Primordial Body, Leakless Golden Body】

【Cultivation Art: Primordial One-Qi Art (Golden Core Section)】

‘Does that look about right?’

Following the conventions of the cultivation world, Lee Hyun changed the label from spiritual power to magical power. The power wielded by cultivators from the Golden Core realm onward was generally called magical power.

He had given considerable thought to the numerical value of his magical power.

A breakthrough into a new major realm drastically altered both its quantity and quality, making it difficult to express with a single number.

Still, this was a handmade status panel for his own convenience, so he settled on a value that felt about right, even if it wasn't entirely precise. The number he arrived at was 50,000.

Lee Hyun left the stone tablet floating before him and stared at it for some time.

He now possessed the Leakless Golden Body, a Nascent Soul-level physique, along with fifty times the magical power of an early Golden Core cultivator...

Back when he first began cultivating, that realm had seemed impossibly distant, attained only by the Patriarchs who upheld the various sects. Now he stood among them.

Lee Hyun fixed the stone tablet to the wall and lay back. He couldn't help smiling as he lay there admiring his handmade status panel.

A short while later, he sat up and inspected the items that had survived the heavenly tribulation.

The Sinking Moon Sword he took from his storage pouch had a hairline crack along one side of its silver-gray blade. If he poured his current magical power into it without restraint, it would snap in an instant. The Six-Leaf Shield, the yellow flying swords, and the Three-Molt Silkworm Robe had already been destroyed beyond recognition.

‘I'll have to get some magic tools or magic treasures. Fortunately, I have plenty of spirit stones and sixteen Golden Core Condensing Pills left. I can sell those while I'm buying what I need.’

He also took out the jade caskets with scorched surfaces and checked that their contents were unharmed. Then he applied fresh Spirit-Sealing Talismans and put them back in his storage pouch.

...

For the next several days, Lee Hyun lived quietly on Qingshi Mountain.

He practiced controlling his new body, studied the map Master Hu had given him, and alternated between examining the diagrams from the ancient Record of Transformation and the Golden Core Section of the 《Primordial One-Qi Art》.

The diagrams showed an enormous beast in various stances, sometimes crouching low to the ground.

At first, he struggled to understand what the pictures meant. But after examining the workings of his own body and assuming those postures, he realized there was an unusual principle behind them.

‘Unlike the Qi-Regulating Method the demon race uses today, this seems to suit my body a little better...’

On reflection, it was not all that strange.

Heaven-and-earth spiritual qi was said to have been far more abundant in ancient times. It was plausible that members of the ancient demon race, not just cultivators of the human race, had tempered their bodies in ways similar to the Primordial Body.

‘I'd like to see the complete inheritance, but I can't just approach someone like a Tier-5 Demon Lord and ask for it... Cangmang Forest is vast, and I don't even know who might have anything useful. I'll have to start gathering information little by little.’

...

He spent the rest of his time searching for a site for Tunnel No. 4. At first, he had planned to descend deep beneath the rocky mountain and create a spacious cavern, but surveying the underground layers with the Ground-Sense Art and Aura-Reading Art revealed a problem.

At around twenty li (about 7.8 km) underground, as with Tunnel No. 3, almost none of the rich spiritual qi he felt on the mountain remained. That would defeat the purpose of possessing a Tier-3 spirit vein.

In the end, Lee Hyun drew upon his experience as society head of the Two Heavens Society and found a relatively deep location that could still receive enough energy from the spirit vein.

By channeling spiritual qi from the Tier-3 spirit vein, he could create an area five li underground with conditions comparable to those around a Tier-2 spirit vein. An adjoining natural cavern in the bedrock also provided plenty of room for trees to grow.

‘But five li is far too shallow... A Tier-4 great demon might find it even with a Tier-2 Spirit-Concealing Formation. In that case... I'd better bring only the Heaven-Origin Divine Tree.’

Unlike Tunnel No. 3, which had proven safe for more than a thousand years, there was still far too much he did not know about Cangmang Forest.

Still, he reckoned he could quickly uproot a single Heaven-Origin Divine Tree and pack it into his storage pouch if an emergency arose.

Of all his spirit plants, the Heaven-Origin Divine Tree was also the one that most urgently needed an environment rich in spiritual qi.

‘And I want to try using Heaven-Origin Force as soon as possible.’

Lee Hyun laid a hand against the rock wall. The solid stone softened beneath his palm, flowing inward as though melting.

On the fifteenth day after settling on Qingshi Mountain, Lee Hyun sat beside the lake brewing tea.

A map of the surrounding area and a diagram of the underground layout lay side by side on the stone table.

As he poured water into his teacup, he suddenly raised his head.

Whoooosh―

Heavy wingbeats thundered from beyond the ridge. The air above the lake was driven aside, sending broad ripples across the water. Four black shapes emerged as the forest's upper branches bowed in unison.

They were four Tier-3 black hawks.

Boom!

The enormous black hawks landed roughly beside the lake, smashing the rocks beneath them. When the gust from their folding wings made the diagrams on the stone table flutter, Lee Hyun calmly reached out and stowed the papers in his storage pouch.

Despite being only Tier-3 demon beasts, the black hawks seemed capable of human-form transformation.

The four soon assumed human form. The man at their head had a sharply hooked nose, and black feathers with a metallic sheen sprouted along his brows, below his ears, and across his shoulders.

His realm was the highest of the four, seemingly close to the peak of Tier 3. All of them, however, had retained their wings.

The man surveyed the cave abode and lakeshore with an arrogant air. He hesitated briefly when he sensed Lee Hyun's demonic qi, then lifted his chin again.

“Who are you, and what are you doing on this mountain?”

“I am Li Dongwu. What brings you here?”

“Who gave you permission to use this mountain?”

“Master Hu permitted me to stay here.”

Lee Hyun pointed toward Lulin Pavilion's identification token hanging at the cave abode's entrance, but the man's scowl only deepened.

“The Black Horn Immortal Lord of Heiyi Ridge has reserved this mountain. The Immortal Lord's nephew will make it his residence after undergoing human-form transformation. Pack your belongings and leave at once.”

He evidently expected the Black Horn Immortal Lord's name alone to make Lee Hyun leave.

Lee Hyun regarded the man for a moment.

He had settled on a guest mountain under Master Hu's care only fifteen days ago, and someone else was already claiming ownership.

‘I see. He's already dragged me into a dispute! I knew there was no such thing as kindness without a price. The demon race is every bit as political as the human race.’

It seemed Master Hu had placed him on a disputed mountain. Still, considering everything Master Hu had done for him, it was only right that Lee Hyun handle a matter like this in return.

Just then, one of the black hawks behind the man strode toward the cave abode's entrance. The stone steps before the cliff cracked beneath its talons.

“So you're copying the human race, even carving stone steps. You'll leave on your own once there's no cave left for you to squat in.”

Lee Hyun's gaze turned icy.

“Stop.”

But the black hawk only snorted, gathering a razor-sharp wind around one wing. Just as it was about to swing at the cave abode's entrance, Lee Hyun vanished from the lakeshore without a trace.

Before the black hawk could register anything amiss and look down, an iron grip clamped around its right ankle.

‘...?!’

Its body was yanked into the air. Gripping its ankle, Lee Hyun twisted at the waist and hurled it straight into the chest of the black hawk beside it before it could even spread its wings.

Boom!

The two tumbled to the ground in a tangled heap, black feathers flying everywhere.

Unable to maintain human form through the pain, they reverted to their true bodies and rolled across the lakeshore.

The leader's eyes widened as two of his companions went down in an instant.

“You bastard!”

He whipped up a black gale and slashed a wing diagonally down at Lee Hyun's chest. Lee Hyun's plain robe tore open, and a harsh metallic screech rang out as the feathers struck his skin.

Screeech!

The black feather tips scraped across his skin, scattering sparks.

Lee Hyun turned the momentum of the man's twisting torso against him, slipping deep inside his guard before the opposite talon could strike.

The moment Lee Hyun's shoulder slipped out of the man's sight, a heavy blow struck the man in the side.

Thud!

A single elbow strike caved in the metal-hard feathers. As the man gasped for breath, Lee Hyun seized his wrist.

Crack!

“Ghk!”

Agony flared as his bones were crushed, and the man frantically unleashed his demon power. His two black wings swept upward behind him, whipping up a vortex that threatened to swallow the lake water and gravel. He tried to use it to pull away, but his trapped wrist did not budge.

As Lee Hyun tightened his grip, golden demon markings flared across his entire body. He hauled on the captured arm and twisted, slamming the hulking man into the ground just as he tried to take flight.

KRAAAASH!

The bedrock by the lake gave way. The man landed on his back, one wing bending at an unnatural angle. The rising vortex broke apart at once, raining down water and stones.

Without giving him a chance to recover, Lee Hyun drove a knee down onto his shoulder and violently twisted the arm in his grip.

Crack-crack!

“S-Stop!”

The man spat blood as black feathers erupted across his neck and cheeks and his body began to swell. Seeing the signs that he was about to revert to his true body and fight back, Lee Hyun slammed him into the ground once more.

Boom!

“...”

The last uninjured black hawk stood with its wings awkwardly half-spread, trembling without a trace of the dignity expected of a Tier-3 demon beast.

The two that had been knocked down also managed to struggle upright, shaking, with broken wings and blood running from their beaks.

“Anything else you want to say?”

One of their beaks opened a fraction, then closed again. Lee Hyun addressed the man pinned beneath him.

“Go to Master Hu and confirm who this land belongs to.”

Lee Hyun lifted the man's head slightly by the back of his neck. He groaned, coughing up dust and blood.

“...I'll confirm it.”

The man barely managed to shift his eyes toward Lee Hyun's hand clamped around his arm. Even with his demon power shielding him, the iron-hard feathers were crumpling wherever those fingers pressed.

Beyond the golden demon markings flickering beneath Lee Hyun's skin, he sensed an aura like dozens of different kinds of ferocious great demons tangled together and snarling in hell. A chill ran down his spine.

‘Just what kind of monstrous bloodline does he have...!’

If Lee Hyun applied even a little more force, his entire arm would be torn off.

“We apologize.”

Lee Hyun looked down at him for a moment, then loosened his grip and lifted his knee from the man's shoulder.

The other three black hawks hurried over, wrapping their wings around the man to help him up as one of his arms hung limp. When Lee Hyun's gaze flicked toward the shattered stone steps, the black hawk with the cracked beak flinched. It hastily pushed the rock fragment it had dislodged with its talons back into place, then backed away.

The black shapes disappeared beyond the ridge in a hurried retreat.

Lee Hyun stretched.

“Hmm... That should have made Master Hu's position even more secure!”

Two days later, at Lulin Pavilion.

Master Hu stared incredulously at the man in black robes, who sat before him with one arm in a cloth sling.

The feathers below his ears had fallen out in patches, and a vivid blue-black bruise in the shape of five fingers showed on the back of his neck above his collar. Of the three black hawks crouched in the branches outside the pavilion, one even had bandages wrapped around its beak.

“But that's Qingshi Mountain, not Qingjiao Mountain...?”

“...?”

As the man raised his head blankly, Master Hu removed his jade spectacles, then put them back on and adjusted them.

‘What a complete birdbrain!’

“The place I discussed with the Black Horn Immortal Lord was Qingjiao Mountain, a little over a thousand li east of Qingshi Mountain.”

“.......”

...

After sending the group away, Master Hu stood by the window for a long while, lost in thought. The fault lay entirely with Heiyi Ridge, but their injuries had been severe.

‘He was formidable enough when he matched strength with Tan Yue, but I never imagined he could be this heavy-handed. He beat those subordinates without hesitation, even with a Tier-4 great demon like the Black Horn Immortal Lord backing them! Could he really be descended from some fierce ancient bloodline that revels in battle....’

He pictured Li Dongwu speaking gently, observing proper etiquette, and reading the human race's books. His nature was not bad; he probably just hadn't learned how to get along with his neighbors or control his strength yet.

‘So even with all that intelligence, he's still a beast... But he's the most promising member of the demon race I've ever seen. He's only so rough because he's lived in the wild like a demon beast. Given time, I can teach him to become a civilized member of the demon race!’

One month later.

Lee Hyun followed the routes Master Hu had indicated as he traveled through the forest, only descending deep underground once he approached the lands of the human race.

He was heading through Xu Kingdom and Xuan Kingdom toward Tunnel No. 3 in northwestern Kun Kingdom.

In the past, he would have stopped at cultivator markets along the way to buy supplies and popular novels. Now, however, even the Spirit-Concealing Art and Aura-Concealing Art could not hide the menacing demonic qi leaking from beneath his skin.

If he showed up at a cultivator market in this state, every cultivator he met would piss themselves.

At least his greatly increased magical power made the Earth Escape Art and Metal Escape Art incomparably smoother to use than before. He could channel energy through any of his limbs, and the layers of earth flowed apart like water.

Before long, he sensed the familiar vibrations of the bedrock and water veins.

When he emerged into one of Tunnel No. 3's passages, a Bonefuzz carrying a water bucket in the distance stopped walking. The golden ball of fuzz inside its skull perked up its antennae.

Squeak?

Lee Hyun raised a hand slightly and sent his mental intent through the Spirit-Nurturing Seal.

“It's me.”

A moment later, the fuzzbee emerged from the Bonefuzz's head and buzzed twice around Lee Hyun. Only then did the other fuzzbees begin flying over from all around to welcome him.

Lee Hyun first inspected the spirit fields. The work he had done before leaving had kept everything in good order.

After examining the life force flowing through the Heaven-Origin Divine Tree's branches and checking the Ringless Divine Tree's leaves and trunk, he felt much more at ease.

“Let's go somewhere nice.”

He prepared the items needed to transplant the Heaven-Origin Divine Tree. He intended to dig it up just before leaving, but first, there were a few things he wanted to test.

...

Standing at the center of the underground training chamber far from the spirit fields, Lee Hyun brought two fingers together.

Hummm―

Great Unity Heavenly Dipper Sword Qi gathered at his fingertips, radiating an intense aura. He followed it with the Sumeru Mountain-Suppressing Seal, and a golden palm imprint appeared, far more sharply defined than before. It seemed almost solid.

‘It really is different.’

Lee Hyun dismissed the sword qi and palm imprint, then activated the technique from the Sumeru Visualization Scripture that he had been most eager to test.

Hummmm―

The air behind him brightened, and the All-Hearing Heavenly King manifestation, compressed to a little over one zhang (about 3.3 m) tall, planted its feet on the stone chamber floor.

When he used its golden hand to lift a rock from the floor, the sensations of weight and resistance reached him clearly through the energy flowing within the Dharma manifestation.

“Finally!”

Reciting the mnemonic formula in his mind, Lee Hyun opened the parasol in the manifestation's left hand. A curtain of golden light flowed down from its rim, curving around the front of the Dharma manifestation.

An iron shard launched with the Sword Control Art struck it with a clang and bounced harmlessly away. The thread of flame he sent after it hit the densely woven golden strands and scattered in all directions.

Magical power and divine sense were consumed in proportion to the force of the attacks it blocked, but its defenses far surpassed those of the Spirit Light Shield or Qi Sphere Barrier.

When he folded the parasol and raised the pagoda in the manifestation's right hand, a golden boundary descended onto the floor. An iron shard sent flying inside immediately wavered and slowed as if caught in a swamp. The tighter he drew the boundary, the stronger the suppressive force became.

‘This is fun!’

Lee Hyun dismissed the Dharma manifestation, took out a jade slip, and pressed it to his forehead to study the other three Heavenly Kings described in the Sumeru Visualization Scripture. There were teachings on the Growth Heavenly King manifestation with its sword, the Wide-Seeing Heavenly King manifestation with its dragon and jewel, and the Nation-Guarding Heavenly King manifestation with its pipa.

‘Which should I learn next? The sound art Nie Xingya from the Yin Bird Sect used last time was quite unusual... Perhaps the Nation-Guarding Heavenly King manifestation with its pipa would be a good choice?’

After briefly reading the Dharma teaching, Lee Hyun sensed that mastering the manifestations of the other three Heavenly Kings would take quite some time.

...

Lee Hyun prepared to leave Tunnel No. 3.

He loosened the surrounding soil with the Soil-Turning Art, dug up the Heaven-Origin Divine Tree without damaging even the finest root, and placed it into a large storage pouch.

He also took along several Tier-2 fuzzbees, some young ones, and a few Bonefuzz puppets to use at his new residence. The remaining fuzzbees and Bonefuzz puppets stayed behind to tend the spirit fields in Tunnel No. 3.

All that remained was to return to Qingshi Mountain, but there was now one place he needed to visit first.

Several days earlier, he had opened the hidden stone box at the society head's private contact point to arrange the sale of some Golden Core Condensing Pills. Inside, he had also found a report that the Two Heavens Society's trade network connecting southern Xuan Kingdom and northern Kun Kingdom had been exposed.

The two sides had arranged to meet near the border soon. According to the report, however, the other side had a Golden Core cultivator, and the Two Heavens Society's own Golden Core member would be hard-pressed to handle the situation.

‘It's about time I went to see for myself.’

The meeting took place in a clearing outside a mountain cultivator market, not far from the border between southern Xuan Kingdom and Kun Kingdom.

Under the moonlight, a dozen or so members of the Two Heavens Society stood around an early Golden Core cultivator wearing a red deer mask. They might as well have been standing on thin ice.

Cultivators from Nanming had taken up positions all around them, all but encircling the group.

Across from them, an old man at mid Golden Core who had not even bothered to conceal his face used his magical power to send a jade slip floating toward Red Deer.

“We aren't asking for anything difficult. From now on, simply deliver the specified quantity of your incoming medicinal ingredients to us before anyone else, and hand over the transaction records and broker lists for three of your bases.”

“What does that have to do with trading medicinal ingredients? That isn't how we conduct business.”

“Then change how you do business, starting now.”

The man beside him, an early Golden Core cultivator in reddish-brown robes, sneered.

“Did you think hiding behind masks would frighten us? Let's not make this harder than it needs to be.”

One of the members stiffened, and Red Deer let his magical power flare. The two Golden Core cultivators opposite him immediately unleashed their own auras, making the air all around them tremble.

Red Deer felt cornered.

He had thought that, with only one Golden Core cultivator on the other side, he could order the members to withdraw and then escape himself if things went wrong. He had never expected a second Golden Core cultivator!

Although the society head had sent word that he would look into the matter, Red Deer hadn't been certain he would come all this way to intervene personally.

Then it happened.

All three Golden Core cultivators suddenly looked in the same direction.

Someone was crossing the clearing toward them, radiating a terrifying aura.

The Nanming cultivators parted to either side, barely daring to breathe, much less block his path.

At last, a man in neat robes stepped out of the shadows. The tiger mask on his face shone white in the moonlight.

He carried no weapon, yet with every step he exuded a savage pressure that seemed to crush the very air around him.

The old man at mid Golden Core instinctively extended his divine sense, then turned deathly pale and immediately withdrew it.

‘A-a Tier-4 great demon who has undergone human-form transformation...?!’
